content:
The All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) New Delhi has announced the examination schedule for the Nursing Officer Recruitment Common Eligibility Test (NORCET 12). This national-level entrance exam serves as the primary gateway for qualified nursing professionals seeking recruitment across various AIIMS campuses and participating central government hospitals throughout India. For thousands of nursing aspirants, securing a Nursing Officer rank represents a prestigious and stable career path within India's premier public healthcare sector.

Understanding the multi-tiered exam pattern, educational requirements, and structured revision strategy is essential for candidate success. This comprehensive guide outlines the official exam schedule, eligibility standards, and an actionable preparation strategy for students and supportive parents.

Overview of AIIMS NORCET 12 Recruitment Process

The NORCET examination is conducted to assess clinical competency, professional knowledge, and aptitude for nursing care responsibilities. The selection procedure consists of two sequential computer-based online stages:

  • Stage 1 (Prelims): A screening test designed to short-list candidates based on foundational nursing principles and general aptitude.
  • Stage 2 (Mains): A advanced assessment focused on practical clinical scenarios, skill-based competencies, and decision-making capabilities required in critical care settings.

Candidate performance in the Stage 2 examination determines the final merit list and institute allocation during central counselling.

AIIMS NORCET 12 Official Exam Schedule

Aspirants must keep track of critical dates to ensure timely application submission and admit card downloads. Candidates are advised to regularly monitor the official AIIMS examination portal at aiimsexams.ac.in for real-time updates and notification brochures.

  • Online Registration Portal: Opens along with the detailed notification rollout, allowing candidates to register and upload verified credentials.
  • Application Correction Window: A brief window provided after registration closes to correct uploaded photographs, signatures, or personal category details.
  • Stage 1 Prelims Exam Date: Conducted across designated examination centres nationwide in online Computer-Based Test (CBT) mode.
  • Stage 2 Mains Exam Date: Scheduled approximately three to four weeks after the declaration of Stage 1 results for qualified candidates.

Nursing Officer Eligibility Criteria and Qualifications

Candidates must ensure they satisfy all academic, professional, and age parameters before submitting their application. Failure to meet these mandatory requirements leads to candidate disqualification during document verification.

1. Academic Qualifications

Applicants must hold one of the following recognized nursing credentials:

  • B.Sc. (Hons.) Nursing or B.Sc. Nursing from an institute recognized by the Indian Nursing Council (INC) or State Nursing Council.
  • B.Sc. (Post-Certificate) or Post-Basic B.Sc. Nursing from an INC-approved institution.
  • Diploma in General Nursing Midwifery (GNM) from an INC-recognized board or council, combined with a mandatory minimum of two years of clinical experience in a hospital containing at least 50 beds after acquiring the diploma qualification.

2. Professional Registration

Candidates must be active Registered Nurses and Midwives (RN/RM) with either the State Nursing Council or the Indian Nursing Council at the time of application submission.

3. Age Limit and Relaxations

The standard age limit for candidates applying for Nursing Officer positions is between 18 and 30 years. Age relaxations apply to reserved categories according to official Central Government guidelines:

  • OBC Candidates: Up to 3 years of relaxation.
  • SC/ST Candidates: Up to 5 years of relaxation.
  • PwBD Candidates: Up to 10 years of general relaxation, subject to disability category rules.

NORCET 12 Exam Pattern and Marking Scheme

Understanding the question distribution and marking parameters helps candidates optimize their speed and accuracy during the test.

Stage 1 (Prelims) Structure

  • Total Questions: 100 Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs).
  • Subject Breakdown: 80 questions focused on nursing course curriculum and 20 questions covering general knowledge, logical reasoning, and basic mathematics.
  • Duration: 90 minutes.
  • Qualifying Criteria: Candidates must score above the prescribed percentile cutoff (generally 50th percentile for General/EWS, 45th percentile for OBC, and 40th percentile for SC/ST) to become eligible for Stage 2.

Stage 2 (Mains) Structure

  • Total Questions: 100 MCQs focused strictly on clinical skills and patient-care scenarios.
  • Duration: 90 minutes.
  • Question Style: Includes image-based, video-based, case-study, and priority nursing intervention questions.
  • Negative Marking: One-third (1/3rd) of a mark is deducted for every incorrect response in both Stage 1 and Stage 2 exams. Unattempted questions carry no penalty.

Comprehensive Preparation Blueprint for Aspirants

Cracking NORCET 12 requires balancing theoretical fundamentals with practical clinical application. The following blueprint outlines a systematic four-point preparation approach.

1. Master Core Nursing Subjects

Prioritize high-weightage topics that form the backbone of the exam. Allocate dedicated study time to Medical-Surgical Nursing, Pharmacology, Obstetrics and Gynecological Nursing, Pediatric Nursing, Anatomy, Physiology, and Psychiatric Nursing. Pay close attention to standard drug dosages, contraindications, normal diagnostic values, and emergency procedures.

2. Focus on Scenario-Based and Skill Questions

Modern NORCET papers increasingly test practical judgment. Study clinical protocols for ICU monitoring, ventilator management, wound dressing, catheterization, and infection control standards. Practicing image-based recognition of medical instruments, ECG patterns, and surgical equipment is vital for the Stage 2 exam.

3. Build Speed and Accuracy through Mock Tests

Since negative marking severely impacts total scores, accuracy is critical. Solve mock tests using timer-based environments to develop pacing. Analyze test performance to identify weak subject domains and reduce guesswork strategies during actual test conditions.

4. Strengthen Non-Nursing Aptitude

Do not ignore the 20 non-nursing questions in Stage 1. Regular practice of current affairs, basic arithmetic, and analytical reasoning can easily yield essential bonus marks that boost overall rank position.

Guidance for Parents Supporting NORCET Candidates

Preparation for high-stakes healthcare entrance tests can be stressful. Parents play a key role by providing a quiet, structured environment and encouraging consistent health, balanced sleep, and positive mindset habits during intensive revision phases.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Q1. Can final-year B.Sc. Nursing students apply for NORCET 12?

Candidates must possess their final degree certificate and active nursing council registration (RN/RM) on or before the application closing date to be eligible.

Q2. Is clinical experience required for B.Sc. Nursing candidates?

No, clinical experience is not required for B.Sc. Nursing or Post-Basic B.Sc. Nursing graduates. Clinical experience in a 50-bed hospital for two years is mandatory only for GNM diploma holders.

Q3. What is the penalty for wrong answers in AIIMS NORCET 12?

Both Stage 1 and Stage 2 exams apply a negative marking rule where 1/3rd of the assigned mark is deducted for each incorrect answer.

Q4. How should candidates verify official exam schedules and venue details?

Candidates must always rely on updates published on the official AIIMS exams portal at aiimsexams.ac.in for authentic announcements, admit card releases, and schedule modifications.

title: INI-CET जनवरी 2027 का परिणाम जारी: सूची में रोल नंबर और MyPage पर पर्सेंटाइल कैसे देखें
description: एम्स ने जनवरी 2027 सत्र की सूची जारी की है। अपना रोल नंबर कैसे खोजें, सूची में नाम न होने पर पर्सेंटाइल कहाँ देखें और सीट आवंटन के लिए किस सूचना का इंतज़ार करें।
content:
एम्स ने जनवरी 2027 सत्र का INI-CET परिणाम जारी कर दिया है। दो अलग-अलग चीज़ें देखनी हैं: सार्वजनिक पीडीएफ में अस्थायी रूप से अर्ह पाए गए अभ्यर्थियों के रोल नंबर हैं। अपना पर्सेंटाइल MyPage पर देखें। परीक्षा देने वाले उन अभ्यर्थियों का पर्सेंटाइल भी वहाँ उपलब्ध है जो इस सूची में नहीं हैं।

जनवरी सत्र की सही सूची पहचानें

एम्स की परीक्षा वेबसाइट पर Results & Announcements में INICET January 2027 वाली सूची खोलें। वेबसाइट पर इसे 7 नवंबर को जारी किया गया है। पीडीएफ पर परिणाम अधिसूचना संख्या 304/2026 और तारीख 6 नवंबर 2026 लिखी है। दोनों तारीखें एक ही परिणाम की हैं। इस सत्र की प्रवेश परीक्षा 1 नवंबर को हुई थी।

प्रवेश पत्र वाला रोल नंबर पीडीएफ में खोजें। सूची रोल नंबर के क्रम में है, इसलिए पहली पंक्ति को पहली रैंक न समझें। एमडी, एमएस, छह वर्षीय डीएम और छह वर्षीय एमसीएच की सूची से एमडीएस का भाग अलग है। सही भाग में अपने रोल नंबर के सामने रैंक और पर्सेंटाइल पढ़ें।

रोल नंबर न मिले तो स्कोर कहाँ देखें?

अपने Candidate ID और पासवर्ड से एम्स पोर्टल के MyPage में प्रवेश करें। पर्सेंटाइल बताता है कि बाकी परीक्षार्थियों की तुलना में आपका प्रदर्शन कैसा रहा। यह सही जवाबों का प्रतिशत नहीं है।

अधिसूचना में दी गई श्रेणीअर्हता के लिए पर्सेंटाइल
अनारक्षित, ईडब्ल्यूएस, प्रायोजित, प्रतिनियुक्त, विदेशी नागरिक और ओसीआई50वाँ
ओबीसी, एससी, एसटी और पीडब्ल्यूबीडी45वाँ
भूटानी नागरिक, केवल पीजीआईएमईआर चंडीगढ़ के लिए45वाँ

रैंक मिलने के बाद भी सीट की पुष्टि क्यों नहीं हुई है?

अभी परिणाम अस्थायी है। सूची में रोल नंबर होने से पात्रता या हर प्रमाणपत्र की वैधता की पुष्टि नहीं होती। ओबीसी या ईडब्ल्यूएस प्रमाणपत्र अपलोड किया है तो अपना पंजीकृत ईमेल देखें। प्रारंभिक जाँच की स्थिति वहीं बताई जाएगी। संस्थान और विषय की पसंद दर्ज करने के लिए अलग निर्देश जारी होंगे।

एम्स नई दिल्ली, परिणाम अधिसूचना 304/2026, 6 नवंबर 2026, पृष्ठ 880। एम्स के परिणाम अनुभाग में जनवरी सत्र की मूल सूची खोलें।

एम्स के परीक्षा कैलेंडर में काउंसलिंग का कार्यक्रम परिणाम से अलग दिया जाता है। परिणाम की अपेक्षित तारीख वाली पुरानी खबर के बजाय अब अपना परिणाम प्रकाशित सूची और MyPage से देखें।

title: ഐഐഎം ബെംഗളൂരു വേനൽക്കാല പ്ലേസ്‌മെന്റ്: 608 പേർക്ക് ഓഫർ, മാസ സ്റ്റൈപൻഡ് വിശദീകരണം
description: ഐഐഎം ബെംഗളൂരുവിൽ പങ്കെടുത്ത 608 പേർക്കും ഓഫർ ലഭിച്ചു. പ്രതിമാസ മധ്യക, ശരാശരി സ്റ്റൈപൻഡും കൺസൾട്ടിങ് മേഖലയുടെ വിഹിതവും മനസ്സിലാക്കാം.
content:
ഐഐഎം ബെംഗളൂരുവിന്റെ 2026 ഒക്ടോബർ 31ലെ അറിയിപ്പനുസരിച്ച്, PGP, PGPBA 2026-28 ബാച്ചുകളിൽനിന്ന് പങ്കെടുത്ത 608 വിദ്യാർഥികൾക്കും വേനൽക്കാല പ്ലേസ്‌മെന്റ് ഓഫറുകൾ ലഭിച്ചു. ഒക്ടോബർ 26-29 നടന്ന പ്രക്രിയയിൽ 128 സ്ഥാപനങ്ങൾ പങ്കെടുത്തു. എംബിഎ പഠനവഴികൾ താരതമ്യം ചെയ്യുമ്പോൾ ഈ തുകകൾ പ്രതിമാസ ഇന്റേൺഷിപ്പ് സ്റ്റൈപൻഡാണെന്ന് ഓർക്കണം; വാർഷിക ശമ്പള പാക്കേജല്ല.

കണക്കിനൊപ്പം അതിന്റെ അളവുകോലും നോക്കണം

മാപനം

സ്ഥാപനം അറിയിച്ച കണക്ക്

ഓഫർ ലഭിച്ച പങ്കാളികളായ വിദ്യാർഥികൾ

608

നിയമന സ്ഥാപനങ്ങൾ

128

മധ്യക സ്റ്റൈപൻഡ്

പ്രതിമാസം ₹2 ലക്ഷം

ശരാശരി സ്റ്റൈപൻഡ്

പ്രതിമാസം ₹1.95 ലക്ഷം

ഓഫറുകളിൽ കൺസൾട്ടിങ്ങിന്റെ വിഹിതം

50.7%

ഈ കണക്കുകൾ ഔദ്യോഗിക വേനൽക്കാല പ്ലേസ്‌മെന്റ് അറിയിപ്പ്യിൽ നിന്നുള്ളതാണ്. 100% എന്ന ഫലം ഈ പ്രക്രിയയിൽ പങ്കെടുത്ത 608 പേരെ സംബന്ധിച്ചതാണ്. ഭാവിയിലെ അപേക്ഷകർക്കുള്ള ഉറപ്പായോ സ്ഥാപനത്തിലെ എല്ലാ പഠനപരിപാടികളുടെയും ഫലമായോ അതിനെ കാണരുത്.

കൺസൾട്ടിങ്ങിന് പുറമെയും അവസരങ്ങളുണ്ട്

22 സ്ഥാപനങ്ങളിൽനിന്ന് 308 കൺസൾട്ടിങ് ഓഫറുകൾ ലഭിച്ചതായി സ്ഥാപനം പറയുന്നു. ധനകാര്യം, സാങ്കേതികവിദ്യ, ഉൽപ്പന്നവുമായി ബന്ധപ്പെട്ട ജോലികൾ, വിപണനം, ജനറൽ മാനേജ്മെന്റ് എന്നിവയും അറിയിപ്പിലുണ്ട്. പങ്കെടുത്ത സ്ഥാപനങ്ങളിൽ ഏകദേശം 40% ആദ്യമായി നിയമനത്തിനെത്തിയവയാണ്.

പ്രത്യേക തൊഴിൽലക്ഷ്യമുള്ള വിദ്യാർഥിക്ക് മൊത്തം പ്ലേസ്‌മെന്റ് ശതമാനത്തേക്കാൾ മേഖലകളിലെ അവസരങ്ങളുടെ വിഭജനം ഉപകാരപ്രദമാകും. നിങ്ങൾ ആഗ്രഹിക്കുന്ന മേഖലയിലെ ജോലികളും തൊഴിൽദാതാക്കളും പരിശോധിക്കുക. ഉയർന്ന മൊത്തം കണക്ക് എല്ലാ വിഭാഗങ്ങളിലും ഒരുപോലെ അവസരമുണ്ടെന്ന സൂചനയല്ല.

മധ്യകവും ശരാശരിയും പറയുന്നത് വ്യത്യസ്ത കാര്യങ്ങൾ

സ്റ്റൈപൻഡ് തുകകൾ ക്രമത്തിൽ നിരത്തുമ്പോൾ നടുവിൽ വരുന്ന മൂല്യമാണ് മധ്യകം. എല്ലാ തുകകളും കൂട്ടി അവയുടെ എണ്ണംകൊണ്ട് ഹരിക്കുമ്പോൾ ശരാശരി കിട്ടും. ഓരോ വിദ്യാർഥിക്കും എത്ര ലഭിച്ചുവെന്ന് ഇവ രണ്ടും വ്യക്തമാക്കുന്നില്ല. വേനൽക്കാല ഇന്റേൺഷിപ്പിന്റെ മാസത്തുക ഗുണിച്ച് വാർഷിക ശമ്പളമായി കണക്കാക്കരുത്.

മറ്റൊരു ബിസിനസ് സ്കൂളുമായി താരതമ്യം ചെയ്യുന്നതിന് മുമ്പ് അത് പ്രതിമാസ സ്റ്റൈപൻഡാണോ, മുഴുവൻ ഇന്റേൺഷിപ്പിന്റെ തുകയാണോ, സ്ഥിരം ജോലിയുടെ ശമ്പളമാണോ എന്ന് നോക്കുക. ബാച്ചും പ്ലേസ്‌മെന്റ് ചക്രവും ഒത്തുനോക്കണം. വ്യത്യസ്ത അളവുകോലുകൾ ഉപയോഗിച്ചാൽ യഥാർഥ വ്യത്യാസമില്ലാതെയും ഒരു പഠനപരിപാടി മെച്ചമോ മോശമോ ആയി തോന്നാം.

പഠനപരിപാടികളെക്കുറിച്ച് അറിയാൻ പ്ലേസ്‌മെന്റ് അറിയിപ്പിനൊപ്പം ഐഐഎം ബെംഗളൂരുവിന്റെ PGP, PGPBA പേജുകളും വായിക്കാം. ഞങ്ങളുടെ ഐഐഎം അഹമ്മദാബാദ് ക്ലസ്റ്റർ 3 വിശദീകരണം, ലഭ്യമായ ജോലി റോളുകളുടെ എണ്ണവും ഓഫർ ലഭിച്ച വിദ്യാർഥികളുടെ എണ്ണവും തമ്മിലുള്ള വ്യത്യാസം വിശദീകരിക്കുന്നു.

title: FMGE ઑક્ટોબર 2026: પ્રશ્નની તકનીકી ભૂલ સામે 2 નવેમ્બર સુધી વાંધો
description: FMGEના પ્રશ્નમાં તકનીકી ભૂલ હોય તો તબીબી પુરાવા સાથે 2 નવેમ્બર સુધી વાંધો મોકલો. પ્રશ્ન અઘરો હતો એવી ફરિયાદ માત્ર સ્વીકારાશે નહીં.
content:
તમે 31 ઑક્ટોબર 2026ના રોજ FMGE આપી હોય અને કોઈ પ્રશ્નમાં તકનીકી ભૂલ હોવાનું માનતા હો, તો NBEMSના બુલેટિન મુજબ 2 નવેમ્બર 2026 સુધી વાંધો રજૂ કરી શકો છો. સમર્થન આપતું તબીબી સાહિત્ય જોડીને સત્તાવાર Communication Web Portal પર નોંધાયેલો ઈમેલ વાપરવો જરૂરી છે. પ્રશ્ન અઘરો હતો એટલી ફરિયાદ આ નિયમ હેઠળ સ્વીકારાતી નથી.

બે દિવસની તક કોને મળે છે?

ઑક્ટોબર 2026નું સત્તાવાર માહિતી બુલેટિનની કલમ 10.2 આ તક માત્ર પરીક્ષામાં હાજર રહેલા ઉમેદવારોને આપે છે. પરીક્ષા પછી વધુમાં વધુ બે કૅલેન્ડર દિવસની મર્યાદા છે. 2 નવેમ્બર પછી રજૂ થયેલા દાવા સ્વીકારવામાં નહીં આવે. પુરાવા સાથે તકનીકી વાંધો હોય તો પરિણામની રાહ ન જુઓ.

NBEMS, FMGE ઑક્ટોબર 2026 માહિતી બુલેટિન, પાનું 89. આ અંશમાં વાંધાની છેલ્લી તારીખ 2 નવેમ્બર 2026 દર્શાવેલી છે. ઑક્ટોબર 2026નું સત્તાવાર માહિતી બુલેટિન

ચોક્કસ ભૂલને પુરાવા સાથે સમજાવો

ચોક્કસ તકનીકી ભૂલ શું છે, તે પ્રશ્નને કેવી રીતે અસર કરે છે અને કયું તબીબી સાહિત્ય તમારા મુદ્દાને સમર્થન આપે છે તે સ્પષ્ટ લખો. પેપર કેવું લાગ્યું તેનો સામાન્ય અનુભવ તકનીકી ભૂલ સાબિત કરતો નથી. તપાસનારને ચોક્કસ સમસ્યા સમજાય એટલી સંક્ષિપ્ત અને સ્પષ્ટ રજૂઆત કરો.

  1. સત્તાવાર પરીક્ષા વેબસાઇટ પરથી NBEMS Communication Web Portal ખોલો.

  2. FMGE અરજીમાં નોંધાયેલો ઈમેલ વાપરો અને પોર્ટલ માગે તે ઉમેદવારની વિગતો આપો.

  3. તકનીકી વાંધો અને તેને સમર્થન આપતું તબીબી સાહિત્ય નિર્ધારિત સમયમાં રજૂ કરો.

  4. સ્વીકૃતિ અથવા સંદર્ભ નંબર અને રજૂ કરેલી સામગ્રીની નકલ સાચવી રાખો.

આ જોગવાઈમાં છેલ્લી તારીખ છે, અલગથી બંધ થવાનો સમય નથી. મધરાત સુધી સમય હશે એમ માનશો નહીં. લોગિન કે દસ્તાવેજ અપલોડની સમસ્યા ઉકેલવા સમય રહે તે રીતે વહેલું મોકલો.

ઉત્તર કી ઉપલબ્ધ થવાની પ્રક્રિયા અલગ છે

કલમ 10.3 અનુસાર ઑક્ટોબર 2026ના અરજદાર લોગિનમાં પ્રશ્ન ID, સાચા જવાબની ID, પસંદ કરેલા જવાબની ID અને દરેક પ્રશ્ન માટે મળેલા ગુણ ઉપલબ્ધ કરાશે. આ જોગવાઈ હોવાનો અર્થ ઉત્તર કી પહેલેથી જાહેર થઈ ગઈ એવો નથી. પ્રકાશન સૂચના અને પ્રવેશની રીત સત્તાવાર FMGE પાનું પર જુઓ.

પરિણામ પછી ફરી તપાસનો નિયમ

બુલેટિન મુજબ પરિણામ 30 નવેમ્બર 2026 સુધી જાહેર થવાની શક્યતા છે. આ અપેક્ષિત સમય છે, પરિણામ જાહેર થયાની પુષ્ટિ નથી. FMGEમાં પુનઃમૂલ્યાંકન, ફરી તપાસ, ગુણનો ફરી સરવાળો કે ગ્રેસ માર્ક્સની જોગવાઈ નથી. પરિણામ પહેલાંના તકનીકી પ્રશ્ન-વાંધાની પ્રક્રિયા સાથે આ માંગણીઓને ભેળવશો નહીં.

ઉત્તીર્ણ થવા માટેના અલગ માપદંડ માટે FMGEના પાસિંગ માર્ક્સની માર્ગદર્શિકા વાંચો. પરીક્ષાની કઠિનતા વિશેના અભિપ્રાયો કે યાદ રહેલા પ્રશ્નો તમારું સત્તાવાર પરિણામ નક્કી કરતા નથી.

title: CBSE Class 10 Science and Social Science Dates 2027: Plan the Gaps
description: Science is on 22 February and Social Science on 8 March in the CBSE Class 10 timetable. Work out usable revision days around languages and optional subjects.
content:
CBSE Class 10 Science is scheduled for 22 February 2027 and Social Science for 8 March 2027. Both papers run from 10:30 am to 1:30 pm IST. The days between them are not automatically a two-week study break: English, Hindi and several optional or language papers fall within that period.

Put the main papers in order

These dates come from pages 4-7 of the official CBSE timetable dated 6 November 2026. The official document below shows Science on PDF page 4 and the later papers on the following pages.

CBSE Class 10 and 12 date sheet, 6 November 2026

Central Board of Secondary Education, notice dated 6 November 2026. Relevant section: PDF page 4. Open the original official document.

Count free dates, then subtract your other exams

There are four calendar dates between Mathematics on 17 February and Science on 22 February: 18, 19, 20 and 21 February. Those are not necessarily four free days. Home Science is on 19 February, while several other subjects occupy 18 and 20 February.

Similarly, there are three intervening dates between Science and English, 23-25 February. A student taking Computer Applications, Information Technology or Artificial Intelligence has a paper on 24 February. Build the revision plan from your complete registered subject list, not only the five rows above.

Give each gap a purpose

Before the board papers begin, identify Science topics that still require a teacher's explanation and complete that work early. During the shorter gap, use attempted answers to decide what to revisit. A final review is easier when diagrams, calculations and explanation errors have already been collected in one place.

For Social Science, maintain a separate list of weak areas and incomplete answers while other papers are underway. Avoid assuming that everything can wait until after Hindi. Some students have other language examinations before 8 March, so the available days differ.

Keep the last session before each paper manageable: review corrections, organise the required documents and follow the actual arrival instructions. This suggested routine does not change the syllabus, paper pattern or any school requirement.

Make the calendar specific to your subjects

Ask the school about an unfamiliar code before removing a paper from your list. Use the weekly revision planning guide to fit small tasks around the dates, and retain the complete official PDF so optional subjects remain visible.

title: How to Avoid Negative Marking in MET 2027: Tips to Improve Accuracy
description: Learn how to avoid negative marking in MET 2027 with smart guessing strategies, time management tips, mock test practice, and techniques to improve accuracy.
content:
The Manipal Entrance Test 2027 is an entrance exam for students who want to get into engineering and other programs at Manipal Academy of Higher Education. To get results, candidates need to concentrate on answering questions correctly, avoid making mistakes that are not needed, and keep good control of exam time.

Knowing the MET 2027 exam pattern and marking scheme is essential before you create a plan to reduce the loss of marks. Candidates must check the rules once the examination details are released.

1. Understand the MET 2027 Marking Scheme

Before you sit for the exam, check the marks you get for answers and the penalties for wrong answers. The marking rules may change depending on the type of question or the year, so do not rely on past years' patterns.

2. Attempt Questions Strategically

Do not attempt every question without considering its difficulty. Answer questions you can solve confidently first, then return to questions that require more time. This approach helps prevent rushed errors.

3. Avoid Random Guesswork

Blind guessing can lower your score if wrong answers have a penalty. If you can remove some choices and make it easier to check the scoring rules before you pick an answer.

4. Get Better at Answering by Taking Mock Tests

Doing tests that are like the MET helps students find the topics they are not good at and the mistakes they often make. After each test, look at the answers you got wrong and see if the mistakes were because of not understanding the idea, making math errors, or not managing time well.

5. Use Your Time Well

Split your time based on the kind of questions and how hard they are. Don't spend much time on one hard question. Make sure you have time left to check your work and look over your answers before you finish the test.

6. Go Over Key Ideas Again

A good understanding of physics, chemistry, and mathematics can help B.Tech hopefuls answer questions correctly. Review formulas, solve math problems, and do questions or example questions when you can.
Quick Tips to Minimize Marks Loss

Common Mistake

What to Do

Blind guessing

Evaluate the risk before answering

Rushed calculations

Check calculations carefully

Spending too long on one question

Move on and return later

Ignoring weak topics

Practise targeted questions

Misunderstanding the marking scheme

Read the official exam instructions

Poor time management

Practise timed mock tests

Conclusion

To avoid negative marking in MET 2027, candidates should understand the marking scheme. Candidates should prioritize accuracy, avoid guessing, and practice timed mock tests. A balanced strategy that combines preparation, careful question selection, and effective time management can help students improve their exam performance. Always confirm the MET 2027 marking rules through the official examination instructions.
author: Neha Sharma
meta_title: MET 2027 Negative Marking: Tips to Minimise Marks Loss

Applying on deadline day Portal crash, payment failure Apply minimum 3 days before closing date
Name mismatch with documents Rejected at document verification Match Aadhaar or Class 10 certificate exactly

Q: My payment was deducted but the form shows incomplete. What do I do?

A: Do not make a second payment. Wait 24 to 48 hours for automatic reconciliation. Log back in and check status. If still incomplete after 48 hours, contact official helpdesk with transaction ID, bank name and payment date and time.

Q: Is there a correction window after the deadline?

A: Yes. Most exam authorities open a correction window 1 to 3 weeks after the application deadline. Not all fields can be corrected - name and date of birth typically cannot. Monitor official website daily after the deadline closes.

title: Navigating 2026-27 Engineering and Medical Admissions: A State-Central Quota Coordination Playbook
description: A practical guide for students and families on how to coordinate state and central seat allocations for engineering and medical admissions in 2026-27, including timelines, counselling, and key decision points.
content:
Executive snapshot: why coordination matters in 2026-27

Engineering and medical admissions in India increasingly hinge on a coordinated approach between state authorities and central quangos. For applicants aiming to optimize options, understanding the sequencing of counselling rounds, seat matrices, and eligibility criteria is essential. This playbook offers a structured path to navigate the 2026-27 admission landscape with clarity on timelines, choice filling, and seat acceptance decisions.

Key timelines to map early

Two major admission tracks run in parallel: centralised counselling for certain national institutes and state-level processes for universities and colleges within each state. While the exact dates vary by year and institution, a typical pattern includes:

  • Pre-counselling registration windows for central institutes and state portals.
  • First round seat allocation based on merit lists and category reservations.
  • Closing of option forms and holding of mop-up rounds, if needed.
  • Document verification and fee payment within specified deadlines.

Students should monitor official portals starting a few weeks before the anticipated registration period and cross-check deadlines with the respective authorities. If there is any ambiguity, seek official guidance promptly to avoid missing windows that impact seat choices.

Understanding the two-track system

The admissions framework typically comprises:

  • Centralised tracks for national institutes and certain medical institutes that pool candidates across states. These often involve a common merit list and a unified counselling process.
  • State tracks for state and regional colleges, including engineering and medical institutions that reserve seats for residents of the state and for various categories.

Students usually receive offers from both tracks based on merit, often with options to participate in both streams. The crucial step is to understand the eligibility criteria and the reservation policies that apply to each track and how they interact during seat allotment.

Reservation categories and seat-sharing nuances

Reservation policies determine how seats are distributed. They vary by state and may include quotas for:

  • Home state residents
  • All-India and other central categories
  • Other backward classes, SC, ST, and economically weaker sections

Some institutes also have management or special category reservations. When filling options, consider how a change in category or a shift from state to central tracks could affect seat availability and fee structures. Always verify current policy details on official portals before final submission.

Choosing a strategy for stream and branch

Branches within engineering and medical tracks can drastically affect future study and career options. A practical approach:

  • List your top preferred branches and cities, then map them to the likelihood of admission within your rank range for each track.
  • Balance dream choices with safety options in both central and state streams.
  • Consider availability of internships, clinical exposure, or lab facilities that align with your interests.

In many cases, a broad set of options in the first rounds increases your chances of a satisfactory outcome in later rounds.

Document preparation and verification

Common documents include identity proofs, academic transcripts, category certificates, domicile proofs, and migration or transfer certificates where required. Start gathering these early and keep both digital and physical copies ready. Some authorities require notarised copies or attested documents; confirm requirements on official portals to avoid delays.

Fee structures and funding considerations

Central and state tracks may differ in tuition and fee structures. Some central institutes have higher tuition but offer robust financial aid if you qualify. State institutes may offer lower fees for residents but have limited scholarship pools. Plan for tuition, hostel, and exam-related costs, and explore scholarship opportunities and hostel allotments through the official portals or designated scholarship portals.

What to do in the lead-up to counselling

  • Prepare a ranked list of at least 10 electives across streams, with top choices clearly marked.
  • Keep track of merit lists and expected cutoff ranges for your category and home-state status.
  • Set up alerts on official portals for round notifications and seat allotment results.
  • Coordinate with schools or mentors to ensure your academic records are up to date.

Parents should help students maintain a calm decision-making process, particularly during stress-filled rounds where seat offers come with tight acceptance windows.

Post-allocation steps and contingency planning

Once a seat is offered, you will typically have a deadline to accept, pay fees, and report to the admitting college. If the offered seat does not meet expectations, you may be eligible for higher options in subsequent rounds. Maintain a backup plan by keeping track of alternate branches and campuses that align with your interests and financial considerations.

Tips for a coordinated family approach

  • Assign a family member to monitor official portals and note critical deadlines.
  • Discuss long-term goals with your child to align branch choice with career interests and geography.
  • Prepare budgetary estimates and potential accommodation needs early to avoid last-minute stress.

Where to verify official guidance

Because policies and deadlines can shift between cycles, rely on official government and university portals for the most accurate information. When in doubt, confirm details with the administering authority before acting on second-hand summaries.

Frequently asked questions

1. How do central and state admissions interact in 2026-27?

Central tracks and state tracks run in parallel with separate merit lists and counselling processes. Candidates may be offered seats from either track based on their rank and category. Always verify eligibility and deadlines on official portals for both tracks.

2. What should I consider when choosing a branch?

Balance personal interest, entrance indicators, future employability, and campus facilities. Consider internship opportunities, research labs, and geographic preferences when ranking options.

3. How soon should I submit option forms?

Submit within the stated windows. Late submissions can close out your chances for top choices and may limit seat availability in subsequent rounds.

4. What happens if I miss a round?

Most programs offer subsequent rounds or mop-up rounds. Keep alternate options ready and monitor notifications closely to maximize opportunities.

5. Do reserved category seats affect general category applicants?

Reservation policies allocate seats within defined categories. General category applicants should be aware of category-wise cutoffs and the impact of state quotas on seats in their home state and at central institutes.

Final note for 2026-27 admissions

Admitting authorities continually refine processes to improve transparency and access. A disciplined, informed approach that integrates both central and state pathways increases the likelihood of securing a seat in a preferred field. Stay organized, confirm details with official sources, and keep your options flexible as rounds unfold.

title: Financial Market Management Class 12: Chapter-wise Last Minute Revision for Exam
description: Prepare for Class 12 Financial Market Management exam with chapter-wise notes, key concepts, and last-minute revision tips.
content:
As the exam for the 1st April Class 12 Financial Market Management is near, it is important that all chapters are revised. The following is a chapter-wise guide for students to efficiently prepare and achieve good marks.

Chapter 1: Introduction to Financial Markets

Financial markets are platforms where financial instruments such as shares, bonds, and securities are bought and sold. They connect savers with investors and facilitate the smooth flow of funds in the economy.

Key Points:

  • Promote economic growth
  • Mobilize savings and investments
  • Ensure efficient allocation of resources

Chapter 2: Types of Financial Markets

Financial markets are classified as follows:

Money Market: It deals in short-term funds, i.e., funds for less than 1 year. The instruments of the money market are Treasury Bills, Commercial Papers, and Certificates of Deposit.

Capital Market: It deals in long-term funds. The instruments of the capital market are shares, debentures, and bonds. It helps companies in raising funds for expansion.

Chapter 3: Financial Instruments

Important financial instruments include:

  • Equity Shares: Ownership in a company and dividend rights
  • Preference Shares: Fixed dividend, priority in assets
  • Bonds & Debentures: Debt instruments with fixed returns
  • Mutual Funds: Pool investors’ money for diversified investment

Chapter 4: Financial Institutions

Financial institutions help markets function smoothly.

- Banks: Deposits, Loans
- Insurance Companies: Providing security against any financial loss
- Mutual Fund Companies: Professional Management of Financial Assets

They also offer investment advice, portfolio management, and risk management.

Chapter 5: Stock Exchange

A stock exchange is a marketplace for buying and selling securities.

Key Points:

- Transparency and liquidity are provided.
- The two main Indian stock markets are the NSE and BSE.
- guarantees ethical trading methods

Chapter 6: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India)

SEBI regulates the securities market.

Functions:

- Defend the interests of investors
- Control middlemen and stock exchanges
- Stop dishonest business practices

Chapter 7: Primary and Secondary Market

Primary Market: First-time issuance of securities, e.g., IPOs.
Secondary Market: Trading of existing securities provides liquidity to investors.

Chapter 8: Mutual Funds

Professionally managed pooled investments are called mutual funds. They enable small investors to effectively access financial markets and lower risk through diversification.

Chapter 9: Risk and Return

  • Higher risk → higher expected return
  • Diversification reduces risk
  • ROI formula: (Gain – Cost) ÷ Cost

Chapter 10: Role of Financial Markets

Financial markets guarantee effective resource distribution, foster capital formation, supply liquidity, and stimulate investments and savings for economic expansion.

Last Minute Tips

  • Revise all key definitions and differences (Money vs Capital Market)
  • Focus on SEBI’s functions and stock exchange operations
  • Practice numerical questions and ROI calculations
  • Stay calm and manage time effectively during the exam

Conclusion

Revision in a chapter-wise manner is useful in enabling students to better organize concepts and recall them during the 1st April exam. These key points and formulas can then be used confidently in attempting questions and scoring high marks in Financial Market Management.

title: AYUSH & Medical Allied Admissions 2026: State Domicile Cutoff Shifts and AYUSH Admissions Central Committees Rules
description: A comprehensive guide to AYUSH and Allied Medical Admissions 2026, exploring AACCC 15% All India Quota rules, 85% state domicile eligibility criteria, and shifting cutoff patterns for BAMS, BHMS, BUMS, and BSMS programs.
content:
Navigating medical admissions in India requires a clear understanding of seat distribution, counseling authorities, and state-level eligibility norms. For aspirants pursuing undergraduate courses in traditional and complementary medicine systems including Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery (BAMS), Bachelor of Homeopathic Medicine and Surgery (BHMS), Bachelor of Unani Medicine and Surgery (BUMS), and Bachelor of Siddha Medicine and Surgery (BSMS), the admission process relies on NEET UG scores processed through two primary channels: central counseling and state quota counseling.

Understanding Central AACCC vs State Quota Counseling

The Ayush Admissions Central Counseling Committee (AACCC), operating under the Ministry of Ayush, manages counseling for 15% of all undergraduate seats across Government and Government-aided colleges nationwide. Additionally, AACCC conducts 100% seat allotment for Deemed Universities, Central Universities (such as Banaras Hindu University), and National Institutes (including the National Institute of Ayurveda, Jaipur, and the All India Institute of Ayurveda).

The remaining 85% of seats in state government colleges and private institutions fall under the jurisdiction of the respective State Counseling Authorities. Understanding this division is critical for candidates strategic seat planning:

  • AACCC Central Pool: 15% All India Quota (AIQ) open to all NEET-qualified candidates across India without domicile restrictions.
  • State Quota Pool: 85% of government seats reserved strictly for state-domiciled candidates according to local reservation policies.
  • Deemed and Central Institutions: All seats filled via AACCC central counseling, with specific institutional eligibility rules applied.

State Domicile Rules for 85% Quota Admissions

State domicile regulations dictate eligibility for the 85% state quota in government AYUSH and allied medical colleges. While rules vary between states, standard criteria generally fall under three primary classifications:

1. Education-Based Domicile

Several states require candidates to have completed continuous schooling (typically Class 10 and Class 12) from recognized boards within the state boundaries. Candidates passing their qualifying exams from outside institutions are required to present native domicile certificates.

2. Parent Residence and Property Ownership

States often require candidates to prove that one or both parents have resided within the state for a continuous period ranging from 7 to 15 years. Valid documentation typically includes permanent residence certificates, land registry papers, or municipal voter records.

3. Open Category Rules for Private Colleges

Private AYUSH colleges in states like Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, and Haryana frequently reserve a portion of non-domicile management seats for candidates from across India. However, state government seats in private institutions remain strictly reserved for local domicile candidates.

Cutoff Shifts in AYUSH and Allied Medical Programs

In recent years, cutoff ranks for BAMS and BHMS admissions have shown significant upward movement. Several structural factors contribute to these shifts across central and state counseling rounds:

  • Increased Demand for Integrative Health: Growing institutional backing and career prospects in government health sectors have elevated candidate interest in BAMS and allied programs.
  • Centralized Registration Tightening: AACCC guidelines restricting candidates who hold seats in state round 2 from participating in central mop-up rounds prevent seat blocking, leading to realistic cutoff movements in final counseling phases.
  • Dynamic State Merit Lists: State merit cutoffs vary based on local applicant volume, state board result distributions, and changes in reservation categories.

Step-by-Step Counseling Strategy for Applicants

To maximize admission chances across both AACCC central pool and state quota seats, candidates should adopt a systematic approach:

  1. Verify NEET Qualification: Ensure your percentile meets the minimum qualifying cutoff specified for your category (UR/EWS/OBC/SC/ST).
  2. Register on AACCC Portal: Complete mandatory registration for 15% AIQ and Central/Deemed seats on the official AACCC portal when counseling windows open.
  3. Monitor State Portal Releases: Register separately on your home state medical admission portal for 85% quota counseling.
  4. Check Domicile Validity: Prepare native resident certificates, revenue officer endorsements, and continuous school certificates well in advance of document verification schedules.
  5. Maintain Informed Choice Filling: Arrange choices based on clinical exposure, faculty reputation, attached hospital bed capacity, and past year closing ranks rather than college location alone.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the role of AACCC in AYUSH admissions?

AACCC conducts centralized NEET UG counseling for 15% All India Quota seats in government AYUSH colleges, 100% seats in Deemed Universities, Central Universities, and National Institutes across India.

Can candidates without state domicile apply for private AYUSH college seats?

Yes, several states allow non-domicile candidates to apply for management quota seats in private AYUSH colleges, though state quota seats in those same colleges remain reserved for local residents.

What programs fall under AYUSH and Allied Medical admissions?

AYUSH programs include BAMS (Ayurveda), BHMS (Homeopathy), BUMS (Unani), and BSMS (Siddha). Allied admissions also cover programs such as Bachelor of Naturopathy and Yogic Sciences (BNYS).

How do state domicile rules impact BAMS cutoff ranks?

State domicile rules limit the applicant pool for 85% state quota seats to local residents, which typically results in lower closing rank cutoffs compared to the competitive 15% All India Quota managed by AACCC.

title: Karnataka PGCET 2026 Result Date: Rank Card Expected Soon at cetonline.karnataka.gov.in
description: Get the latest analytical forecast on the Karnataka PGCET 2026 result date, step-by-step instructions to download your rank card, tie-breaker rules, and counselling insights.
content:
The Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA) is expected to declare the Karnataka PGCET 2026 Result shortly on its official website. Candidates who appeared for the state-level entrance exam for admission into MBA, MCA, MTech, and MArch programmes will soon be able to access and download their official rank cards online.

To check the scorecard, candidates must log in to the official portal using their unique registration number. This article provides an analytical forecast of the declaration timeline, step-by-step instructions to download the rank card, and key information regarding what follows the results.

Quick Answer: Karnataka PGCET 2026 Result Status

  • Official Portal: cetonline.karnataka.gov.in
  • Expected Result Release: Shortly (Expected in August 2026 based on live trackers and previous trends)
  • Credentials Required: PGCET 2026 Registration Number
  • Programs Covered: Postgraduate courses including MBA, MCA, MTech, and MArch across Karnataka colleges

Key Facts: Karnataka PGCET 2026

Before diving into the analytical forecast, here is a summary of the essential facts regarding the exam and result declaration process:

ParametersDetails
Exam Conducting BodyKarnataka Examinations Authority (KEA)Exam NameKarnataka Post Graduate Common Entrance Test (PGCET)
Exam FrequencyOnce a year
Courses OfferedMBA, MCA, MTech, ME, MArch
Official Websitecetonline.karnataka.gov.in / kea.kar.nic.in
Result Declaration ModeOnline (Through candidate login portal)

Analytical Forecast: When will the Karnataka PGCET 2026 Result be Released?

Historically, KEA releases the postgraduate common entrance test results within 3 to 4 weeks after the exam is successfully conducted and the provisional answer key objection window is closed. For the academic year 2026, educational trackers and competitor portals have reported active preparations by KEA to publish the results shortly.

The evaluation of answer sheets and resolution of candidates objections on the provisional answer key are in their final stages. Based on historical trends of other state-level exams such as the Karnataka Common Entrance Test, the postgraduate rank lists are typically released in the afternoon or evening on the specified declaration day. Candidates are advised to keep their exam hall ticket handy, as the registration number printed on it is mandatory to unlock the scorecard.

How to Download Karnataka PGCET 2026 Rank Card

Once KEA activates the direct link, candidates can follow these straightforward steps to check their scores and obtain their rank cards:

  1. Visit the Official Website: Open a web browser and go to the official Karnataka Examinations Authority website at cetonline.karnataka.gov.in/kea/.
  2. Navigate to Latest Announcements: Locate the 'Latest Announcements' or 'Admission' section on the homepage.
  3. Click the Result Link: Click on the link titled 'Karnataka PGCET 2026 Result / Rank Card'.
  4. Enter Credentials: Input your PGCET 2026 registration number in the designated field. Double-check the characters to prevent login errors.
  5. Submit and View: Click the 'Submit' button. Your sectional scores, overall marks, and state ranks will appear on the screen.
  6. Print and Save: Download the scorecard PDF and print multiple physical copies. These will be mandatory during physical document verification.

Understanding Score Normalization and Tie-Breaker Criteria

When the Karnataka Post Graduate Common Entrance Test is conducted in multiple sessions, KEA applies a normalization process to ensure fair grading across varying difficulty levels. The final merit lists and ranks are prepared using this normalized score system.

In the event that two or more candidates secure identical marks, KEA employs specific tie-breaking rules to assign ranks:

  • For MBA/MCA: If scores are equal, preference is given to the candidate with higher marks in the qualifying undergraduate degree. If a tie persists, the age of the candidate is considered, and the older candidate is awarded the better rank.
  • For MTech/MArch: The academic performance in the relevant engineering or architecture branch is analyzed. GATE-qualified candidates are generally given separate priority during the initial merit list preparation before local PGCET-only ranks are finalised.

What Happens After the Karnataka PGCET Result?

The release of the rank cards marks the beginning of the centralized counseling process. Candidates who obtain a qualifying rank will be invited to participate in the document verification process. Depending on official instructions, this may be conducted online or at designated physical help centres across the state.

Key documents required for verification include:

  • Karnataka PGCET 2026 Rank Card and Hall Ticket
  • Class 10 (SSLC) and Class 12 (2nd PUC) Marks Sheets
  • Degree Semester Marks Cards and Degree Certificate (or Provisional Degree Certificate)
  • Study Certificate signed by the Block Education Officer (BEO) to prove domicile requirements
  • Income and Caste Certificate (if claiming reservations under specific categories)

After successful verification, candidates will receive a secret key to log in and participate in option entry. Through the option entry portal, students can prioritize their choice of top institutes in the state, such as Karnataka College of Management (KCM), Bangalore for management courses, or other prominent state institutions.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

1. Will the Karnataka PGCET 2026 result be sent by post?

No. KEA does not send hard copies of scorecards or rank cards to candidates via post. Scorecards can only be downloaded online from the official website cetonline.karnataka.gov.in.

2. Can I apply for re-evaluation of my PGCET answers?

Since the evaluation process is highly computerized and the answer key objection window is provided prior to the results, KEA does not allow re-evaluation or re-totalling of papers after the final rank card is published.

3. What if there is an error in my PGCET rank card?

If you notice discrepancies in your name, registration number, or category listed on your downloaded rank card, you must contact KEA helpdesk immediately before the counseling registration closes.

4. Are GATE-qualified candidates required to check PGCET results?

Candidates with valid GATE scores who applied for admission are assigned separate ranks. They must verify their details through the GATE rank list links provided on the official website.

title: CTET September 2026 Extended Registration Guide: Subject Combination Rules, Fee Deadlines, and Exam Center Selection
description: Essential guide to CTET September 2026 extended registration, detailed subject combination rules, fee deadlines, and exam center allocation advice for candidates.
content:
Overview of CTET September 2026 Extended Registration

The Central Board of Secondary Education conducts the Central Teacher Eligibility Test to benchmark the quality of educators entering government and private schools across India. Following requests from applicant communities and educational institutes, the registration window for the CTET September 2026 examination has been extended. This extra time allows candidates to carefully verify their personal details, review qualifications, and accurately select subject combinations before submitting their final application.

Passing CTET is a mandatory requirement for teaching positions in central government institutions such as Kendriya Vidyalayas, Navodaya Vidyalayas, and schools under tribal welfare departments. It is also recognized by many state governments and private schools nationwide. Applicants must make full use of this extended timeline to ensure all submission steps are completed without technical errors.

Key Fee Payment Deadlines and Schedule

Completing the application form is only the first part of the process. Your application remains incomplete until the prescribed examination fee is successfully credited to the board account. Candidates must monitor the payment reconciliation status immediately after transaction completion.

  • Online Registration Extension: Applicants can fill out candidate details and upload documents up to the extended cutoff date announced on the portal.
  • Fee Payment Cutoff: Online payment gates remain active through debit cards, credit cards, or net banking up to the published deadline.
  • Final Confirmation Page Download: The confirmation page generates only after successful fee verification. Download and save multiple copies for your records.

If your account gets debited but the portal shows payment pending, allow up to 24 to 48 hours for automatic reconciliation. If the status does not change, contact the official CTET helpdesk promptly with your transaction reference number.

Detailed Subject Combination Rules for Paper 1 and Paper 2

Selecting the appropriate paper and subject combination is critical because your teaching eligibility depends on matching your educational background with your chosen test paper.

Paper 1: Primary Stage (Classes I to V)

Paper 1 evaluates candidates planning to teach primary classes. It consists of five compulsory sections: Child Development and Pedagogy, Language I, Language II, Mathematics, and Environmental Studies. Candidates must select two distinct languages from the offered options. Language I should ideally be the medium in which you intend to teach, while Language II tests secondary communication skills.

Paper 2: Elementary Stage (Classes VI to VIII)

Paper 2 is meant for candidates targeting upper primary teaching roles. The core structure includes Child Development and Pedagogy, Language I, and Language II. The primary choice comes in the main subject domain:

  • Mathematics and Science: Designed for candidates with a Bachelor of Science (B.Sc.), B.Tech, or equivalent background with relevant coursework in mathematics or natural sciences.
  • Social Studies / Social Science: Designed for candidates with a Bachelor of Arts (B.A.), Bachelor of Commerce (B.Com), or humanities degrees.
  • Other Subject Graduates: Applicants holding professional degrees or non-traditional combinations must select either Mathematics/Science or Social Studies depending on their graduation coursework and teaching goals.

Ensure that your language choices in Language I and Language II do not overlap. Selecting the same language for both papers will result in rejection during application processing or validation stages.

Selecting Exam Center Preferences Wisely

CBSE allocates exam centers on a first-come, first-served basis according to capacity limits across cities. Candidates who complete their application and fee payment early receive priority when preferred exam cities are assigned.

Tips for Choosing Test Centers

  • Choose Nearest Cities First: List your home district or adjacent major cities as your top choices to minimize travel hassles on exam day.
  • Check Seat Availability: The online portal displays real-time availability of exam seats in selected cities. If your first choice is full, select the next closest alternative immediately.
  • Plan Ahead for Logistics: Consider local transport facilities, lodging options, and travel times when selecting backup cities.

Once assigned in the final hall ticket, exam city allocations are rarely changed by the board, except under severe administrative requirements.

Step-by-Step Guide to Complete Extended Registration

  1. Visit the Official Portal: Access the official CTET website and navigate to the September 2026 application link.
  2. New Registration: Fill in basic details including name, date of birth, mobile number, and email address to generate your application number.
  3. Fill Application Form: Input academic credentials, teaching diploma/degree details, and select your paper preference (Paper 1, Paper 2, or Both).
  4. Select Subject Combination & Languages: Carefully choose your main subject for Paper 2 and select unique choices for Language I and Language II.
  5. Upload Documents: Upload clear scanned copies of your recent passport-sized photograph and signature strictly as per prescribed dimensions and file sizes.
  6. Pay Examination Fee: Complete the transaction using available digital payment modes.
  7. Save Confirmation Page: Print and store the generated confirmation page safely. This serves as proof of valid submission.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Can I apply for both Paper 1 and Paper 2 together?

Yes. Candidates who meet the eligibility criteria for both primary and upper primary levels can apply for both papers in a single application form by paying the combined examination fee.

What should I do if my payment fails but money is debited?

Wait for automated bank reconciliation within 24 to 48 hours. If the confirmation page is still not generated, contact the board support desk with payment proof before the registration deadline closes.

Can I change my subject combination after submitting the form?

Changes are only allowed during the official correction window provided by CBSE. After the correction window closes, no further requests for changing papers, subject combinations, or languages will be entertained.

How are exam centers allocated if my preferred city is full?

If seat capacity in your preferred city is exhausted, the portal will prompt you to choose an alternative available city. Early submission increases the likelihood of getting your top city choice.

description: BVP CET 2027 ಗಡುವು ಕೋರ್ಸ್‌ಗೆ ಅನುಗುಣವಾಗಿ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. BTech, BBA/BCA, ಕಾನೂನು, ನರ್ಸಿಂಗ್ ಮತ್ತು ಸ್ನಾತಕೋತ್ತರ ಕೋರ್ಸ್‌ಗಳ ಅಧಿಕೃತ ದಿನಾಂಕಗಳನ್ನು ತಿಳಿಯಿರಿ.
content:
ಭಾರತಿ ವಿದ್ಯಾಪೀಠವು 2027-28ರ ಪದವಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸ್ನಾತಕೋತ್ತರ CETಗಳಿಗೆ ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕ ವೇಳಾಪಟ್ಟಿಗಳನ್ನು ಬಿಡುಗಡೆ ಮಾಡಿದೆ. ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಕೋರ್ಸ್‌ಗಳಿಗೂ ಒಂದೇ ಅರ್ಜಿ ಗಡುವು ಇಲ್ಲ. ಎಂಜಿನಿಯರಿಂಗ್, ಮ್ಯಾನೇಜ್‌ಮೆಂಟ್, ಕಾನೂನು, ನರ್ಸಿಂಗ್ ಅಭ್ಯರ್ಥಿಗಳು ಅಧಿಕೃತ ದಾಖಲೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ತಮ್ಮ ಕೋರ್ಸ್‌ನ ಸರಿಯಾದ ಸಾಲು ನೋಡಬೇಕು.

ಕ್ಯಾಲೆಂಡರ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಗುರುತಿಸಬೇಕಾದ ದಿನಾಂಕಗಳು

ಕೆಳಗೆ ಎರಡು ಅಧಿಕೃತ ವೇಳಾಪಟ್ಟಿಗಳಿಂದ ಆಯ್ದ ಕೋರ್ಸ್‌ಗಳಿವೆ. ಎಲ್ಲ ದಿನಾಂಕಗಳು 2027ಕ್ಕೆ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸಿವೆ. ಫಲಿತಾಂಶದ ದಿನಾಂಕ ನಿಗದಿತ ವೇಳಾಪಟ್ಟಿ ಮಾತ್ರ; ಫಲಿತಾಂಶ ಈಗಾಗಲೇ ಬಿಡುಗಡೆಯಾಗಿದೆ ಎಂದಲ್ಲ.

ಭಾರತಿ ವಿದ್ಯಾಪೀಠದ 2027-28 ಪದವಿ CET ವೇಳಾಪಟ್ಟಿ, 27 ಅಕ್ಟೋಬರ್ 2026 ಆವೃತ್ತಿ. ಅಧಿಕೃತ ಪದವಿ PDF

ಹೋಲುವ ಹೆಸರಿನ ಕೋರ್ಸ್‌ಗಳ ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಮಾರ್ಗ ಬೇರೆ

ಮೊದಲ ವರ್ಷದ BTech ಹಾಗೂ ನೇರ ಎರಡನೇ ವರ್ಷದ BTech ಗಡುವು ಬೇರೆ. ಎರಡನೇ ವರ್ಷದ ಪ್ರವೇಶಕ್ಕೆ ಅರ್ಜಿ ಗಡುವು 14 ಜೂನ್, ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ 19 ಜೂನ್. ಐದು ವರ್ಷದ ಸಮಗ್ರ ಕಾನೂನು ಕೋರ್ಸ್ ಮತ್ತು ಮೂರು ವರ್ಷದ LLBಗೂ ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕ ವೇಳಾಪಟ್ಟಿಗಳಿವೆ.

ಪೂರ್ಣ PDF ಉಳಿಸಿಕೊಂಡು ನಿಖರ ಕೋರ್ಸ್ ಹೆಸರು, ಪರೀಕ್ಷಾ ಕೋಡ್ ಗುರುತಿಸಿ. ಎರಡು ಕೋರ್ಸ್ ಆಯ್ಕೆ ಮಾಡಿದರೆ ಪರೀಕ್ಷಾ ದಿನಾಂಕಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ದಿನಕ್ಕೆ ಬರುತ್ತವೆಯೇ ನೋಡಿ. ವೇಳಾಪಟ್ಟಿ ಇರುವುದೇ ನಿಮ್ಮ ಅರ್ಹತೆಯ ದೃಢೀಕರಣವಲ್ಲ.

ಕೌನ್ಸೆಲಿಂಗ್ ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕ ಮುಂದಿನ ಹಂತ

BTech ಎಂಜಿನಿಯರಿಂಗ್ ಕೌನ್ಸೆಲಿಂಗ್ 16ರಿಂದ 19 ಜೂನ್, BBA/BCAಗೆ 14 ಮತ್ತು 15 ಜೂನ್, BMAT ಗುಂಪಿಗೆ 3 ಮೇ ನಿಗದಿಯಾಗಿದೆ. ಇವು ಭವಿಷ್ಯದ ಹಂತಗಳು. ಫಲಿತಾಂಶ ಅಥವಾ ಸೀಟು ಹಂಚಿಕೆ ಈಗಾಗಲೇ ಲಭ್ಯವಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಭಾವಿಸಬೇಡಿ.

ಮೂರು ವರ್ಷದ LLBಯ ಅನುದಾನಿತ ವಿಭಾಗಕ್ಕೆ 14 ಜೂನ್, ಅನುದಾನರಹಿತ ವಿಭಾಗಕ್ಕೆ 23 ಜೂನ್ ಕೌನ್ಸೆಲಿಂಗ್ ಇದೆ. ಸ್ಥಳ, ದಾಖಲೆ ಮತ್ತು ವರದಿ ಮಾಡುವ ನಿಯಮಗಳಿಗೆ ಕೋರ್ಸ್‌ನ ಮುಂದಿನ ಅಧಿಕೃತ ಸೂಚನೆಗಳನ್ನು ಓದಿ.

ಅರ್ಜಿ ಸಲ್ಲಿಸುವ ಮೊದಲು ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ

ವಿಶ್ವವಿದ್ಯಾಲಯದ ವೆಬ್‌ಸೈಟ್‌ನಿಂದ ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಲಿಂಕ್ ತೆರೆಯಿರಿ. ದಿನಾಂಕಗಳಿಗೆ ಅಧಿಕೃತ PDF ಬಳಸಿ, ಅರ್ಜಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸರಿಯಾದ ಕೋರ್ಸ್ ಹಾಗೂ 2027 ಪ್ರವೇಶ ವರ್ಷವಿದೆಯೇ ಖಚಿತಪಡಿಸಿ. ಬೇರೊಂದು ಕೋರ್ಸ್‌ನ ದಿನಾಂಕ ನಿಮ್ಮ ಅರ್ಜಿಗೆ ಅನ್ವಯಿಸಬೇಡಿ.

ಸಂಬಂಧಿತ ಕೈಪಿಡಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ವಿಷಯಗಳು, ಅಂಕಗಳ ಅರ್ಹತೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪಾವತಿಸಬೇಕಾದ ಶುಲ್ಕ ಓದಿ. ಒಂದು ಕೋರ್ಸ್‌ನ ನಿಯಮ ಇನ್ನೊಂದಕ್ಕೆ ಅನ್ವಯಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಸಲ್ಲಿಸಿದ ಅರ್ಜಿ, ಪಾವತಿ ದೃಢೀಕರಣ ಉಳಿಸಿ; ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ ಮತ್ತು ಕೌನ್ಸೆಲಿಂಗ್‌ಗೆ ಮೊದಲು ಪರಿಷ್ಕೃತ ಸೂಚನೆಗಳನ್ನು ನೋಡಿ.

title: RRB Group D Result 2026 Update: No Results Before April 15 Amid Ongoing Court Case
description: RRB Group D Result 2026 is delayed due to a court case. Check the latest update, the next hearing date (April 15), and the expected result timeline.
content:
Due to the legal proceedings that are still going on, there have been delays in releasing the RRB Group D Result 2026, causing anxiety amongst the candidates. The latest information regarding the result has stated that the result will only be released after April 15, 2026.

Why is the RRB Group D Result Delayed?

The reason for the delay is that there is an ongoing court case concerning the recruitment process. Matters pertaining to selection and some rules have made it necessary for the results to be put on hold until a conclusion is reached by the court.

Next Hearing Date: April 15

The next hearing for the case is to take place on April 15, 2026. Once this deadline expires, it might become apparent when the verdict will be announced. If the injunction is not upheld, the results might be disclosed soon after that.

Impact on Recruitment Process

In addition, this postponement has had an impact on the next phases of the recruitment process. For instance, the Physical Efficiency Test (PET) that comes after the written test will also have to be put off.

Key Highlights

Particulars Details
Exam Name RRB Group D 2026
Conducting Body Railway Recruitment Board (RRB)
Result Status Delayed
Reason for Delay Ongoing Court Case
Next Hearing Date April 15, 2026
Official Website https://www.rrbcdg.gov.in

Final Update

The candidates should remain informed through official notifications and have their login credentials handy. The final verdict that follows the court case is very important for the determination of the result date.

title: WBCHSE সেমেস্টার ব্যবস্থা: নতুন নির্দেশ পর্যন্ত বর্তমান পরিকল্পনা মেনে চলুন
description: সেমেস্টার বাতিলের প্রযোজ্য সরকারি আদেশ প্রতিষ্ঠিত হয়নি। WBCHSE-র বর্তমান পরিকল্পনা মেনে নিজের পরীক্ষার্থী বিভাগ স্কুল থেকে নিশ্চিত করুন।
content:
পশ্চিমবঙ্গের উচ্চমাধ্যমিক পড়ুয়াদের WBCHSE আনুষ্ঠানিক পরিবর্তন না আনা পর্যন্ত প্রযোজ্য সেমেস্টার পরিকল্পনা চালিয়ে যাওয়া উচিত। সেমেস্টার ব্যবস্থা বাতিলের সরকারি আদেশ প্রতিষ্ঠিত হয়নি। কাউন্সিলের বর্তমান বার্ষিক কর্মপরিকল্পনায় একাদশ শ্রেণির সেমেস্টার II এবং দ্বাদশ শ্রেণির সেমেস্টার IV এখনও আছে।

আলোচনা মানেই প্রস্তুতি বদলানোর নির্দেশ নয়

অনিশ্চিত খবরের কারণে সেমেস্টারের কাজ বাদ দেবেন না বা বার্ষিক পরীক্ষার প্রস্তুতিতে চলে যাবেন না। কাউন্সিলের সরকারি বিজ্ঞপ্তি দেখে স্কুলে নিজের সিলেবাস ও পরীক্ষার্থী বিভাগ জেনে নিন। পরিবর্তনে প্রভাবিত শ্রেণি, বছর ও নতুন ব্যবস্থায় যাওয়ার নির্দেশ স্পষ্ট থাকা দরকার।

স্কুলের মাধ্যমে হওয়া ধাপগুলি পরিকল্পনায় রাখুন

বার্ষিক কর্মপরিকল্পনা দ্বাদশ শ্রেণির সেমেস্টার IV ক্লাস অক্টোবর 2026 থেকে দেখায়। স্কুল-পরিচালিত এনরোলমেন্ট, অ্যাডমিট কার্ড ও ব্যবহারিক ধাপ থিয়োরির রুটিন থেকে আলাদা। কাউন্সিল জানিয়ে তারিখ বদলানোর অধিকার রাখে।

এই তথ্য দিয়ে স্কুলে জিজ্ঞাসার প্রশ্ন তৈরি করুন। এনরোলমেন্ট তথ্য ঠিক কি না, কোন ব্যবহারিক বা প্রজেক্ট কাজ বাকি এবং চূড়ান্ত ব্যবস্থা কীভাবে জানানো হবে, তা নিশ্চিত করুন। কর্মপরিকল্পনা বিষয়ভিত্তিক থিয়োরির রুটিনের বিকল্প নয়।

সেমেস্টার ও পুরনো সিলেবাসের বিজ্ঞপ্তি মেশাবেন না

কাউন্সিলের পরিকল্পনায় সেমেস্টার IV, সেমেস্টার III সাপ্লিমেন্টারি এবং পুরনো সিলেবাসের উচ্চমাধ্যমিক পরীক্ষা আলাদা আছে। একটি বিভাগের বিজ্ঞপ্তি স্বয়ংক্রিয়ভাবে অন্য বিভাগে প্রযোজ্য ধরে নেবেন না।

থিয়োরির তারিখের জন্য সরকারি রুটিন বিভাগে শিরোনাম সাবধানে পড়ুন। কর্মপরিকল্পনা বিস্তারিত পরীক্ষার সূচি আলাদা বিজ্ঞপ্তির ওপর ছেড়েছে। প্রযোজ্য রুটিন পাওয়া পর্যন্ত অনুমান করা তারিখ পাকা যাতায়াত বা রিভিশন সূচিতে রাখবেন না।

সেমেস্টার IV পরিকল্পনা নির্দেশিকা আলাদা সূচিগুলির পটভূমি দেয়। বর্তমান সিলেবাস পড়তে থাকার পাশাপাশি নিজের বিভাগ এবং স্কুলের বাকি কাজ নিশ্চিত করাই এখন দরকারি পদক্ষেপ।

title: Maharashtra NEET UG 2026 CAP Round 1 Physical Joining: Original Document Retention and Security Deposit Terms
description: Comprehensive guide to Maharashtra NEET UG 2026 CAP Round 1 physical joining, detailing original document retention rules, fee payment, and security deposit forfeiture terms.
content:
Following the publication of the seat allotment result for Maharashtra NEET UG 2026 CAP Round 1, candidates allotted seats in medical and dental colleges across the state must proceed with the physical joining process. Completing the reporting phase within the stipulated timeline is mandatory to confirm admission. Candidates and parents must carefully navigate the verification of original documents, fee payment procedures, and security deposit retention rules enforced by the State Common Entrance Test Cell (CET Cell), Maharashtra.

Overview of Physical Joining for Maharashtra NEET UG 2026

Physical joining requires candidates to visit the allotted institute in person with all required original certificates, self-attested photocopies, and the prescribed admission fees. Failing to report within the designated schedule results in automatic cancellation of the allotted seat, rendering the candidate ineligible for subsequent regular CAP rounds under specific condition rules.

Upon reaching the institute, college authorities perform an intensive physical verification of all academic, reservation, and identity credentials before granting provisional admission.

Original Document Verification and Retention Rules

One of the crucial aspects of the reporting process is the mandatory submission of original documents. In accordance with the guidelines set by the CET Cell and the Maharashtra University of Health Sciences (MUHS), the allotted college retains all original certificates until the candidate completes the course or formally withdraws under sanctioned resignation terms.

Mandatory Documents Required at Admission

  • NEET UG 2026 Admit Card and Score Card
  • Aadhaar Card or valid photo identity proof
  • Class 10 (SSC) Passing Certificate and Marksheet
  • Class 12 (HSC) Marksheet and Passing Certificate
  • Domicile Certificate issued by the competent authority in Maharashtra
  • Nationality Certificate or valid Indian Passport
  • Category Certificate, Caste Validity Certificate, and Non-Creamy Layer Certificate (if applicable)
  • College Leaving Certificate / Transfer Certificate
  • Medical Fitness Certificate (as per prescribed CET Cell format)
  • Migration Certificate (for candidates from non-State boards)

Rules Regarding Original Document Retention

Colleges hold the candidate's original documents for verification by the university and regulatory councils. To avoid inconvenience during the academic year, candidates are advised to keep multiple scanned copies and physical photocopies of all certificates before handing them over to the college administration.

If a candidate upgrades to another institution in subsequent CAP rounds, the current institute must issue a retention certificate and release the original documents immediately upon presentation of the new allotment letter.

Security Deposit Terms and Fee Payment Rules

To secure a seat during physical reporting, candidates must pay the requisite tuition and institutional fees alongside complying with security deposit terms.

Tuition Fee Payment Guidelines

Fees must be paid strictly via Demand Draft (DD) or online payment modes specified by the respective college. Cash payments are generally not accepted. Candidates claiming fee concessions under reserved categories must present valid supporting documents during verification.

Security Deposit Forfeiture and Retention Conditions

The state counseling body imposes strict security deposit rules to prevent non-genuine candidates from holding seats unnecessarily. Key rules include:

  • Retention after Joining: If a candidate joins the allotted seat in CAP Round 1 and submits the Status Retention Form, the security deposit is adjusted against institute fees or refunded at the end of the counseling cycle.
  • Resignation Penalty: Resigning from an allotted seat after the prescribed cutoff date leads to forfeiture of the security deposit and potential liability to pay college penalty fees depending on the round.
  • Free Exit Provision: Candidates who are allotted a seat in CAP Round 1 but choose not to report can exit without forfeiting their deposit, depending on the specific round guidelines issued by the CET Cell for that academic session. Always verify exact exit rules on the official CET Cell portal.

Step-by-Step Procedure at the Allotted College

  1. Reporting: Arrive at the allotted institute within the specified date and time window.
  2. Document Verification: Present original documents along with two sets of self-attested photocopies to the college scrutiny committee.
  3. Fee Payment: Submit the tuition fee demand draft and obtain an official fee receipt.
  4. Status Retention Option: Decide whether to submit the Status Retention Form to lock the seat or refrain from submitting it to remain eligible for an upgrade in CAP Round 2.
  5. Confirmation Receipt: Collect the official admission selection letter and document retention receipt signed by the institute head.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do colleges keep original certificates during Maharashtra NEET UG admission?

Yes, allotted colleges retain all original documents during the physical reporting phase for university verification until admission is finalized or upgraded.

What happens if I do not report for physical joining in CAP Round 1?

Failing to report results in the cancellation of the allotted seat. Check the official portal to confirm eligibility for subsequent rounds based on current exit rules.

Can I upgrade my seat in CAP Round 2 after joining in Round 1?

Yes, candidates who physically join in Round 1 without filling out the Status Retention Form remain eligible for an upgrade in CAP Round 2.

How is the admission fee paid during physical reporting?

Fees are typically paid using a Demand Draft drawn in favor of the allotted institute or through approved online payment portals.

When is the security deposit forfeited in Maharashtra NEET UG counseling?

The security deposit is forfeited if a candidate holding a seat resigns beyond the permissible deadline or violates resignation rules set by the CET Cell.

What is a Document Retention Certificate?

It is an official acknowledgement issued by the college listing all original documents submitted by the student at the time of physical reporting.

content:
CUET UG 2025 Exam Dates Announced – Exam to Be Held from May 8 to June 1

The National Testing Agency (NTA) has officially announced the exam window for the Common University Entrance Test (CUET) UG 2025. According to the notification, the CUET UG 2025 exam will be held between May 8 and June 1, 2025, across various test centers in India and abroad.

The detailed schedule, including exam dates, subject-wise distribution, and shift timings, will soon be made available on the official NTA CUET website. Candidates are advised to regularly check the portal for updates.

CUET UG 2025 – Key Highlights

Detail Information
Exam Name CUET UG 2025
Conducting Body National Testing Agency (NTA)
Exam Window May 8 to June 1, 2025
Mode of Exam Computer-Based Test (CBT)
Official Website nta.ac.in
 

About CUET UG 2025

The Common University Entrance Test (CUET) for Undergraduate programs (UG) is a centralized entrance test introduced by the University Grants Commission (UGC) and conducted by NTA. It aims to streamline the admission process for central, state, private, and deemed universities across India.

CUET UG enables students to apply to multiple universities using a single entrance exam score, making the process transparent, efficient, and student-friendly.

CUET UG 2025 Exam Format

  • Mode of Exam: Computer-Based Test (CBT)

  • Question Type: Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs)

  • Sections: Language, Domain-Specific Subjects, and General Test

  • Duration: Varies by subject and slot

  • Marking Scheme: +5 for correct answer, -1 for wrong answer

Important Instructions

  • The exact date and shift timing for each candidate will be mentioned in their admit card.

  • Students must carry a valid photo ID proof along with the admit card to the exam center.

Final Thoughts

With CUET UG 2025 scheduled from May 8 to June 1, candidates must begin revising and preparing their subject-wise strategies. Stay connected with the official CUET portals for city slips, admit cards, and schedule updates. CUET UG continues to be a game-changer for undergraduate admissions in India, giving students a fair and uniform platform to showcase their academic potential.

title: NEET MDS 2026 রাউন্ড 3: কলেজে যাওয়ার আগে চূড়ান্ত ফল দেখুন
description: MCC-এর অস্থায়ী তালিকা ভর্তি নিশ্চিত করে না। 30 অক্টোবরের বিজ্ঞপ্তি পড়ুন এবং বরাদ্দ কলেজে যাওয়ার আগে চূড়ান্ত ফল যাচাই করুন।
content:
NEET MDS 2026 তৃতীয় রাউন্ডের অস্থায়ী তালিকায় আসন দেখালেই বরাদ্দ চূড়ান্ত হয় না। MCC-এর 30 অক্টোবরের বিজ্ঞপ্তি অনুযায়ী, চূড়ান্ত ফল প্রকাশের পরেই বরাদ্দ কলেজে যোগাযোগ করতে হবে। রিপোর্টিংয়ের জন্য রওনা দেওয়ার আগে ফলের ধরন দেখুন।

অস্থায়ী তালিকার অর্থ কী?

MCC জানিয়েছে, তালিকাটি নির্দেশক এবং পরিবর্তন হতে পারে। এতে দেখানো আসনের উপর প্রার্থীর অধিকার তৈরি হয় না। তাই অস্থায়ী নথির স্ক্রিনশট চূড়ান্ত বরাদ্দ বা পরবর্তী ভর্তির নির্দেশের বিকল্প নয়।

মেডিক্যাল কাউন্সেলিং কমিটির 30 অক্টোবর 2026-এর বিজ্ঞপ্তি। MCC-এর মূল বিজ্ঞপ্তি পড়ুন.

অসংগতি জানানোর সময়সীমা শেষ

প্রার্থীর লগইনের Candidates Grievances And Query Redressal System-এর মাধ্যমে 31 অক্টোবর 2026 সকাল 10টা পর্যন্ত অসংগতি জানানোর সুযোগ ছিল। সেই সময়সীমা শেষ হয়েছে। ইমেল, নতুন অভিযোগ বা খবরের শিরোনাম দেখে সময় বেড়েছে ধরে নেবেন না। আগে অভিযোগ জানিয়ে থাকলে প্রাপ্তিস্বীকার সংরক্ষণ করুন এবং লগইনে পাওয়া উত্তর অনুসরণ করুন।

এবার চূড়ান্ত ফল যাচাই করুন

  1. MCC-এর MDS কাউন্সেলিং পেজে তৃতীয় রাউন্ডের ফলের পুরো নাম পড়ুন। বর্তমানে যুক্ত বিজ্ঞপ্তিটি অস্থায়ী ফলের।

  2. MCC চূড়ান্ত ফল প্রকাশ করলে পুরনো স্ক্রিনশটের উপর নির্ভর না করে নিজের তথ্য আবার মিলিয়ে নিন।

  3. তারপর যাত্রা বা ভর্তি ফি দেওয়ার আগে বর্তমান রিপোর্টিং নির্দেশ এবং বরাদ্দ প্রতিষ্ঠানের প্রয়োজনীয়তা পড়ুন।

MCC-এর MDS কাউন্সেলিং পেজ

আবেদনের তথ্য, সংরক্ষিত পছন্দ এবং অভিযোগের প্রাপ্তিস্বীকার একসঙ্গে রাখুন। আগের রাউন্ড 3 রেজিস্ট্রেশন গাইডটি পূর্ববর্তী ধাপ বোঝায়; রেজিস্ট্রেশনের তারিখ থেকে বরাদ্দ চূড়ান্ত হওয়ার নিশ্চয়তা মেলে না।

title: DU ET 2026 admissions 2026 counselling timeline central state portals detailed
description: Understand the DU ET 2026 admissions process, counselling timeline, and how to use central and state portals for a smooth admission journey for Indian students and parents.
content:
What you gain from this article

This guide outlines the DU ET 2026 admissions process, the counselling timeline, and how to navigate central and state portals. It helps students and parents anticipate key dates, prepare documents, and compare counselling options across central and state channels.

Overview of DU ET 2026 admissions

Key dates and the counselling timeline

  • Application window: The admission cycle typically opens a few weeks after the release of the entrance results. Prepare to submit the application form within the allotted timeframe, including fee payment and document uploads.
  • Entrance result release: Results for DU ET 2026 are announced on the official portal. Candidates should download scorecards and note their subject-wise marks, rank, and category.
  • First round counselling: Central and/or state portals may initiate allotment rounds. Candidates must register for counselling, select preferred courses and colleges, and pay counselling fees if required.
  • Document verification: During counselling, applicants may need to present identity proofs, educational transcripts, category certificates, and reservation documents where applicable.
  • Seat allotment and reporting: After seat allotment, candidates must report to the allotted college within the given deadline, complete admission formalities, and pay any remaining fees.
  • Subsequent rounds: If seats remain, additional rounds or mop-up rounds may be conducted. Stay alert to portals for new allotments and deadlines.

Central portal vs state portals: which path applies?

DU admissions are routed through a combination of central and state-level portals depending on the course, category, and jurisdiction. Here is a practical way to approach the process:

  • Central portal: Used for unified registration, common counselling, and seat allotment for many DU programmes. It consolidates application data and streamlines shortlisting across affiliated colleges.
  • State portals: Some states operate their own counselling portals for special admissions, management quota seats, or regional tie-ups. For applicants in states with specific DU tie-ins or reserved seats, check the state portal instructions for eligibility and timelines.
  • Documentation: Regardless of the path, maintain copies of mark sheets, identity proofs, category certificates, migration certificates if applicable, and receipts of all payments. Original documents are typically required at the reporting stage to the allotted college.
  • Channel coordination: If you receive a seat through the central process but belong to a state quota, follow the college’s guidance on merging or transferring that seat if permitted by the rules.

Documents you’ll typically need

  • Class 12 or qualifying exam mark sheet and certificate
  • DU ET 2026 result card or score report
  • Identity proof (Aadhaar, passport, etc.)
  • Category certificate (if applicable)
  • Migration certificate (if required by the college)
  • Entrance test admit card (if mandated for counselling)
  • Passport-sized photographs and signature

Strategy for a smooth counselling experience

  • Monitor portals daily: Keep an eye on the central counselling portal and any state portals that may apply to your region or course.
  • Prioritise courses and colleges: List programs in order of preference with realistic cutoffs and seat availability based on past trends.
  • Prepare backup options: Have a second and third-choice plan in case your first choice seat is not allotted in early rounds.
  • Verify eligibility before choices: Ensure your eligibility criteria align with the selected course to avoid disqualification at a later stage.
  • Complete verification promptly: When called for document verification, attend on time with all originals and photocopies to prevent delays.

How to use central and state portals effectively

Follow these steps to navigate the process efficiently:

  1. Register on the central counselling portal if your chosen programmes require it.
  2. Fill in education details carefully and upload scanned documents in the requested format.
  3. Check the list of participating colleges and courses for the current admission cycle.
  4. Submit choices in order of preference, then confirm and pay the required counselling fee if applicable.
  5. For state portals, follow the state-required steps, which may include separate registration, choice locking, and fee payment.
  6. Track seat allotment results on the respective portal and report to the allotted college if selected.

Common questions about DU ET 2026 admissions

Question 1: When will the DU ET 2026 counselling start?

Counselling typically begins after the entrance results are announced. Exact dates are published on the official portal and participating state portals. Check notifications regularly and set reminders for deadlines.

Question 2: Do I need to pay counselling fees?

Many counselling processes require a non-refundable counselling or registration fee. Fees vary by portal and category. Confirm the exact amount on the official site and complete the payment within the stated window.

Question 3: Can I change my course or college after seat allotment?

Sometimes a window allows changes within the same round or in subsequent rounds. Rules differ by portal and programme. Review the guidelines on the portal and act before the indicated deadlines.

Question 4: What if I don’t get a seat in the first round?

Keep your options open by choosing backup courses and colleges. Remaining seats are typically allocated in later rounds or mop-up rounds. Stay updated via the portal notifications.

Question 5: How can I verify my documents before reporting?

Cross-check the required documents list on the official portal. Ensure all copies are clear, legible, and match the information in your application. Originals are checked during reporting to the college.

Question 6: Is it possible to apply through both central and state portals?

In some cases, applicants may engage with both, but this depends on programme rules and jurisdiction. Follow the official instructions for your chosen course and region to avoid duplication or conflicts.

What to do next

Review your shortlisted courses, create a realistic plan of action for the counselling rounds, and ensure you have all required documents ready. For official timelines and detailed instructions, rely on the published notices on the appropriate central and state portals. If you have confusions about eligibility or seat allotment rules, contact the designated helplines or college admission desks for clarification.

Note on accuracy

Timelines, eligibility, and portal processes can vary by year and jurisdiction. Always verify details on the official admission portals and the relevant college websites before acting on any information. This article provides a practical framework to approach DU ET 2026 admissions and counselling with a clear action plan.

title: Uttarakhand Exam Scams 2025 - Ongoing Protests & UKSSSC Paper Leak Updates
description: The UKSSSC exam scams 2025 in Uttarakhand sparked widespread protests following an alleged paper leak. This blog covers the incident, arrests, government response, and preparation tips for aspirants.
content:
A significant scandal burst in Uttarakhand in September 2025 following a purported paper leak during the graduate-level test administered by the Uttarakhand Senior Services Selection Commission (UKSSSC). The state saw massive demonstrations after the leak, which happened just 30 minutes before the exam started. Candidates have called for a CBI inquiry, the exam to be canceled, and the perpetrators to face adverse effects.

The Incident

Three pages of the test were shot and shared on social media as part of the leak. Khalid Malik, the primary suspect, allegedly climbed a rear wall to get inside the testing facility, got past security, and concealed a cell phone in his socks. His sister submitted the exam pages to an assistant professor in Tehri after he took a picture of them in a restroom. The study, which revealed significant security flaws, traveled swiftly.

Arrests and Investigation

  1. Khalid Malik first eluded authorities before being taken into custody.
  2. Due to their suspected roles, his sister and an assistant professor are also detained.
  3. Concerns regarding exam security were raised when investigations showed that CCTV cameras inside exam halls were turned off and that mobile jammers were not placed in every room.

Timeline of Events

 

Date Event Action Taken
Sep 10, 2025 UKSSSC exam begins Paper leak occurs within 30 minutes
Sep 11, 2025 Leak spreads on social media Public outrage increases
Sep 12, 2025 Khalid Malik arrested Sister & assistant professor taken into custody
Sep 13–14, 2025 Protests in Dehradun Delegation meets CM Pushkar Singh Dhami; investigation promised

Protests and Government Response

Mass protests were sparked by the leak in Dehradun and other Uttarakhand cities. The Uttarakhand Berozgar Sangh and other groups led the protesters, who called for changes to the exam procedure and accountability. A comprehensive inquiry will be conducted, and anybody found guilty would face severe consequences, Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami promised. nevertheless, student organizations are still demanding a CBI investigation to guarantee complete openness.

Conclusion

Serious questions about the accuracy of Uttarakhand's recruitment exams are brought to light by the UKSSSC exam scandals and ongoing protests. Aspirants continue to seek transparency despite the actions taken by authorities. The verdict in this instance could establish a standard for the state's handling of any future exam violations.
