That is a calendar comparison, not a guaranteed preparation break. Count only the clear days between your own registered papers. Put other examinations into the calendar first, then choose realistic revision sessions and a timed practice slot matching the duration of this paper.

Before travelling to the examination centre

The start time is not an arrival deadline. Read the admit-card instructions for reporting, entry and the documents you need. If the school shares a revised CBSE notice, compare its class, code and date before changing your calendar. Do not infer a new date from a social-media headline.

CBSE says important instructions will be issued separately and students must follow the admit card. Communication devices are not allowed inside the examination centre. Check the instructions for permitted materials before packing your bag.

title: CAT 2026 Registration Checklist: Documents, Certificate Formats, and Fee Details
description: Prepare for CAT 2026 registration starting August 3, 2026. Get the complete checklist of required documents, scan specifications, certificate formats, and application fee details.
content:
Quick Answer

The registration process for the Common Admission Test (CAT) 2026 begins on August 3, 2026. Conducted by IIM Indore, the exam is scheduled for November 29, 2026. To complete your application smoothly, you must upload scanned copies of your passport-size photograph, signature, and category or PwD certificates (if applicable). The CAT 2026 registration fee is Rs 2,700 for General, OBC, and EWS candidates. Candidates are advised to keep their academic marksheets (Class 10, Class 12, and Graduation) and valid government-approved ID proofs ready before starting the online application.

Key Facts for CAT 2026 Registration

Before diving into the detailed document checklist, here is a quick overview of the essential dates, conducting body, and fee structures for CAT 2026:

Event / Parameter Details
Conducting Authority Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Indore
Registration Start Date August 3, 2026
CAT 2026 Exam Date November 29, 2026
General / OBC / EWS Fee Rs 2,700
SC / ST / PwD Fee To be updated on the official website (usually 50% of the standard fee)
Official Website iimcat.ac.in

Comprehensive CAT 2026 Registration Documents Checklist

To avoid last-minute errors or application rejection, candidates must compile and verify their academic and personal records. The following documents are essential for completing the application:

1. Personal and Identification Documents

  • Valid Email ID and Mobile Number: Ensure these remain active until the entire selection process is complete, as all official communications will be sent here.
  • Government-Approved Photo ID: Aadhaar Card, Passport, Voter ID, PAN Card, or Driving License. Keep a scanned copy handy for reference.

2. Image and Signature Specifications

The exam authorities require strictly defined specifications for uploading photos and signatures. Failing to meet these dimensional and format criteria might prevent form submission:

  • Passport-Size Photograph: Must be a recent color photograph, ideally not older than six months. It should have a white or light-coloured background. The format must be JPG or JPEG.
  • Scanned Signature: Sign on a clean sheet of white paper using a blue or black ink pen. Scan the signature and crop it to the required dimensions in JPG or JPEG format.

3. Academic History Details

You do not need to upload your high school or college graduation degree certificates during the initial registration. However, you must enter precise marks. Keep these documents ready for manual entry:

  • Class 10 / SSC / Equivalent Marksheet (Roll number, board name, year of passing, and aggregate percentage).
  • Class 12 / HSC / Equivalent Marksheet (Stream, board name, year of passing, and aggregate percentage).
  • Bachelor's Degree Marksheet / Cumulative GPA (Degree name, university, duration of the course, status of completion, and marks obtained).
  • Master's Degree and Professional Degrees (CA, CS, ICWA, etc.) if applicable.

4. Category and Disability Certificates

Candidates applying under reserved quotas must download the official certificate templates from the CAT website, get them signed by competent authorities, and upload them as PDFs:

  • SC/ST Certificates: Must be issued by an authorized government body.
  • OBC-NCL Certificate: Ensure the certificate is valid for the current financial year and complies with the central government format.
  • EWS Certificate: Income and asset certificate issued by a competent authority, valid for the financial year.
  • PwD Certificate: Mandatory for candidates seeking reservation under the Persons with Benchmark Disability category, specifying the percentage of disability.

Step-by-Step Guidance to Fill the CAT 2026 Application Form

Follow these structured steps to ensure an error-free registration once the portal goes live on August 3:

  1. New Candidate Registration: Go to the official website and click on 'New Candidate Registration'. Fill in your name, date of birth, email address, mobile number, and country. Generate an OTP to verify your credentials. A unique User ID and Password will be sent to your registered email and mobile number.
  2. Log in and Access Application Form: Log in using the received credentials and select 'Go to Application Form'. The form is divided into sections: Personal Details, Academics, Work Experience, Programmes, Test City, and Payment.
  3. Fill Academics & Work Experience: Carefully enter your marks across Class 10, Class 12, and Graduation. If you have full-time professional experience post-graduation, calculate and enter the exact number of months. Part-time or internship experience is generally not considered.
  4. Select Programmes and IIMs: Choose the post-graduate programmes you wish to apply for across various IIMs. Select your preferred interview cities for each selected program.
  5. Upload Documents: Upload your passport photograph, signature, and category certificates in the designated slots. Ensure the file sizes conform to the portal's limits.
  6. Select Test Cities: You will have the option to choose up to six preferred test cities. The allocation is usually done based on availability and preference order.
  7. Online Payment: Pay the registration fee using credit cards, debit cards, net banking, or UPI. Download the payment confirmation receipt and save a PDF copy of your completed application form.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

What is the starting date for CAT 2026 registration?

The online registration portal opens on August 3, 2026. Candidates can apply online through the official portal at iimcat.ac.in.

Can I edit my academic marks after submitting the application?

No, candidates cannot change their core academic details once the application fee is paid and the form is submitted. While a short correction window is provided later, it is usually limited to correcting uploaded photographs, signatures, and test city preferences. Double-check all entries before final payment.

What is the registration fee for General and Reserved category students?

The registration fee is Rs 2,700 for General, OBC, and EWS candidates. Candidates belonging to SC, ST, and PwD categories typically receive a relaxed fee structure, details of which will be finalized in the official notification.

Which IIM is conducting the CAT exam in 2026?

IIM Indore is the conducting authority for the CAT 2026 exam, scheduled to take place on November 29, 2026.

Can final-year graduation students apply for CAT 2026?

Yes, candidates in their final year of graduation or those awaiting results can apply. They must provide their aggregate marks up to the pre-final semester during registration.

title: DU, JNU, and BHU 2026–27 admissions: key steps and timelines
description: A practical timeline and step-by-step checklist for Indian students and parents navigating DU, JNU, and BHU admissions for 2026–27, with important dates, eligibility notes, and preparation guidance.
content:
Make the Right Start: understand the 2026-27 admission landscape

For prospective undergraduates and research entrants, DU, JNU, and BHU offer diverse programs across arts, sciences, commerce, and professional streams. The 2026-27 admission cycle emphasizes centralised application windows for many courses and department-specific deadlines for others. Start by identifying your target programs, eligibility criteria, and the official application portals. Keep in mind that each university may publish separate notices for entrance tests, counseling, and seat allotment. Always verify dates on the official authority sites as timelines may shift due to regulatory updates or exam schedules.

Identify programs and eligibility early

  • DU: Focus on undergraduate honors programs, professional courses, and select vocational degrees. Eligibility typically requires a qualifying senior secondary examination with minimum marks specified by each college or program. Some courses may require a common entrance or merit-based selection within the college framework.
  • JNU: Primarily known for humanities, social sciences, and international studies at the undergraduate and postgraduate levels. Entrance testing and/or merit-based shortlisting govern many programs, with some departments hosting their own assessments.
  • BHU: Offers integrated and single-degree programs across arts, science, commerce, and professional streams. Admission may involve entrance tests or merit-based shortlisting, depending on the faculty and course type.

Step-by-step admissions timeline

Note: Always cross-check dates on the official university portals. The following timeline reflects common patterns observed in recent cycles and may vary by program.

  1. August-September - Program selection and eligibility review: Compile your class 12 or qualifying exam marks, subject requirements, and any necessary migration or category documents. Prepare necessary identification and contact details for the application portal.
  2. October - Application window opens: Submit applications for DU, JNU, and BHU where applicable. Upload scanned documents such as mark sheets, identity proof, and passport-sized photographs. Some programs require payment of application fees and selection test opt-in.
  3. November - Entrance tests and merit lists: Many courses announce test schedules or announce that merit-based lists will be released. Register for tests if required and prepare for potential online or offline exams.
  4. December - Result declarations and first cutoffs: Universities publish first admission lists or cutoffs. Shortlisted candidates should verify their eligibility and proceed with admission formalities in a limited window.
  5. January-February - Counseling and document verification: The central counselling or college-level processes begin. You may need to present original documents for verification, pay fees, and finalize seat allocation. Watch for any additional rounds or waitlists.
  6. March - Final admissions: Confirm seats, submit original documents if required, and complete any campus registration or orientation steps for the new academic year.

Documentation and preparation checklist

  • Mark sheets and passing certificates from the qualifying exam
  • Identity proof (Aadhaar, passport, or other government ID)
  • Address proof and category certificates if applicable
  • Passport-sized photographs as required by each portal
  • Migration certificate if transferring from another board or university
  • Entrance test admit cards or scores, if required by specific programs
  • Provisional seat allotment letters and fee payment receipts

Financial planning and scholarships

Tuition and associated costs differ across DU, JNU, and BHU. Students should budget for tuition, hostel, and mess charges where applicable. Look for eligibility criteria and deadlines for scholarships, merit-based waivers, and government student aid schemes. Many universities publish information on scholarships for reserved categories, merit excellence, or need-based assistance. Prepare required income or domicile documentation if applying for financial support.

Tips for competitive programs

  • Prioritize programs with clear entrance timelines and documented cutoff patterns to avoid last-minute confusion.
  • Maintain a ready set of scanned documents to expedite the application process across portals.
  • Keep several backup choices within each university to increase admission chances in case a preferred course is unavailable.
  • Set reminders for deadlines and regularly monitor official notices for any schedule changes.

Common questions about DU, JNU, and BHU admissions 2026-27

What is the typical application window for these universities?

Most undergraduate programs open applications in October and close within a few weeks. Some departments may have separate windows or require tests before shortlisting. Always confirm on the official site of each university.

Do all programs require entrance tests?

No. Many programs rely on merit based on qualifying exam marks, while others, especially in humanities and social sciences, may require a department level entrance or combined selection criteria. Check the specific course page for details.

How many rounds of seat allocation are typical?

Admission processes often include one or more rounds of seat allotment, followed by document verification and fee payment. Some years see additional rounds or waitlists depending on intake and vacancies.

What documents are essential at verification?

Carry original documents along with photocopies of mark sheets, identity proof, category certificates if applicable, migration certificate if transferring, and proof of address. Some universities may require scanned copies uploaded during application too.

Can I apply to multiple universities in the same cycle?

Yes. You can submit separate applications to DU, JNU, and BHU, ensuring you meet each program’s eligibility criteria and deadlines. Monitor each portal independently for status updates.

What should I do if I miss a deadline?

Missing a deadline often leads to losing the chance to participate in the current admission cycle. Some programs offer a late or special round, but these are not universal. Check official notices immediately for any late admission windows.

Decision time: choosing the right program

Beyond rankings, consider faculty strength, research opportunities, internship avenues, campus life, and the geographic location. If you aim for postgraduate studies or research, programs at JNU and BHU may offer robust opportunities in specific disciplines. For broad-based programs and accessible campus facilities, DU colleges provide a wide range of options. Compare the course structure, credit requirements, and language of instruction to align with your long-term goals.

What to verify on official portals

Timelines and eligibility criteria can shift due to policy changes or exam date modifications. Before acting on any information, confirm the latest notices, required documents, and specific steps on the official university websites or their admitted student portals. If any detail remains unclear, contact the university’s admission office for clarification.

Frequently asked questions

1) When should I start preparing for the admission cycle?

Begin by gathering the essential documents and identifying target programs at least two to three months before applications open. Create a checklist with deadlines to stay organized.

2) How many programs should I apply to across these universities?

Consider applying to 3-6 programs across the three institutions to balance risk and coverage, depending on your merit and interests. Prioritize a mix of safety, target, and challenging options.

3) What is the role of entrance tests in JNU and BHU?

Some courses require department-level tests or combined assessments. If your chosen program demands a test, plan study time and register within the specified window.

4) How should I handle scholarships and fee waivers?

Look for government and university-specific scholarship details early. Prepare income proofs and category certificates if you may qualify for financial support. Apply within the scholarship deadlines if required.

Bottom line

Admitting to DU, JNU, or BHU in 2026-27 hinges on early program selection, timely applications, and a clear plan for document verification and counseling. With careful preparation, you can navigate the admission process efficiently, maximize your chances, and begin the next phase of your academic journey with confidence.

title: BTech Placement Claims: Five Questions Parents Should Ask Colleges
description: Before paying BTech fees, ask five evidence-based questions about batch size, placement eligibility, median salary, recruiters and refund terms.
content:
A high BTech package can make a college look affordable before you check who actually received it. Before paying admission fees, ask for five things in writing: the graduating batch size, placement eligibility, median salary, recruiter-level hiring details and refund conditions. These answers show whether the promise covers most students or only a small group.

Use the replies while you compare colleges. A counsellor’s verbal assurance won’t help much after the payment deadline.

How large was the graduating BTech batch?

Ask for the total batch strength, branch-wise if available, along with the number of students placed and the number who received the advertised top package. A single high offer can look impressive while representing very few students. Request the placement report for the same campus and graduating year. Don’t compare a university-wide figure with one branch without checking what it includes.

Who could actually sit for placements?

“Placement percentage” has no meaning until you know the denominator. Ask whether backlogs, attendance shortages, unpaid dues, branch restrictions or other conditions removed students from campus drives. Also ask how the college counted students who chose higher studies, entrepreneurship or off-campus work.

  • Total students in the graduating BTech batch
  • Students allowed to participate
  • Students receiving at least one offer
  • Students still seeking work when the season ended

Placement assistance isn’t the same as a job offer.

What was the median salary?

Ask for the median, not only the highest package, and ask how many offers were included. The median is the middle salary in an arranged list, so one unusually high offer has less effect. Check whether the figure separates fixed pay, variable pay, joining bonuses and stock benefits.

Compare that median with four-year tuition, hostel and compulsory charges. The decision should rest on the typical outcome, not the poster headline.

Which recruiters hired, and for how many roles?

Request recruiter names, role titles, hiring numbers, work locations, eligible branches and the graduating batch involved. A company logo doesn’t prove that it hired many students. While you explore courses, check whether the advertised roles fit your branch. Software roles may accept several branches; core engineering openings can be narrower.

What happens if you withdraw?

Get the fee schedule, cancellation rule, refund timeline and non-refundable items in writing. Ask whether the college or an affiliated university controls the refund, and whether hostel, training or caution money is handled separately. Save the brochure, offer letter, receipts and written replies.

If the college avoids a basic data request, treat that response as decision information. Placement claims deserve documents before admission, not explanations after graduation.

title: JEE Main Maths Coordinate Geometry: Core Strategy & Guide
description: A comprehensive preparation guide focusing on the Coordinate Geometry unit for the JEE Main Mathematics paper. Explore high-yield topics like conic sections, straight lines, circles, and standard tangent equations, along with actionable strategies and tracking methods to secure maximum marks in the 2027 engineering entrance exam.
content:
For engineering aspirants targeting the Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) Main 2027, the Mathematics section is often the most time-consuming and analytically demanding segment of the paper. However, within this rigorous section lies a highly standardized and rewarding domain: Coordinate Geometry.

Unlike abstract calculus problems that may require obscure substitutions, Coordinate Geometry relies on fixed geometric principles, standard algebraic equations, and visual locus plotting. Conic Sections (Parabola, Ellipse, Hyperbola) form a predictable high-return block within the mathematics syllabus. Because the National Testing Agency (NTA) consistently tests these concepts heavily in both the multiple-choice and numerical value sections, mastering this unit is non-negotiable for securing a top percentile. This comprehensive guide breaks down the core syllabus, high-yield formulas, expected weightage, and the strategic preparation required to dominate Coordinate Geometry.

Core Syllabus Breakdown: What You Need to Master

Coordinate geometry requires absolute precision and spans a wide variety of interconnected shapes and systems. The syllabus is broadly divided into four progressive segments, each building algebraically upon the last.

Cartesian System and Straight Lines: This is the foundational bedrock of the unit. Coordinate geometry spans the Cartesian system, distance formulas, section formulas, locus, and shift of origin. You must be highly fluent in translating geometric conditions into algebraic equations. The study of straight lines includes slope, various forms of equations, the angle between lines, and concurrent lines. Mastering the calculation of the perpendicular distance of a point from a line and the equations of angle bisectors will save you critical minutes on exam day.

Circles: The circle is heavily tested, both as an independent concept and in combination with straight lines and other conics. The syllabus for circles covers standard and general equations, parametric forms, tangents, normals, intersecting circles, and common chords. The concept of the radical axis, the family of circles (circles passing through the intersection of a line and a circle, or two circles), and orthogonality conditions are frequent testing favorites.

Conic Sections (Parabola, Ellipse, Hyperbola): This segment is heavily formula-driven and highly analytical, focusing on standard equations, focus, directrix, eccentricity, tangents, and normal properties.

  • Parabola: You must master the standard forms, focal chords, and the parametric coordinates. Tangent and normal equations in slope form are practically guaranteed to appear.

  • Ellipse & Hyperbola: These two shapes are mathematically linked by their eccentricity values. You must memorize the standard equations, the length of the latus rectum, auxiliary circles, and director circles. Understanding the conjugate hyperbola and asymptotes will also provide a significant edge.

High-Yield Topics and Expected Weightage

To optimize your revision schedule, you must prioritize this unit heavily. Coordinate Geometry typically accounts for 15% to 20% of the entire mathematics paper, making it one of the largest standalone blocks outside of Calculus.

The table below outlines the core segments and their expected frequency in a standard JEE Main shift.

Core Segment

Key Focus Areas for Practice

Expected Questions

Conic Sections (Parabola, Ellipse, Hyperbola)

Focus, directrix, eccentricity, tangents, and normal properties.

2 - 3

Circles

Parametric forms, tangents, intersecting circles, common chords.

1 - 2

Straight Lines & Cartesian System

Distance formulas, locus, shift of origin, concurrent lines.

1 - 2

Candidates can reliably expect 4 to 6 questions from the combined Coordinate Geometry unit per shift, translating to a massive 16 to 24 marks.

Essential Formulas for Instant Recall

During the 180-minute computer-based test, deriving complex tangent conditions from scratch is a severe waste of time. Maintain a dedicated formula sheet and ensure the following relationships are memorized flawlessly:

Tactical Preparation and Execution Strategy

Securing marks in Coordinate Geometry requires a blend of rigorous algebraic discipline and spatial visualization.

  • Draw Rough Cartesian Sketches: Never attempt a locus, circle, or conic section problem without drawing a quick, rough sketch on your scratchpad. Visualizing the intersection of a line and a parabola, or the position of a focus relative to a directrix, prevents catastrophic setup errors and helps eliminate illogical MCQ options immediately.

  • Master Parametric Coordinates: Using parametric coordinates (like $(a\cos\theta, b\sin\theta)$ for an ellipse) drastically simplifies the algebra compared to using standard $(x, y)$ Cartesian variables, especially in questions involving tangents and normals.

  • Beware of Calculation Traps: Coordinate Geometry numericals frequently involve heavy algebraic expansions, quadratic equations, and complex roots. Ensure your calculation speed is flawless to avoid silly decimal or sign errors, as Section B carries a strict -1 negative marking penalty.

Conclusion

Mastering JEE Main Maths: Coordinate Geometry is an absolute strategic necessity for crossing the 99th percentile threshold. Because this block relies heavily on standard formulas and predictable tangent properties, it provides an incredible return on your invested study time. Conic Sections form a predictable high-return block, and mastering the analytical properties of tangents, normals, and common chords guarantees reliable marks. Maintain clean, disciplined calculations to avoid negative marking, meticulously track your progress, and secure these guaranteed 16 to 24 marks to build immense confidence on exam day.

title: NIC Scientific and Technical Assistant Recruitment 2026: GATE 2024-2026 Merit Selection without Written Exam
description: Explore the NIC Scientific and Technical Assistant Recruitment 2026 details. Learn about the GATE 2024-2026 merit selection without a written exam, eligibility criteria, application process, and career prospects.
content:
The National Informatics Centre (NIC) operates under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) to provide technology infrastructure and IT solutions to the Government of India. For candidates aspiring to build a secure career in central government IT services, the NIC Scientific and Technical Assistant Recruitment 2026 offers an exceptional avenue. This recruitment drive simplifies the selection pathway by leveraging valid GATE performance instead of conducting a separate written test.

Overview of NIC Recruitment 2026

Under this recruitment drive, NIC hires qualified engineering graduates and computer science professionals to fill positions such as Scientific Assistant and Technical Assistant across central departments. Candidates evaluated on their Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering (GATE) scores from 2024, 2025, or 2026 can apply directly for shortlisting.

ParametersKey Highlights
Recruiting BodyNational Informatics Centre (NIC / NIELIT)
Post NamesScientific Assistant, Technical Assistant
Selection ProcessGATE Score Merit (2024 to 2026) followed by Document Verification
Primary DisciplinesComputer Science, Information Technology, Electronics & Communication
Job LocationAcross India (NIC Headquarters and State Centers)

Eligibility Criteria and Educational Qualifications

Before filling out the online registration form, candidates must ensure they meet all prescribed educational requirements and age limits.

1. Academic Qualifications

  • Scientific Assistant: M.Sc. in Computer Science, MCA, or B.E./B.Tech in Computer Science, Information Technology, Electronics and Communication, or related technical disciplines from a recognized university.
  • Technical Assistant: Pass in B.E./B.Tech, B.Sc. (Computer Science/IT), or M.Sc./MCA in relevant engineering or science branches.

2. GATE Score Requirement

Applicants must possess a valid GATE score card in Computer Science and Information Technology (CS) or Electronics and Communication Engineering (EC) from GATE 2024, 2025, or 2026. Higher normalized marks improve shortlisting rank.

3. Age Limit

The standard upper age limit for general category candidates is usually 30 years. Government relaxation rules apply for reserved categories, including OBC, SC, ST, and PwD applicants.

Selection Process: Direct Merit Shortlisting

Unlike traditional public sector hiring processes that involve multi-tier written examinations, the current hiring process relies on GATE normalized scores.

  1. Initial Application Screening: Verification of submitted GATE score cards, educational degrees, and personal details.
  2. Merit List Generation: Candidates are ranked purely based on their GATE score in the respective paper.
  3. Document Verification: Shortlisted individuals are called to produce original certificates, GATE score cards, category documents, and identification proofs.
  4. Final Offer Letter: Issuance of appointment orders based on rank position, medical fitness, and background check verification.

Step-by-Step Online Application Process

Candidates must submit their applications through the designated portal specified in the official employment notification.

  • Visit the official portal at nic.in or nielit.gov.in.
  • Locate the recruitment section for Scientific and Technical Assistant posts.
  • Complete user registration with a valid email address and mobile number.
  • Enter your academic records and valid GATE registration details accurately.
  • Upload clear scanned copies of your photograph, signature, GATE score card, and category certificate.
  • Pay the prescribed application fee via online payment options if applicable.
  • Submit the final application form and save a printout for future reference.

Salary and Career Progression

title: CLAT 2027: അന്തിമ അപേക്ഷ, ഫീസ്, പണമടയ്ക്കുംമുമ്പുള്ള പരിശോധനകൾ
description: CLAT 2027 പൂർണ അപേക്ഷയും ഫീസും 2026 ഒക്ടോബർ 31 രാത്രി 11:59നകം സമർപ്പിക്കണം. UG ഫീസ്, പിന്നീട് മാറ്റാനാകാത്ത വിവരങ്ങൾ, രേഖാപരിശോധന അറിയാം.
content:
CLAT 2027 അപേക്ഷ പൂർണമായി പൂരിപ്പിച്ച് അന്തിമമായി സമർപ്പിക്കുന്നതും ഫീസ് അടയ്ക്കുന്നതും 2026 ഒക്ടോബർ 31 രാത്രി 11:59നകം പൂർത്തിയാകണം. ലോഗിൻ ഉണ്ടാക്കുന്നതോ ഫോമിന്റെ കുറച്ചു ഭാഗം പൂരിപ്പിക്കുന്നതോ മാത്രം പോരാ. പരീക്ഷ 2026 ഡിസംബർ 6നാണ് നിശ്ചയിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നത്; ആദ്യം അപേക്ഷ ശരിയായി പൂർത്തിയാക്കുക.

ഔദ്യോഗിക CLAT 2027 അപേക്ഷാ പോർട്ടൽ

പണമടയ്ക്കുംമുമ്പ് മൂന്ന് വിവരങ്ങൾ ഉറപ്പാക്കുക

UG അല്ലെങ്കിൽ PGയിൽ ഉദ്ദേശിക്കുന്ന പ്രോഗ്രാം തിരഞ്ഞെടുക്കുക. വിഭാഗവും BPL പ്രഖ്യാപനവും ഹാജരാക്കാനാകുന്ന രേഖകളുമായി ഒത്തുനോക്കുക. കുറഞ്ഞ ഫീസിനുവേണ്ടി മാത്രം വിഭാഗം തിരഞ്ഞെടുക്കരുത്. അപേക്ഷ സമർപ്പിച്ച് പണമടച്ചശേഷം പ്രോഗ്രാം, വിഭാഗം, BPL വിവരങ്ങൾ മാറ്റാനാകില്ല. അപേക്ഷ അവസാനിക്കുന്ന തീയതിക്കുശേഷം തിരുത്തലുകൾ സ്വീകരിക്കില്ല. പിന്നീട് തിരുത്താൻ അവസരം കിട്ടുമെന്ന് കരുതരുത്.

UG അപേക്ഷയ്ക്ക് വേണ്ട ഫീസ്

General/OBC അപേക്ഷാ ഫീസ് ₹4,000; SC/ST/BPL/PwD വിഭാഗങ്ങൾക്ക് ₹3,500. ബാങ്ക് ഇടപാട് ചാർജ് അധികമാണ്; പേയ്മെന്റ് പേജിൽ കാണിക്കും. അപേക്ഷാ ഫീസ് തിരികെ നൽകുകയോ മറ്റൊരു തുകയിലേക്ക് ക്രമീകരിക്കുകയോ ഇല്ല. മുൻവർഷ ചോദ്യപേപ്പറുകൾക്ക് പ്രത്യേകം ₹500; ഇത് അപേക്ഷാ ഫീസിൽ ഉൾപ്പെടുന്നില്ല.

ഔദ്യോഗിക പഴയ ചോദ്യപേപ്പറുകളുടെ വിലയും ലഭ്യതയും

പേരുകളും രേഖകളും ഒത്തുനോക്കുക

നിങ്ങളുടെയും മാതാപിതാക്കളുടെയും പേരുകൾ സർട്ടിഫിക്കറ്റുകൾ, മാർക്ക് ലിസ്റ്റ്, തിരിച്ചറിയൽ രേഖ എന്നിവയുമായി താരതമ്യം ചെയ്യുക. അക്ഷരങ്ങളും പേരുകളുടെ ക്രമവും പരിശോധിക്കുക. വ്യത്യാസങ്ങൾ പരീക്ഷാ യോഗ്യതയെയോ പ്രവേശനത്തെയോ ബാധിക്കാം. ലളിതമായ പശ്ചാത്തലത്തിൽ മുന്നിലേക്ക് നോക്കി എടുത്ത സമീപകാല പാസ്പോർട്ട് ഫോട്ടോ, ഒപ്പ്, ബാധകമായ വിഭാഗം, PwD അല്ലെങ്കിൽ BPL സർട്ടിഫിക്കറ്റ് തയ്യാറാക്കുക. അപ്‌ലോഡ് ഫോർമാറ്റിന് ഔദ്യോഗിക ഫോമിലെ നിർദേശങ്ങൾ പിന്തുടരുക.

അക്കൗണ്ടിൽ സമർപ്പണം ഉറപ്പാക്കുക

പുതിയ അപേക്ഷകർ ആദ്യം മൊബൈൽ നമ്പർ സ്ഥിരീകരിക്കണം. രജിസ്റ്റർ ചെയ്ത നമ്പറും പാസ്വേഡും ഉപയോഗിച്ച് കയറി എല്ലാ ഭാഗങ്ങളും, പ്രത്യേകിച്ച് പിന്നീട് മാറ്റാനാകാത്ത പ്രഖ്യാപനങ്ങളും വീണ്ടും വായിക്കുക. ഓൺലൈൻ പണമടച്ചശേഷം അക്കൗണ്ടിൽ മടങ്ങിയെത്തി പൂർണ അപേക്ഷ സമർപ്പിച്ചോ എന്ന് പരിശോധിക്കുക. അന്തിമ അപേക്ഷയും പണമടച്ച രസീതും സൂക്ഷിക്കുക. നില വ്യക്തമല്ലെങ്കിൽ ഔദ്യോഗിക പോർട്ടലിലെ ഹെൽപ് ഡെസ്കിനെ സമയമുണ്ടായിരിക്കെ സമീപിക്കുക. അപൂർണ അപേക്ഷ പരിഗണിക്കില്ല; പ്രഖ്യാപിക്കാത്ത സമയം നീട്ടലിനായി കാത്തിരിക്കരുത്.

title: NEET UG Reporting: What to Check Before You Pay and Join a College
description: A practical NEET UG counselling checklist for checking reporting proof, category documents, fee demands and seat details before you pay or join a medical college.
content:
An allotment in NEET UG counselling is not the same as a safe final decision. Before paying a large amount or handing over original documents, confirm the seat, fee demand, reporting status and category details in writing. A missing document or unclear receipt can cost you time, money or the chance to act in the next counselling stage.

Keep the allotment letter, application record and every message from the counselling authority together. The round instructions for your year and category control the final requirement, not a WhatsApp message from a broker or an informal promise at the college counter.

What should you verify at the reporting desk?

Ask the college to show how your allotted seat is recorded in its admission system. The course, college, academic year, seat type and category should match your allotment letter. If the staff says the seat has been changed, upgraded or converted, ask for the written rule and the authority’s approval before agreeing.

  • Take a signed or stamped reporting acknowledgement with your name, application number, course and reporting date.
  • Check whether the receipt identifies tuition fees, hostel charges, caution deposit, examination charges and any other amount separately.
  • Pay only through a traceable method and keep the transaction reference, fee receipt and a scanned copy.
  • Ask which documents the college is retaining and demand a written list of anything kept temporarily.

Documents can decide whether reporting is complete

Carry originals for inspection and several self-attested copies, but don’t surrender an original without an acknowledgement. Your NEET UG result or score record, allotment letter, identity proof, academic certificates, photographs and medical fitness papers may be checked. Category, disability, domicile, income or other claim-based documents need extra care because a mismatch can affect the seat itself.

Read every name, date of birth, category entry and certificate number. A spelling difference that looks minor at home can become a reporting objection at the college.

When should you pause payment?

Stop and ask for written clarity if the amount is higher than the published fee communication, the receipt is unavailable, the seat details differ, or staff pressure your family to pay immediately. A demand split across several personal accounts is another reason to wait and seek clarification from the responsible counselling authority.

For a wider decision, compare the allotted college with other options in our college comparison section. Before leaving the campus, save photographs of the notice board, receipt and acknowledgement. Small paperwork now protects your medical admissions decision later.

Find your Marketing and Sales entry in the PDF

The timetable entry is for Marketing and Sales under the code shown above. If your school record uses a different code or course name, ask the school to resolve that difference before following this date.

title: யுபி போர்டு தேர்வு மையப் பட்டியல் 2027: மாவட்ட PDF பார்ப்பது எப்படி?
description: 2027 யுபி போர்டு உத்தேச தேர்வு மையப் பட்டியலில் மாவட்டம், பள்ளியைத் தேடுவது எப்படி? ஆட்சேபனை காலக்கெடு மற்றும் நவம்பர் 6 நடவடிக்கையை அறியுங்கள்.
content:
யுபி போர்டின் 2027 மாவட்ட வாரியான தேர்வு மையப் பட்டியல் உத்தேசமானது. அதில் உள்ள இடத்தை இறுதி தேர்வு மையமாகக் கருதி பயணத்தைத் திட்டமிட வேண்டாம். சரியான மாவட்டத்தின் முழு PDF கோப்பைப் பார்த்து, ஒதுக்கீட்டை பள்ளியில் உறுதிப்படுத்துங்கள்.

உங்கள் மாவட்டத்திற்கான கோப்பைத் தேர்ந்தெடுக்கவும்

அதிகாரப்பூர்வ பட்டியலில் மாவட்டப் பெயர், குறியீடு, பதிவிறக்க இணைப்பு உள்ளன. ஆக்ரா 01, லக்னோ 34, பிரயாக்ராஜ் 55 என்பவை மாவட்டக் குறியீடுகள். பெயரையும் குறியீட்டையும் ஒப்பிடுங்கள்; அட்டவணையின் வரிசை எண் பள்ளிக் குறியீடு அல்ல.

அதிகாரப்பூர்வ மாவட்ட வாரியான உத்தேச பட்டியல்

முழு PDF கோப்பைப் பதிவிறக்கி பள்ளிப் பெயர் அல்லது குறியீட்டைத் தேடி, தொடர்புடைய முழுப் பதிவையும் படியுங்கள். ஸ்கேன் செய்யப்பட்ட கோப்பில் தேட முடியாவிட்டால் பள்ளி அலுவலகத்தின் உதவியைப் பெறுங்கள். பகிரப்பட்ட திரைப்பிடிப்பை மட்டும் நம்ப வேண்டாம்.

ஆட்சேபனை காலம் முடிந்த பிறகான நடவடிக்கை

26 அக்டோபர் 2026 அறிவிப்பின்படி காரணங்களும் ஆதாரங்களும் இணைந்த இணையவழி ஆட்சேபனைகளை 28 அக்டோபர் 2026 வரை அளிக்கலாம் என்றிருந்தது. அந்தக் காலம் முடிந்துவிட்டது; அதன் பிறகு ஆட்சேபனைகள் ஏற்கப்படாது என்று அறிவிப்பு கூறுகிறது. மாவட்டப் பள்ளி ஆய்வாளர்கள் அவற்றைப் பரிசீலித்து தீர்வு கண்டு, மாவட்டக் குழு ஒப்புதல் அளித்த அல்லது பரிந்துரைத்த பட்டியல் அறிக்கையை 6 நவம்பர் 2026க்குள் இணையத்தில் அனுப்ப வேண்டும்.

நவம்பர் 6 என்பது மாவட்ட அதிகாரிகள் அறிக்கை அனுப்பும் கடைசி நாள். அன்றே இறுதிப் பட்டியல் அல்லது அனுமதிச் சீட்டு வெளியாகும் என்ற அறிவிப்பு அல்ல. உத்தேச ஒதுக்கீட்டையும் இறுதி தேர்வு இடத்தையும் வேறுபடுத்திப் பாருங்கள்.

தேர்வு இடத்தை உறுதிப்படுத்தும் முன்

பதிவிறக்கிய கோப்பை வைத்திருந்து, பதிவிறக்கிய நேரத்தைக் குறித்துக் கொள்ளுங்கள். திருத்தப்பட்ட PDF வந்தால் உங்கள் பள்ளிப் பதிவை மீண்டும் ஒப்பிடுங்கள். பகிரப்பட்ட படத்தில் மாவட்டத் தலைப்பு, முக்கிய குறிப்புகள் அல்லது பிந்தைய மாற்றங்கள் விடுபட்டிருக்கலாம்.

பள்ளிப் பெயர், ஒதுக்கீடு அல்லது இடத்தில் சந்தேகம் இருந்தால் பள்ளியிடம் கேளுங்கள். காலக்கெடுவிற்குப் பிறகு அனுப்பும் செய்தி ஆட்சேபனை செயல்முறையை மீண்டும் திறக்காது. வாரியமும் பள்ளியும் வழங்கும் அடுத்த அறிவுறுத்தல்களைப் பின்பற்றுங்கள். இறுதி அனுமதிச் சீட்டில் முகவரியைப் பார்த்து மையத்தை உறுதிப்படுத்திய பிறகே பயண வழியைத் தேர்ந்தெடுங்கள். உத்தேச பட்டியல் தேர்வறை நுழைவு ஆவணம் அல்ல.

யுபி போர்டின் அடுத்த அறிவுறுத்தல்கள்

இந்தக் கட்டுரையை ஆங்கிலத்தில் படிக்கவும்

title: Top 5 Soft Skills Recruiters Want from College Graduates
description: Discover the top 5 soft skills that recruiters look for in college graduates. Learn how communication, teamwork, problem-solving, adaptability, and leadership can shape your career.
content:
Although you might get shortlisted for a job based on your grades, your soft skills are what really make you stand out in interviews. Today's recruiters are looking for graduates who can collaborate, communicate, and adjust to real-world situations in addition to technical expertise.

These are the top 5 soft talents that employers will be looking for in college graduates in 2025, so keep them in mind as you get ready for internships or campus placements.

1. Communication Skills

The foundation of any workplace is effective communication. Candidates that can effectively and clearly communicate their ideas are valued by recruiters, whether they are talking with colleagues, writing business emails, or presenting ideas.

  • Why it matters: Errors and delays can result from poor communication.
  • Join debate clubs, work on producing succinct articles or reports, and practice public speaking as ways to get better.

2. Teamwork & Collaboration

Teamwork is the lifeblood of most businesses. Graduates who can collaborate with a variety of groups, appreciate differing viewpoints, and support common objectives are preferred by recruiters.

  • Why it matters: A team player ensures a more efficient workflow and increases production.
  • Ways to get better include volunteering for student organizations, taking part in group projects, and learning how to handle conflict.

3. Problem-Solving Skills

Every employment role has its share of difficulties. Instead of waiting for directions, recruiters seek graduates who can assess problems and come up with workable solutions.

  • Why it matters: Managers are less stressed, time is saved, and value is added by problem-solvers.
  • How to get better: To hone your thinking, try case studies, riddles, or hackathons.

4. Adaptability

New positions, emerging technologies, and unforeseen difficulties are all part of the ever-evolving workplace. Candidates that are adaptable and willing to change are admired by recruiters.

  • Why it matters: Companies that have flexible workers are more competitive.
  • How to get better: Keep up with current developments, pick up new skills, and push yourself.

5. Leadership Skills

Leadership is more than just overseeing a group of people; it also entails accepting accountability, exercising initiative, and motivating others. Graduates who demonstrate leadership even at entry levels are valued by recruiters.

  • Why it matters: Leaders inspire others and advance projects.
  • How to get better: Plan student activities, lead group projects, and guide juniors.

Conclusion

Although having technical knowledge could help you get an interview, soft skills are more important for job advancement. Recruiters will remember you if you start honing these five skills: leadership, problem-solving, communication, teamwork, and flexibility.

title: A Practical, Region-Specific Admissions Calendar for MBBS, Engineering, and Law Across India 2026-27
description: A hands-on, region-aware timeline for MBBS, engineering, and law admissions in India for 2026-27, with month-by-month actions, state-by-state variations, and practical tips for students and parents.
content:
Overview: Why a regional view matters

India’s admissions landscape for MBBS, engineering, and law varies by state, university, and entrance exam pattern. A practical calendar that accounts for regional deadlines, counseling windows, and document submission timelines helps families avoid last-minute stress and missed seats. This guide consolidates typical timelines for 2026-27 and highlights region-specific nuances where they commonly occur.

General framework for MBBS admissions

MBBS admissions typically involve national and state-level eligibility checks, entrance results, and centralized or state-level counseling. The process often includes online application windows, document verification, choice filling, and seat allotment. While exact dates shift each year, the following structure remains a reliable reference for planning.

  • Qualifying exam result declaration: usually between May and July; plan for potential re-evaluation or revision windows in late July.
  • Application/registration for counseling: commonly opens in July or August, with varied closing dates by state or university.
  • Document verification and choice filling: typically August to September; ensure all required documents are prepared early.
  • Seat allotment rounds: multiple rounds span from August to September, with reporting and admission formalities following each round.

Engineering admissions: opening moves and regional pockets

Engineering admissions hinge on national entrance results, state-level engineering entrance tests, or university-based admissions. Regional differentiators include host state counseling portals, quota allocations, and special categories. A practical approach is to map the main routes you plan to pursue and align them with the state timelines.

  • National-level entrance results: plan for rank-based counseling to begin soon after results are announced, typically in July or August.
  • State-level exams and counseling: many states run separate rounds with distinct deadlines. Expect separate portals for registration, document verification, and seat allotment.
  • Institute-level admissions: some institutes conduct direct admissions or closing rounds; track notification portals for specific programs.

Law admissions: common tracks and regional differences

Law admissions may follow national entrance tests, state-level tests, or university-specific processes. The Common Law admission test and state entrance avenues are popular pathways, with counseling and seat allocation often coordinated by centralized portals. Regional differences can appear in eligibility criteria, reservation policies, and counseling timelines.

  • National or state entrance results: anticipate counseling windows within August and September.
  • Choice filling and verification: ensure documents are ready and uploaded correctly; regional variations may require additional local certificates.
  • Seat allotment: multiple rounds with reporting deadlines; final admission may require enrollment documentation and fee payment.

Constructing your regional calendar

To make the process less overwhelming, create a region-specific calendar that maps your preferred programs to the authorities that administer them in your state. Here are practical steps:

  • Identify your target pathways: MBBS through state and central medical councils, engineering through state counseling or national exams, law through state or national routes.
  • List key authorities by state: each state often has a dedicated counseling portal and a timetable that governs admissions for its institutions.
  • Copy exact dates from official portals: preserve the sequence of registration, document verification, choice filling, and seat allotment rounds.
  • Prepare documents early: identity proofs, academic certificates, domicile or residence proofs, and category certificates should be ready well before deadlines.
  • Set reminders for deadline clusters: admissions often have multiple deadlines clustered in August and September; avoid last-minute submissions.

Sample region-aware timeline (typical windows, dates vary by state)

Use this as a reference scaffold. Always verify with the official state or university portals for 2026-27 exact dates.

  1. June-July: verify eligibility criteria and gather required documents; monitor official announcements for merit lists or cutoffs.
  2. July-August: begin registration in your state/central counseling portal; start document verification processes if offered online.
  3. August: fill and update choices; ensure you meet any local eligibility checks or reservation requirements.
  4. September: seat allotment rounds and reporting; confirm admission with prescribed fee payments and original documents.
  5. October: if required, complete any lapsed formalities or migration/transfer processes for regional programs.

Region-specific tips for Indian students and parents

  • Prioritize regional options: many states reserve spots for local residents; including a mix of government and private institutes can increase your chances.
  • Track portal reliability: some portals experience heavy traffic during peak windows; have backups like printouts of essential documents and offline records.
  • Reserve category considerations early: if you belong to a reserved category, verify certificate validity, format, and submission deadlines to avoid disqualification.
  • Coordinate with the school careers counselor: they can provide state-specific guidance, including documents and the best time to apply.
  • Prepare for possible changes: nationwide circumstances or policy updates can shift timelines; stay informed through official channels and trusted guidance.

What to do if dates shift or you miss a deadline

Missed deadlines are challenging but not always final. Check whether late registration, special rounds, or stray seats are announced by the authorities. If there is any flexibility, act quickly to contact the counseling helpline or official helpdesk. Do not rely on unofficial channels for critical deadlines.

FAQs

1. How do I find the exact counseling dates for my state?

Visit the official counseling portal for your state or the university conducting admissions. Timelines are published there and updated if changes occur.

2. Can I apply to MBBS, engineering, and law in the same state simultaneously?

Yes, you can pursue multiple pathways in the same state if deadlines overlap. Maintain separate application records, verify document requirements for each program, and track different counseling rounds.

3. What if I have a gap year or domicile changes during admissions?

domicile status and regional quotas often matter. If your eligibility depends on local residency, ensure you meet the stipulated duration and provide valid proofs when submitting certificates.

4. Are there reserved categories I should consider early?

Yes. If you belong to a reserved category or a specific local quota, verify the certificate validity, required issuing authorities, and submission deadlines at the earliest.

5. Should I wait for multiple rounds or lock in early?

Early registration and provisional seat acceptance can reduce last-minute stress. However, monitor all rounds and keep options open until final admission is secured.

Final note

Admissions across MBBS, engineering, and law hinge on a mix of national results and state-level counseling. A region-specific calendar helps families align preparation with deadlines, avoid last-minute bottlenecks, and make informed choices about programs and institutions. Regularly check official portals for updates, confirm requirements for your region, and plan with a realistic calendar that accommodates local variations.

title: JEE Main 2027 ലൈവ് ഫോട്ടോ പൊരുത്തക്കേട്: ക്യാമറയും QR വഴിയും
description: JEE Main 2027 ലൈവ് ഫോട്ടോ പൊരുത്തപ്പെടുന്നില്ലെങ്കിൽ NTAയുടെ ക്യാമറ, QR, സ്കാൻ ചിത്രം, തിരിച്ചറിയൽ വിവര നിർദേശങ്ങൾ പരിശോധിക്കുക.
content:
JEE Main 2027 അപേക്ഷയിൽ ലൈവ് ഫോട്ടോ പൊരുത്തപ്പെടുന്നില്ലെന്ന സന്ദേശം വന്നാൽ ക്യാമറയിലെ പ്രശ്നവും തിരിച്ചറിയൽ വിവരങ്ങളിലെ പ്രശ്നവും വേർതിരിച്ചു കാണുക. ലൈവ് ചിത്രത്തിനൊപ്പം അടുത്തിടെ എടുത്ത പാസ്‌പോർട്ട് വലുപ്പമുള്ള ചിത്രത്തിന്റെ സ്കാൻ പകർപ്പും NTA ആവശ്യപ്പെടുന്നു. ഒരു ഫയൽ മാറ്റിയാൽ മറ്റേ ഘട്ടത്തിലെ പ്രശ്നം സ്വയം മാറില്ല. ഒരു പ്രത്യേക പുനഃശ്രമം പൊരുത്തക്കേട് തീർക്കുമെന്ന് ബുള്ളറ്റിൻ ഉറപ്പുനൽകുന്നില്ല.

NTA നിർദേശിക്കുന്ന രീതിയിൽ ലൈവ് ചിത്രം എടുക്കുക

2027 വിവര ബുള്ളറ്റിൻ പ്രകാരം അപേക്ഷ നൽകുന്ന ഉപകരണത്തിന്റെ ക്യാമറ ഓണാക്കുകയോ വെബ്ക്യാം ബന്ധിപ്പിക്കുകയോ ചെയ്യണം. വെളുത്ത പശ്ചാത്തലവും മതിയായ വെളിച്ചവും വേണം. മാസ്കില്ലാതെ ചെവികൾ ഉൾപ്പെടെ മുഖം വ്യക്തമായിരിക്കണം. 80% മുഖം കാണണമെന്നാണ് NTA പറയുന്നത്.

ഉപകരണം വെബ്ക്യാം പിന്തുണയ്ക്കുന്നില്ലെങ്കിൽ മൊബൈൽ ഫോണോ ടാബ്‌ലെറ്റോ ഉപയോഗിച്ച് QR കോഡ് സ്കാൻ ചെയ്യാൻ ബുള്ളറ്റിൻ അനുവദിക്കുന്നു. ഔദ്യോഗിക അപേക്ഷാ പ്രക്രിയയിൽ കാണുന്ന സൗകര്യം ഉപയോഗിക്കുക. അനുയോജ്യമായ ഉപകരണത്തിൽ സ്വന്തം ചിത്രം എടുക്കാനുള്ള വഴിയാണിത്; മറ്റൊരാളുടെ ചിത്രം പകരം നൽകാനുള്ള അനുമതിയല്ല.

NTA, JEE Main 2027 വിവര ബുള്ളറ്റിൻ, അച്ചടിച്ച പേജ് 9: തിരിച്ചറിയലും ലൈവ് ഫോട്ടോയും സംബന്ധിച്ച നിർദേശങ്ങൾ. NTA നിർദേശിക്കുന്ന രീതിയിൽ ലൈവ് ചിത്രം എടുക്കുക

വീണ്ടും ശ്രമിക്കുന്നതിന് മുമ്പ് ബ്രൗസറിന് ക്യാമറ അനുമതിയുണ്ടോ, പ്രിവ്യൂവിൽ നിങ്ങളുടെ മുഖം കാണുന്നുണ്ടോ എന്ന് നോക്കുക. ഉപകരണം സ്ഥിരമായി പിടിച്ച് മുഖഭാഗങ്ങൾ മറയ്ക്കുന്ന നിഴൽ ഒഴിവാക്കുക. ഇവ ചിത്രത്തിന്റെ ഗുണനിലവാരത്തിന് സഹായിക്കാം. തിരിച്ചറിയൽ താരതമ്യം എന്തുകൊണ്ട് പരാജയപ്പെട്ടു എന്ന് തെളിയിക്കുകയോ സ്വീകാര്യത ഉറപ്പാക്കുകയോ ചെയ്യുന്നില്ല.

സ്കാൻ ചിത്രത്തിന് പ്രത്യേകം വ്യവസ്ഥകൾ

സ്കാൻ ചെയ്ത പാസ്‌പോർട്ട് ചിത്രം അടുത്തിടെ എടുത്ത നിറമുള്ളതായിരിക്കണം. വെളുത്ത പശ്ചാത്തലത്തിൽ മാസ്കില്ലാതെ ചെവികൾ ഉൾപ്പെടെ 80% മുഖം കാണണം. വ്യക്തമായ JPG അല്ലെങ്കിൽ JPEG ഫയലിന്റെ വലുപ്പം 10 kB മുതൽ 200 kB വരെയായിരിക്കണം.

അപ്‌ലോഡ് ചെയ്യാനിരിക്കുന്ന യഥാർഥ ഫയൽ പരിശോധിക്കുക; മെസേജിങ് ആപ്പിലെ ചെറിയ പ്രിവ്യൂ മാത്രം നോക്കരുത്. ആവർത്തിച്ചുള്ള കംപ്രഷൻ വലുപ്പപരിധി പാലിച്ചാലും മുഖം അവ്യക്തമാക്കാം. പൊരുത്തപരിശോധന ഒഴിവാക്കാൻ മുഖസവിശേഷതകൾ മാറ്റരുത്. സ്വന്തം ചിത്രം ഉപയോഗിച്ച് പോർട്ടലിലെ നിർദേശങ്ങൾ പാലിക്കുക.

വീണ്ടും ശ്രമിക്കുന്നതിന് മുമ്പ് തിരിച്ചറിയൽ വിവരങ്ങൾ

NTAയുടെ ഒക്ടോബർ 28 രജിസ്ട്രേഷൻ നിർദേശം സ്വന്തം DigiLocker, JanParichay അല്ലെങ്കിൽ e-Pramaan പ്രവേശനവിവരങ്ങൾ ഉപയോഗിക്കാൻ പറയുന്നു. പുതിയ വിവരങ്ങൾ ലഭിക്കാൻ ഫോം പൂരിപ്പിക്കുന്നതിന് മുമ്പ് DigiLocker Re-KYC ചെയ്യാനും നിർദേശിക്കുന്നു. പേരും ജനനത്തീയതിയും പത്താം ക്ലാസ് സർട്ടിഫിക്കറ്റുമായോ മാർക്ക് ലിസ്റ്റുമായോ പൊരുത്തപ്പെടണം.

UIDAI മാർഗനിർദേശപ്രകാരം ഫോട്ടോ ഉൾപ്പെടെയുള്ള ആധാർ വിവരങ്ങൾ പുതുക്കിവയ്ക്കാൻ ബുള്ളറ്റിൻ പ്രത്യേകം പറയുന്നു. Re-KYCയും ആധാർ പുതുക്കലും വ്യത്യസ്ത നടപടികളാണ്. Re-KYC പഴയ ആധാർ ഫോട്ടോ മാറ്റുമെന്നോ എല്ലാ ലൈവ് ഫോട്ടോ പൊരുത്തക്കേടുകളും തീർക്കുമെന്നോ നിർദേശത്തിൽ പറയുന്നില്ല.

അതേ പിശക് തുടരുമ്പോൾ

കൃത്യമായ പിശക് സന്ദേശവും അത് വരുന്ന ഘട്ടവും കുറിച്ചുവയ്ക്കുക. ഔദ്യോഗിക JEE Main വെബ്‌സൈറ്റിലെ NTA സഹായകേന്ദ്രവുമായി ബന്ധപ്പെടുക. രജിസ്ട്രേഷൻ നിർദേശത്തിൽ 011-40759000, jeemain@nta.ac.in എന്നിവയുണ്ട്. പ്രശ്നം വിശദീകരിച്ച് ഔദ്യോഗിക മാർഗത്തിലൂടെ ആവശ്യപ്പെട്ടാൽ അപേക്ഷാ റഫറൻസ് നൽകുക. പാസ്‌വേഡോ OTPയോ പങ്കിടരുത്.

ക്യാമറ പ്രിവ്യൂ ശരിയായത് അപേക്ഷ പൂർത്തിയായതിന് തുല്യമല്ല. സേവ് ചെയ്ത ഫോട്ടോയും ഫോമും പരിശോധിച്ച് ആവശ്യമായ ഘട്ടങ്ങൾക്കു ശേഷം ലഭിക്കുന്ന സ്ഥിരീകരണം സൂക്ഷിക്കുക. വീണ്ടും പണം നൽകുന്നതിന് മുമ്പ് പുതിയ അപേക്ഷയും തിരുത്തലും സംബന്ധിച്ച മാർഗദർശി വായിക്കുക. പുതിയ ഫോം ഫോട്ടോ പിശകിനുള്ള ഉറപ്പായ പരിഹാരമല്ല.

title: ISC Biology Exam Analysis 2026: Difficulty Level, Question Pattern & Answer Key
description: ISC Biology Exam Analysis 2026 is out. Check the difficulty level, question pattern, important topics asked, and answer key details for the ISC Class 12 Biology exam conducted by CISCE.
content:
The ISC Biology Exam 2026 for Class 12 students has been conducted successfully by the Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE). After the completion of the examination, students and teachers have shared their views on the difficulty level of the question paper. It is found that the question paper was almost balanced and followed the syllabus.

Majority of the students found the question paper moderate. The questions in the question paper required conceptual knowledge rather than memory-based knowledge. The students who have followed the textbook thoroughly and the previous year's question papers have attempted the examination confidently. The students found a few questions challenging.

ISC Biology Exam 2026 Overview

Particulars Details
Exam Name ISC Biology Exam 2026
Conducting Body Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE)
Exam Level Class 12 Board Examination
Overall Difficulty Moderate
Question Type Short, descriptive, and diagram-based
Major Topics Genetics, Ecology, Human Reproduction, Biotechnology

The format of the question paper was standard for the ISC test. The majority of the short answer questions in Section A were straightforward. Students were required to provide clear explanations of biological topics in Section B's medium-length questions. Long questions in Section C required in-depth answers and visuals.

Genetics, human reproduction, biotechnology, ecology, and plant physiology were some of the key subjects. Teachers saw that all of the topics from the syllabus were covered in the exam, so it was imperative that the pupils grasp the material.

It was observed by the students that questions based on diagrams were included, and hence, they were scoring. Although some questions were tricky, the exam was found to be fair.

Conclusion

The ISC Biology Exam 2026 was moderate and well-structured. Students who had focused on concepts and had regular practice were able to score well. Now, students are awaiting the final results. They can also make an estimation of their marks by using unofficial answer keys provided by their teachers or coaching institutes.

title: CSAB Special Rounds: When the Extra Fee Is Worth the Upgrade
description: A practical guide for JoSAA candidates weighing CSAB Special Rounds by seat risk, extra costs and realistic branch or college improvement.
content:
CSAB Special Rounds can improve your engineering seat after JoSAA, but they can also add payment pressure and uncertainty. Enter only when the possible branch or institute change is worth losing comfort with your present option, spending more and handling fresh reporting requirements.

If your current seat is an unwanted branch at a less preferred institute, trying for a better fit may make sense. If you already hold a seat you can afford and would happily join, staying put may be wiser. This is a decision about fit and money, not just a bigger college name.

Should you risk your present seat for a possible upgrade?

Begin with the seat in your allotment letter. Then write down every CSAB option you would genuinely accept. A choice is useful only if you would pay for it, relocate for it and join that branch after allotment.

  • Enter with a clear reason: the new option improves your branch, institute or both in a way that matters to your career plans.
  • Think twice: you are chasing a familiar name while ignoring branch content, location, hostel expenses or family finances.
  • Do not guess the rule: participation, allotment, non-payment and withdrawal can affect seat handling under the applicable admission-year conditions.

Vacancies are not promises. The result depends on seats left after JoSAA, your eligibility, rank and the choices of other candidates. Last year's closing rank may give context, but it cannot tell you what will happen this year.

What should your family count as the real CSAB cost?

Look beyond the registration screen. Check the current CSAB information brochure for the applicable payment, any amount connected with a fresh allotment, institute reporting charges, travel, hostel advance and document expenses. Read the refund and forfeiture clauses too. The first amount displayed may not be your total exposure.

Ask plainly: if this seat is allotted, can we fund and join it without cancelling the plan under stress? If the answer is no, remove that choice. A dependable seat beats an upgrade that the family cannot sustain.

How can you fill choices without creating a problem?

  1. Rank branches and institutes by your own joining preference.
  2. Delete every option you would reject after checking curriculum, location, hostel cost and reporting conditions.
  3. Save the submitted list and payment receipt.
  4. Read the current CSAB notice for eligibility, vacant-seat treatment and the effect on your JoSAA seat before paying.

CSAB is the authority responsible for these special rounds, while the admission-year notice controls the live rules. Separate those rules from your own judgement. You can also compare colleges before deciding whether the possible change is genuinely better.
author: Geethika Reddy

title: A practical yearlong admissions calendar for Indian MBBS and B Tech with regional backup paths
description: A structured, month-by-month admissions plan for Indian MBBS and B Tech aspirants, including regional backup options, essential deadlines, counseling steps, and guidance for students and parents to navigate exams, admissions, and choice-of-institution decisions.
content:
Why a yearlong calendar matters for MBBS and B Tech aspirants

Competition for MBBS seats and engineering programs remains intense. A disciplined, yearlong plan helps families coordinate academic preparation, entrance test readiness, application timelines, and financial planning. This article provides a practical calendar for a full academic year, with regional backup paths that can reduce stress and improve odds of admission.

Baseline timeline for MBBS and B Tech admissions

In India, admission processes are coordinated across entrance tests, statewide or national counseling, and college-level admissions. The calendar below outlines a steady progression from initial test preparation to final seat allocation. Where regional variations exist, use the regional backup paths described later to ensure alternate options remain open.

Months 1-3: Foundation and test readiness

  • Clarify goals: decide MBBS vs B Tech focus and identify preferred regions (home state versus neighboring states).
  • Register for relevant entrance tests or board exam review sessions, if applicable. Confirm eligibility criteria for targeted programs.
  • Develop a study plan: allocate weekly hours for core subjects, practice tests, and time for counseling research.
  • Collect documents early: identity proofs, birth certificates, 10th/12th mark sheets, class certificates, and category certificates if applicable.

Months 4-6: Entrance preparation intensifies

  • Start practice with topic-wise and full-length mock tests tailored to the chosen streams.
  • Monitor exam patterns and syllabus with official notifications; adjust preparation focus accordingly.
  • Explore regional options: for MBBS, some states or central bodies run parallel or tie-up admissions. For B Tech, consider state-level engineering entrance patterns and counseling portals.
  • Begin early financial planning: estimate tuition, hostel, and living costs; identify scholarships or fee waivers where available.

Months 7-9: Counseling preparation and application filing

  • Prepare a master list of target colleges across regions, including backup options within reasonable travel distance.
  • Draft application materials and verify required documents for each college or state counseling portal.
  • Register for counseling portals that align with target programs and complete profiles with accurate data.
  • Track application deadlines and exam result release dates; set reminders for certificate verification windows.

Months 10-12: Seat allotment, migration plans, and final decisions

  • Monitor seat allotment results and undergo verification processes promptly to avoid submission backlogs.
  • For MBBS: prepare for document verification rounds and counseling-specific requirements; for B Tech: secure admission offers and confirm seats within allotted timeframes.
  • Finalize backup plans: if preferred programs are not allotted, pivot to regional options with viable admission chances.
  • Plan logistics: housing, travel, and campus orientation preparations should align with confirmed seat timelines.

Regional backup paths for Indian students and parents

Regional strategies can reduce risk by creating parallel tracks that lead to admission even if the primary target is delayed or uncertain. The following backups are commonly feasible across many states:

  • MBBS backups: explore allied medical programs such as BDS, BAMS, BAMS-Ayurveda, or BSC Nursing in nearby states, where entrance competition may differ. Consider private colleges with transparent fee structures and scholarship options. If a state conducts its own counseling, identify adjacent states with reciprocal practice rules for later transfer or internship alignment.
  • B Tech backups: identify engineering colleges in neighboring states with favorable cutoff trends or late counseling rounds. Private engineering institutes often have rolling admissions or late seat allotment windows that can secure a seat if public counseling tightens.
  • Financial backups: map out institutes with Scholarship schemes, tuition waivers, or merit-based aid that apply across regions. Create a priority list by estimated annual cost and potential return on investment.
  • Logistics backups: consider institutions with campuses in multiple cities or states, enabling easier relocation within your region if a preferred campus seats out.

Always verify dates and requirements on official admission portals and the institution’s own site. Timelines can shift due to regulatory updates, seat matrix changes, or novel counseling rounds. Treat the calendar as a framework and update it as official notices arrive.

  • Keep a shared calendar with key dates and reminders for both student and parent roles.
  • Maintain a document vault with scanned copies of essential certificates and identification ready for upload.
  • Balance study with rest and mental health breaks to sustain performance across a year of preparation.
  • Engage with school or coaching mentors who provide verified information on the latest admission processes.

Q1: When should I start preparing for MBBS or B Tech admissions?

Ahead of the academic year start, typically three to six months before major entrance tests or counseling openings is a prudent start. Use the early months to build fundamentals, then intensify practice and exam readiness.

Q2: How do regional backups work in practice?

Regional backups involve identifying credible alternatives in nearby states with different admission timelines, exam patterns, or seat matrices. If the primary option is delayed or oversubscribed, a backup plan with a nearby state increases the likelihood of timely admission.

Q3: What documents are essential for counseling rounds?

Common essentials include identity proof, academic transcripts, domicile or residence certificates (if required for state quotas), category certificates, passport-sized photographs, and all relevant invitation or admit cards. Always verify the exact list for each counseling round.

Q4: How should I manage finances during the yearlong process?

Estimate tuition, hostel, and living costs for target programs. Explore scholarships, merit waivers, and loan options early. Build a contingency fund and plan for possible regional backup tuition variations.

Q5: Can I change my course after seat allotment?

Changing courses typically has strict rules and limited windows. If possible, confirm transfer policies with the institution before finalizing admission and consider backup options in parallel to avoid lost opportunities.

Final note

The yearlong admissions calendar is a practical tool for students and parents to stay organized, reduce stress, and increase the chance of securing a seat in MBBS or B Tech programs. Always cross-check dates with official authorities and college portals. Use regional backup paths to keep options open without compromising your core goals.

title: Admissions Insights: Predicting State-Quota Seat Availability Across Top Indian Institutes for 2026-27
description: A practical guide for Indian students and parents on how state-quota seat trends at premier institutes are shaping 2026-27 admissions, with actionable steps to plan and maximize opportunities.
content:
Understanding State-Quota Seats and Why They Matter in 2026-27

State-quota seats are reserved categories within the central and state engineering and medical admissions ecosystem. They allocate a portion of seats to students from a state, offering a clearer path for domicile-based applicants. In 2026-27, several premier institutes have refined their quota policies to balance across regions, while maintaining merit-based selection. For families, this means tracking state-specific announcements, eligibility criteria, and seat allotment timelines becomes part of the early planning process.

Key Institutes and What to Watch This Admission Cycle

Top Indian institutes typically publish annual seat matrices that include state-quota allocations. While exact numbers vary year to year, here are common patterns to monitor:

  • State-domicile quotas often reflect candidate pools from the same state; larger states may retain a higher share due to population size.
  • Some institutes adjust quota percentages to address regional gaps in representation or to align with national policy directives.
  • A few institutes reserve seats for certain categories within the state quota, such as economically weaker sections or reserved categories, subject to eligibility criteria.

Predicting seat availability involves synthesizing official notices, historical allocation data, and current-year admission guidelines. Practical steps include:

  • Review state-quota policies announced by each institute for the 2026-27 cycle. Note any changes from the prior year.
  • Compare state-wise cut-offs and seats from the previous admission year to identify states with rising demand or slack in supply.
  • Track counselling authorities and seat-mapping portals that publish seat distribution by state and category.
  • Maintain a spread of options: consider institutes within your state and in neighboring regions where quota patterns may differ.

Grounded scenarios help families anticipate where to focus efforts:

  • If your state has a high applicant volume for a particular institute, the state-quota seats may fill quickly in early rounds. Prepare by ensuring eligibility and documentation are ready ahead of counselling windows.
  • States with balanced applicant pools may offer more flexibility in later rounds. In such cases, securing a seat through the state quota could be feasible even if merit rankings are tight.
  • Some institutes reserve a portion of seats for special categories within the state quota. Check if you qualify and what documentation is required to maintain eligibility across rounds.

A well-rounded plan reduces uncertainty and increases chances of admission through state quotas. Consider these actions:

  • Create a state-focused shortlist: identify institutes where your domicile is strongly represented and where recent trends hint at favorable quota allocations.
  • Align academics with quota expectations: ensure board exam performance and eligibility requirements meet or exceed the minimum criteria for state quotas.
  • Keep documents ready: domicile proofs, category certificates, and other mandated records should be organized to accelerate counselling processes.
  • Engage with official communication channels: regularly check the institute’s admission portal and the designated state counselling authority for updates and deadlines.

While exact seats shift annually, a structured approach helps families stay prepared:

  • Identify the institutes where state-quota seats are most likely to influence the final admission outcome in 2026-27.
  • Monitor any changes to quota allocation policies announced during the early weeks of the cycle.
  • Prepare for multiple rounds of counselling by maintaining eligibility across potential options.

  1. What exactly is a state-quota seat and who qualifies?

    A state-quota seat is a portion of total seats reserved for candidates domiciled in a particular state. Eligibility generally depends on domicile proof and meeting minimum academic criteria. Specific rules vary by institute and cycle, so verify on the official admission portal.

  2. How predictable are state-quota seat allocations across top institutes?

    Patterns exist from year to year, but allocations can change due to policy adjustments, demographic shifts, and counselling outcomes. Use historical data as a guide, but rely on official notices for current numbers.

  3. When should families start tracking state-quota information?

    Begin as soon as the cycle is announced. Early monitoring helps identify states with competitive pressure and allows time to prepare required documentation.

  4. What documents are commonly required for state-quota admissions?

    Common documents include domicile proof, category certificates if applicable, 10th/12th mark sheets, board or exam conduct certificates, and identity proofs. Confirm exact requirements on the official admission portal.

  5. Can a student switch institutes if the state-quota seat allocation changes?

    Most counselling processes allow options within the declared seats, but changes depend on the current year’s rules and seat availability. Always review the latest counselling guidelines before making decisions.

  6. Where can families verify official seat counts and rounds?

    Refer to the official admission portals and the state counselling authority’s announcements for authentic, current information. Do not rely on third-party summaries for critical deadlines.

  7. What should be prioritized in the first round of counselling?

    Prioritize institutes where your state quota is likely to secure a seat based on your domicile and category. Have backup options ready in case seat availability shifts between rounds.

title: CBSE 2027 PDF डेटशीट है, मार्कशीट नहीं: क्या डाउनलोड करें
description: 6 नवंबर 2026 को जारी CBSE PDF में कक्षा 10 और 12 की परीक्षा तिथियां हैं। जानें इसमें क्या मिलता है और यह व्यक्तिगत मार्कशीट क्यों नहीं है।
content:
CBSE ने 6 नवंबर 2026 को कक्षा 10 और 12 की वर्ष 2027 की परीक्षा डेटशीट जारी की है। इस PDF में विषयों के नाम, कोड, परीक्षा की तारीखें और समय दिए गए हैं। यह किसी छात्र की व्यक्तिगत मार्कशीट नहीं है और इसमें प्राप्त अंक नहीं मिलेंगे।

अगर इस घोषणा के बाद आपने “CBSE 2027 मार्कशीट PDF” खोजा है, तो परीक्षा की योजना बनाने के लिए कक्षा 10 और 12 की आधिकारिक डेटशीट डाउनलोड करें। इस सार्वजनिक दस्तावेज को पढ़ने के लिए रोल नंबर या व्यक्तिगत जानकारी देने की जरूरत नहीं है।

CBSE कक्षा 10 और 12 डेटशीट, 6 नवंबर 2026

नई डेटशीट में किन तारीखों की पुष्टि है?

कक्षा 10 का पूरा परीक्षा कार्यक्रम 16 फरवरी से 9 मार्च 2027 तक है। कक्षा 12 का कार्यक्रम 16 फरवरी से 9 अप्रैल 2027 तक है। आपकी पहली और आखिरी परीक्षा स्कूल में दर्ज विषयों पर निर्भर करेगी। पूरे कार्यक्रम की अंतिम तारीख हर छात्र की अंतिम परीक्षा नहीं होती।

विषय का कोड देखने से पहले अपनी कक्षा वाला भाग खोलें। संयुक्त PDF में दोनों कक्षाओं के कुछ विषयों के नाम समान हैं। कक्षा का शीर्षक देखे बिना कॉपी की गई तारीख आपके लिए गलत हो सकती है। सेकेंडरी स्कूल परीक्षा की प्रविष्टियां समझने के लिए कक्षा 10 की विषयवार तारीखों की अंग्रेजी मार्गदर्शिका भी देख सकते हैं।

अगर आपको वास्तव में अंक या मार्कशीट चाहिए

डेटशीट जारी होने का अर्थ परिणाम घोषित होना नहीं है। यह दस्तावेज न व्यक्तिगत अंक देता है, न मार्कशीट जारी होने की तारीख बताता है। परिणाम और दस्तावेजों से जुड़े निर्देश जारी होने पर CBSE की आधिकारिक वेबसाइट और अपने स्कूल से जानकारी लें।

इस सार्वजनिक डेटशीट को डाउनलोड करने के लिए किसी असंबंधित पेज पर व्यक्तिगत विवरण भरना आवश्यक नहीं है। आधिकारिक PDF का लिंक सुरक्षित रखें और “मार्कशीट” लिखे किसी डाउनलोड बटन पर आगे बढ़ने से पहले दस्तावेज का शीर्षक पढ़ें।

title: CUCET 2027 বৃত্তি: খরচ ধরার আগে পর্যায় ও কোর্স মিলিয়ে নিন
description: একই CUCET নম্বরে পর্যায় ও কোর্স অনুযায়ী বৃত্তির হার বদলাতে পারে। 2027-এর সাধারণ হার ও পঞ্জাবের বিশেষ ম্যানেজমেন্ট কোর্সের ব্যতিক্রম দেখুন।
content:
CUCET 2027-এ 80 নম্বর সাধারণ প্রথম পর্যায়ের তালিকায় 50% বৃত্তির মধ্যে পড়ে, কিন্তু দ্বিতীয় পর্যায়ে 40%। কিছু বিশেষ কোর্সের নিজস্ব হার রয়েছে। পরিবারকে কত দিতে হবে হিসাব করার আগে সঠিক পর্যায়, ক্যাম্পাস ও কোর্সের পুরো নামের সঙ্গে স্কোর মিলিয়ে নিন।

সাধারণ বৃত্তির হার পর্যায়ভেদে বদলায়

চণ্ডীগড় বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের সরকারি পোর্টালে প্রথম পর্যায় অক্টোবর 2026 থেকে মে 2027 এবং দ্বিতীয় পর্যায় জুন 2027 থেকে ভর্তি শেষ হওয়া পর্যন্ত বলা রয়েছে। প্রথম পর্যায়ে আবেদন করার বিকল্প আছে; দ্বিতীয় পর্যায় বন্ধ দেখাচ্ছে। এগুলি বিস্তৃত সময়সীমা, দিনভিত্তিক পরীক্ষার ক্যালেন্ডার বা আবেদনের নির্দিষ্ট শেষ তারিখ নয়।

নীচের তুলনায় প্রকাশিত স্কোরের সীমা দেওয়া হয়েছে। 30 থেকে 39.99 নম্বরের ক্ষেত্রে পোর্টাল কোনো শতাংশ বৃত্তির প্রতিশ্রুতি না দিয়ে যোগ্য বলেছে। বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের নিশ্চয়তা ছাড়া সীমার কাছাকাছি নম্বরকে বাড়িয়ে পরের স্তরে ধরবেন না।

পঞ্জাবের কিছু ম্যানেজমেন্ট কোর্সের আলাদা হার

পঞ্জাব ক্যাম্পাসে MBA (FinTech & AI), MBA (Banking, Financial Services & Insurance), MBA (Strategic-HR) এবং নির্দিষ্ট B.Com. Applied Finance and Analytics বা Forensic Accounting and Fraud Investigation কোর্সের আলাদা হার রয়েছে। এগুলিতে 90.01-100 ও 80-90 উভয় ক্ষেত্রেই 40%; ছবিতে দেখানো পরের চারটি নিচের স্তরে যথাক্রমে 30%, 20%, 15%, 10%। MBA (Applied Finance and Analytics) with PwC-র জন্য আলাদাভাবে বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের ওয়েবসাইট দেখতে বলা হয়েছে। সাধারণ 100% শিরোনাম প্রতিটি ম্যানেজমেন্ট কোর্সে প্রয়োগ করবেন না।

পোর্টাল বলছে, মাইগ্রেশনের মাধ্যমে আসা পড়ুয়াদের বৃত্তি প্রযোজ্য নয়। উত্তরপ্রদেশ ক্যাম্পাসের বিশেষ কোর্সের আলাদা বিভাগ রয়েছে; পঞ্জাবের ব্যতিক্রমগুলিকে ওই ক্যাম্পাসের সম্পূর্ণ নিয়ম ভাববেন না। ফি-র অনুমান গ্রহণের আগে নির্দিষ্ট কোর্স ও ক্যাম্পাস যাচাই করুন।

চণ্ডীগড় বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের CUCET 2027 পোর্টাল: পর্যায়ভিত্তিক হার, পঞ্জাব ম্যানেজমেন্টের ব্যতিক্রম এবং মাইগ্রেশন পড়ুয়াদের বর্জনের শর্ত। পাতায় আলাদা প্রকাশের তারিখ নেই।

সরকারি CUCET 2027 বৃত্তির পোর্টাল

ফি-র বাজেট করার আগে বৃত্তি নিশ্চিত করুন

স্কোরকার্ড রাখুন এবং ভর্তি বিভাগকে অফার বা ফি-র বিবরণীতে প্রযোজ্য বৃত্তি নিশ্চিত করতে বলুন। কোন কোন ফি অন্তর্ভুক্ত, কতদিন সুবিধা থাকবে এবং নবীকরণের শর্ত কী, তা জিজ্ঞাসা করুন। তালিকায় শতাংশ লেখা মানে টিউশন, হস্টেল, খাবার ও সব খরচ মকুব নয়। বিস্তারিত স্পষ্ট না হওয়া পর্যন্ত সম্মিলিত মোট খরচ থেকে বৃত্তির শতাংশ বাদ দেবেন না।

Q: Is there a correction window after the deadline?

A: Yes. Most exam authorities open a correction window 1 to 3 weeks after the application deadline. Not all fields can be corrected - name and date of birth typically cannot. Monitor official website daily after the deadline closes.

title: UGC NET June 2026 Paper Choice: How Subject Eligibility Narrows Options
description: Can your UGC NET subject differ from your postgraduate degree? Check the NTA rule, match your academic subject and protect your teaching or research plans.
content:
A different UGC NET subject is not automatically allowed just because its syllabus looks familiar. For the June 2026 cycle, the current NTA bulletin must establish whether your postgraduate subject can be paired with the NET subject you want. The supplied official evidence does not contain that bulletin or its subject-eligibility text, so no article can honestly confirm the permitted relationship yet.

That uncertainty has a real cost. An ineligible choice can waste your attempt, while a poorly matched subject may restrict how useful the result is for later assistant professor or research applications.

Can your NET subject differ from your postgraduate subject?

Only if the June 2026 NTA rules permit that relationship. The responsible authority is the National Testing Agency, which conducts UGC NET. Its official website is the place to check the current notice, bulletin and subject list: UGC NET official website. Until the June 2026 eligibility wording is available, treat every coaching chart, old PDF or informal subject map as unconfirmed.

What should you match before choosing the paper?

Put these three details on one page before opening the application form:

  1. Your exact postgraduate discipline: Use the wording on your degree certificate, marksheets and specialisation documents. “Arts” or “science” is too broad.
  2. The proposed NET subject: Check the exact subject entry and any permitted related-discipline instruction in the current NTA bulletin.
  3. Your intended use: Decide whether you’re targeting assistant professor eligibility, a Junior Research Fellowship route or admission to a research programme. Later institutions and vacancies may apply their own conditions.

Why a nearby subject can still be a poor choice

Suppose your postgraduate degree is in one social-science specialisation and you select another paper because its topics seem easier. That may help your preparation, but it doesn’t prove that NTA accepts the pairing or that the result will support the teaching subject you want to claim. A syllabus match is not an eligibility match.

Read the June 2026 bulletin on the UGC NET June 2026 exam guide only as a planning aid, not as a replacement for the NTA notice. Before payment, record the bulletin section or official clarification reference that supports your subject choice. If no such wording is available, pause the application and seek written clarification from NTA. Keep the reply with your academic documents.
