title: SRMJEEE 2027: Notification, Eligibility, Pattern & Syllabus
description: Read the complete guide on SRMJEEE 2027. Find out about the official notification, eligibility criteria, registration dates, exam pattern, and core syllabus.
content:
The SRM Joint Engineering Entrance Examination (SRMJEEE) is a national-level test conducted by the SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST). It is the mandatory gateway for admission into undergraduate engineering (B.Tech) programs across SRM campuses. Conducted in a Remote Proctored Online Mode (RPOM), the exam evaluates candidates in physics, chemistry, mathematics (or biology), English, and aptitude. This guide covers the 2027 notification details, academic eligibility, application timeline, paper pattern, and a subject-wise syllabus breakdown to streamline your preparation.

Official Notification and Important Dates

The official notification for SRMJEEE 2027 is expected to be released in October or early November 2026. The examination is typically conducted in two to three distinct phases between April and July. Candidates can apply for and appear in multiple phases to improve their scores, with the highest score considered for final merit ranking.

  • Application Form Release: Expected in the first week of November 2026.

  • Phase 1 Exam Dates: Expected in the third or fourth week of April 2027.

  • Phase 2 Exam Dates: Expected in the second or third week of June 2027.

  • Phase 3 Exam Dates: Expected in the first week of July 2027.

  • Slot Booking & Admit Card: Opens 2 to 3 days before the respective exam phase dates.

Academic and Age Eligibility Criteria

Before filling out the application, candidates must ensure they meet SRMIST’s strict eligibility parameters.

  • Age Limit: Candidates must be at least 16 years and 6 months old by July 31, 2027.

  • Academic Qualification: Applicants must have passed or be appearing for their Class 12 board examinations in 2027 from a recognized central or state educational board.

  • Mandatory Subjects: For standard B.Tech programs, candidates must have Physics and Mathematics as compulsory subjects, along with Chemistry, Biotechnology, or Information Technology. For Biotechnology or Genetic Engineering courses, Physics, Chemistry, and Biology (PCB) are accepted.

  • Minimum Marks: A minimum aggregate of 60% in the core subjects (PCM or PCB) is required.

Registration and Application Process

The application process is conducted entirely online through the official SRM admissions portal.

  1. Registration: Create an account using a valid email ID and mobile number. A verification link will be sent to the registered email address.

  2. Application Form: Fill in your personal details, academic history, and communication address.

  3. Document Upload: Upload a scanned, recent passport-size photograph and a signature according to the specified dimensions.

  4. Fee Payment: Pay the non-refundable application fee (typically ₹1,400 per phase) using a credit card, debit card, or net banking.

  5. Slot Booking: Once the Online Test Booking System (OTBS) window opens, select your preferred exam date and time slot. The admit card will be generated immediately after booking.

Examination Pattern and Marking Scheme

SRMJEEE 2027 is a Computer-Based Test taken from home. Candidates must have a desktop or laptop with a working webcam and microphone; mobile phones are not permitted. The test lasts for 2 hours and 30 minutes (150 minutes).

The question paper contains 130 multiple-choice questions (MCQs), carrying 1 mark each. There is no negative marking for incorrect or unattempted questions.

Syllabus Overview

The syllabus is based on the Class 11 and Class 12 NCERT curriculum.

  • Mathematics: Algebra, Matrices, Determinants, Differential and Integral Calculus, Analytical Geometry (2D and 3D), Vector Algebra, Probability, and Trigonometry.

  • Physics: Mechanics, Electrostatics, Current Electricity, Electromagnetic Induction (EMI), Optics, Thermodynamics, Modern Physics, and Semiconductor Devices.

  • Chemistry: Physical Chemistry (Chemical Kinetics, Electrochemistry, Thermodynamics), Organic Chemistry (Compounds containing Oxygen and Nitrogen, General Organic Chemistry), and Inorganic Chemistry (Coordination Compounds, p-Block, and d-Block elements).

  • English and Aptitude: Reading comprehension, grammar correction, vocabulary (synonyms and antonyms), logical reasoning, data interpretation, and basic numerical ability.

Strategic Preparation Tips

Because the exam requires you to solve 130 questions in 150 minutes, speed is essential.

  • Clear the Easy Sections First: The Chemistry and English & Aptitude sections consist of 55 questions that require minimal calculation. Finish these quickly to save time for Mathematics and Physics.

  • Rely on NCERT: Approximately 60% to 70% of the questions are direct applications of concepts found in standard NCERT textbooks.

  • Attempt All Questions: With absolutely zero negative marking, never leave a question blank. Use logical elimination for difficult problems before the timer runs out.

  • Check Tech Requirements: Test your hardware (webcam, internet connection) a week before the exam to ensure compatibility with the Secure Exam Browser required by the university.

Conclusion

Clearing SRMJEEE 2027 requires a clear understanding of the exam's unique structure and syllabus. By ensuring you meet the 60% aggregate eligibility requirement and completing your registration early, you secure your preferred testing slot. Focus your daily revision on Class 11 and 12 NCERT concepts, specifically prioritizing high-weightage topics like calculus, electrodynamics, and organic chemistry. Since there is no negative marking and the test is conducted in a remote proctored mode, your success depends on rapid execution, strict time management, and setting up a calm, technically sound testing environment at home.

title: Comprehensive Indian Education Scholarships: Mapping Merit-Based and Need-Based Awards with Application Timelines
description: A practical guide to India's flagship scholarships, detailing merit-based and need-based awards, eligibility, application timelines, and tips for students and parents navigating the scholarship landscape.
content:
Understanding the Scholarship Landscape in India

Indian students face a diverse range of scholarships offered by central and state governments, public universities, and private foundations. These awards typically fall into two broad categories: merit-based, which reward academic excellence or specific achievements; and need-based, which focus on a family's financial circumstances. A clear mapping helps families plan early, align goals with deadlines, and maximize the chances of securing funding for education from school through postgraduate studies.

Merit-Based Scholarships: Recognizing Academic Excellence

Merit-based scholarships reward high performance, leadership, or specific talents. Common examples include national-level fellowships for higher education, state merit scholarships for undergraduate study, and targeted awards for STEM, arts, or sports excellence. Eligibility often depends on exam scores, class XII or undergraduate marks, and sometimes performance in auditions or interviews.

  • Typical eligibility: minimum percentage or grade point average, qualifying entrance or board exams, and sometimes a cap on family income.
  • Common benefits: full or partial tuition coverage, maintenance stipends, and access to mentorship networks.
  • Application windows: many merit-based scholarships open once per academic year, with deadlines ranging from late spring to early summer for the upcoming session.

Need-Based Scholarships: Support Based on Financial Need

Need-based scholarships target families with limited resources. They consider household income, assets, and family size, with some programs requiring demonstrated hardship. These awards may cover tuition, living expenses, and sometimes books or equipment.

  • Typical eligibility: family income below a specified threshold, possession of certain documents (income proofs, domicile, etc.), and sometimes a means-tested assessment.
  • Common benefits: partial to full tuition coverage, student stipends, and sometimes accommodation support.
  • Application windows: need-based programs often align with academic calendars but can have rolling cycles or multiple intake periods.

Where to Find Scholarships and How They Are Structured

Understanding the source of funding helps applicants anticipate required documents and the level of competition. Central government schemes frequently target all-India applicants, while state schemes may prioritize residents or students entering state universities. University-level scholarships can be highly specific, such as department-level fellowships or reserved seats for certain categories. Private and corporate offerings may have unique eligibility criteria and timelines, sometimes with early notification of award results.

Key Application Timelines to Track

Timely applications are crucial. While exact dates change yearly, these patterns help families build a planning calendar:

  • Merit-based national fellowships: often open in late winter to early summer; selection processes may include entrance tests, interviews, or panel reviews.
  • State and university scholarships: windows typically open after admissions decisions or at the start of the academic year; some programs run annual cycles with deadlines in summer.
  • Need-based awards: cycles can be rolling or aligned with financial-year quarters; many require annual renewals and annual income proofs.
  • Documentation commonly required: academic records, identity proofs, domicile certificates, income certificates, bank statements, and parent or guardian consent where applicable.

Step-by-Step: How to Build a Scholarship Plan

  1. Identify potential scholarships early: list merit and need-based options appropriate to the student’s stage (school, undergraduate, postgraduate, or professional courses).
  2. Check official timelines and eligibility: note the exact criteria and required documents; bookmark official pages for reminders.
  3. Prepare a core set of documents in advance: educational transcripts, identity and identity-proofs, and income-related documents if pursuing need-based awards.
  4. Build a calendar with milestones: outline application opening dates, submission deadlines, recommendation letters, and any required tests or interviews.
  5. Tailor each application: emphasize strengths relevant to the scholarship’s aims while maintaining accuracy and honesty.
  6. Monitor results and plan for contingencies: have backup scholarships and keep exploring new opportunities as timelines shift.

Practical Tips for Indian Students and Parents

  • Verify the official source before submitting sensitive information. If details are uncertain, check the relevant authority’s website for the latest updates and documents required.
  • Maintain a master file of documents with copies and originals readily available for quick submissions.
  • Seek guidance from school counsellors or university financial aid offices to align applications with course choices.
  • Prepare strong letters of recommendation and, where applicable, ensure referees are aware of deadlines and criteria.
  • Be mindful of renewal requirements for ongoing scholarships; many require annual income proofs and performance updates.

Sample Timeline for a Typical Undergraduate Pathway

Year 1: Research and shortlist 4-6 merit-based scholarships and 2-3 need-based options. Prepare documents and start applications 6-9 months before admission. Attend any required interviews or aptitude tests.

Year 2: If selected, manage renewal requirements and apply for fresh cycles. Begin exploring postgraduate scholarships if continuing studies.

Year 3: Complete ongoing scholarships’ renewal processes and compile achievements for future applications. Maintain eligibility by meeting academic or financial criteria as required.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q1. How early should I start looking for scholarships?

Around 9-12 months before the intended start of the course is a practical window to research, prepare documents, and submit applications.

Q2. Do I need separate applications for merit-based and need-based scholarships?

Yes. Each program has its own criteria and application process. Some supporting documents overlap, but ensure you complete all required sections for each award.

Q3. What documents are most commonly required?

Academic transcripts, identity proofs, proof of residence, income certificates, bank statements, and letters of recommendation are frequently requested. Always confirm the exact list on the official portal.

Q4. Can scholarships be renewed after the first year?

Many merit-based and some need-based scholarships require annual renewal, which may involve maintaining a minimum grade or re-submitting income proofs.

Q5. What should I do if I miss a deadline?

Contact the scholarship authority promptly to learn about any late submission policies or possible waiting lists. Do not assume late submissions will be accepted.

Q6. How can I improve my chances of securing multiple awards?

Build a strong overall profile with consistent academics, relevant achievements, clear statements of purpose, and well-chosen recommendations. Apply to multiple programs to diversify options.

Closing Notes

Scholarships open doors beyond financial support. They recognize effort, potential, and commitment to learning. A proactive, organized approach increases the likelihood of securing both merit and need-based awards. Always verify details on the official authority website and follow that site for the most current timelines and requirements.

வகுப்பு மற்றும் பாடம்குறியீடுதேர்வுத் தேதிநேரம் (IST)கால அளவு

அதிகாரப்பூர்வ PDF-இல் உங்கள் பாடத்தைப் படிப்பது எப்படி?

பக்கம் 4, 10 இல் முதலில் வகுப்பின் தலைப்பைப் பாருங்கள். பிறகு 409, 809 என்ற பாடக் குறியீட்டைத் தேடுங்கள். ஒரு தேதியோ நேரமோ பல வரிகளுக்குப் பொதுவாக இருக்கலாம். கைப்பேசியில் முழுப் பக்கத்தையும் பெரிதாக்கிப் பாருங்கள்.

பள்ளிப் பதிவில் உள்ள பாடப் பெயரையும் குறியீட்டையும் ஒப்பிடுங்கள். ஒன்றுக்கும் மேற்பட்ட வகுப்பில் பெயர் வந்தால் உங்கள் வகுப்புக்கான வரியை மட்டும் எடுத்துக் கொள்ளுங்கள்.

ஆங்கிலத் தேர்வுடன் தேதிகளை ஒப்பிடுங்கள்

10ஆம் வகுப்பு உணவு உற்பத்தி (409) தேர்வுத் தேதி 18 பிப்ரவரி 2027. English Language and Literature (184) தேர்வுத் தேதி 26 பிப்ரவரி 2027. இரு தேதிகளுக்குமிடையே 8 நாட்கள் உள்ளன. 12ஆம் வகுப்பு உணவு உற்பத்தி (809) தேர்வுத் தேதி 6 மார்ச் 2027. English Core (301) தேர்வுத் தேதி 5 மார்ச் 2027. இரு தேதிகளுக்குமிடையே 1 நாட்கள் உள்ளன.

இந்த இடைவெளி முழுவதும் படிக்க விடுமுறை என்று பொருளல்ல. உங்கள் மற்ற பாடங்களையும் நாட்காட்டியில் குறித்து, எந்தத் தேர்வும் இல்லாத நாட்களைக் கணக்கிடுங்கள். மாதிரித் தேர்வை எழுதும்போது உங்கள் தாளுக்கு ஒதுக்கிய நேரத்தைப் பயன்படுத்துங்கள்.

செய்முறைத் தேர்வுக்கு வேறு தேதி இருக்கலாம்

இந்த வரி வாரியம் நடத்தும் தேர்வுக்குரியது. செய்முறை, செயல்திறன் மதிப்பீடு, திட்டப்பணி அல்லது அகமதிப்பீடு இருந்தால் அதன் தேதியையும் தேவையான பொருட்களையும் பள்ளியிடம் கேட்டுத் தெரிந்துகொள்ளுங்கள்.

தேர்வு மையத்துக்குள் தொடர்பு சாதனங்களை எடுத்துச் செல்ல அனுமதி இல்லை. எடுத்துச் செல்லக்கூடிய பொருட்களுக்கு வாரியத்தின் தனி அறிவுறுத்தல்களையும் அனுமதிச் சீட்டையும் பின்பற்றுங்கள்.

title: BITSAT 2027 Syllabus: Subject-Wise Topics & PDF
description: Review the complete BITSAT 2027 syllabus with subject-wise topics for Physics, Chemistry, Maths, English, and Logical Reasoning. Download the official PDF.
content:
BITSAT 2027 Syllabus: Subject-Wise Topics & Official PDF

The Birla Institute of Technology and Science Admission Test (BITSAT) is the mandatory entrance examination for admission into undergraduate engineering and science programs across BITS Pilani, Goa, and Hyderabad campuses. The BITSAT 2027 syllabus is directly aligned with the Class 11 and Class 12 NCERT curriculum.

Because the examination requires candidates to solve 130 questions in 180 minutes, success relies on speed, accuracy, and a thorough understanding of the specific topics outlined by the examining authority. This guide provides a direct breakdown of the subject-wise topics, the examination pattern, and instructions for accessing the official syllabus document.

BITSAT 2027 Examination Pattern

Understanding the exam structure dictates how you navigate the syllabus. The test is a 3-hour Computer-Based Test (CBT) featuring 130 multiple-choice questions for a total of 390 marks.

The question distribution is strictly categorized into four parts:

  • Part I: Physics (30 Questions)

  • Part II: Chemistry (30 Questions)

  • Part III: English Proficiency (10 Questions) and Logical Reasoning (20 Questions)

  • Part IV: Mathematics or Biology (40 Questions)

Candidates receive +3 marks for every correct answer and incur a -1 mark penalty for every incorrect answer. Unattempted questions carry zero marks. If a candidate completes all 130 questions before the 180 minutes expire, they have the option to attempt 12 extra bonus questions (3 each from Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics/Biology, and Logical Reasoning). Attempting the bonus section locks the original 130 answers, preventing further modifications.

Physics Syllabus Breakdown

The Physics section tests formula application and conceptual understanding rather than multi-page derivations.

Mechanics and Waves

  • Kinematics and Dynamics: Motion in a straight line, projectile motion, relative motion, Newton’s laws of motion, friction, and circular motion.

  • Work and Energy: Work-energy theorem, conservative forces, and elastic/inelastic collisions.

  • Rotational Motion: Moment of inertia, torque, angular momentum conservation, and rolling motion.

  • Oscillations and Waves: Simple harmonic motion (SHM), resonance, standing waves, beats, and the Doppler effect.

Electrodynamics and Thermodynamics

  • Electrostatics and Current Electricity: Coulomb’s law, Gauss’s law, capacitance, Ohm’s law, Kirchhoff’s rules, and potentiometer applications.

  • Magnetism and AC Circuits: Biot-Savart law, Ampere’s law, Faraday’s law of induction, Lenz’s law, and LCR circuits.

  • Heat and Thermodynamics: Kinetic theory of gases, first and second laws of thermodynamics, heat transfer, and Carnot engine efficiency.

Optics and Modern Physics

  • Optics: Lens maker’s formula, total internal reflection, Young’s double-slit experiment, and diffraction.

  • Modern Physics: Photoelectric effect, Bohr’s atomic model, mass defect, radioactive decay, and semiconductor logic gates.

Chemistry Syllabus Breakdown

The Chemistry section requires factual recall and rapid calculation, drawing heavily from the NCERT textbook.

Physical Chemistry

  • Atomic Structure and States of Matter: Quantum numbers, Bohr model, ideal gas equation, and crystal lattice structures.

  • Thermodynamics and Equilibrium: Enthalpy, entropy, Gibbs free energy, Le Chatelier’s principle, pH calculations, and buffer solutions.

  • Kinetics and Electrochemistry: Rate laws, Arrhenius equation, Nernst equation, and Faraday’s laws of electrolysis.

Organic Chemistry

  • Basic Principles: IUPAC nomenclature, isomerism (structural and stereoisomerism), and electronic effects (inductive, resonance, hyperconjugation).

  • Hydrocarbons and Functional Groups: Reactions and mechanisms (SN1, SN2, E1, E2) for alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, haloalkanes, alcohols, phenols, ethers, aldehydes, ketones, and carboxylic acids.

Inorganic Chemistry

  • Chemical Bonding: VSEPR theory, hybridization, Molecular Orbital Theory (MOT), and hydrogen bonding.

  • Periodic Table and Block Elements: Periodic trends, properties of s-Block, p-Block, and transition metals (d and f-Block).

  • Coordination Compounds: Werner’s theory, Crystal Field Theory, and IUPAC nomenclature.

Mathematics Syllabus Breakdown

Mathematics carries the highest weightage (40 questions, 120 marks) and demands extensive calculation practice.

Algebra and Probability

  • Algebra: Complex numbers (polar form, cube roots of unity), quadratic equations, arithmetic and geometric progressions, permutations and combinations, binomial theorem, and matrices (adjoint, inverse, determinants).

  • Probability: Conditional probability, Bayes' theorem, and standard statistical measures (mean, variance, standard deviation).

Calculus

  • Differential Calculus: Limits, continuity, differentiability, applications of derivatives (tangents, normals, maxima, minima), and Rolle's theorem.

  • Integral Calculus: Standard integration formulas, definite integrals, properties of definite integrals, area under curves, and first-order differential equations.

Coordinate Geometry and Vectors

  • Two-Dimensional Geometry: Straight lines, distance formulas, circles, parabolas, ellipses, and hyperbolas.

  • Three-Dimensional Geometry and Vectors: Dot and cross products, scalar triple product, direction cosines, and equations of lines and planes in space.

English Proficiency and Logical Reasoning

This section offers 30 highly accessible questions that can significantly boost your overall score.

  • English Proficiency: Synonyms and antonyms, one-word substitution, sentence completion, grammar usage, error detection, and short reading comprehension passages.

  • Logical Reasoning: Analogies, classification, series completion, logical deduction, figure matrix, pattern recognition, paper folding, and embedded figures.

Downloading the Official Syllabus PDF

Candidates must base their final preparation strictly on the official syllabus released by BITS Pilani.

  1. Visit the official BITS admissions portal at bitsadmission.com.

  2. Navigate to the "Downloads" or "Information Brochure" section.

  3. Click on the link for the BITSAT 2027 Syllabus PDF and save the document.

Click here to download the Syllabus

Conclusion

Securing a high score in the BITSAT examination depends on thorough coverage of the prescribed syllabus and the ability to solve questions rapidly. Because the paper includes 130 questions across Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, English, and Logical Reasoning within a 180-minute window, balancing calculation speed with accuracy is mandatory. By prioritizing high-weightage chapters like Calculus, Chemical Bonding, and Electrodynamics, and practicing the language and reasoning sections regularly, candidates can confidently target a score above 300. Download the official PDF, stick to the defined topics, and utilize timed mock tests to refine your execution strategy.

title: CSAB 2026 Special Rounds: Is a NIT Upgrade Worth the Extra Risk?
description: Should you risk a secured JoSAA seat for CSAB 2026? Compare branch fit, fees, refund terms, reporting duties and possible seat loss before choosing.
content:
CSAB 2026 special rounds can improve your NIT option, but an upgrade attempt may also affect the seat you hold through JoSAA. Don’t treat it as a free second chance. First check what the final CSAB 2026 information bulletin says about participation, payment, withdrawal, allotment and institute reporting.

The Central Seat Allocation Board conducts special counselling for participating NITs, IIITs and other institutions covered by its yearly rules. The exact participating institutes, payment heads, refund treatment and deadlines can change. The final 2026 bulletin is not available in the evidence supplied for this article, so no amount or deadline should be treated as confirmed here.

What is the real risk to your JoSAA seat?

There are four separate points to check: registering for CSAB, submitting choices, receiving an allotment and completing payment or reporting. The 2026 bulletin must state whether your earlier JoSAA seat remains available at each point.

If CSAB allots a seat, the next action may involve accepting that allotment, paying the named CSAB amount, uploading documents or reporting to the institute. If you don’t complete a required step, the allotment may be cancelled under the applicable rule. Do not assume your old JoSAA seat, a new CSAB seat or a refund will automatically return to you. That outcome depends on the specific clause and missed step.

When is the upgrade worth attempting?

A NIT label alone isn’t a good reason to gamble. Separate the decision into three questions:

  • Branch upgrade: Does the new course have subjects, laboratories and career routes you prefer?
  • Institute upgrade: Is the campus change worth giving up a better-fit branch where you already hold a seat?
  • Location or cost trade-off: Can your family manage hostel, mess, travel and emergency costs?

Use our college comparison page to place the two exact branches side by side. Score curriculum, acceptable alternatives, total four-year cost and your willingness to report. If you’d only accept the new seat because of its NIT name, leave it out.

What should you record before choosing?

  1. Save your JoSAA allotment letter and every payment receipt.
  2. Write down the exact CSAB choices you would join without regret.
  3. Compare both payment obligations and each refund clause in the 2026 bulletin.
  4. Mark document, payment and institute-reporting steps from the live CSAB notice.

If your current branch is acceptable and the possible gain is small, keeping the secured option may be wiser. If the branch change solves a real problem, calculate the downside before submitting choices. For related counselling decisions, see our entrance exams page. Publication of any 2026-specific fee, date or seat-protection claim should wait for the final CSAB bulletin.

title: UP Police Constable PET 2025: Complete Overview
description: Learn about UP Police Constable PET 2025 including eligibility, physical test details, activities, and career opportunities. Prepare for the recruitment process effectively.
content:
For applicants hoping to join the Uttar Pradesh Police, the UP Police Constable Physical Efficiency Test (PET) 2025 is an important step in the hiring process. PET assesses applicants' endurance, stamina, and physical fitness to make sure they can perform the rigorous responsibilities of a police constable.

Eligibility Criteria

  1. Written Exam Requirement: To sit for PET, a candidate must have passed the written exam for UP Police Constables.
  2. Age Limit: normally between the ages of 18 and 25, while government regulations allow for age relaxation for certain categories.
  3. Citizenship: An Indian national is required.

Physical Test Components

The PET is designed to test agility, strength, and overall fitness. The main components include:

Activity Requirement Time Limit

Long Jump 3.5 m (male) / 2.7 m (female) -

Other tasks may include push-ups, rope climbing, or shot put depending on official notifications. Candidates must meet the minimum standards to qualify.

Importance of PET

  1. Verifies that applicants are physically fit to carry out police tasks.
  2. serves as a vital filter during the hiring process.
  3. equips applicants to meet the demanding requirements of law enforcement.

Career Opportunities

Candidates can advance in the UP Police Constable recruitment process by passing the PET, which opens doors to employment in several police departments as well as a steady government job with benefits and room for advancement. The PET is an essential step toward a successful police career because this position demands commitment, self-control, and physical fitness.

title: NEET UG 2026 Choice Filling: How to Rank Courses, Not Just Colleges
description: Build a NEET UG 2026 preference order using course fit, full cost, bonds, clinical training, location and exit terms.
content:
NEET UG 2026 choice filling should follow your genuine acceptance order, not a college’s reputation. Never place a seat above another just because it looks harder to obtain if you would not join it. Compare every course and college combination for affordability, bond exposure, training fit and exit flexibility before you rank it.

The official NEET UG website carries notices and actions from the National Testing Agency. Seat allocation and choice-filling rules depend on the applicable counselling authority, quota and route. That may mean a central, state or other authorised counselling process. Follow the notice issued for your specific route, not a general post about NEET counselling.

What is the safest ranking rule?

Use this order: rank only seats you would accept, then compare full cost, bond exposure, training fit and exit flexibility. A famous college still belongs below a less famous option if its fee, service condition or course type does not work for your family.

  1. Acceptability: Remove any course you would refuse today. MBBS, BDS and AYUSH programmes lead to different training and work paths.
  2. Full cost: Add tuition, hostel, food, travel, instruments, examination charges and stated institutional fees across the programme. Ask whether fees can change.
  3. Bond exposure: Record service obligations, duration, resignation conditions and stated financial liability from the applicable notice or institution document.
  4. Training fit: Check patient load, internship structure, hospital access and whether clinical training is shared across departments. Ask who supervises interns and where rotations take place.
  5. Exit flexibility: Check resignation deadlines, refund or penalty terms and who holds original documents. Do not assume a low fee means an easy exit.

What should your comparison sheet contain?

Write the evidence beside each option before opening the choice-filling page. If a detail is missing, mark it as unverified rather than guessing.

Decision areaRecordQuestion or red flag
CourseWould I complete it?Would I refuse it if allotted today?
CostFull expected payable amountAre hostel, exam or other charges excluded?
BondDuration and liabilityWhat exact notice states the penalty?
TrainingHospital, patients and internship planIs access shared or clearly assigned?
ExitResignation and document conditionsWho holds originals, and when can they be returned?

Keep copies of the fee, bond and counselling documents you used. For wider exam context, see the NEET UG exam guide, but use the notice for your quota and counselling route when locking choices. That distinction can prevent an allotment your family cannot afford or accept.

title: SRMJEEE 2027 Syllabus: Subject-Wise Topics
description: Explore the detailed SRMJEEE 2027 syllabus with subject-wise topics for Physics, Chemistry, Maths, and Biology to streamline your exam preparation today.
content:
SRMJEEE 2027 Syllabus: Subject-Wise Topics & Core Strategy

Securing a seat across any of the prestigious campuses of the SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST) demands a meticulous and strategic understanding of the SRMJEEE 2027 syllabus. Every year, tens of thousands of engineering and biotechnology aspirants compete for limited seats in one of India's most highly sought-after private university entrance examinations. Unlike many other national-level tests, the SRM Joint Engineering Entrance Examination (SRMJEEE) tests you not just on the core sciences, but also heavily evaluates your linguistic proficiency and analytical aptitude.

To maximize your chances of securing a top rank and unlocking the specialization of your choice-be it Computer Science or Biotechnology-you must align your daily study schedule perfectly with the official curriculum. This comprehensive guide breaks down the subject-wise topics across Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology, English, and Aptitude, ensuring you do not waste precious time on out-of-bounds concepts.

Understanding the Exam Pattern Context

Before diving directly into the chapter-wise breakdowns of the SRMJEEE 2027 syllabus, it is crucial to understand how this curriculum is translated into the actual test environment. The SRMJEEE is typically conducted in a Remote Proctored Online Mode (RPOM), meaning candidates can take the test from the comfort of their homes using a secure exam browser.

The question paper contains a total of 125 Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs), adding up to 125 marks. The duration of the exam is exactly 2 hours and 30 minutes (150 minutes). A massive strategic advantage of the SRMJEEE over exams like JEE Main is the absolute lack of negative marking. For every correct answer, you are awarded +1 mark, and you lose zero marks for incorrect or unattempted questions. Therefore, it is highly recommended to attempt every single question on the paper.

Physics Syllabus Breakdown: Concepts and Numericals

Physics in the SRMJEEE tests both your theoretical foundations and your ability to apply complex formulas under immense time pressure. The syllabus bridges the standard Class 11 and Class 12 NCERT curriculum.

Mechanics and Properties of Matter: This block forms the fundamental backbone of your preparation. You must thoroughly master Units and Measurement, Kinematics, Laws of Motion, and Work, Energy, and Power. Rotational Motion and Gravitation are incredibly high-yield topics. Gravitation is mathematically very similar to Electrostatics, so mastering one provides a dual advantage. Furthermore, do not neglect the Mechanics of Solids and Fluids, focusing heavily on Hooke’s law, surface tension, and Bernoulli’s theorem.

Electrodynamics and Magnetism: This is historically the most heavily tested zone. It encompasses Electrostatics, Current Electricity, Magnetic Effects of Current, and Electromagnetic Induction (EMI) alongside Alternating Currents (AC). Current Electricity consistently carries a very high weightage; ensure your grasp on Kirchhoff's laws, Wheatstone bridges, and potentiometer applications is absolutely flawless.

Optics and Modern Physics: Ray Optics and Wave Optics demand excellent geometric visualization and formula recall. Modern Physics-covering the Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms, Nuclei, and Electronic Devices-is highly predictable. These chapters rely primarily on direct formula applications and yield quick marks.

Chemistry Syllabus Breakdown: The Rank Booster

Chemistry is almost universally acknowledged by successful SRMJEEE candidates as the ultimate scoring subject. Because it features less convoluted mathematics, you can race through this section, saving critical minutes for the tougher Math or Aptitude questions.

Physical Chemistry: This section demands both conceptual understanding and calculation speed. You will encounter chapters like Some Basic Concepts in Chemistry (Mole Concept), Atomic Structure, Thermodynamics, Solutions, Chemical Equilibrium, Redox Reactions, and Chemical Kinetics. You must rigorously practice the numerical aspects of Electrochemistry and Kinetics, ensuring your decimal calculation accuracy is flawless.

Inorganic Chemistry: This branch demands absolute mastery of your standard textbooks. You will study the Classification of Elements and Periodicity, followed immediately by Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure, which is deeply conceptual. Other crucial chapters include the p-Block, d-Block, and f-Block elements, concluding with Coordination Compounds, which consistently yield multiple direct questions.

Organic Chemistry: Rote memorization will not save you here; you need a solid grasp of reaction mechanisms and electronic displacements. Start by deeply understanding General Organic Chemistry (GOC). From there, you will tackle Hydrocarbons, Haloalkanes and Haloarenes, Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers, Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids, and Amines. Biomolecules remains a highly scoring, theory-based chapter that you should revise close to the exam date.

Mathematics Syllabus Breakdown: The Time Consumer

For standard B.Tech aspirants, Mathematics is often the most time-consuming section. The syllabus is vast and requires rigorous analytical endurance.

Calculus: This forms the highest-weightage block in the entire syllabus. It begins with Limits, Continuity, and Differentiability, bridging into Integral Calculus (Definite and Indefinite Integrals), and concluding with Differential Equations. Mastering standard substitution techniques, partial fractions, and the fundamental properties of definite integrals is non-negotiable.

Algebra: Algebra forms another massive chunk of the paper. You will encounter Sets, Relations and Functions, Complex Numbers and Quadratic Equations, Matrices and Determinants, Permutations and Combinations, and Sequence and Series. Matrices and Determinants are algorithmic, predictable, and offer an excellent return on the time invested in learning them.

Coordinate Geometry and Vectors: Coordinate Geometry requires you to memorize standard equations and tangency conditions across Straight Lines, Circles, and Conic Sections (Parabola, Ellipse, Hyperbola). Vectors and Three-Dimensional Geometry rely heavily on spatial visualization (direction ratios, cross/dot products, shortest distance) and yield multiple high-density questions.

Biology Syllabus Breakdown (For Biotechnology Aspirants)

Candidates aiming for B.Tech in Biotechnology or Biomedical Engineering will attempt the Biology section instead of Mathematics. This section demands immense retention of factual data and terminology.

Core Biological Sciences: The SRMJEEE 2027 syllabus for Biology spans Botany and Zoology. Important modules include Diversity in the Living World, Structural Organization in Animals and Plants, and Cell Structure and Function.

Advanced Systems and Genetics: You must focus heavily on Human Physiology and Plant Physiology, as these hold significant weightage. The chapters on Reproduction, Genetics and Evolution, Biology and Human Welfare, and Biotechnology and its Applications are incredibly vital. Ecology and Environment provide straightforward, theory-based questions that are easy to secure.

English and Aptitude: The Deciding Factors

Unlike most traditional engineering entrance exams, the SRMJEEE 2027 syllabus integrates dedicated sections for English and Aptitude. Though they carry fewer marks, they often become the deciding factor between a good rank and a great rank in a highly competitive exam with no negative marking.

  • English (5 Questions): Focuses heavily on reading comprehension, basic grammar, synonyms, and antonyms. You will typically be asked to read a short passage or a dialogue and answer questions based on the inferred context.

  • Aptitude (10 Questions): This section evaluates your fundamental logical and numerical reasoning. Topics include the Number System, Percentages, Profit and Loss, Linear and Quadratic Equations, Direction Sense Test, Ordering and Ranking, and basic Geometry.

Subject-Wise High-Weightage Snapshot

To streamline your study timeline, here is a concise overview of the exam distribution according to the official pattern.

Subject

Number of Questions

Marks Allotted

Total Weightage Strategy

Physics

35

35

High focus on Electrodynamics & Modern Physics.

Chemistry

35

35

Prioritize Coordination Compounds and GOC.

Mathematics / Bio

40

40

Heaviest section; master Calculus and Vectors.

English

5

5

Quick, high-accuracy comprehension reading.

Aptitude

10

10

Rapid numerical problem solving and logic.

Student Preparation Checklist & Tracking

Knowing the syllabus is only half the battle. To optimize your daily schedule, you must track your mock tests and revision cycles systematically. For tracking your mock test scores, time spent per section, and documenting your weak chapters, refer to the Manav-Content WorkBook verbatim to keep your revision highly organized. Avoid the temptation to blindly study out of sequence. Stick to the prescribed curriculum and prioritize previous years' question patterns.

Conclusion

Conquering the entrance exam requires far more than just brute-force studying; it requires a deeply strategic approach to the SRMJEEE 2027 syllabus. By understanding the distinct weightage across Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics (or Biology), and fine-tuning your speed for the English and Aptitude sections, you can seamlessly navigate the RPOM test environment. Build a highly organized daily tracking routine, take advantage of the zero negative marking rule by practicing aggressive time management, and keep refining your weak spots to secure your desired branch at the SRM Institute of Science and Technology.

title: WBCHSE সেমেস্টার III: ফলের সম্ভাব্য সময় ও আপত্তি জমার নতুন সময়সীমা
description: WBCHSE-র পরিকল্পনায় নভেম্বর 2026-এর দ্বিতীয় সপ্তাহের মধ্যে ফল প্রকাশের কথা রয়েছে। আপত্তি জমার সময় বেড়ে 2 নভেম্বর বিকেল 3টা হয়েছে। সরকারি বিজ্ঞপ্তি পড়ুন।
content:
WBCHSE-র বার্ষিক কর্মপরিকল্পনায় দ্বাদশ শ্রেণির সেমেস্টার III-এর ফল নভেম্বর 2026-এর দ্বিতীয় সপ্তাহের মধ্যে অনলাইনে প্রকাশের কথা বলা হয়েছে। নির্দিষ্ট তারিখ বা সময় দেওয়া নেই। সম্ভাব্য সপ্তাহকে ফলের লিঙ্ক চালু হওয়ার ঘোষণা ধরে না নিয়ে আলাদা বিজ্ঞপ্তির অপেক্ষা করুন।

এখানে দুটি বছরের পার্থক্য বোঝা জরুরি। ফল প্রকাশের সময়টি 2026 সালে, কিন্তু বর্তমান আপত্তি-সংক্রান্ত বিজ্ঞপ্তিতে একে উচ্চমাধ্যমিক পরীক্ষা 2027-এর সেমেস্টার III বলা হয়েছে। কোনো বিজ্ঞপ্তি অনুসরণ করার আগে সেমেস্টার ও পরীক্ষাবর্ষ মিলিয়ে নিন।

ফল প্রকাশের সময়সীমা নির্দিষ্ট দিনক্ষণ নয়

যথাযথ বিজ্ঞপ্তি দিয়ে তারিখ পরিবর্তন করা হতে পারে বলেও বার্ষিক পরিকল্পনায় জানানো হয়েছে। পরবর্তী ঘোষণার জন্য সংসদের বিজ্ঞপ্তির পাতা দেখুন। সার্চে দেখা শিরোনাম বা পুরোনো ফলের পাতা একা এই সেমেস্টারের ফল প্রকাশের প্রমাণ নয়।

সংসদের বার্ষিক কর্মপরিকল্পনা · সংসদের বিজ্ঞপ্তি

আপত্তি জমার সময় বেড়ে 2 নভেম্বর

30 অক্টোবর 2026-এর পৃথক বিজ্ঞপ্তিতে প্রয়োজনীয় ফি-সহ আপত্তির আবেদন অনলাইন পোর্টালে জমা দেওয়ার সময় 2 নভেম্বর 2026, 15:00 পর্যন্ত বাড়ানো হয়েছে। সেমেস্টার III উচ্চমাধ্যমিক পরীক্ষা 2027-এর পরীক্ষার্থী এবং এই সেমেস্টার সাপ্লিমেন্টারি হিসেবে দেওয়া পরীক্ষার্থীদের উদ্দেশে বিজ্ঞপ্তিটি জারি হয়েছে।

WBCHSE-র 30 অক্টোবর 2026-এর বিজ্ঞপ্তি: প্রয়োজনীয় ফি-সহ আপত্তি জমার সময় 2 নভেম্বর 2026 বিকেল 3টা পর্যন্ত।

সময়বৃদ্ধির মূল বিজ্ঞপ্তি

এই সময়বৃদ্ধি আপত্তি জমার প্রক্রিয়ার জন্য, ফল প্রকাশের জন্য নয়। বিজ্ঞপ্তিতে 14 অক্টোবর 2026-এর আগের বিজ্ঞপ্তির উল্লেখ রয়েছে; নতুন ফি-র অঙ্ক বা ফলের তারিখ জানানো হয়নি। মূল নির্দেশ পড়ুন এবং সঠিক পোর্টাল বা আবেদন জমার পদ্ধতি নিয়ে স্কুলের সাহায্য নিন।

এখন পড়ুয়াদের করণীয়

আপত্তি জানাতে চাইলে সংশোধিত সময়সীমার আগেই প্রক্রিয়া শেষ করে আবেদন জমা ও ফি দেওয়ার নিশ্চিতকরণ সংরক্ষণ করুন। ফর্ম শুরু করা মানেই চূড়ান্ত জমা হওয়া নয়। ফলের ঘোষণা এলে সংসদের দেওয়া লিঙ্ক ব্যবহার করুন, সেমেস্টার ও পরীক্ষাবর্ষ মিলিয়ে দেখুন এবং স্কুলে আলোচনার জন্য ফল সংরক্ষণ করুন।

অপেক্ষার সময় সেমেস্টার IV-এর পড়াশোনা চালিয়ে যান। বার্ষিক পরিকল্পনায় সেমেস্টার IV ও সেমেস্টার III সাপ্লিমেন্টারির এনরোলমেন্ট 2 থেকে 23 ডিসেম্বর 2026 পর্যন্ত রাখা হয়েছে। স্কুলের নির্দেশ এবং সংসদের পরবর্তী সংশোধন অনুসরণ করুন। সেমেস্টার IV-এর পৃথক নির্দেশিকায় পরিকল্পিত সময়সীমা ও বিষয়ভিত্তিক রুটিনের তফাত ব্যাখ্যা করা রয়েছে।

title: NEET 2026 Exam Cancelled LIVE, Re-NEET Dates, Official Notice, Latest NTA News
description: NEET 2026 Exam Cancelled LIVE; Re-NEET Dates, Official Notice, Latest NTA News
content:
Key Takeaways

  • This guide covers everything about neet 2026 exam cancelled live; - dates, eligibility, process, and fees in one place.
  • Verify all dates on the official exam authority website. They change every year.
  • Apply at least 3 days before the deadline. Portals crash under peak traffic every single year.
  • Category certificates must be current-year valid before you start the application.
  • Save your application number in multiple places immediately after submitting.

Getting neet 2026 exam cancelled live; right is the difference between securing your seat and waiting another year. This guide covers every step - from eligibility to submission - so you can move forward without second-guessing anything.

Complete Exam Calendar 2026

Important Dates and Deadlines

Set reminders at least three days before each deadline. Indian exam portals go down under heavy load on the last day - every year, without exception. Apply early.

Event Tentative Date Your Action
Official Notification Check official site Read the full PDF before applying
Registration Opens Check official site Register on Day 1
Last Date to Apply Check official site Submit 3 days before this
Correction Window After registration closes Only chance to fix errors
Admit Card Release Check official site Download and verify immediately
Exam Date Check official site Reach center 60 minutes early
Result Declaration After exam Keep roll number ready
Counselling Start After result Register separately for counselling
Official source only: Only trust URLs ending in .nic.in or .gov.in for government exam dates. Third-party countdown websites are frequently incorrect and are not updated after official changes.

Eligibility Criteria - Check Every Point First

Verify every eligibility criterion before you start filling the form. A single missed criterion means rejection - even after payment, even after completing the entire application.

Criterion Requirement Important Note
Educational Qualification Class 12 pass or appearing From a recognised board
Minimum Percentage 45-75% in Class 12 (varies) SC/ST typically get 5% relaxation
Subject Combination As per official notification Verify this before applying
Age Limit 17-25 years (varies by exam) Some exams also limit attempts
Category Certificate Required for SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwD OBC-NCL must be current financial year
Nationality Indian citizen NRI/OCI as per specific eligibility clause

Check Your Eligibility - Free Tool

Step-by-Step Application Process

Follow these steps in this exact order. Skipping any step or doing them out of sequence creates problems that are very difficult to fix after submission.

Step 1 - Read the Official Notification PDF First

Before opening the form, download and read the complete official notification PDF from the exam authority website. Every rejection at the verification stage traces back to something the student skipped in this document. It takes 20 minutes and can save you an entire year.

Step 2 - Register With Your Own Credentials

Use your personal email address and mobile number - not a parent's or a friend's. All OTPs, admit card links, result notifications, and counselling updates are sent here. If you lose access, recovery requires formal documentation and takes weeks.

Step 3 - Fill the Form Accurately

Your name must match exactly what is on your Aadhaar card or Class 10 certificate - same spelling, same spacing, same initials. Date of birth must match your board documents. Category must be correct. These are the fields that cannot be changed after submission in most cases and cause the most rejections.

Step 4 - Upload Documents to Specification

Every upload has a specific file format (JPG/PNG), maximum file size, and pixel dimensions. Portals fail silently when specifications are not met - your form looks submitted but the document is missing. Use a scanner app rather than a phone camera. Resize files before uploading.

Step 5 - Pay the Fee and Save Proof Immediately

After successful payment, download your application PDF and payment receipt before closing the browser tab. Screenshot your application number and store it in at least three places. You will need this number for every future step.

If payment fails: Do not pay again immediately. Wait 24-48 hours for the failed transaction to auto-reverse. Contact your bank with the transaction ID if it has not reversed after 48 hours. Duplicate payments are very difficult to get refunded.

Application Fee Structure

Category Fee (Approx.) Mode of Payment
General / OBC-NCL / EWS As per official notification Online only
SC / ST / PwD (Female) Reduced or nil Online only
Female Candidates (General) May be reduced - check notice Online only

Common Mistakes That Lead to Rejection

  • Wrong photo: Must be recent (within 3 months), white background, ears visible, no spectacles, no cap or hat. Phone selfies and WhatsApp profile pictures are rejected consistently.
  • Expired OBC-NCL certificate: Valid for the current financial year only (April to March). If yours predates April 1 of this year, get a fresh one before applying.
  • Applying on the deadline day: Portal load causes timeouts and payment failures every year. Apply three days early - every time.
  • Name mismatch: One extra space, one spelling difference, or a missing initial can flag your application at verification.
  • Not reviewing the form before submitting: Go through every field on the preview page before clicking submit. What is wrong now must be fixed now.

What to Do Right Now

You have everything you need to move forward. Students who get into good colleges are not necessarily smarter - they are better prepared and faster to act on accurate information.

Set your deadline reminders today. Gather your documents this week. Submit your application at least three days before the closing date. Then put your complete focus on preparation.

title: CBSE इयत्ता 10 आणि 12 आसामी परीक्षा 2027: तारीख, विषय संकेतांक आणि वेळ
description: इयत्ता 10च्या आसामी (संकेतांक 014) विषयाचा पेपर 27 फेब्रुवारी 2027 रोजी 10:30 ते 13:30 या वेळेत आहे. इयत्ता 12च्या आसामी (संकेतांक 114) विषयाचा पेपर 3 मार्च 2027 रोजी 10:30 ते 13:30 या वेळेत आहे.
content:
इयत्ता 10च्या आसामी (संकेतांक 014) विषयाचा पेपर 27 फेब्रुवारी 2027 रोजी 10:30 ते 13:30 या वेळेत आहे. इयत्ता 12च्या आसामी (संकेतांक 114) विषयाचा पेपर 3 मार्च 2027 रोजी 10:30 ते 13:30 या वेळेत आहे.

CBSEने 6 नोव्हेंबर 2026 रोजी प्रसिद्ध केलेल्या मुख्य परीक्षेच्या वेळापत्रकात ही नोंद आहे. हे परीक्षेचे वेळापत्रक आहे; गुणपत्रिका नाही. अधिकृत CBSE वेळापत्रक

आसामी पेपरचा कालावधी

इयत्ता आणि विषयसंकेतांकपरीक्षेची तारीखवेळ (IST)कालावधी
इयत्ता 10: Assamese01427 फेब्रुवारी 202710:30 - 13:303 तास
इयत्ता 12: Assamese1143 मार्च 202710:30 - 13:303 तास

केंद्रीय माध्यमिक शिक्षण मंडळ, 6 नोव्हेंबर 2026, पृष्ठ 5: विषय संकेतांक, तारीख आणि वेळ. मूळ PDFमधील हे पृष्ठ पाहा

केंद्रीय माध्यमिक शिक्षण मंडळ, 6 नोव्हेंबर 2026, पृष्ठ 9: विषय संकेतांक, तारीख आणि वेळ. मूळ PDFमधील हे पृष्ठ पाहा

अधिकृत PDFमध्ये आपली नोंद कशी शोधाल?

पृष्ठ 5, 9 वर प्रथम इयत्तेचे शीर्षक पाहा, मग 014, 114 हा संकेतांक शोधा. तारीख किंवा वेळ दाखवणारा एकच रकाना अनेक ओळींना लागू असू शकतो. फोनवर पान मोठे करून पूर्ण ओळ वाचा.

शाळेतील नोंदणीवरचा संकेतांक आणि अभ्यासक्रमाचे पूर्ण नाव तपासा. दुसऱ्या इयत्तेलाही तेच नाव असल्यास फक्त स्वतःच्या इयत्तेची ओळ निवडा.

इंग्रजीच्या पेपरशी तारखांची तुलना

इयत्ता 10चा आसामी (014) पेपर 27 फेब्रुवारी 2027 रोजी आहे. इंग्रजी भाषा आणि साहित्य (184)चा पेपर 26 फेब्रुवारी 2027 रोजी आहे. दोन तारखांमध्ये 1 दिवसांचे अंतर आहे. इयत्ता 12चा आसामी (114) पेपर 3 मार्च 2027 रोजी आहे. English Core (301)चा पेपर 5 मार्च 2027 रोजी आहे. दोन तारखांमध्ये 2 दिवसांचे अंतर आहे.

हे सर्व दिवस अभ्यासासाठी सुट्टीचे असतील असे नाही. आपले इतर पेपरही दिनदर्शिकेत नोंदवून परीक्षा नसलेले मधले दिवस मोजा. सरावासाठी मूळ पेपरइतकाच वेळ ठेवा.

परीक्षा केंद्राकडे निघण्यापूर्वी

पेपर सुरू होण्याची वेळ म्हणजे केंद्रावर पोहोचण्याची अंतिम वेळ नव्हे. उपस्थिती, प्रवेश व कागदपत्रांसाठी प्रवेशपत्र पाहा. तारीख बदलल्याचे समजल्यास बोर्डाच्या सुधारित सूचनेत इयत्ता, संकेतांक व तारीख जुळवा.

केंद्रात संपर्क साधने नेण्यास परवानगी नाही. काय नेता येईल हे ठरवताना CBSEच्या स्वतंत्र सूचना आणि प्रवेशपत्रावरील नियम पाळा.

title: CBSE ધોરણ 10 Foundation Skill for Sciences પરીક્ષા 2027: તારીખ, વિષય કોડ અને સમય
description: ધોરણ 10માં Foundation Skill for Sciences (કોડ 421)નું પેપર 25 ફેબ્રુઆરી 2027ના રોજ 10:30થી 12:30 વાગ્યા સુધી છે.
content:
ધોરણ 10માં Foundation Skill for Sciences (કોડ 421)નું પેપર 25 ફેબ્રુઆરી 2027ના રોજ 10:30થી 12:30 વાગ્યા સુધી છે.

CBSEએ 6 નવેમ્બર 2026ના મુખ્ય પરીક્ષાના સમયપત્રકમાં આ વિગતો આપી છે. આ પરીક્ષાની તારીખો છે; આ PDF ગુણપત્રક નથી. સત્તાવાર CBSE સમયપત્રક

કેન્દ્રીય માધ્યમિક શિક્ષણ બોર્ડ, 6 નવેમ્બર 2026, પાનું 5: વિષય કોડ, તારીખ અને સમય. મૂળ PDFનું આ પાનું જુઓ

સત્તાવાર PDFમાં તમારો વિષય શોધો

પાનું 5 ખોલીને પહેલાં ધોરણનું મથાળું જુઓ અને પછી કોડ 421 શોધો. એક જ તારીખ કે સમયનું ખાનું અનેક વિષયોને લાગુ પડી શકે છે. ફોન પર આખું પાનું મોટું કરીને વાંચો.

શાળાની નોંધણીમાં લખેલા કોડ અને વિષયના પૂરાં નામ સાથે સરખાવો. એક જ નામ બીજા ધોરણમાં પણ હોય તો તમારા ધોરણની પંક્તિ જ પસંદ કરો.

અંગ્રેજીના પેપર સાથે તારીખો સરખાવો

ધોરણ 10માં Foundation Skill for Sciences (421)ની પરીક્ષા 25 ફેબ્રુઆરી 2027ના રોજ છે. English Language and Literature (184)ની પરીક્ષા 26 ફેબ્રુઆરી 2027ના રોજ છે. બંને તારીખ વચ્ચે 1 દિવસનો તફાવત છે.

આ બધા દિવસ વાંચવા માટેની રજા નથી. બીજાં પેપર પણ કૅલેન્ડરમાં લખીને વચ્ચે પરીક્ષા ન હોય એવા જ દિવસો ગણો. પ્રેક્ટિસ કરતી વખતે મૂળ પેપર જેટલો સમય રાખો.

પ્રાયોગિક પરીક્ષાની તારીખ અલગ તપાસો

આ પંક્તિ બોર્ડે નક્કી કરેલા પેપરની છે. પ્રાયોગિક પરીક્ષા, પ્રદર્શન, પ્રોજેક્ટ કે આંતરિક મૂલ્યાંકન હોય તો તેની તારીખ અને જરૂરી સામગ્રી શાળાને પૂછો.

કેન્દ્રમાં સંચાર ઉપકરણો લઈ જવાની છૂટ નથી. બીજું શું લઈ જઈ શકાય તે માટે CBSEની અલગ સૂચનાઓ અને પ્રવેશપત્રના નિયમો પાળો.

यदि आप इस परीक्षा की तैयारी कर रहे हैं, तो यहाँ जानिए IBPS PO 2025 की महत्वपूर्ण तिथियाँ, परीक्षा पैटर्न, कट-ऑफ ट्रेंड्स और तैयारी टिप्स।

title: NATA vs AAT: What is the Difference? Key Comparisons & Career Scope
description: Confused between NATA and AAT? Discover the key differences, eligibility criteria, exam pattern, and career opportunities for both architecture entrance exams. Find out which one suits you best!
content:
NATA vs AAT: What is the Difference? Key Comparisons & Career Scope

Introduction

If you are aspiring to become an architect in India, you might have come across two major entrance exams: NATA (National Aptitude Test in Architecture) and AAT (Architecture Aptitude Test). While both exams assess architectural aptitude, they differ in terms of purpose, eligibility, syllabus, exam pattern, and scope. This article provides an in-depth comparison between NATA vs AAT, helping you understand their key differences and guiding you in making the right career choice.

What is NATA?

NATA (National Aptitude Test in Architecture) is a national-level entrance exam conducted by the Council of Architecture (CoA) for admission to B.Arch (Bachelor of Architecture) programs in various private and government colleges across India. It is one of the most recognized exams for architecture aspirants.

Key Features of NATA:

  • Conducted by: Council of Architecture (CoA)

  • Exam Level: National

  • Mode: Online (Computer-based & Drawing test on paper)

  • Eligibility: 10+2 with Mathematics or Diploma with Mathematics

  • Duration: 3 hours

  • Number of Attempts: Twice a year

  • Colleges Accepting NATA: Private & Government Architecture Colleges (Except IITs, NITs, and SPAs)

What is AAT?

AAT (Architecture Aptitude Test) is conducted by the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) for candidates who clear the JEE Advanced exam and wish to pursue a B.Arch program at IIT Roorkee, IIT Kharagpur, and IIT Varanasi.

Key Features of AAT:

  • Conducted by: IITs

  • Exam Level: National

  • Mode: Offline (Pen & Paper Based)

  • Eligibility: Must qualify JEE Advanced

  • Duration: 3 hours

  • Number of Attempts: Once per year

  • Colleges Accepting AAT: IIT Roorkee, IIT Kharagpur, and IIT BHU

NATA vs AAT: Key Differences

Factors NATA AAT
Conducting Body Council of Architecture (CoA) IITs
Eligibility 10+2 with Mathematics or Diploma with Mathematics Must clear JEE Advanced
Exam Mode Online + Offline Offline (Pen & Paper)
Exam Duration 3 Hours 3 Hours
Subjects Covered Drawing, General Aptitude, PCM Architecture Aptitude, Freehand Drawing, Geometrical Drawing
Number of Attempts Twice a Year Once a Year
Colleges Accepting Score Private and Government Architecture Colleges (Except IITs, NITs, SPAs) IIT Roorkee, IIT Kharagpur, IIT BHU
Career Scope Various architecture careers in India and abroad Highly competitive jobs in core architecture firms, government projects, and research institutions

Exam Syllabus Comparison

NATA Syllabus:

  1. Mathematics: Algebra, Trigonometry, Probability, Coordinate Geometry

  2. General Aptitude: Logical Reasoning, Visual Perception, Analytical Thinking

  3. Drawing Test: Sketching, 3D Visualization, Perspective Drawing

AAT Syllabus:

  1. Freehand Drawing: Sketching of objects and scenes

  2. Geometrical Drawing: Perspective drawing, shape formation

  3. Architectural Awareness: Famous buildings, history of architecture

  4. Imagination & Aesthetic Sensitivity: Creativity, color theory

Which Exam Should You Choose?

  • If you aspire to join IITs for B.Arch, then AAT is the right choice. However, you must first clear JEE Advanced.

  • If you want to get into private or government architecture colleges across India, then NATA is the best option.

  • AAT is more challenging as it is limited to IITs, whereas NATA has a wider scope in terms of the number of colleges accepting the score.

Career Scope After NATA and AAT

Career Opportunities After NATA

Students who qualify NATA and complete their B.Arch degree can pursue careers in:

  • Architectural Design: Work in private architecture firms.

  • Urban Planning: Government roles in town and urban planning.

  • Interior Designing: Specializing in home and commercial space design.

  • Construction Management: Overseeing construction projects.

  • Freelance Architect: Running independent architectural projects.

Career Opportunities After AAT

Since AAT is specifically for IIT graduates, career opportunities include:

  • Top Architecture Firms: Firms like Gensler, Foster + Partners, and Hafeez Contractor.

  • Government Projects: Smart city planning, defense structures, heritage conservation.

  • Research and Academics: Teaching and research in architecture.

  • Entrepreneurship: Starting an independent architecture firm.

Conclusion

Both NATA and AAT are important entrance exams for architecture aspirants, but they cater to different sets of students. If you are aiming for IITs, AAT is your path, but it requires clearing JEE Advanced. If you want a broader range of college options, NATA is the better choice. Understanding your career goals and preparation level will help you decide which exam suits you best.

title: NEET UG 2027 counselling: central vs state portals deadlines explained
description: Key deadlines and practical steps for NEET UG 2027 counselling, detailing how central and state portals differ, when to register, and how to avoid common mistakes for students and parents.
content:
Important takeaway: choose counseling path early and track portal deadlines to secure a seat

As NEET UG 2027 results roll out and counselling approaches begin, students face a pivotal choice between central (federal) and state-level counselling portals. Understanding the timelines, eligibility criteria, and document requirements prevents last-minute scrambles and helps families plan finances and logistics. Below is a clear, action-oriented guide to central vs state counselling, with deadlines and practical steps tailored for Indian students and parents.

What central counselling covers and who should consider it

  • Central counselling typically consolidates seats across participating institutes under a unified process. It is common for seats in national institutes and certain central universities that admit medical students through a common portal.
  • Eligibility often hinges on NEET ranking, category status, and reservations applicable at the central level. Some institutes may have specific eligibility conditions beyond NEET scores.
  • Advantages include standardized documentation requirements and a single application workflow, but seat availability may vary and some high-demand institutes might have limited central allocations.

What state counselling covers and who should consider it

  • State counselling manages seats within a particular state’s medical colleges, dental colleges, and some government or private institutions affiliated to the state university system.
  • States often reserve a portion of seats for in-state students and may offer separate quotas for different categories. State counselling can provide broader seat options within the state and sometimes faster processing times.
  • Benefits include proximity, potential fee differences, and alignment with state-specific admission norms. However, the state process may require separate registrations and particular document sets for each state portal.

Key deadlines to track for NEET UG 2027 counselling

  • Result declaration window: After the NEET UG 2027 exam cycle, results are announced by the governing authority. Note the exact date and time published by the official portal.
  • Registration period: Central and state portals open registrations for counselling within a defined window. This is typically a few days to a couple of weeks after results are released. Delays in registration can reduce seat options.
  • Choice filling and locking: Candidates must fill and confirm their preferred institutes and courses. Complete this step before the stated deadline to avoid losing seats.
  • Seat allotment and reporting: Allocation announcements precede mandatory reporting to the allotted institutes. Timely reporting is essential to secure the seat and initiate admission formalities.

How to decide between central and state portals

  • Rank and reservation alignment: If your category reservations or domicile status align strongly with a state, state counselling can yield favorable outcomes.
  • Geography and costs: Consider travel, hostel, and tuition differences. Some states offer lower fees for in-state students, with variations across colleges.
  • Institute preferences: If a specific central institute is a priority, central counselling may be the best route. If multiple preferred colleges lie within a state, state counselling could maximize choices.

Step-by-step plan for the 2027 cycle

  1. Check NEET UG 2027 result timing and gather essential documents (rank card, identity proofs, domicile/caste certificates if applicable, passport-sized photos, and academic records).
  2. List target institutes under central and state schemas. Note the intake, fees, and reservation rules for each option.
  3. Register on the central portal and the relevant state portals (if targeting both paths). Create backups and keep login credentials secure.
  4. Fill choices thoughtfully: prioritize top institutes while ensuring a realistic mix of backup options in case of seat shifts.
  5. Monitor allotment rounds and be ready for reporting to the allocated institute within the specified window.

Common pitfalls and how to avoid them

  • Missing deadlines: Set calendar reminders for opening and closing dates. Even a day’s delay can close a preferred option.
  • Document mismatches: Ensure names, date of birth, and certificates exactly match NEET records. Inconsistencies can stall processing or lead to seat loss.
  • Overlapping choices: If you apply in both central and state portals, ensure you understand fee structures and software constraints to prevent confusion during allotment.
  • Fee payments: Track payment deadlines and confirm successful fee submission within the portal to avoid seat forfeiture.

What to verify on the official portals

  • Authorized timelines and any provisional dates published for counselling rounds.
  • Seat matrices and state-wise or institute-wise eligibility criteria.
  • Instructions for reporting to allotted institutes, including documents required at admission.

FAQ (visible in content)

What is the main difference between central and state NEET UG counselling?

Central counselling consolidates seats across participating institutes under a unified process, while state counselling manages seats within a specific state’s colleges with state-specific rules and quotas.

When should I start registering for counselling?

Register as soon as the counselling portals open after the results are declared. Do not wait for the last day to avoid technical issues or missing out on seats.

Can I apply to both central and state portals?

Yes, many candidates apply to both. Remember that each portal operates independently, with separate timelines, documentation, and fee structures.

What happens if I miss a deadline?

You may lose eligibility for that rounds of counselling or seat category. Always check the official notices and act quickly to preserve options.

How do I know which seats I’m eligible for?

Eligibility is determined by NEET rank, category reservations, domicile status, and specific institute rules published on the official portals.

Verification note for parents

Parents should keep multiple copies of essential documents, confirm spelling consistency across all records, and be prepared for verification checks during the allotment and admission phases. If there is any doubt about a certificate’s acceptability, refer to the official authority’s guidance and keep copies in both digital and physical forms.

title: ICSE, ISC Date Sheet 2027: Is the 10 AM Start Confirmed?
description: CISCE’s 2027 subject-wise timetable is still awaited. A reported 10 AM start is not confirmed; use the official schedule for paper dates, reading time and reporting instructions.
content:
The ICSE and ISC 2027 subject-wise timetables are still awaited on the CISCE website. A 10 AM start for ICSE papers is not confirmed in the current official notices, so do not plan your exam-day arrival around that reported proposal.

Use the Council’s official website and your school’s instructions for the final dates and timings. ICSE is the Class 10 examination; ISC is Class 12. Each student needs the timetable matching their own class and registered subjects.

Will ICSE papers start at 10 AM?

There is no confirmed 2027 timetable establishing that start time in the Council’s current notices. A proposal or media forecast does not settle the reporting time, reading period or start of answer writing.

These are different instructions. When the timetable is released, read what it says about entering the examination room, receiving the question paper and beginning answers. Do not assume that one clock time covers all three, or that every paper has the same duration.

Find the complete official PDF

Open the relevant 2027 notice from CISCE’s notification archive. Check the examination year and class before saving the linked PDF. If your school forwards a copy, compare its title and pages with the Council’s version.

Keep the full document rather than only a cropped subject list. Instructions and subsequent corrections can affect how you use the schedule. Ask your teacher about a missing or differently named subject instead of selecting a similar paper yourself.

Build a revision calendar once dates arrive

  • Match every registered subject with its paper name and code.

  • Record the examination date, start time and duration separately.

  • Mark practical or assessment directions that require school confirmation.

  • Count the actual gaps between papers before assigning revision days.

Until then, keep a weekly study plan that does not depend on a predicted first examination date. Avoid booking travel solely around an unofficial timetable.

Specimen papers can help now

CISCE has published a notice on specimen question papers and answer keys. Use the resources for your subjects to practise the format and identify weak topics. Their release does not announce the examination timetable.

After a timed attempt, separate content mistakes from unfinished answers. Revise the weak topic before repeating a paper. The DekhoCampus education news page also carries school-examination updates.

title: CLAT 2027: आवेदन की समयसीमा 7 नवंबर तक बढ़ी
description: CLAT 2027 के UG और PG आवेदन 7 नवंबर 2026 रात 11:59 बजे तक जमा करें। भुगतान, बंद हो चुके फ़ील्ड और परीक्षा तारीख के नियम समझें।
content:
CLAT 2027 का अधूरा आवेदन पूरा करने के लिए अब 7 नवंबर 2026, रात 11:59 बजे तक का समय है। राष्ट्रीय विधि विश्वविद्यालयों के संघ ने UG और PG दोनों की ऑनलाइन आवेदन समयसीमा बढ़ाई है। आवेदन पूरा करके अपने खाते में भुगतान की स्थिति भी सुनिश्चित करें।

UG और PG के लिए नई अंतिम तारीख

31 अक्टूबर की अधिसूचना पहले की अंतिम तारीख को बदलती है। इससे आवेदन जमा करने का अतिरिक्त समय मिला है; भुगतान के बाद बंद हो चुके विवरण बदलने की नई सुविधा घोषित नहीं हुई है।

राष्ट्रीय विधि विश्वविद्यालयों का संघ: 31 अक्टूबर 2026 की समयसीमा विस्तार अधिसूचना। मूल अधिसूचना पढ़ें

अपने मौजूदा खाते से आवेदन पूरा करें

आधिकारिक CLAT 2027 पोर्टल पर लॉगिन करें। पहली बार आवेदन करने वाले पंजीकरण के निर्देश अपनाएं। भुगतान से पहले नाम और व्यक्तिगत विवरण प्रमाणपत्रों से मिलाएं; UG या PG चयन, श्रेणी और अपलोड किए दस्तावेज जांचें। आधिकारिक CLAT पोर्टल

पूरा फॉर्म और भुगतान दोनों जरूरी हैं। केवल ड्राफ्ट सेव करना आवेदन जमा करना नहीं है। प्रक्रिया पूरी होने पर खाते में स्थिति देखें तथा आवेदन और भुगतान की प्राप्ति सुरक्षित रखें। असफल या लंबित लेनदेन को अंतिम मिनट तक न छोड़ें।

भुगतान कर चुके हैं तो फ़ील्ड प्रतिबंध देखें

UG निर्देशों के अनुसार आवेदन जमा करने और भुगतान के बाद प्रोग्राम, श्रेणी और BPL फ़ील्ड नहीं बदले जा सकते। समयसीमा बढ़ने से ये प्रतिबंध नहीं हटे हैं। गलती हो तो नया फॉर्म भरने को समाधान मानने से पहले CLAT हेल्पडेस्क से उपलब्ध कार्रवाई पूछें। UG आवेदन निर्देश

जमा करने या भुगतान की समस्या के लिए clat@consortiumofnlus.ac.in पर लिखें या 080-47162020 पर कॉल करें। अधिसूचना में फोन सहायता सोमवार से शनिवार सुबह 10 बजे से शाम 5 बजे तक दी गई है। समस्या स्पष्ट लिखें और जवाब सुरक्षित रखें।

परीक्षा की तैयारी जारी रखें

आवेदन की अवधि बढ़ना परीक्षा टलना नहीं है। UG निर्देशों में परीक्षा 6 दिसंबर 2026 को निर्धारित है, जरूरत पड़ने पर संशोधन के अधीन। आवेदन का काम जल्दी पूरा करें और आगे की सूचना के लिए संघ का पोर्टल देखें।

title: CUET UG 2027 Scorecard: How Universities Use Subjects Differently
description: A high CUET UG 2027 score may not suit every course. Learn how language, domain and General Test papers can affect university eligibility.
content:
CUET UG 2027 scorecard marks won’t work like one universal admission total. A university programme may check a named domain subject, a language paper, the General Test, or a prescribed combination. So a strong overall performance can still leave you ineligible for a preferred course.

Check the paper requirement before you arrange preferences or pay an application fee. That one change in order can save you from choosing courses your scorecard cannot support.

Why the same score can produce different eligibility outcomes

Your scorecard may show separate scores for individual papers, but the 2027 format and display must be confirmed from the applicable official exam material. The participating university’s programme-specific eligibility and merit notice controls the decision, and those rules may change for 2027.

Programme conditionWhat may be checkedPossible problem
Named domain subjectThe required school subjectA high total cannot replace a missing paper
Language conditionAn accepted language paperDomain marks may not satisfy it
General Test conditionThe General Test scoreA course may remain unavailable without it
Paper combinationA stated mix of papersGood marks in the wrong subjects may not help

How to test a course against your scorecard

Use a separate row for every programme, even when two course names sound almost identical. Record the rule, then match it against the papers you actually took.

  1. List your language, domain and General Test papers as they appear on the scorecard.
  2. Write the programme’s required subjects and accepted combinations.
  3. Mark whether each paper affects eligibility, merit calculation, or both.
  4. Keep eligibility and competitiveness separate. Meeting a condition does not promise a seat.
  5. Drop a preference when the required paper is absent, unless the university notice gives a clear alternative.

Illustrative example: why a missing language paper matters

Suppose a student scores well in Economics, Business Studies and the General Test, but does not have the language paper required by Programme A. That student may still appear academically strong, yet Programme A can be unavailable. Programme B might accept the domain subjects without that language condition. This is an illustration, not a confirmed 2027 university rule or named course example.

What to confirm before submitting preferences

Read each university’s applicable 2027 programme notice. Check accepted languages, domain combinations, General Test use and the merit formula. Save the notice with your application records and contact the university admission office if its wording is unclear. The official programme rule, not a coaching chart or a total-score comparison, should decide your final preference list.

Your shortlist becomes easier to judge when you compare colleges using the same priorities.

title: CAT 2026 Admit Card Login: Download Route, Password Help and PDF Checks
description: Use the CAT website’s admit-card login, recover forgotten credentials through the official portal and check your allotted centre and reporting time.
content:
The official CAT 2026 website now provides an “Admit Card / Application Form Download” login and lists 6 November as the start of admit-card downloads. Use that route with your registered User ID and password, then look for the admit-card document inside your account.

A public login link cannot confirm that every individual account has a downloadable card. If your dashboard does not show it, follow the current portal instructions and contact the official help desk rather than assuming your application has been rejected. The website lists the CAT test day as 29 November 2026.

Start at the CAT website, then sign in

Open iimcat.ac.in and choose Login beneath “Admit Card / Application Form Download”. The linked candidate login asks for User ID, password and the displayed captcha. Do not enter those details on a forwarded imitation page or share them with someone offering to download the card for you.

The login page itself has a general application-form heading. Reach it through the CAT website so you can confirm that you are using the route the organiser provides. After signing in, choose the admit-card option shown in your own dashboard and save the PDF when it is available.

Forgot your User ID or password?

The candidate login includes a Forgot User ID/Password link. Use that recovery option and follow its instructions. If the captcha is unclear, the same page provides “Get New Image”. Enter the characters from the newly displayed image.

For a continuing access problem, use the contact information on the official CAT website. It identifies cat2026_helpdesk@iimidr.ac.in as the CAT help-desk email. Explain the error and when it occurs, without sending your password or any one-time code.

Read the allotted details before arranging travel

Once you have the card, compare your name and registration details with your application. Check the test date, session, reporting time, centre name and complete address printed on the document. A familiar venue name is not enough if there are several branches or campuses.

  • Read the document’s instructions for identification, photographs, declarations and permitted items.

  • Check every page of the saved PDF. A blank, cut-off or unreadable printout should be resolved before you travel.

  • Keep a saved copy and make the printout required by the admit-card instructions. Do not assume that a phone screen replaces it.

  • If a personal detail appears wrong, contact the official help desk promptly. Do not edit the issued document yourself.

Keep mock-test practice separate from the admit card

The official mock test helps you learn the on-screen controls. It does not establish your allotted test session or centre. For practice, see the CAT mock-test controls guide; for attendance details, use your own admit card and any later official instructions.

Older download-date announcements can remain in search results. Use the current CAT website and your candidate account for the next step, and avoid treating a predicted release time or another candidate’s experience as proof of your own document status.

title: கர்நாடக PGCET 2026: நவம்பர் 4க்குள் புதிய விருப்பங்களைப் பதிவிடுங்கள்
description: PGCET இறுதி நீட்டிக்கப்பட்ட சுற்றில் பழைய விருப்பங்கள் ஏற்கப்படாது. வைப்புத்தொகைக்கு நவம்பர் 3, விருப்பப் பதிவுக்கு நவம்பர் 4 என்ற தனித்தனி கெடுக்களை அறியுங்கள்.
content:
கர்நாடக PGCET 2026 இறுதி நீட்டிக்கப்பட்ட சுற்றில் பங்கேற்பவர்கள் 4 நவம்பர் 2026 பிற்பகல் 2 மணிக்குள் புதிய விருப்பங்களை சமர்ப்பிக்க வேண்டும். முந்தைய சுற்றின் விருப்பங்கள் கணக்கில் கொள்ளப்படாது என KEA கூறுகிறது. முன்பே சேமித்த பட்டியல் இந்தச் சுற்றில் பங்கேற்பதை உறுதி செய்யாது.

வைப்புத்தொகைக்கான காலம் முதலில் முடிகிறது

படி

அதிகாரப்பூர்வ காலம்

காப்பு வைப்புத்தொகை செலுத்துதல்

31 அக்டோபர் முதல் 3 நவம்பர் 2026 வரை

புதிய விருப்பப் பதிவு

அக்டோபர் 31 பிற்பகல் 2 மணி முதல் நவம்பர் 4 பிற்பகல் 2 மணி வரை

தற்காலிக இட ஒதுக்கீட்டு முடிவு

நவம்பர் 5 பிற்பகல் 1 மணிக்குப் பிறகு

கர்நாடகத் தேர்வு ஆணைய அறிவிப்பு, 29 அக்டோபர் 2026, பக்கம் 2. வைப்புத்தொகைக்கான காலம் முதலில் முடிகிறது.

காப்பு வைப்புத்தொகை ₹35,000; SC/ST விண்ணப்பதாரர்களுக்கு ₹10,000. ஏற்கெனவே கல்லூரியில் ஆஜராகி சேர்ந்தவர்கள் இந்த வைப்புத்தொகையைச் செலுத்தத் தேவையில்லை. செலுத்த வேண்டியவர்களுக்கு இடம் ஒதுக்கப்பட்டால் அது கட்டணத்தில் சரிசெய்யப்படும். பின்னர் மீதிக் கட்டணம் அல்லது கல்லூரியில் ஆஜராகும் நிபந்தனையைத் தவறினால் அறிவிப்பின்படி தொகை பறிமுதல் மற்றும் அபராதம் ஏற்படலாம்.

விருப்பங்களை நிரப்புமுன் தகுதியைப் பாருங்கள்

முன்பு இடம் ஒதுக்கப்படாதவர்கள் காலியிடங்களுக்குப் பங்கேற்க அறிவிப்பு அனுமதிக்கிறது. கல்லூரியில் ஏற்கெனவே ஆஜரானவர்கள் மேம்பட்ட இடத்தை நாடலாம். அபராதம் செலுத்திய பின் இடத்தை ரத்து செய்தவர்களுக்கும் நிபந்தனைகள் உள்ளன.

அக்டோபர் 13-15இல் இடம் கிடைத்தும் பணம் செலுத்தவோ கல்லூரியில் ஆஜராகவோ செய்யவில்லை என்றால், தொடருமுன் தகுதிப் பகுதியைக் கவனமாகப் படியுங்கள். சிறப்பு ஆஜராகும் வாய்ப்பு அக்டோபர் 31 மாலை 6 மணியுடன் முடிந்துவிட்டது. உள்நுழைவுப் பக்கம் திறப்பதைத் தகுதி உறுதிப்பாடாகக் கருத வேண்டாம்.

ஏற்கத் தயாராக உள்ள விருப்பங்களை வரிசைப்படுத்துங்கள்

KEA PGCET பக்கத்தைத் திறந்து பொருத்தமான இட விவரங்களைப் பார்த்து, உண்மையான முன்னுரிமை வரிசையில் புதிய விருப்பங்களைப் பதிவிடுங்கள். சேமிக்குமுன் ஒவ்வொரு விருப்பத்தின் படிப்பையும் கல்லூரியையும் சரிபாருங்கள். இறுதியாகச் சமர்ப்பித்த பட்டியல் மற்றும் தேவைப்படும் வைப்புத்தொகை ரசீதை வைத்திருங்கள்.

நவம்பர் 5 முடிவு தற்காலிகமானது எனக் குறிப்பிடப்பட்டுள்ளது. அதன் வெளியீட்டுடன் சேர்க்கை முடிந்ததாகக் கருதாமல் அடுத்த அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வழிமுறைகளைப் பின்பற்றுங்கள். நீட்டிக்கப்பட்ட சுற்று வழிகாட்டி முந்தைய அறிவிப்பையும் வைப்புத்தொகை நிபந்தனைகளையும் விளக்குகிறது.
