title: Class 12 Retirement of Partner Questions | Accountancy Commerce CBSE 2026 Important Numericals
description: Learn Class 12 Retirement of Partner questions with easy numericals, formulas, and solved examples for CBSE 2026. High-weightage topics explained simply to help students score maximum marks.
content:
Introduction: Retirement of Partner in Class 12 Accountancy

In Class 12 Accountancy (Commerce CBSE), Retirement of Partner is one of the most high-weightage and scoring chapters in Partnership Accounts.
Students often find this chapter difficult due to multiple calculations, but with proper practice, it becomes one of the easiest topics to score full marks.

This article includes:

  • Important retirement of partner questions

  • Step-by-step numericals

  • Key formulas

  • Exam tips

  • FAQs for CBSE 2026

What is Retirement of a Partner?

Retirement of a partner means when an existing partner leaves the partnership firm voluntarily, and the remaining partners continue the business.

Main adjustments required:

  • New profit-sharing ratio

  • Gaining ratio

  • Treatment of goodwill

  • Revaluation of assets and liabilities

  • Settlement of retiring partner’s capital

High Weightage Topics in Retirement of Partner (CBSE 2026)

Topic Marks Weightage Difficulty
Gaining Ratio 2–4 Marks Easy
Goodwill Treatment 4–6 Marks Medium
Revaluation Account 4–6 Marks Medium
Capital Adjustment 6–8 Marks Hard
Retiring Partner’s Loan Account 2–4 Marks Easy

These topics are easy-to-score units if practiced well.

Important Formulas for Retirement of Partner

Concept Formula
New Share = Old Share × Remaining Ratio  
Gaining Ratio = New Share – Old Share  
Retiring Partner’s Share of Goodwill = Total Goodwill × Retiring Partner’s Share  
New Capital = Total Capital × New Ratio  

Important Class 12 Retirement of Partner Questions (CBSE Style)

1. Gaining Ratio Question

A, B, and C are partners sharing profits in the ratio 3:2:1. C retires. A and B decide to share profits equally.
Find the gaining ratio of A and B.

Solution:
Old Ratio = 3:2
New Ratio = 1:1
A’s gain = 1/2 – 3/5 = 5/10 – 6/10 = –1/10 (Loss)
B’s gain = 1/2 – 2/5 = 5/10 – 4/10 = 1/10

Gaining Ratio = 0 : 1

2. Goodwill Treatment Question

A, B, and C share profits in 4:3:3. C retires. Firm’s goodwill is valued at ₹60,000. Pass journal entries.

Retiring partner’s share = 60,000 × 3/10 = ₹18,000
Remaining partners bring cash in gaining ratio.

3. Revaluation Account Question

On retirement of B, assets were revalued and liabilities increased. Prepare Revaluation Account and show journal entries.

This is a very common 6–8 mark question in CBSE papers.

4. Capital Adjustment Question

A, B, and C share profits in 5:3:2. C retires. Total capital of new firm is ₹1,00,000.
Calculate new capitals of A and B.

5. Retiring Partner Loan Account

If retiring partner’s dues are not paid immediately, show treatment in Retiring Partner Loan Account.

Step-by-Step Process to Solve Retirement Numericals

Step 1: Calculate New Profit Sharing Ratio

Step 2: Find Gaining Ratio

Step 3: Pass Goodwill Journal Entries

Step 4: Prepare Revaluation Account

Step 5: Prepare Partners’ Capital Accounts

Step 6: Prepare Balance Sheet

Exam Tips to Score High in Retirement of Partner

✔ Learn formulas by heart
✔ Practice journal entries daily
✔ Solve at least 10 numericals from NCERT
✔ Focus on goodwill and capital adjustment
✔ Use proper format in accounts

These tricks help students score 10–15 marks easily.

Conclusion

Retirement of Partner is one of the most important and scoring chapters in Class 12 Accountancy CBSE 2026.
With regular practice of numericals, journal entries, and formats, students can easily secure full marks.
Focus on high-weightage units like goodwill, revaluation, and capital adjustment for fast revision before exams.

title: Operation Theatre Technology Course After 12th: Complete Eligibility, Fees & Career Scope
description: Explore the best Operation Theatre Technology courses after 12th. Discover B.Sc and diploma programs, eligibility, fee structures, and the booming paramedical career scope.
content:
If you are fascinated by the medical field and want to work inside the high-stakes environment of a surgical room without spending years pursuing an MBBS, an Operation Theatre Technology (OTT) course after 12th is your ideal academic pathway.

Surgeons do not operate alone. Behind every successful complex surgery is a highly trained team of allied healthcare professionals managing the sterile environment, organizing surgical instruments, and assisting with anesthesia equipment. Operation Theatre Technologists (also known as OT Technicians) are the backbone of modern surgical wards. As the healthcare sector expands with multi-specialty hospitals and advanced surgical clinics, the demand for certified allied healthcare workers is surging.

This comprehensive guide covers everything a science student needs to know about entering this recession-proof medical sector-from undergraduate degrees and diplomas to academic eligibility, tuition fees, and long-term career prospects.

Top Educational Pathways After Class 12

Students can choose between comprehensive multi-year university degrees or short-term diplomas depending on their career goals and timeline. A bachelor's degree is highly recommended for those aiming for senior supervisory roles in large hospitals.

Course Level

Popular Program Options

Typical Duration

Core Focus & Educational Objectives

Undergraduate Degree

B.Sc. in Operation Theatre Technology (B.Sc OTT)

3 to 4 Years (includes internship)

Comprehensive training in surgical procedures, advanced anesthesia machinery, and clinical management.

Undergraduate Diploma

Diploma in Operation Theatre Technology (DOTT)

2 Years

Fast-tracked, skill-oriented learning focusing on basic sterilization, equipment handling, and surgical assistance.

Certification Programs

Certificate in OT Technician

6 to 12 Months

Entry-level, rapid training for basic hospital ward support and instrument sterilization.

Core Eligibility Criteria and Admission Pathways

Securing admission into a paramedical course like OTT requires a foundational understanding of the sciences, though it does not carry the extreme competitive pressure of traditional medical entrance exams.

  • Academic Stream: Candidates must have completed their Class 12 board examinations in the Science stream.

  • Mandatory Subjects: Physics, Chemistry, and Biology (PCB) is the standard requirement. Some universities also accept students with a PCM (Mathematics) background for paramedical technology courses, though Biology is heavily preferred.

  • Minimum Aggregate Marks: A minimum aggregate of 50% in core science subjects is generally required for general category candidates (45% for SC/ST/OBC categories).

  • Entrance Examinations:

    • Is NEET Required? No. The NEET examination is specifically for MBBS, BDS, and AYUSH courses. B.Sc OTT does not require NEET.

    • University/State Level Exams: Many states conduct common paramedical entrance tests. Additionally, top private institutes like CMC Vellore, Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MAHE), and Jamia Hamdard conduct their own institutional aptitude tests.

    • Merit-Based Admissions: A large number of government and private colleges offer direct admission based strictly on Class 12 board exam percentages.

Course Fee Structure Overview

The financial investment for an Operation Theatre Technology program is significantly lower than traditional medical degrees, offering an excellent return on investment (ROI).

Institution / Course Type

Estimated Total Fees

Key Considerations

Government Medical Colleges (B.Sc)

₹20,000 to ₹80,000

Highly subsidized fees, massive clinical exposure in government hospitals, but competitive merit cutoffs.

Private Universities (B.Sc)

₹1,50,000 to ₹4,50,000

State-of-the-art simulation labs, modern surgical equipment training, and dedicated placement cells.

Diploma in OTT (DOTT)

₹40,000 to ₹1,20,000

Highly cost-effective; gets you into the workforce quickly as a junior technician.

Core Syllabus: What Will You Learn?

A professional OTT curriculum transitions students from basic human anatomy to handling high-tech life-support systems. During a B.Sc program, you will undergo rigorous clinical rotations and master:

  • Anatomy and Physiology: Detailed study of the human body, organ systems, and how surgical interventions affect them.

  • Infection Control & Sterilization: The critical science of maintaining a 100% sterile environment, autoclaving surgical tools, and preventing post-operative infections.

  • Anesthesia Technology: Assisting anesthesiologists with preparing medical gases, monitoring patient vitals (heart rate, blood pressure), and managing ventilators.

  • Surgical Instruments & Procedures: Learning the names, functions, and handling protocols of hundreds of specific surgical tools used in neurosurgery, orthopedics, and cardiology.

  • Ethics and Patient Care: Preparing patients psychologically and physically before they are wheeled into the operating room.

Career Scope, Job Profiles, and Salary Outlook

Graduating with an Operation Theatre Technology degree opens doors across government district hospitals, massive private healthcare chains (like Apollo, Max, Fortis), emergency trauma centers, and specialized surgical day-care clinics.

Job Profile

Core Responsibilities

Average Starting Salary (LPA)

OT Technician / Technologist

Prepares the operating room, arranges sterile instruments, and assists surgeons directly during procedures.

₹2.5 to ₹4.5 LPA

Anesthesia Assistant

Helps the anesthesiologist prepare doses, monitors vital signs during surgery, and manages post-op recovery.

₹3.0 to ₹5.0 LPA

Infection Control Specialist

Ensures strict hygiene and sterilization protocols are maintained across the surgical and ICU wards.

₹3.0 to ₹4.5 LPA

Senior OT Manager

Manages the scheduling of multiple operating rooms, oversees junior technicians, and handles equipment inventory.

₹5.5 to ₹9.0 LPA

Salary Growth: In the allied healthcare sector, experience dictates your paycheck. A fresher might start at ₹3.0 Lakhs per annum, but with 5 to 7 years of hands-on surgical experience, OT Technologists routinely command ₹6.0 Lakhs to ₹10.0 Lakhs per annum. Furthermore, experienced Indian paramedical staff are in massive demand in the UK, Canada, and Gulf countries, offering vastly higher international remuneration.

Conclusion

Pursuing an Operation Theatre Technology course after 12th is a highly strategic choice for science students who want a stable, respected, and fast-paced career in healthcare. The field offers the adrenaline of the surgical ward without the grueling decade-long commitment required to become a surgeon. By securing admission into a reputed B.Sc program, mastering advanced surgical machinery, and completing your mandatory clinical internships with dedication, you can step into a vital, life-saving profession with excellent job security and global employability.

description: MCC ತಾತ್ಕಾಲಿಕ ಪಟ್ಟಿ ಪ್ರವೇಶವನ್ನು ಖಚಿತಪಡಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಅಕ್ಟೋಬರ್ 30ರ ಸೂಚನೆ ಓದಿ, ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯಾದ ಕಾಲೇಜಿಗೆ ಹೋಗುವ ಮೊದಲು ಅಂತಿಮ ಫಲಿತಾಂಶ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ.
content:
NEET MDS 2026 ಮೂರನೇ ಸುತ್ತಿನ ತಾತ್ಕಾಲಿಕ ಪಟ್ಟಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸೀಟು ಕಾಣಿಸುವುದೇ ಅಂತಿಮ ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲ. ಅಕ್ಟೋಬರ್ 30ರ MCC ಸೂಚನೆಯ ಪ್ರಕಾರ, ಅಂತಿಮ ಫಲಿತಾಂಶ ಪ್ರಕಟವಾದ ನಂತರವೇ ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯಾದ ಕಾಲೇಜನ್ನು ಸಂಪರ್ಕಿಸಬೇಕು. ದಾಖಲಾತಿಗಾಗಿ ಹೊರಡುವ ಮೊದಲು ಫಲಿತಾಂಶದ ಪ್ರಕಾರವನ್ನು ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ.

ತಾತ್ಕಾಲಿಕ ಪಟ್ಟಿಯ ಅರ್ಥವೇನು?

ಈ ಪಟ್ಟಿ ಸೂಚನಾತ್ಮಕವಾಗಿದ್ದು ಬದಲಾಗಬಹುದು ಎಂದು MCC ತಿಳಿಸಿದೆ. ಅದರಲ್ಲಿ ಕಾಣಿಸುವ ಸೀಟಿನ ಮೇಲೆ ಅಭ್ಯರ್ಥಿಗೆ ಹಕ್ಕು ಉಂಟಾಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ತಾತ್ಕಾಲಿಕ ದಾಖಲೆಯ ಸ್ಕ್ರೀನ್‌ಶಾಟ್ ಅಂತಿಮ ಹಂಚಿಕೆಗೆ ಅಥವಾ ನಂತರದ ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಸೂಚನೆಗಳಿಗೆ ಪರ್ಯಾಯವಲ್ಲ.

ವೈದ್ಯಕೀಯ ಕೌನ್ಸೆಲಿಂಗ್ ಸಮಿತಿಯ 30 ಅಕ್ಟೋಬರ್ 2026ರ ಸೂಚನೆ. MCC ಮೂಲ ಸೂಚನೆ ಓದಿ.

ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸ ತಿಳಿಸುವ ಗಡುವು ಮುಗಿದಿದೆ

ಅಭ್ಯರ್ಥಿ ಲಾಗಿನ್‌ನ Candidates Grievances And Query Redressal System ಮೂಲಕ 31 ಅಕ್ಟೋಬರ್ 2026 ಬೆಳಗ್ಗೆ 10 ಗಂಟೆಯವರೆಗೆ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸ ತಿಳಿಸಲು ಸೂಚನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಅವಕಾಶವಿತ್ತು. ಆ ಗಡುವು ಮುಗಿದಿದೆ. ಇಮೇಲ್, ಹೊಸ ದೂರು ಅಥವಾ ಸುದ್ದಿ ಶೀರ್ಷಿಕೆಯಿಂದ ಗಡುವು ವಿಸ್ತರಿಸಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಭಾವಿಸಬೇಡಿ. ಈಗಾಗಲೇ ದೂರು ಸಲ್ಲಿಸಿದ್ದರೆ ಸ್ವೀಕೃತಿಯನ್ನು ಉಳಿಸಿ, ಲಾಗಿನ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಬಂದ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಅನುಸರಿಸಿ.

ಈಗ ಅಂತಿಮ ಫಲಿತಾಂಶ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ

  1. MCC MDS ಕೌನ್ಸೆಲಿಂಗ್ ಪುಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಮೂರನೇ ಸುತ್ತಿನ ಫಲಿತಾಂಶದ ಪೂರ್ಣ ಹೆಸರನ್ನು ಓದಿ. ಪ್ರಸ್ತುತ ಲಿಂಕ್ ಮಾಡಿರುವ ಸೂಚನೆ ತಾತ್ಕಾಲಿಕ ಫಲಿತಾಂಶಕ್ಕೆ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸಿದೆ.

  2. MCC ಅಂತಿಮ ಫಲಿತಾಂಶ ಪ್ರಕಟಿಸಿದಾಗ ಹಳೆಯ ಸ್ಕ್ರೀನ್‌ಶಾಟ್ ನಂಬದೆ ನಿಮ್ಮ ದಾಖಲೆಯನ್ನು ಮತ್ತೆ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ.

  3. ನಂತರ ಪ್ರಯಾಣ ಅಥವಾ ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಶುಲ್ಕ ಪಾವತಿಸುವ ಮೊದಲು ಪ್ರಸ್ತುತ ವರದಿ ಮಾಡುವ ಸೂಚನೆಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯಾದ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಯ ಅಗತ್ಯಗಳನ್ನು ಓದಿ.

MCC MDS ಕೌನ್ಸೆಲಿಂಗ್ ಪುಟ

ಅರ್ಜಿ ವಿವರಗಳು, ಉಳಿಸಿದ ಆಯ್ಕೆಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ದೂರು ಸ್ವೀಕೃತಿಯನ್ನು ಒಟ್ಟಿಗೆ ಇಡಿ. ಹಿಂದಿನ ಮೂರನೇ ಸುತ್ತಿನ ನೋಂದಣಿ ಮಾರ್ಗದರ್ಶಿ ಹಿಂದಿನ ಹಂತವನ್ನು ವಿವರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ನೋಂದಣಿ ದಿನಾಂಕಗಳಿಂದ ಹಂಚಿಕೆ ಅಂತಿಮವಾಗಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಖಚಿತವಾಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

ಮೂರನೇ ಸುತ್ತಿನ ನೋಂದಣಿ ಮಾರ್ಗದರ್ಶಿ

title: NMAT 2026 Slot Booking: Admit Card Timing and Retake Rules
description: Check your booked NMAT appointment, when to download the admit card and how the seven-day retake gap affects your exam plans.
content:
Your NMAT admit card is not available immediately after booking. GMAC makes it available seven days before your scheduled exam, so the date that matters is your own appointment. Check that appointment in your account before planning travel or a retake.

The regular registration and scheduling window ended on 25 October 2026. GMAC lists exam delivery from 2 November to 20 December 2026 on its NMAT exam page. Do not assume that an unfinished booking can still be completed after the deadline unless GMAC announces another opportunity.

Check that you have an exam appointment

Paying the registration fee and booking a seat are separate steps. Under GMAC's scheduling instructions, candidates use the booking option in their account after registration and payment, then select an available centre, date and time. Seats depend on availability.

If you have already booked, compare the appointment details in your dashboard with the confirmation email. Note the exact centre address and start time. If you paid but cannot find an appointment, contact NMAT support; a payment receipt alone should not be treated as proof that a seat is booked. Our NMAT registration and scheduling deadline guide explains the distinction.

Download the card for your booked date

The official admit-card instructions require a fresh printed copy for each attempt. The seven-day download rule is tied to your exam date, not one common release date for all candidates. For example, a 2 November appointment reaches that point on 26 October; a later appointment has a later download date.

Check that the photograph is clear and matches the identification you will carry. For a blank or unclear photograph, contact NMAT candidate support before the exam. Do not leave a name or photograph mismatch to be resolved at the centre.

Plan a retake around the seven-day gap

GMAC's registration and retake rules allow up to three attempts in a testing cycle. After a valid score, you may book the next attempt immediately, but the next exam must be at least seven days after the previous attempt. An available booking button does not remove that minimum gap.

Leave room within the exam window for both preparation and an available seat. Before paying for another attempt, read the admissions rules of each business school you are applying to. Do not assume every institution will use your highest score or accept a later attempt.

Prepare for check-in at the centre

GMAC asks test-centre candidates to arrive at least 45 minutes before the appointment. Carry the printed admit card and an accepted original, unexpired photo ID. Its test-centre checklist lists Aadhaar, an Indian passport, PAN card, voter ID and driving licence among the accepted identification documents.

Check the route to the exact address on your appointment and allow extra time for travel. Keep your confirmation details accessible, but follow the admit card and official checklist for what must be presented at check-in.
author: Geethika Reddy
meta_title: NMAT 2026 Slot Booking: Admit Card and Retake Rules
meta_description: Check your NMAT 2026 appointment, the seven-day admit-card download rule, retake gap and documents needed at the test centre.

title: GATE 2027 Robotics and Automation Paper Strategy: Interdisciplinary Syllabus Breakdown and PSU Career Scope
description: Comprehensive guide for GATE 2027 Robotics and Automation paper covering interdisciplinary syllabus breakdown, preparation strategy, MTech admissions, and PSU career opportunities.
content:
The Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering (GATE) 2027 provides a significant gateway for engineering graduates seeking advanced research and public sector employment in India. Among the specialized papers, Robotics and Automation stands out as a prime choice for candidates from mechanical, electrical, electronics, computer science, and instrumentation disciplines. Understanding the interdisciplinary syllabus breakdown and structuring a disciplined preparation timeline is essential for success.

Understanding the GATE 2027 Robotics and Automation Syllabus Structure

The GATE Robotics and Automation paper evaluates fundamental engineering principles alongside specialized topics. The curriculum bridges multiple traditional branches, requiring candidates to build strong cross-domain competence.

Core Subject Segments

  • General Aptitude and Engineering Mathematics: Covers linear algebra, calculus, differential equations, numerical methods, probability, statistics, spatial aptitude, and analytical reasoning.
  • Robotic Kinematics and Dynamics: Focuses on rigid body transformations, Denavit-Hartenberg (D-H) parameters, forward and inverse kinematics, velocity kinematics, Jacobians, trajectory planning, Newton-Euler dynamics, and Euler-Lagrange formulations.
  • Sensors, Actuators, and Signal Processing: Includes operational amplifiers, analog and digital sensors, encoders, resolvers, vision systems, pneumatic and hydraulic actuators, electric drives, and signal conditioning.
  • Control Systems and Automation: Encompasses transfer functions, transient response analysis, frequency response methods, stability analysis (Routh-Hurwitz, Nyquist, Bode), state-space modeling, PID controllers, PLCs, and SCADA architectures.
  • AI, Computer Vision, and Programming: Features fundamental algorithms, object recognition, image processing, kinematic simulation, ROS concepts, path planning, and basic machine learning techniques.

Step-by-Step Preparation Strategy for GATE 2027

Mastering an interdisciplinary paper requires a structured study plan spanning several months.

Phase 1: Foundation Building (Months 1 to 4)

Focus on foundational topics such as Engineering Mathematics, Basic Control Systems, and Linear Circuit Theory. Candidates from non-mechanical backgrounds should prioritize rigid body mechanics and dynamic modeling, while mechanical students must master operational amplifiers and digital electronics fundamentals.

Phase 2: Core Topic Mastery (Months 5 to 8)

Dedicate this phase to D-H parameters, inverse kinematics equations, PID tuning techniques, state-space representations, and sensor interfaces. Solve standard textbook problems to solidify conceptual clarity.

Phase 3: Revision and Mock Testing (Months 9 to 12)

Shift focus to full-length test series, timed practice sessions, and revision of short notes. Regularly practice using the GATE virtual calculator to build speed and accuracy.

MTech Admissions and PSU Career Opportunities

Qualifying the Robotics and Automation paper opens diverse academic and professional pathways for engineering graduates.

MTech and Higher Education Prospects

Top Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), National Institutes of Technology (NITs), and Indian Institute of Science (IISc) offer specialized post-graduate programs in Mechatronics, Robotics, Autonomous Systems, and Cyber-Physical Systems. A valid GATE score also enhances applications for direct PhD admissions in premier research organizations.

PSU Recruitment and Industrial Scope

Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) in defense, aerospace, power generation, and heavy manufacturing increasingly seek engineers skilled in automation and modern control systems. Organizations involved in defense research, space exploration, nuclear power, and advanced manufacturing evaluate GATE performance during recruitment drives. Candidates should periodically verify specific eligibility criteria on official PSU recruitment portals.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is eligible to appear for the GATE 2027 Robotics and Automation paper?

Candidates holding a bachelor's degree in engineering or technology (B.E./B.Tech) or those currently in their final or pre-final year of undergraduate programs in relevant disciplines are eligible to apply.

Which engineering branches benefit most from choosing this paper?

Students from Mechanical, Electrical, Electronics and Communication, Computer Science, and Instrumentation Engineering benefit significantly due to the strong overlap between their core curriculum and the interdisciplinary syllabus.

Can a GATE score in Robotics and Automation qualify candidates for PSU jobs?

Yes, several public sector undertakings and research organizations utilize valid GATE scores to recruit engineers for technical roles related to automation, control systems, and advanced robotics.

How should non-mechanical engineering students approach robot kinematics and dynamics?

Non-mechanical students should begin with basic vector mechanics, matrix transformations, and rigid body dynamics before progressing to Denavit-Hartenberg representations and Lagrangian formulations.

What standard reference books are recommended for this paper?

Standard texts include Introduction to Robotics by John J. Craig for kinematics and dynamics, Modern Control Engineering by Katsuhiko Ogata, and Sensor Technology Handbooks for instrumentation.

title: Tamil Nadu NEET PG Rank List 2026: Check Your Quota and Addendum
description: Government and management quota rank lists are available. Match your application number, check the addendum and keep rank-list status separate from allotment.
content:
Tamil Nadu’s provisional NEET PG rank lists for the 2026-27 session are available for government and management quota applicants. Open the list for the quota you applied under, then search using your application number or NEET roll number. Finding your name is a step in counselling; it is not a college allotment.

Use the list that matches your application

The Selection Committee has separate PDFs for government quota PG degree and diploma candidates and management quota candidates. Government-quota entries include general rank, community rank, service status and incentive information, while the management-quota document shows its own rank and marks fields. Compare the labels before comparing numbers.

The official site also lists DNB broad-specialty and post-MBBS diploma candidates separately for service applicants. Do not use a DNB list, an MDS dental list or an undergraduate medical list to decide your MD or MS counselling status.

Read the addendum alongside the original PDF

A government-quota PG rank-list addendum is also listed on the Selection Committee website. Check it along with the original list, especially if you cannot locate your application in the earlier PDF. The site publishes separate eligibility lists for categories such as NRI, minority, PwD and the specified CMC seat routes. Read the notice that applies to your claim rather than assuming the general rank list settles every category condition.

Compare the entry with your own records

Check the application number, NEET roll number, name, marks and any category or service details shown for you. Keep your submitted application, scorecard and supporting certificates beside the PDF. If something appears inconsistent, use the Selection Committee’s current instructions and official contact route to raise the issue. Keep a copy of what you submit.

A name-only search can miss spelling differences or return someone else. An application or roll number is a better way to locate your entry, followed by a check of the remaining details.

Prepare choices without assuming a seat is confirmed

Build a shortlist of course and college combinations you would genuinely accept. Check the applicable fee, bond and document conditions in the current prospectus before ordering those preferences. Follow the separate counselling schedule and vacancy notices for registration, choice filling and allotment. This rank-list release does not itself announce your reporting deadline or guarantee admission.

title: CAT 2026 ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪತ್ರ: ಅಧಿಕೃತ ಲಾಗಿನ್, ಪಾಸ್‌ವರ್ಡ್ ನೆರವು ಮತ್ತು PDF ಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ
description: CAT ಅಧಿಕೃತ ವೆಬ್‌ಸೈಟ್ ಮೂಲಕ ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪತ್ರದ ಲಾಗಿನ್ ತೆರೆಯಿರಿ. ಮರೆತ ವಿವರಗಳನ್ನು ಮರಳಿ ಪಡೆಯುವುದು ಮತ್ತು ಪರೀಕ್ಷಾ ಕೇಂದ್ರ, ಹಾಜರಾತಿ ಸಮಯ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸುವುದು ಹೇಗೆ ಎಂದು ತಿಳಿಯಿರಿ.
content:
CAT 2026 ಅಧಿಕೃತ ವೆಬ್‌ಸೈಟ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಈಗ “Admit Card / Application Form Download” ಲಾಗಿನ್ ಇದೆ. ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪತ್ರ ಡೌನ್‌ಲೋಡ್ ಆರಂಭದ ದಿನವಾಗಿ ನವೆಂಬರ್ 6 ಅನ್ನು ಸೂಚಿಸಿದೆ. ನೋಂದಾಯಿತ User ID ಮತ್ತು ಪಾಸ್‌ವರ್ಡ್ ಬಳಸಿ ಈ ಮಾರ್ಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಾಗಿನ್ ಮಾಡಿ, ನಿಮ್ಮ ಖಾತೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪತ್ರದ ಆಯ್ಕೆ ನೋಡಿ.

ಸಾರ್ವಜನಿಕ ಲಾಗಿನ್ ಲಿಂಕ್ ಇರುವುದರಿಂದ ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಬ್ಬರ ಖಾತೆಯಲ್ಲೂ ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪತ್ರ ಸಿದ್ಧವಾಗಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಖಚಿತವಾಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ನಿಮ್ಮ ಡ್ಯಾಶ್‌ಬೋರ್ಡ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಪತ್ರ ಕಾಣದಿದ್ದರೆ ಪೋರ್ಟಲ್ ಸೂಚನೆಗಳನ್ನು ಅನುಸರಿಸಿ ಅಧಿಕೃತ ಸಹಾಯ ಕೇಂದ್ರವನ್ನು ಸಂಪರ್ಕಿಸಿ. ಅರ್ಜಿ ತಿರಸ್ಕೃತವಾಗಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಊಹಿಸಬೇಡಿ. ವೆಬ್‌ಸೈಟ್ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಯ ದಿನವನ್ನು 29 ನವೆಂಬರ್ 2026 ಎಂದು ತಿಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

CAT ವೆಬ್‌ಸೈಟ್‌ನಿಂದಲೇ ಲಾಗಿನ್ ಮಾಡಿ

ಅಧಿಕೃತ ತಾಣದಲ್ಲಿ “Admit Card / Application Form Download” ಅಡಿಯ Login ಆಯ್ಕೆಮಾಡಿ. ಅಲ್ಲಿನ ಅಭ್ಯರ್ಥಿ ಲಾಗಿನ್ ಪುಟ User ID, ಪಾಸ್‌ವರ್ಡ್ ಮತ್ತು ಪರದೆಯ ಕ್ಯಾಪ್ಚಾ ಕೇಳುತ್ತದೆ. ಯಾರೋ ಕಳುಹಿಸಿದ ನಕಲಿ ಪುಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಈ ವಿವರಗಳನ್ನು ನಮೂದಿಸಬೇಡಿ; ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪತ್ರ ಡೌನ್‌ಲೋಡ್ ಮಾಡಿಕೊಡುವುದಾಗಿ ಹೇಳುವವರಿಗೂ ನೀಡಬೇಡಿ.

ಲಾಗಿನ್ ಪುಟದ ಶೀರ್ಷಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಅರ್ಜಿ ನಮೂನೆಯ ಉಲ್ಲೇಖವಿದೆ. ಆಯೋಜಕರು ನೀಡಿರುವ ಮಾರ್ಗವೇ ಎಂದು ಖಚಿತಪಡಿಸಲು CAT ತಾಣದಿಂದ ಹೋಗಿ. ಲಾಗಿನ್ ಆದ ಬಳಿಕ ನಿಮ್ಮ ಡ್ಯಾಶ್‌ಬೋರ್ಡ್‌ನ ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪತ್ರ ಆಯ್ಕೆ ತೆರೆಯಿರಿ. PDF ಲಭ್ಯವಾದಾಗ ಉಳಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳಿ.

User ID ಅಥವಾ ಪಾಸ್‌ವರ್ಡ್ ಮರೆತಿದ್ದರೆ

ಅಭ್ಯರ್ಥಿ ಲಾಗಿನ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ Forgot User ID/Password ಲಿಂಕ್ ಇದೆ. ಅದನ್ನು ತೆರೆಯಿರಿ ಮತ್ತು ಮರುಪಡೆಯುವ ಸೂಚನೆಗಳನ್ನು ಅನುಸರಿಸಿ. ಕ್ಯಾಪ್ಚಾ ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟವಾಗಿಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೆ ಅದೇ ಪುಟದಲ್ಲಿ “Get New Image” ಆಯ್ಕೆಮಾಡಿ. ಹೊಸ ಚಿತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಅಕ್ಷರ ಅಥವಾ ಅಂಕಿಗಳನ್ನು ನಮೂದಿಸಿ.

ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಸಮಸ್ಯೆ ಮುಂದುವರಿದರೆ ಅಧಿಕೃತ CAT ತಾಣದ ಸಂಪರ್ಕ ವಿವರಗಳನ್ನು ಬಳಸಿ. ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಸಹಾಯ ಕೇಂದ್ರದ ಇಮೇಲ್ cat2026_helpdesk@iimidr.ac.in ಎಂದು ಇದೆ. ಯಾವ ಹಂತದಲ್ಲಿ ಯಾವ ದೋಷ ಕಾಣುತ್ತದೆ ಎಂಬುದನ್ನು ತಿಳಿಸಿ; ಪಾಸ್‌ವರ್ಡ್ ಅಥವಾ ಒಮ್ಮೆ ಬಳಸುವ ಕೋಡ್ ಕಳುಹಿಸಬೇಡಿ.

ಪ್ರಯಾಣದ ಮೊದಲು ನಿಮಗೆ ನಿಗದಿಯಾದ ವಿವರಗಳನ್ನು ಓದಿ

ಪತ್ರ ದೊರೆತ ಬಳಿಕ ಹೆಸರು ಮತ್ತು ನೋಂದಣಿ ವಿವರಗಳನ್ನು ಅರ್ಜಿಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ. ಪತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಯ ದಿನ, ಅವಧಿ, ಹಾಜರಾಗಬೇಕಾದ ಸಮಯ, ಕೇಂದ್ರದ ಹೆಸರು ಮತ್ತು ಸಂಪೂರ್ಣ ವಿಳಾಸ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ. ಒಂದೇ ಹೆಸರಿನ ಹಲವು ಶಾಖೆ ಅಥವಾ ಕ್ಯಾಂಪಸ್ ಇದ್ದರೆ ಕೇಂದ್ರದ ಹೆಸರು ಪರಿಚಿತವಾಗಿರುವುದು ಮಾತ್ರ ಸಾಕಾಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

  • ಗುರುತಿನ ದಾಖಲೆ, ಭಾವಚಿತ್ರ, ಘೋಷಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಅನುಮತಿಸಲಾದ ವಸ್ತುಗಳ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಪತ್ರದ ಸೂಚನೆಗಳನ್ನು ಓದಿ.

  • ಉಳಿಸಿದ PDFನ ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ಪುಟ ತೆರೆಯಿರಿ. ಖಾಲಿ, ಕತ್ತರಿಸಿದ ಅಥವಾ ಓದಲು ಆಗದ ಮುದ್ರಣವನ್ನು ಪ್ರಯಾಣದ ಮುನ್ನ ಸರಿಪಡಿಸಿ.

  • PDF ಪ್ರತಿಯನ್ನು ಉಳಿಸಿ, ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪತ್ರದ ಸೂಚನೆಯಂತೆ ಮುದ್ರಿತ ಪ್ರತಿ ತೆಗೆದುಕೊಳ್ಳಿ. ಫೋನ್ ಪರದೆಯೇ ಅದರ ಬದಲಿಗೆ ಸಾಕು ಎಂದು ಭಾವಿಸಬೇಡಿ.

  • ವೈಯಕ್ತಿಕ ವಿವರ ತಪ್ಪಿದ್ದರೆ ತಕ್ಷಣ ಅಧಿಕೃತ ಸಹಾಯ ಕೇಂದ್ರವನ್ನು ಸಂಪರ್ಕಿಸಿ. ನೀಡಿದ ದಾಖಲೆಯನ್ನು ನೀವೇ ತಿದ್ದಬೇಡಿ.

ಅಣಕು ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪತ್ರಕ್ಕೆ ಪರ್ಯಾಯವಲ್ಲ

ಅಧಿಕೃತ ಅಣಕು ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ ಪರದೆಯ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣಗಳನ್ನು ಕಲಿಯಲು ನೆರವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಅದು ನಿಮಗೆ ನಿಗದಿಯಾದ ಪರೀಕ್ಷಾ ಅವಧಿ ಅಥವಾ ಕೇಂದ್ರವನ್ನು ತಿಳಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಅಭ್ಯಾಸಕ್ಕಾಗಿ CAT ಅಣಕು ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಯ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣಗಳ ಮಾರ್ಗದರ್ಶಿ ಓದಬಹುದು. ಹಾಜರಾತಿ ವಿವರಗಳಿಗೆ ನಿಮ್ಮ ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪತ್ರ ಮತ್ತು ನಂತರದ ಅಧಿಕೃತ ಸೂಚನೆಗಳನ್ನು ಅನುಸರಿಸಿ.

ಹಳೆಯ ಡೌನ್‌ಲೋಡ್ ದಿನಾಂಕದ ಸುದ್ದಿಗಳು ಹುಡುಕಾಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಉಳಿದಿರಬಹುದು. ಮುಂದಿನ ಕ್ರಮಕ್ಕೆ ಪ್ರಸ್ತುತ CAT ತಾಣ ಮತ್ತು ನಿಮ್ಮ ಖಾತೆಯನ್ನು ನೋಡಿ. ಊಹಿಸಿದ ಬಿಡುಗಡೆ ಸಮಯ ಅಥವಾ ಇನ್ನೊಬ್ಬ ಅಭ್ಯರ್ಥಿಯ ಅನುಭವ ನಿಮ್ಮ ದಾಖಲೆಯ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಗೆ ಸಾಕ್ಷಿಯಾಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

title: Competitive Exams After 12th Commerce | Career Opportunities
description: Looking for the best competitive exams after Class 12 Commerce? Check out the top exams that open doors to careers in business, law, finance, and beyond.
content:
Choosing the right career path after completing Class 12th Commerce can be overwhelming. One of the most effective ways to build a rewarding career is by preparing for competitive exams. These exams open doors to reputed colleges, universities, and professional courses that can shape your future. Here’s a detailed list of the top competitive exams after 12th Commerce for students looking to explore opportunities in management, finance, law, design, and more.

1. Chartered Accountancy (CA) Foundation Exam

The CA Foundation is one of the most sought-after professional exams for commerce students right after Class 12. It is conducted by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) and is the first step toward becoming a Chartered Accountant.

  • Eligibility: Students who have passed Class 12 can apply.

  • Subjects: Accounting, Business Laws, Mathematics, Economics, and Logical Reasoning.

  • Duration: The full CA course usually takes around 4–5 years to complete.

  • Career Scope: After becoming a CA, you can work as an Auditor, Tax Consultant, Financial Advisor, or even a Chief Financial Officer (CFO).

Why choose it?
It is a respected profession with high salaries and great career opportunities in India and abroad.

2. Company Secretary (CS) Foundation Exam

The CS Foundation Exam is the first stage to become a Company Secretary, conducted by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI). It is a great choice for students interested in corporate law, business regulations, and management.

  • Eligibility: Students who have passed Class 12 from any stream (except Fine Arts) can apply.

  • Subjects: Business Environment, Business Management, Legal Aptitude, Economics, and Accounts.

  • Duration: The full CS course takes about 3–4 years to complete (Foundation → Executive → Professional).

  • Career Scope: After completing CS, you can work as a Company Secretary, Legal Advisor, Compliance Officer, or Corporate Consultant in private companies, MNCs, or government organizations.

Why choose it?
It is a prestigious career with strong demand in the corporate world. CS professionals are experts in handling company laws, mergers, acquisitions, and corporate governance.

3. Cost and Management Accounting (CMA) Foundation Exam

The CMA Foundation Exam is the first step to becoming a Cost and Management Accountant, conducted by the Institute of Cost Accountants of India (ICMAI). It is a good option for students interested in finance, accounting, cost management, and business strategy.

  • Eligibility: Students who have passed Class 12 (any stream except Fine Arts) can apply.

  • Subjects: Fundamentals of Economics, Accounting, Laws, and Business Mathematics.

  • Duration: The full CMA course takes about 3–4 years to complete (Foundation → Intermediate → Final).

  • Career Scope: After completing CMA, you can work as a Cost Accountant, Finance Manager, Budget Analyst, Corporate Planner, or Internal Auditor in industries and companies.

Why choose it?
CMA professionals are in high demand for their expertise in cost control, financial planning, and decision-making. It’s a great choice if you enjoy numbers and financial analysis.

4. Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) Entrance Exams

The BBA Entrance Exams are conducted by different universities and colleges for admission into Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) programs. This course is ideal for students who want to build a career in business, management, or entrepreneurship.

  • Eligibility: Students who have passed Class 12 (any stream) can apply.

  • Popular Exams: IPMAT (IIMs), DU JAT (Delhi University), NPAT (NMIMS), SET BBA (Symbiosis University).

  • Subjects in Exams: English, Quantitative Ability (Maths), Logical Reasoning, and General Knowledge.

  • Course Duration: The BBA degree takes 3 years to complete.

  • Career Scope: After BBA, you can work as a Business Manager, Marketing Executive, HR Professional, Financial Analyst, or pursue an MBA for higher studies.

Why choose it?
BBA is one of the best options for commerce students who want to enter the corporate world early. It builds strong business skills and opens doors to management careers.

5. Law Entrance Exams (CLAT, AILET, LSAT)

If you are interested in law, justice, and legal studies, then law entrance exams are the best option after 12th Commerce. These exams give admission into top law universities and colleges in India.

  • Eligibility: Students who have passed Class 12 (any stream) with at least 45% marks can apply.

  • Popular Exams:

    • CLAT (Common Law Admission Test): For admission into National Law Universities (NLUs).

    • AILET (All India Law Entrance Test): For admission into National Law University, Delhi.

    • LSAT (Law School Admission Test): For admission into various private law colleges in India.

  • Subjects in Exams: Legal Aptitude, English, Logical Reasoning, General Knowledge, and Elementary Maths.

  • Course Duration: The BA LLB (Hons.) program usually takes 5 years to complete.

  • Career Scope: After law, you can become a Lawyer, Legal Consultant, Corporate Lawyer, Judge (after higher exams), or work in government and private firms.

Why choose it?
A career in law is prestigious and offers diverse opportunities in corporate firms, courts, legal consultancies, and even international organizations.

6. CUET (Common University Entrance Test)

The CUET is a national-level entrance exam conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA). It is used for admission into central universities, state universities, and other participating institutions across India. Commerce students can apply for courses like B.Com, BBA, Economics, Accounting, and Business Studies.

  • Eligibility: Students who have passed Class 12 (any stream) can apply.

  • Subjects in Exam: Language Test, Domain Subjects (like Accountancy, Business Studies, Economics, Mathematics), and a General Test (reasoning, GK, current affairs).

  • Mode: Online (Computer-based).

  • Course Duration: Most undergraduate courses are 3 years long.

  • Career Scope: CUET offers a wide range of options, leading to careers in finance, management, economics, law, teaching, or government services depending on the chosen course.

Why choose it?
CUET gives you a chance to study in top universities like Delhi University, BHU, JNU, and more, with equal opportunity for all students.

7. Hotel Management Entrance Exams (NCHMCT JEE)

The NCHMCT JEE (National Council for Hotel Management and Catering Technology Joint Entrance Exam) is the main exam for students who want to pursue a career in hotel management and hospitality. It opens the door to top institutes like IHMs (Institute of Hotel Management).

  • Eligibility: Students who have passed Class 12 in any stream can apply.

  • Subjects in Exam: English, Reasoning, General Knowledge, Service Aptitude, and Numerical Ability.

  • Course Duration: The popular course is B.Sc. in Hospitality and Hotel Administration, which takes 3 years.

  • Career Scope: After completing the course, you can work as a Hotel Manager, Event Planner, Chef, Airline Catering Executive, Cruise Manager, or in Tourism & Hospitality Services.

Why choose it?
Hotel Management offers exciting career opportunities in India and abroad with good salary packages, along with the chance to work in luxury hotels, airlines, and international chains.

8. Design Entrance Exams (NIFT, NID, UCEED)

For commerce students who are creative and interested in fashion, design, or innovation, design entrance exams are a great choice. These exams give admission into top design institutes in India.

  • Eligibility: Students who have passed Class 12 in any stream can apply.

  • Popular Exams:

    • NIFT (National Institute of Fashion Technology Entrance Exam): For fashion design and technology.

    • NID (National Institute of Design Entrance Exam): For product design, communication design, and industrial design.

    • UCEED (Undergraduate Common Entrance Examination for Design): Conducted by IIT Bombay for design courses.

  • Subjects in Exams: Creativity, Drawing, Logical Reasoning, English, General Knowledge, and Problem-Solving Skills.

  • Course Duration: Most design courses take 4 years.

  • Career Scope: After completing a design degree, you can work as a Fashion Designer, Interior Designer, Graphic Designer, UX/UI Designer, or Creative Director.

Why choose it?
Design careers are exciting, highly creative, and in demand globally. They allow you to combine art with technology and business.

9. Actuarial Science Exams (ACET)

The ACET (Actuarial Common Entrance Test) is the entry exam for students who want to become an Actuary. It is conducted by the Institute of Actuaries of India (IAI). This career is best for students who enjoy mathematics, statistics, and finance.

  • Eligibility: Students who have passed Class 12 with Mathematics are eligible.

  • Subjects in Exam: Mathematics, Statistics, English, Data Interpretation, and Logical Reasoning.

  • Mode: Online computer-based test.

  • Course Duration: It usually takes around 5–7 years to clear all actuarial exams (done alongside graduation or job).

  • Career Scope: After becoming an actuary, you can work as a Risk Analyst, Insurance Specialist, Investment Planner, or Pension Fund Manager in banks, insurance firms, and financial companies.

Why choose it?
Actuaries are highly paid professionals because they are experts in risk management and financial forecasting. It’s a perfect career for commerce students who love working with numbers.

10. Banking and Insurance Exams

Banking and insurance are among the most popular career choices for commerce students. Some exams can be attempted after Class 12, while most higher-level posts require graduation. These exams open the way to jobs in banks, insurance companies, and financial institutions.

  • Eligibility: For entry-level posts, Class 12 is enough; for officer-level posts, graduation is required.

  • Popular Exams:

    • SBI Clerk/PO Exams

    • IBPS Clerk/PO Exams

    • LIC AAO/ADO Exams

    • NIACL & UIIC Insurance Exams

  • Subjects in Exams: Quantitative Aptitude, Reasoning, English, General Awareness, and Computer Knowledge.

  • Career Scope: Jobs include Clerk, Probationary Officer (PO), Insurance Agent, Financial Service Executive, and Relationship Manager.

Why choose it?
Banking and insurance jobs are stable, well-paying, and provide opportunities for career growth, along with job security and government benefits.

CONCLUSION 

Commerce students today have a wide range of competitive exams to choose from after Class 12. Whether you are interested in finance, law, management, design, or hospitality, these exams provide multiple pathways to build a successful career. The key is to identify your strengths, career goals, and areas of interest before selecting the right exam to prepare for.After completing Class 12 Commerce, students have a wide range of competitive exams to choose from, depending on their interests and career goals. Whether you are passionate about finance (CA, CMA, CS, ACET), management (BBA, CUET, Banking), law (CLAT, AILET, LSAT), or creative fields (NIFT, NID, UCEED, Hotel Management), each exam opens the door to exciting opportunities.

title: GATE 2027 Application Form via GOAPS: DigiLocker Verification, Photo Formatting Rules, and Registration Troubleshooting
description: Complete guide for GATE 2027 registration via GOAPS. Learn about DigiLocker identity verification, photograph and signature formatting rules, and fee payment troubleshooting.
content:
The Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering (GATE) 2027 application process is conducted entirely online through the GATE Online Application Processing System (GOAPS). Candidates seeking admission to Master's programs or recruitment in Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) must complete their registration accurately to avoid application rejection. Understanding the step-by-step registration workflow, document requirements, and technical guidelines ensures a smooth submission process.

Understanding the GOAPS Portal and Account Registration

The GOAPS portal is the official gateway for all GATE registration activities, including form submission, document uploads, fee payment, and admit card downloads. Candidates must begin by creating a new user account using a valid email address and an active mobile number.

  • Enrollment ID Generation: Upon successful account creation, a unique GOAPS Enrollment ID is generated and sent to the candidate via email and SMS.
  • Password Creation: Choose a strong password containing letters, numbers, and special characters to secure your application profile.
  • Dual Verification: Verify both the email address and mobile number through One-Time Passwords (OTPs) before proceeding to the application form.

DigiLocker Identity Verification Process

To streamline candidate authentication and reduce data discrepancies, the GATE organizing institute integrates identity verification via DigiLocker during the GOAPS application process.

How DigiLocker Verification Works

  1. In the personal details section of the GOAPS form, select the option for DigiLocker identity verification.
  2. Log in to your DigiLocker account using your registered Aadhaar number or mobile credentials.
  3. Grant permission to share official identity documents, such as your Aadhaar card, with the GOAPS system.
  4. The portal automatically fetches and verifies your name, date of birth, and gender directly from the official repository.

If a candidate does not have a DigiLocker account, creating one prior to filling out the GATE application form is highly recommended. For those unable to use DigiLocker, manual entry of valid government identity details (Aadhaar, Passport, PAN Card, Voter ID, or Driving License) is permitted, though additional identity verification may be required at the examination center.

Photo and Signature Formatting Rules

Image rejection is one of the most common reasons GATE applications are flagged for correction. Adhering strictly to the official visual guidelines prevents delay or rejection.

Photograph Requirements

  • Background: Plain white or light-colored background only.
  • Face Coverage: The face must cover 60% to 70% of the total photo area, looking directly at the camera with a neutral expression.
  • Dimensions: Standard aspect ratio requiring 3.5 cm width × 4.5 cm height (350 × 450 pixels minimum).
  • File Size & Format: JPEG or JPG format, ranging between 20 KB and 200 KB.
  • Restrictions: No caps, sunglasses, or colored glasses. Normal prescription spectacles are allowed if there is no glare on the lenses.

Signature Specifications

  • Ink and Paper: Draw a clean signature using a black or dark blue ink pen on a white paper background within a rectangular box.
  • Dimensions: Aspect ratio requiring 2 cm height × 6 cm width (at least 160 × 560 pixels).
  • File Size & Format: JPEG or JPG format, ranging between 10 KB and 200 KB.
  • Restrictions: Signatures in capital letters, initials only, or blurry scans will be rejected.

Document Upload Guidelines

In addition to your photograph and signature, specific supporting documents must be uploaded in PDF format:

  • Category Certificate (SC/ST): Valid certificate issued by a competent authority in PDF format (10 KB to 300 KB).
  • PwD Certificate: Mandatory for candidates seeking concession under the Persons with Benchmark Disabilities category.
  • Dyslexic Certificate: Required for candidates claiming scribe assistance under dyslexic criteria.

GOAPS Registration Troubleshooting and Solutions

Candidates occasionally encounter technical obstacles during online registration. Here are verified solutions to common issues:

1. OTP Not Received

If you do not receive the verification OTP on your mobile or email, wait at least 5 minutes before clicking the resend button. Check your email spam or junk folder. Ensure your mobile number is not on Do Not Disturb (DND) mode for transactional messages.

2. Payment Failure or Deducted Amount Not Reflected

If your bank account is debited but the GOAPS portal shows the payment status as pending or incomplete, do not immediately make a second payment. Wait 24 to 48 hours for automatic bank reconciliation. If the status remains unpaid, initiate a fresh transaction. Any duplicate successful payment will be automatically refunded to the original payment source after the application window closes.

3. Image Upload Errors

If the system rejects your uploaded photo or signature, check the file extension and exact pixel dimensions. Use standard graphic editor tools to resize the images to fit within the specified file size (KB) limits without lowering the resolution.

4. Discrepancies in Name or Personal Details

Ensure the name entered in the application matches your official photo identity card exactly. Any discrepancy between the name on your GATE application and your identity card can cause issues on the day of the exam. If an error is detected after submission, monitor the portal for the official application correction window to rectify allowed fields.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is GOAPS in the GATE registration process?

GOAPS stands for GATE Online Application Processing System. It is the centralized official online portal used by candidates to fill out application forms, upload documents, pay fees, track status, and download admit cards.

Is DigiLocker verification mandatory for GATE 2027 registration?

DigiLocker verification is the preferred and seamless method for identity validation. While highly recommended, candidates who face technical constraints can manually upload scanned copies of an approved government photo identity card.

What are the file size and dimension requirements for the GATE photo upload?

The candidate photograph must be in JPEG or JPG format, sized between 20 KB and 200 KB. It should have a white background, measuring approximately 3.5 cm × 4.5 cm with the face occupying 60% to 70% of the frame.

What should I do if my fee payment fails but money is debited?

Wait 24 to 48 hours for the payment status to update via bank reconciliation. If it remains unsuccessful, make a new payment. Any excess debited amount for failed transactions is refunded by the organizing authority after processing.

Can I correct mistakes in my GATE application form after submission?

Yes, the organizing institute opens a dedicated application correction window after the initial registration period ends. Minor details such as exam city, paper choice, category, or photo corrections can be edited during this timeframe, sometimes subject to an additional correction fee.

title: Bihar BEd CET 2026 Instant Admission: Refund and Reporting Checks
description: Before paying for a Bihar BEd CET 2026 instant seat, check written refund terms, receipts, reporting proof and document custody.
content:
A Bihar BEd CET 2026 instant-admission offer isn’t proof that your seat is secure. Before paying, get the allotment or admission record, full fee breakup, refund terms and reporting deadline in writing. Keep receipts, screenshots and bank records together. If the college won’t provide these basics, pause.

A public update dated 25 September 2026 refers to final-round instant-admission activity. The supplied evidence doesn’t include a matching official counselling notice, so treat the update as unverified until the authorised Bihar BEd CET counselling portal shows your offer and the controlling 2026 notice.

What should you verify before paying for Bihar BEd CET 2026 instant admission?

Ask for proof that connects your name, BEd course, college and reporting date to the authorised counselling process. The responsible authority and a verified 2026 deadline aren’t established in the available evidence, so don’t let a college desk, agent or phone call replace the official record.

  • Save the portal status, allotment record or authorised admission receipt.
  • Request an itemised breakup for counselling, tuition, university charges, security deposit and hostel fees.
  • Get the withdrawal cut-off, refundable amount, claim method and responsible office in writing.
  • Pay only through the stated channel and check that the receipt shows the college, date, amount and transaction reference.

No verified 2026 refund condition is available in the supplied evidence. A fee described as “instant admission” doesn’t automatically become refundable. Ask how each payment is treated.

How should Bihar BEd CET 2026 reporting handle original documents?

description: Find out which CUET UG 2027 form errors may be editable, which can affect eligibility, and how to check NTA’s correction instructions safely.

CUET UG 2027 Form Correction may help with selected data-entry mistakes, but it won’t repair every submitted detail. So don’t assume a wrong identity detail, category claim or qualifying-exam record can be changed later.

When NTA releases its instructions, check the notice on the official CUET UG website. That notice, not a coaching-group message, will decide what you can edit.

What can CUET UG 2027 Form Correction cover?

CUET UG 2027 Form Correction is a restricted editing window, not a fresh application. NTA may open selected fields, but the permitted list must come from the 2027 notice. The practical question is simple: does the mistake affect contact, identity, reservation or course eligibility?

title: IIM Lucknow Family Business MBA: Who Can Apply Without CAT?
description: The MBA-FB route is for eligible family-business owners and successors. Check the ₹20 crore business condition, accepted tests and phase deadlines.
content:
IIM Lucknow’s MBA in Family Business offers an admission route through GMAT, GRE or the institute’s entrance examination. It is aimed at owners and next-generation members of family enterprises, so applicants should check the business eligibility conditions before treating it as another general MBA option.

Start with the family-business requirement

The official application instructions require the applicant to be an owner or scion of a family business or enterprise. They specify a minimum business investment or annual turnover of ₹20 crore. Applicants shortlisted for interview must produce documentary evidence supporting the business information entered in the form.

The academic requirement includes a bachelor’s degree under a 10+2+3 or 10+2+4 education pattern, or an equivalent academic qualification, with at least 50% marks or equivalent CGPA. Where a university provides a CGPA conversion formula, use that formula. The application page explains IIM Lucknow’s method where no institutional formula is available.

Check the accepted test route

The listed routes are a valid GMAT score, a valid GRE score or IIM Lucknow’s entrance examination. CAT is not listed as an admission route for MBA-FB. The official instructions accept only test-centre-based GMAT or GRE scores, and the score must remain valid up to the application deadline. IIM Lucknow’s entrance examination is to be held at its Noida campus.

Do not assume that another IIM Lucknow programme’s test or work-experience rules apply here. Use the MBA-FB instructions for this application.

Prepare the application before paying

The institute lists 31 December 2026 as the Phase 1 application deadline and 2 April 2027 for Phase 2. The application fee is ₹3,000 and is non-refundable. The form must be submitted online.

Prepare your photograph, signature, applicable test-score document, school certificates and marksheets, and the combined degree and semester-mark documents requested in the form. Keep relevant category or disability certificates ready where applicable. Check the business details carefully against your supporting records.

You can preview the application more than once before submitting it, but the instructions say changes are not allowed after submission. Review names, scores, qualifications and uploaded files before the final click.

Plan for time away from the business

The programme page describes a two-year MBA at the Noida campus, with on-campus modules of seven days each month. Its projects include work on the participant’s own family enterprise. Discuss this attendance commitment and the responsibilities you will retain at work before applying.

Check the year and examination category first

The date-sheet directory includes schedules for other examinations, including 2026 supplementary and SOS examinations. A timetable on the official website can still be the wrong one for your class, examination year or candidate category.

When the 2027 schedule appears, read its heading before recording any dates. Match your subjects and check the instructions on the document itself. If your school's message and a downloaded schedule differ, ask the school to confirm which board notice applies.

Find your class in the model-paper directory

HPBOSE groups its model papers by class. Class 10 students should look under Matric; regular Class 12 students should use the Regular Plus Two section. The directory also contains E-Series papers and material for other classes, so take a moment to check the group heading.

Download the relevant subject paper and read the year, marks and instructions printed on it. Ask your teacher whether it matches the syllabus you are studying. The directory is a practice resource, not confirmation of the 2027 examination dates.

Turn one practice attempt into a revision list

After attempting a paper, separate mistakes caused by missing subject knowledge from those caused by incomplete answers or misreading a question. Pick a small set of weak areas to revise, then attempt those questions again without looking at your earlier answers.

content:
Steve Smith's Influence on Youth Cricket Academies

Steve Smith, one of cricket's modern greats, has made significant contributions to the sport, particularly through his incredible performances on the international stage. As his milestones continue to attract attention, his impact on the game extends beyond just statistics. Importantly, this influence can be leveraged by youth cricket academies across India to inspire and ignite young cricketers' passion for the sport.

Understanding the Motivational Pull of Steve Smith

His story showcases traits such as resilience, hard work, and the importance of skill development. For many young cricketers, Smith represents the idea that with dedication, they too can achieve greatness.

Capitalizing on Current Trends

How can young cricketers watch or learn from Steve Smith?

title: CLAT Rank List vs NLU Preference: Which One Should Guide Choices?
description: Use your CLAT rank, category, course choice and budget to build an NLU preference list that is realistic without chasing a famous name blindly.
content:
Your CLAT rank list shows your position. It doesn’t decide your NLU preference list for you. Use rank to judge what may be realistic, then order choices by the course, college, location and cost you’d genuinely accept.

That distinction matters. A high-profile NLU with an unwanted course can leave you with a seat you never planned to join, while a less famous option may fit your academic and financial plans better.

Should rank or course preference come first?

Course preference should decide the order; rank should test whether the list is realistic. This is an editorial planning method, not an allotment rule issued by the Consortium of NLUs. The Consortium’s current counselling notice and seat information for your cycle must decide what is officially available and how the process works.

For instance, if you prefer BA LLB over BBA LLB, don’t place BBA LLB higher only because the institution is better known. Programme availability differs by NLU and by counselling cycle, so check the current choices before treating either course as an option.

How should you read the CLAT rank list?

Overall rank is only one filter. Your practical choices can change when category, domicile-linked seats, programme and seat movement are considered. Don’t turn an old closing rank into a promise for the present cycle.

  • Category: Check the category information that applies to you, including any document or domicile condition stated for the relevant seat.
  • Programme: Confirm whether the NLU offers your preferred course in the current counselling data.
  • College: Check location, hostel, travel, total fees and the academic setting.
  • Acceptance: Remove any option you’d refuse if it became your allotted seat.

A rank that appears suitable for a newer NLU is only a hypothetical illustration unless backed by a verified, cycle-specific closing-rank record. Treat past movement as context, not certainty. You can also compare entrance exams and explore law courses if your plan includes alternatives.

What order should you use while filling preferences?

  1. Write your non-negotiables: course, budget, city or family constraints.
  2. Group choices as ambitious, realistic and safer using rank and applicable category information.
  3. Order each group by genuine preference, not social media reputation.
  4. Check whether the lowest choice is still acceptable after adding living and travel costs.
  5. Before submission, read the Consortium of NLUs instructions for your cycle and verify every selected programme and category condition.

A shorter list you’d actually accept is safer than a long list built to look impressive. Parents, ask one practical question: can the family fund and support this choice if it is allotted?

title: Pathways to Indian Education Scholarships for Women in STEM
description: A practical overview for Indian students and parents detailing scholarship options, eligibility, application steps, and timelines for women pursuing STEM education in higher education institutions.
content:
Lead: Unlock financial pathways that empower women in STEM to pursue coveted Indian and institutional scholarships

For Indian families supporting daughters in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics, scholarships can be a turning point. Government schemes, university fellowships, and foundation grants increasingly target women in STEM, with emphasis on undergraduate, postgraduate, and research programs. This guide explains practical pathways, eligibility essentials, and step-by-step application strategies to maximize chances of securing support in 2026.

Why scholarships for women in STEM matter now

Women remain underrepresented in many STEM fields. Scholarships help reduce financial barriers, enable early specialization, and encourage sustained academic and research engagement. Many programs also include mentorship, internship opportunities, and internships that build professional networks, which can translate into stronger career trajectories after graduation.

Key opportunities at a glance

  • Central and state government initiatives focused on women’s education and STEM capacity building.
  • University-specific fellowships and merit-based scholarships for engineering, sciences, and data-focused programs.
  • Private foundations and corporate social responsibility programs targeting women researchers and engineers.
  • Campus-wide grants for women pursuing research degrees, including master’s and doctoral studies.

Who can apply and typical eligibility

Eligibility varies by program, but common criteria include academic merit, financial need, domicile in India, and a focus on STEM fields. Many scholarships target specific groups such as first-generation learners, economically disadvantaged students, or those pursuing research-intensive tracks. Applicants should have a clear study plan, a track record of coursework or projects in STEM, and letters of recommendation from teachers or mentors.

How to identify suitable scholarships

  • Government schemes designed to expand access to higher education for women in technical disciplines.
  • University grants offered to meritorious women entering undergraduate or postgraduate STEM programs.
  • Industry-funded fellowships that promote women in engineering, computer science, healthcare tech, and related fields.
  • Research- and scholarship-oriented fellowships for aspiring scientists and scholars.

To begin, search for programs aligned with your daughter’s field of study, degree level, and place of study. Review eligibility notes carefully, including any prerequisites such as entrance exam performance, language requirements, or prior research experience. If in doubt, contact the program office for clarity before submitting materials.

Practical steps to strengthen an application

  1. Prepare a clear academic narrative: articulate the STEM focus, career goals, and how the scholarship would enable those goals.
  2. Show evidence of merit: transcripts, standardized test scores if applicable, and any relevant project or internship experience in STEM.
  3. Demonstrate leadership and initiative: include extra-curricular projects, coding clubs, science fairs, robotics teams, or research assistantships.
  4. Build strong references: request letters from mentors who understand the applicant’s STEM potential and commitment to scholarship goals.
  5. Gather financial documents early: income certificates, domicile proof, and any prior scholarships or awards.
  6. Prepare a precise budget and purpose statement: explain how funds will be used (tuition, equipment, travel for conferences, etc.).

Application timeline and tips for 2026

Deadlines for scholarships often align with academic cycles, typically around the start of the academic year. Create a personalized timeline that includes:

  • Research phase and shortlist of programs (2-3 months before deadlines).
  • Drafting and revising essays or statements of purpose (1-2 months before deadlines).
  • Securing letters of recommendation (4-6 weeks before due date).
  • Submitting materials and confirming receipt with the scholarship office.

Proactive communication helps. If documents are pending, inform the office and keep a cadence of check-ins. Maintain copies of all submissions and confirmations for reference.

Common pitfalls and how to avoid them

  • Incomplete forms or missing documents: double-check each section and maintain a checklist.
  • Weak personal statements: tie your experiences to future impact in STEM and to the scholarship’s mission.
  • Overlooking financial need validation: provide accurate and current income information as required.
  • Ignoring deadlines: set reminders and plan submission well before due dates.

What to expect after applying

Notification timelines vary by program. Some offer interim confirmations, while others announce results months after the deadline. If a scholarship is awarded, there may be a formal offer, acceptance steps, and sometimes an orientation or onboarding process. For recipients, plan how funds will be disbursed, whether directly to institutions or through a stipend, and clarify any reporting requirements.

Verification note for parents and students

For accurate details on eligibility, documents, and deadlines, consult the official authority administering each program. Policies can change, and guidelines may differ across schemes and institutions. When in doubt, verify directly with the scholarship office or the university financial aid office involved with the program.

Frequently asked questions

What types of scholarships are most common for women in STEM in India?

Merit-based undergraduate and postgraduate scholarships, need-based grants, and research fellowships are common. Many programs also offer mentorship, internships, and conference funding as part of the award.

Who should write letters of recommendation for STEM scholarships?

Teachers, professors, or research supervisors who know the applicant well and can attest to STEM ability, perseverance, and potential for scholarly contribution should write the letters. Provide them with a summary of achievements and the scholarship’s focus.

How can I demonstrate financial need effectively?

Prepare official income certificates, tax documents if applicable, and any relevant family income statements required by the program. Include a brief narrative that contextualizes the applicant’s financial constraints and how the scholarship would alleviate barriers.

Is a research proposal required for all STEM scholarships?

Not all programs require a formal research proposal. Some focus on academic merit and leadership potential. If a proposal is requested, tailor it to the field and align it with the applicant’s long-term goals.

How can families stay organized during the process?

Maintain a shared checklist, track deadlines on a calendar, and store digital copies of all documents in a secure folder. Schedule periodic reviews with a school counselor or mentor to ensure progress stays on track.

Final note

Across India, dedicated programs now more than ever aim to widen access for women pursuing STEM. By choosing programs aligned with the student’s strengths, organizing a compelling application, and meeting all criteria, families can improve the odds of securing scholarship support that accelerates academic and research ambitions.

title: NIFT Situation Test Preparation: What Shortlisted BDes Students Need
description: Shortlisted for the NIFT BDes Situation Test? Use this practical plan for material handling, quick prototypes, observation notes and timed presentation.
content:
Being shortlisted for the NIFT BDes Situation Test changes the preparation game. This is not another drawing paper where polished shading can rescue weak thinking; you’ll need to turn a prompt, limited materials and a short working window into a clear design response. Start by checking the latest notice, test instructions and schedule on the official NIFT admissions page, then practise under similar pressure.

The real mark-losing mistake is treating the Situation Test as a craft competition. A neat model with no visible idea, poor use of materials or a weak explanation can hurt more than a simple model that solves the brief cleanly.

What should NIFT BDes candidates practise first?

Build a small practice kit with paper, cardboard, thread, wire, straws, coloured sheets, tape, glue and recycled packaging. Don’t collect expensive art supplies. The test is about decisions, handling and communication, so ordinary materials are enough.

  1. Material handling: Make one object each day using only two or three materials. Try folding, slotting, weaving, scoring and joining without hiding every connection under glue.
  2. Quick prototypes: Set a 35 to 45-minute limit and create a model for a familiar need, such as a desk organiser for a small room or a rain shelter for a bus stop. Make the form stable before decorating it.
  3. Observation notes: Spend five minutes studying a chair, bag or street vendor’s setup. Record its users, movement, storage problems and useful features. These notes train you to design from observation rather than memory.

How do you present the model without losing marks?

Keep a final 10-minute block for cleaning edges, checking stability and arranging the model. Then prepare a short explanation: what problem did you identify, why did you choose this form, and how do the materials support the idea?

Practise speaking in four or five clear sentences. Parents can help by asking one blunt question: “Why is this shape or material necessary?” If the answer is only “It looked good”, the concept needs more work.

What should you do after shortlisting?

Make a seven-day routine: four timed models, two observation exercises and one full mock with presentation. Photograph each model and write down what failed, such as a weak base, wasted material or an unclear user. Fix one failure in the next attempt.

Use the NIFT exam guide for the wider admission route, but don’t assume old coaching material reflects the latest Situation Test instructions. NIFT’s official notice remains the deciding document for the test format, reporting details and any required items.

title: JEE Advanced 2027: Should a Qualified Student Skip the Attempt?
description: A practical decision guide for JEE Main-qualified students weighing JEE Advanced preparation against an existing college option and counselling deadlines.
content:
Qualifying JEE Main does not mean you must sit for JEE Advanced 2027. Appear if an IIT course is a real goal, your preparation gap is manageable and you can protect your current college option. Skip it only after comparing the likely rank outcome with the branch, cost and security of the seat you already have.

This is not an IIT-versus-NIT popularity contest. It is a decision about time, money and the kind of engineering course you actually want.

When is JEE Advanced worth the extra preparation?

Keep the attempt open when you can name the IIT course or branch you want, rather than chasing the label alone. It may also make sense when your JEE Main performance shows workable Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics basics, with identifiable topics costing you marks.

  • You can solve mixed PCM questions under a timer, not only familiar chapter exercises.
  • Your preferred IIT branch offers a clear advantage for your academic or career plan.
  • You can study without missing college fees, document checks or counselling actions.

Run one timed PCM paper and list your three largest topic gaps. That result is more useful than a hopeful rank prediction. For paper structure and current 2027 notices, check the JEE Advanced exam guide and the official JEE Advanced website. The exam authority, not a coaching post, will settle the applicable eligibility, fee and schedule.

When should you accept the college option you already have?

Accepting a suitable NIT, IIIT or state engineering seat can be the wiser call when the Advanced gap covers most of the syllabus, your timed-paper performance is weak or the available branch already fits your plan. A known seat with a manageable fee can beat months of uncertain preparation.

Do not surrender that safety net casually. Ask the institution for its payment, withdrawal and refund rules in writing. Counselling timelines may overlap, and losing a confirmed option before an IIT allotment can leave you with neither choice nor peace of mind.

Make the decision without gambling your admission

  1. Record your current college, branch, first-year cost and payment deadline.
  2. Set a realistic Advanced rank range based on timed practice, not wishful thinking.
  3. Block study time around counselling tasks and document requirements.
  4. Keep the existing admission route active until an official allotment and payment decision change your position.

One attempt can be worth protecting. But it should keep a serious IIT pathway open, not delay a good college merely because the word IIT feels difficult to refuse.

content:
The Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) Main is one of the major engineering entrance examinations in India. Conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA), it is an important examination for students seeking admission to undergraduate engineering programmes at NITs, IIITs and other participating institutions. Preparing with previous-year question papers is a useful way to become familiar with the examination format and practise different types of questions.

Students looking for the JEE Main 2025 January 28 Shift 1 question paper PDF can use the download section below. The paper can be used for self-assessment, revision and practising questions from the three subjects covered in JEE Main Paper 1: Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics.

Candidates can access the question paper using the PDF section below. Once the file is uploaded, students will be able to open or download it for practice.

JeeMains_28_Jan_Shift(1)2025

The PDF will be added to this section.

Why Should You Practise the JEE Main 2025 Question Paper?

Solving previous-year question papers can help candidates understand how concepts are tested in the actual examination. It also gives students an opportunity to evaluate their preparation before appearing for another entrance test.

Here are some benefits of practising the January 28 Shift 1 paper:

  • Understand the question format: Get familiar with the way questions are presented across Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics.

  • Improve time management: Practise completing questions within a fixed time limit.

  • Identify weak areas: Find topics where you make repeated mistakes or need additional revision.

  • Evaluate preparation: Check your performance and understand which subjects require more attention.

  • Build exam confidence: Regular practice can help reduce uncertainty about the examination format.

How to Prepare Using Previous-Year JEE Main Papers

For effective practice, attempt the question paper in an environment similar to the actual examination. Set a timer and try to complete the paper without referring to notes or solutions. After finishing, review your answers and identify the questions you could not solve correctly.

Pay attention to mistakes caused by conceptual gaps, calculation errors or incorrect question selection. Revise the relevant topics and practise similar questions. Instead of focusing only on the number of questions attempted, work on improving accuracy and understanding.

Students should also practise papers from different examination dates and shifts to gain exposure to a wider range of questions. Maintain a record of performance to track improvement over time.

Conclusion

The JEE Main 2025 January 28 Shift 1 question paper can be a useful practice resource for engineering aspirants. Download the PDF from the section above once available, attempt it under timed conditions and review your mistakes. Consistent practice, concept revision and performance analysis can help students prepare more effectively for JEE Main.

content:

2026 నవంబర్ 6న విడుదల చేసిన CBSE ప్రధాన పరీక్షల షెడ్యూల్‌లో ఈ వివరాలు ఉన్నాయి. ఇది పరీక్షల టైమ్‌టేబుల్ మాత్రమే; మార్కుల జాబితా కాదు. అధికారిక CBSE టైమ్‌టేబుల్

తరగతి, పేపర్కోడ్పరీక్ష తేదీసమయం (IST)వ్యవధి

పేజీ 5, 11లో ముందుగా తరగతి శీర్షిక చూసి, తర్వాత 408, 808 కోడ్ గుర్తించండి. ఒక తేదీ లేదా సమయం వరుసగా ఉన్న అనేక సబ్జెక్టులకు వర్తించవచ్చు. ఫోన్‌లో పూర్తి పేజీని పెద్దదిగా చేసి చదవండి.

పాఠశాల నమోదు వివరాల్లోని కోడ్, కోర్సు పేరు సరిపోల్చుకోండి. ఒకే పేరుతో వేర్వేరు తరగతుల పేపర్లు ఉన్నా మీ తరగతి వరుసనే ఎంచుకోండి.

ఇంగ్లిష్ పేపర్‌తో తేదీలను పోల్చుకోండి

10వ తరగతి వ్యవసాయం (408) పరీక్ష 25 ఫిబ్రవరి 2027న ఉంటుంది. ఆంగ్ల భాష మరియు సాహిత్యం (184) పరీక్ష 26 ఫిబ్రవరి 2027న ఉంటుంది. ఈ రెండు తేదీల మధ్య 1 రోజుల తేడా ఉంది. 12వ తరగతి వ్యవసాయం (808) పరీక్ష 29 మార్చి 2027న ఉంటుంది. English Core (301) పరీక్ష 5 మార్చి 2027న ఉంటుంది. ఈ రెండు తేదీల మధ్య 24 రోజుల తేడా ఉంది.

ఈ తేడా మొత్తం చదువుకోడానికి దొరికే సెలవు కాదు. మీ ఇతర పరీక్షలను కూడా క్యాలెండర్‌లో పెట్టి, మధ్యలో పరీక్ష లేని రోజులను మాత్రమే లెక్కించండి. సాధన చేసేటప్పుడు అసలు పేపర్ వ్యవధిని పాటించండి.

ప్రాక్టికల్స్‌కు వేరే షెడ్యూల్

ఈ వరుస బోర్డు పేపర్‌కు సంబంధించినది. ప్రాక్టికల్, ప్రదర్శన, ప్రాజెక్టు లేదా అంతర్గత మూల్యాంకనం ఉంటే వాటి తేదీ, తీసుకెళ్లాల్సిన సామగ్రి గురించి పాఠశాలలో అడగండి.

కేంద్రంలోకి కమ్యూనికేషన్ పరికరాలను అనుమతించరు. తీసుకెళ్లే వస్తువుల విషయంలో CBSE విడిగా ఇచ్చే సూచనలను, అడ్మిట్ కార్డులోని నియమాలను పాటించండి.
