title: Maharashtra NEET UG 2026 Revised State Merit List Analysis: Group A MBBS and BDS Seat Allotment Matrix and Choice Preference Protocol
description: Comprehensive analysis of the Maharashtra NEET UG 2026 revised state merit list for Group A MBBS and BDS seats, detailing allotment rules, seat matrix dynamics, and choice filling strategies for candidates.
content:
The State Common Entrance Test Cell, Maharashtra, oversees the centralized admission process for undergraduate health science courses across government, municipal, and private institutions. For medical aspirants targetting MBBS and BDS courses categorized under Group A, understanding the revised State Merit List (SML) along with the seat allotment matrix is critical. Strategic planning during choice preference filling directly impacts admission outcomes across state quota and institutional quota seats.

Understanding the Maharashtra NEET UG 2026 Revised State Merit List

The revised State Merit List is published after verifying uploaded documents, candidate eligibility claims, and resolving category correction requests. It establishes an absolute merit rank for each registered candidate within Maharashtra.

  • State Merit Rank (SMR): Indicates a candidate's relative position among all eligible applicants in the state.
  • Category Rank: Reflects rank within specific reservation categories such as SC, ST, VJ/DT, NT-A/B/C/D, OBC, EWS, and SEBC.
  • Horizontal Reservation Ranks: Applies to specific claims including Persons with Disabilities (PwD), Defense personnel wards (DEF-1, DEF-2, DEF-3), and Orphan candidates.

Group A Seat Matrix Structure for MBBS and BDS

Seats under Group A are partitioned across several categories, governance structures, and regional quotas. Candidates must evaluate the published seat matrix prior to lock-in of preference forms.

1. Government and Corporation Medical/Dental Colleges

85% of total seats in government and municipal corporation institutes are filled via the State Quota, while the remaining 15% fall under the All India Quota (AIQ) administered by the MCC.

  • 70% Regional Quota: Allocated to candidates from the respective university region (Rest of Maharashtra, Vidarbha, or Marathwada).
  • 30% State Quota: Available to eligible candidates across the entire state regardless of their specific region of schooling.

2. Unaided Private Medical and Dental Colleges

Private institutions reserve 85% of their intake for State Quota applicants (including general, reserved, and institutional quota divisions) and 15% under the NRI/Management Quota.

Choice Preference Protocol and Strategic Option Form Filling

The preference filling process requires careful analysis of previous year cutoff trends, candidate SMR, and seat availability. The State CET Cell operates a computer-automated allotment system based strictly on merit and submitted preferences.

Key Rules of Preference Allocation

  1. Descending Order of Preference: Candidates must order their choice codes starting with their most preferred institution and course.
  2. Mandatory Retention (Status Retention): Admitted candidates who receive their first choice preference are automatically locked out of subsequent rounds. Candidates receiving lower preferences can retain their seat while opting for betterment in Round 2 or Round 3.
  3. Penalty Provisions: Non-joining after accepting a seat in later rounds can lead to forfeiture of security deposits or disqualification from further state counseling rounds depending on published rules.

Step-by-Step Checklist for Parents and Aspirants

  • Verify SMR and category rank in the official revised state merit list document.
  • Cross-check college codes (4-digit numerical identifiers) before final form submission.
  • Ensure constitutional quota documentation (Caste Certificate, Validity Certificate, Non-Creamy Layer) is valid for the 2026-2027 academic period.
  • Regularly verify official seat matrix updates on the CET Cell portal for any added seats or quota revisions.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between State Rank and All India Rank in Maharashtra NEET UG counseling?

All India Rank (AIR) is your nationwide position assigned by NTA based on your NEET score. State Rank (SMR) is assigned by the Maharashtra State CET Cell, ranking only eligible state candidates for 85% state quota seats.

Can a candidate upgrade their seat in Round 2 if assigned a preference in Round 1?

Yes. If a candidate is allotted a seat other than Choice 1 in Round 1, they can join the allotted college, submit a betterment option, and participate in Round 2 without filling a Status Retention Form.

What happens if a candidate submits the Status Retention Form?

Submitting the Status Retention Form locks the seat allotted in that round. The candidate voluntarily exits further rounds of state counseling for Group A courses.

Are private medical college seats subject to state reservation policies?

Yes. 85% State Quota seats in private colleges apply Maharashtra state reservation policies for category students, though tuition fee concession policies vary between government and private setups.

title: BITSAT Session 2 Exam 2026 - Dates, Application, Eligibility, Exam Pattern
description: BITSAT Session 2 Exam 2026 complete guide covering application process, eligibility, syllabus, exam pattern, fees, cut-off, counselling, and preparation tips.
content:
Introduction

The BITSAT Session 2 Exam is conducted by Birla Institute of Technology and Science (BITS), Pilani for admission to its integrated first-degree programmes. It serves as an additional opportunity for students who wish to improve their scores or missed the first session.

This exam is important because BITSAT scores are the sole criterion for admission to BITS campuses, making performance in Session 2 crucial for engineering aspirants across India.

Key Highlights

Event Schedule
Application Start Date 15 January 2026
Application Last Date 20 May 2026
Exam Dates 22 June 2026 to 26 June 2026
Result Date 3 July 2026
 

Exam Summary

BITSAT Session 2 is a computer-based online test that assesses a candidate’s proficiency in Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, English Proficiency, and Logical Reasoning. The exam focuses on speed, accuracy, and conceptual clarity.

Application Process

The application process is fully online.

Steps to apply:

  • Visit the official BITS admission portal

  • Register using basic personal details

  • Fill the application form carefully

  • Upload required documents

  • Pay the applicable fee

  • Submit and save the confirmation page

Eligibility Criteria

  • Candidates must have passed Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics

  • Proficiency in English is mandatory

  • Minimum qualifying marks in Class 12 are required as per official guidelines

  • Admission eligibility is subject to BITS policies

Syllabus

The syllabus is based on NCERT Class 11 and 12.

Candidates must carefully go through their class 11 and 12 syllabus of Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics. 40 questions are asked from Physics and Chemistry combined while 45 questions will be put up from Mathematics/Biology. Some important topics from each section are listed below :

Exam Pattern

Section Details
Mode Online (Computer-Based Test)
Question Type Objective
Sections PCM + English & Logical Reasoning
Scoring As per official marking scheme
 

Exam Cut Off (Overview)

BITSAT cut-off scores vary by:

  • Campus (Pilani, Goa, Hyderabad)

  • Course preference

  • Overall performance of candidates

Cut-offs are released during the admission rounds.

Application Fees (Indicative)

Exact fee details are published in the official notification.

Exam Centres

BITSAT Session 2 is conducted in major cities across India, covering key regions such as North, South, East, West, and Central India to ensure accessibility.

Note: Although candidates fill their preference of BITSAT exam center while filling out the application form, BITS Pilani, however, reserves the final right to allocate test centers to candidates. In case of any unforeseen events such as lack of accommodation facilities at a particular center, any technical glitches, etc. the exam conducting authority reserves the right to add or delete any center and make the necessary changes accordingly

Counselling Process

Admissions are conducted through BITS Online Counselling, where candidates:

  • Submit preferences

  • Participate in multiple admission rounds

  • Receive seat allotment based on merit

Preparation Tips

  • Strengthen NCERT fundamentals

  • Practice speed-based mock tests

Conclusion

BITSAT Session 2 offers a valuable second chance for aspirants aiming for BITS campuses. Timely application, focused preparation, and careful monitoring of official updates are essential.

Students are advised to regularly check the official website for latest updates.

title: JEE Main Mock Test 2027: Practice Online & Check Preparation
description: Prepare for JEE Main 2027 with online mock tests, previous-year papers and subject-wise practice. Find the official NTA test link, exam pattern, marking scheme and tips to analyse your performance.
content:

How to Calculate Your Mock Test Score

For a test that follows the standard marking scheme, use this formula:

Score = (Correct answers × 4) − (Incorrect answers × 1)

For example, if a candidate answers 50 questions correctly, gets 10 questions wrong and leaves the remaining questions unanswered:

  • Correct-answer marks: 50 × 4 = 200

  • Negative marks: 10 × 1 = 10

  • Unattempted questions: 0 marks

Estimated score = 200 − 10 = 190 out of 300.

This calculation is applicable only when the practice paper follows the stated marking scheme. It does not predict a candidate's final NTA score or percentile.

2. JEE Main Chemistry Mock Test

title: A Practical Guide to Indian Entrance Exam Fee Structures: Comparing Tuition, Coaching, and Exam-Linked Scholarships Across States
description: Understand the real costs of Indian entrance exams, compare tuition and coaching fees, and navigate scholarships tied to exam performance across states to plan a financially sustainable path to higher education.
content:
Understanding the Landscape of Entrance Exam Fees

India’s entrance exams for engineering, medical, management, and other professional streams come with varied fee structures. Costs aren’t limited to the test form; coaching, study materials, mock tests, and optional preparatory courses can significantly influence the overall outlay. State boards and central authorities determine application fees, while private coaching centers and online platforms set coaching charges. The key is to map all potential costs over the preparation period and align them with the candidate’s goals and family budget.

Tuition and Coaching Fees: What to Expect

Coaching fees differ widely by city, city tier, and the level of individualized attention. On average, you’ll encounter three broad bands:

  • Group coaching and classroom programs - affordable to moderate prices, often bundled with study materials and test series. Typical costs range from a few thousand to several tens of thousands of rupees per year depending on the institute and program length.
  • Topic-specific or crash courses - shorter durations focused on particular subjects or exam patterns. These can be a few thousand rupees for a short program or up to around 20,000 INR for extended modules.
  • Personalized or top-tier coaching - private tutoring or premium institutes with small batches and extensive mock tests. Fees here can run well above 50,000 INR per year and may include access to online portals, doubt-clearing sessions, and performance analytics.

When evaluating coaching, consider the return on investment beyond the price tag. Look for clear metrics: pass rates, average percentile improvements, and the institute’s track record for specific exams. Ask about batch size, faculty qualifications, and whether study materials and test series are included in the fee.

Exam Fees: The Core Cost to Register and Appear

Exam registration fees are usually fixed by the organizing body and differ by category, gender, and location for some exams. In many cases, the base fee is modest, but there can be added charges for late registration, additional paper options, or exam city changes. It helps to check the official notification for the current year’s schedule and fees, and to budget for potential inflation or fee revisions planned by the authority.

Scholarships and Fee Concessions Linked to Exams

Several states run scholarship or concession schemes linked to entrance outcomes, academic performance, or financial need. These schemes can substantially reduce the cost of preparation and admission. Common patterns include:

  • Entrance-score scholarships based on merit in a qualifying test; these may cover partial tuition or provide fee waivers for subsequent years.
  • District or state-district scholarships aimed at first-time entrants from specific regions or underrepresented communities. Eligibility may hinge on family income, category status, or rural-urban location.
  • Integrated fee waivers offered by some universities or state boards to students who secure a minimum percentile and meet income criteria.

Scholarships often combine multiple components: a cap on total cover, renewal criteria tied to year-on-year performance, and conditions such as maintaining a minimum GPA. To maximize eligibility, track official announcements, gather required documents early, and apply within stated windows.

Cost-Benefit Thinking: How to Plan Across States

State-wise differences in coaching costs, availability of test centers, and scholarship ecosystems can meaningfully affect overall expenditure. Here are practical steps to compare across states:

  • List the exams you will target and identify the corresponding registration fees, the typical coaching options available locally, and their price bands.
  • Estimate a yearly budget for coaching, materials, and mock tests. Include travel and incidental costs if you plan to attend live coaching or test centers outside your city.
  • Assess scholarship chances by reviewing past year cutoffs and eligibility rules. Note any binding conditions, such as maintaining a minimum attendance rate or course completion requirements.
  • Determine break-even points by comparing the total cost of coaching plus exam fees against the potential benefit of admission to a preferred program and university. In some cases, a modest coaching package with strong institutional support can be more effective than a premium but scattered approach.

One practical approach is to start with a conservative budget, prioritizing essential coaching that directly aligns with the target exam’s syllabus and pattern. Reserve funds for essential exam fees and a contingency for late registration or changes in applicant plans.

State-Specific Nuances to Watch For

States manage many aspects of entrance preparation and admission differently. Some common considerations include:

  • Availability of statewide or district-level scholarships tied to entrance performance or family income
  • Coaching presence and fee norms in tier 2 and tier 3 cities, which can differ markedly from metropolitan centers
  • Policies on fee reimbursement or credit for students pursuing public or semi-public universities after admission

Whether you are aiming for engineering, medicine, or management programs, the total cost picture matters as much as the exam strategy. Start with a clear map of required fees, explore scholarship options early, and choose a plan that fits your budget while keeping the focus on your academic goals.

Practical Checklist

  • Compile a yearly budget covering coaching, materials, mock tests, and exam registration fees.
  • Identify 2-3 coaching options in your city and compare price, success rates, and included resources.
  • Review scholarship schemes applicable to your state and program; note application windows and required documents.
  • Track fee revisions announced by exam authorities and plan for any potential cost increases.
  • Keep a calendar of deadlines for registrations, scholarship applications, and admission-related milestones.

Takeaway

Rational planning around fees and scholarships can make competitive entrance preparation financially sustainable. By comparing coaching tiers, understanding exam fees, and actively pursuing state-linked scholarships, students and families can optimize both costs and outcomes across states.

FAQ

Q: How should I prioritize coaching investments when on a tight budget?

A: Focus on high-impact coaching aligned with the exam syllabus, supplemented by strong self-study and targeted mock tests. Choose a reasonable program that offers clear progress tracking and exam-pattern familiarity.

Q: Are scholarship applications usually time-sensitive?

A: Yes, most state and central schemes have fixed windows. Prepare documents early and monitor official notices for deadlines.

Q: Do exam fees vary by location?

A: Some exams have location-based adjustments or late registration charges; always check the current year’s official notification.

Q: Can I combine scholarships with coaching discounts?

A: In many cases, yes. Some institutes partner with scholarship programs or offer discounts to students who qualify for public schemes.

content:
Physical Chemistry Numericals Class 12 CBSE – Complete Exam Guide

Introduction

Physical Chemistry numericals play a decisive role in the CBSE Class 12 Chemistry exam. Every year, a significant portion of marks comes from calculation-based questions that test clarity of concepts rather than memorisation.

For many students, numericals feel difficult only because formulas are not linked properly with concepts. Once the logic is clear, Physical Chemistry becomes one of the most scoring parts of the paper.

Why Physical Chemistry Numericals Matter in CBSE Class 12

Physical Chemistry focuses on measurable quantities, laws, and mathematical relationships. Questions are direct, structured, and often repetitive in pattern. With regular practice, students can score full marks from this section.

High-scoring chapters include:

  • Solutions

  • Electrochemistry

  • Chemical Kinetics

  • Thermodynamics

  • Surface Chemistry

  • Solid State

Chapter-Wise Important Physical Chemistry Numericals

Chapter Key Numerical Topics Exam Focus
Solid State Density, unit cell, packing efficiency Short numericals
Solutions Molarity, molality, Raoult’s law, osmotic pressure Long numericals
Thermodynamics Enthalpy change, Hess’s law Concept-based
Electrochemistry EMF, Nernst equation, Faraday’s laws Very high
Chemical Kinetics Rate constant, half-life Repeated patterns
Surface Chemistry Adsorption isotherms Direct formula
Coordination Compounds Magnetic moment (simple) Short answers

Most Repeated Numerical Types

Students preparing for boards should master these common patterns:

  • Calculation of cell potential using Nernst equation

  • Rate constant and half-life from given data

  • Osmotic pressure to find molar mass

  • Conductance and molar conductivity

  • Density of unit cell problems

  • Enthalpy change using bond energies

Step-by-Step Method to Solve Numericals

  1. Read the question carefully and identify what is asked

  2. Write the correct formula first

  3. Convert units (very important)

  4. Substitute values neatly

  5. Show calculations stepwise

  6. Write the final answer with correct unit

CBSE awards marks for method, not only the final answer.

Important Formulas to Revise Daily

Topic Formula
Molarity M = moles of solute / litre of solution
Nernst Equation E = E⁰ − (0.059/n) log Q
Half-Life (1st order) t½ = 0.693 / k
Osmotic Pressure π = CRT
Density (Unit Cell) Density = (Z × molar mass) / (a³ × NA)

Common Mistakes Students Should Avoid

  • Forgetting unit conversion

  • Using wrong value of R

  • Skipping calculation steps

  • Writing formula after calculation

  • Ignoring significant figures

Avoiding these mistakes alone can increase marks by 10–15%.

How to Prepare Physical Chemistry Numericals for Exams

  • Practice NCERT back exercises thoroughly

  • Solve previous 10 years’ board questions

  • Maintain a formula notebook

  • Revise numericals daily for 30 minutes

  • Focus more on Electrochemistry and Solutions

Conclusion

Physical Chemistry numericals are not difficult—they are systematic. Students who focus on concepts, formulas, and presentation can turn this section into a major scoring advantage. Regular practice and smart revision are the keys to success.

Students are advised to revise formulas daily and practice NCERT numericals before the exam.

title: National Merit and Need-Based Scholarships for Indian Undergraduates 2026 27 A Practical Regional Coverage Guide
description: A region-by-region practical guide for Indian undergraduates and families outlining how national merit and need-based scholarships work, who qualifies, how to apply, and timelines for 2026–27 across Indian states.
content:
Executive takeaway: smarter planning unlocks scholarship funding

For Indian undergraduates, national merit and need-based scholarships offer substantial support. This guide breaks down eligibility, application steps, and state-specific nuances for 2026-27, with practical timelines and checklists you can use now.

Understanding the landscape: merit versus need-based scholarships

National programs commonly recognize high academic achievement, leadership, and potential. Merit scholarships are typically awarded to top performers based on standardized exams and class performance. Need-based awards prioritize financial need demonstrated via income documentation and family circumstances. Some programs combine both criteria or adjust awards by academic level, course, or institution type.

Key points to note: eligibility rules vary by program, how funds are disbursed (direct to college, to student account, or via a consortium), and renewal conditions each year. Always verify current guidelines on the official authority portal before beginning an application.

Who qualifies in 2026-27: typical criteria by category

  • : usually require top-tier performance in national or state-level exams, a minimum grade point average, and evidence of consistent academic advancement. Some programs also consider leadership, research, or community service in the selection process.
  • : assessed via family income, number of dependents, and financial constraints. Applicants may need to provide recent income certificates, tax documents, or affidavits, along with academic records showing the student’s potential.
  • : some awards are restricted to certain disciplines,-degree types (UG vs. integrated programs), or specific colleges or public universities. Private colleges may have their own supplementary awards that align with national schemes.

Regional coverage: what families across states should expect

Regional realities shape application strategy. In many states, the same national programs are administered through state education departments or designated nodal agencies. Registration windows, required documents, and renewal criteria can differ, making regional planning essential.

Common regional patterns include:

  • Common deadlines clustered around the academic year start, with rolling consideration in some cases.
  • Bifurcated processes where merit-based and need-based tracks have separate application portals or sections within a single portal.
  • Document requirements that emphasize family income verification, academic records, and identity proofs to prevent delays in disbursal.

Practical steps to start now

  1. : list national merit and need-based scholarships that align with your course, college tier, and state of residence.
  2. : gather marksheets, identity proofs, and income documents. Prepare a concise resume highlighting leadership, competitions, volunteer work, and research if relevant.
  3. : many scholarships require maintaining a minimum GPA, continuous enrollment, and satisfactory conduct records to renew each year.
  4. : mark application opening dates, document submission deadlines, and any interview or placement assessment windows.
  5. : some awards require renewal each year, while others provide multi-year funding contingent on performance.

Documents checklist by category

  • Identity: Aadhaar, passport, or other government-issued ID as specified
  • Academic records: class 10 and 12 marksheets or equivalent, and latest semester/annual grades
  • Income evidence: latest income certificate, tax return summary, or equivalent documentation
  • Proof of course and institution: admission letter, program details, and college acknowledgment
  • Recommendation or leadership evidence: letters or certificates if required by the program

Common pitfalls and how to avoid them

  • Missing deadlines: set reminders a month before and a week before each deadline.
  • Inaccurate income data: ensure documents reflect current financial status; mistakes can disqualify or delay awards.
  • Incomplete applications: double-check all sections; incomplete submissions are often rejected by default.
  • Ignoring renewal requirements: failing to meet annual GPA or enrollment standards can terminate funding immediately.

What to expect from the process

Most programs provide notification within a few weeks to a few months after the application window closes. Disbursement methods vary; funds may be issued directly to the college to cover tuition and fees or deposited into the student’s account for other expenses. Renewal communications typically begin a few weeks before a new academic term, with confirmation requests for the upcoming year.

Regional contact points and where to verify details

Since procedures differ by state and institution, your first reference should be the official state education portal or the official scholarship authority website. If a portal lists multiple scholarship options, use the search filters to identify those that match your program, degree level, and residency. Always verify current instructions and contact details on the official site before submitting documents.

Sample timeline for a 2026-27 application

  • June-July 2026: gather documents, identify eligible programs, confirm deadlines
  • August-September 2026: complete and submit initial applications, prepare renewal materials if currently receiving funds
  • October-November 2026: respond to requests for additional information, prepare for any interviews
  • December 2026-January 2027: receive award letters and begin disbursal planning

Visible FAQ

What is the main difference between merit-based and need-based scholarships?

Merit-based awards recognize high academic achievement or leadership, while need-based awards focus on financial need. Some programs combine both criteria for eligibility and award size.

When should I start the application for 2026-27?

Begin as soon as the official window opens. Many programs have fixed deadlines, while a few offer rolling consideration. Check the official portal for exact dates.

What documents are usually required for income verification?

Common documents include an income certificate issued by a local revenue authority, tax return summaries, or bank statements. Specific programs may require different forms, so verify on the official site.

How are funds disbursed?

Disbursal can be directly to the college account to cover tuition, or a student account credit for living and other expenses. Some programs release funds in stages based on ongoing eligibility.

What if I miss a renewal deadline?

Missing renewal criteria can end the scholarship for the following term. If extenuating circumstances apply, contact the scholarship office promptly to explore options or reinstatement possibilities.

Conclusion: plan strategically, verify each step

National merit and need-based scholarships can significantly alleviate the cost of higher education. A regionally aware approach-tracking state-specific requirements, preparing the right documents, and adhering to renewal conditions-helps families maximize chances of securing and maintaining awards for 2026-27.

31 ಅಕ್ಟೋಬರ್ 2026ರಂದು FMGE ಬರೆದಿದ್ದು, ಯಾವುದಾದರೂ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ತಾಂತ್ರಿಕ ದೋಷವಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಭಾವಿಸಿದರೆ, NBEMS ಮಾಹಿತಿ ಕೈಪಿಡಿಯ ಪ್ರಕಾರ 2 ನವೆಂಬರ್ 2026ರವರೆಗೆ ಆಕ್ಷೇಪಣೆ ಸಲ್ಲಿಸಬಹುದು. ಬೆಂಬಲಿಸುವ ವೈದ್ಯಕೀಯ ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯವನ್ನು ಲಗತ್ತಿಸಿ, ಅಧಿಕೃತ Communication Web Portalನಲ್ಲಿ ನೋಂದಾಯಿತ ಇಮೇಲ್ ಬಳಸಿ ಸಲ್ಲಿಸಬೇಕು. ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ ಕಠಿಣವಾಗಿತ್ತು ಎಂಬ ಕಾರಣ ಮಾತ್ರ ಈ ನಿಯಮದಡಿ ಸ್ವೀಕಾರವಾಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

ಎರಡು ದಿನಗಳ ಅವಕಾಶ ಯಾರಿಗೆ?

ಅಕ್ಟೋಬರ್ 2026ರ ಅಧಿಕೃತ ಮಾಹಿತಿ ಕೈಪಿಡಿಯ ವಿಭಾಗ 10.2 ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಗೆ ನಿಜವಾಗಿ ಹಾಜರಾದ ಅಭ್ಯರ್ಥಿಗಳಿಗೆ ಮಾತ್ರ ಈ ಅವಕಾಶ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಯ ನಂತರ ಗರಿಷ್ಠ ಎರಡು ಕ್ಯಾಲೆಂಡರ್ ದಿನಗಳ ಮಿತಿ ಇದೆ. ನವೆಂಬರ್ 2ರ ನಂತರ ಬಂದ ಯಾವುದೇ ಆಕ್ಷೇಪಣೆಯನ್ನು ಪರಿಗಣಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಆಧಾರಸಹಿತ ತಾಂತ್ರಿಕ ಆಕ್ಷೇಪಣೆ ಇದ್ದರೆ ಫಲಿತಾಂಶಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ಕಾಯಬೇಡಿ.

NBEMS, FMGE ಅಕ್ಟೋಬರ್ 2026 ಮಾಹಿತಿ ಕೈಪಿಡಿ, ಪುಟ 89. ಈ ಭಾಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಆಕ್ಷೇಪಣೆಯ ಕೊನೆಯ ದಿನಾಂಕ 2 ನವೆಂಬರ್ 2026 ಎಂದು ನೀಡಲಾಗಿದೆ. ಅಕ್ಟೋಬರ್ 2026ರ ಅಧಿಕೃತ ಮಾಹಿತಿ ಕೈಪಿಡಿ

ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ದೋಷಕ್ಕೆ ವೈದ್ಯಕೀಯ ಆಧಾರ ನೀಡಿ

ಯಾವ ವಿಷಯದಲ್ಲಿ ತಾಂತ್ರಿಕ ದೋಷವಿದೆ, ಅದು ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಯ ಮೇಲೆ ಹೇಗೆ ಪರಿಣಾಮ ಬೀರುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು ಯಾವ ವೈದ್ಯಕೀಯ ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯ ನಿಮ್ಮ ವಾದವನ್ನು ಬೆಂಬಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ ಎಂಬುದನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟವಾಗಿ ಬರೆಯಿರಿ. ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಪತ್ರಿಕೆ ಹೇಗನಿಸಿತು ಎಂಬ ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ವಿವರಣೆ ತಾಂತ್ರಿಕ ದೋಷಕ್ಕೆ ಸಾಕ್ಷಿಯಲ್ಲ. ಪರೀಕ್ಷಕರು ನಿಖರ ಸಮಸ್ಯೆಯನ್ನು ಅರ್ಥಮಾಡಿಕೊಳ್ಳುವಂತೆ ಸಂಕ್ಷಿಪ್ತವಾಗಿ ವಿವರಿಸಿ.

  1. ಅಧಿಕೃತ ಪರೀಕ್ಷಾ ವೆಬ್‌ಸೈಟ್‌ನಿಂದ NBEMS Communication Web Portal ತೆರೆಯಿರಿ.

  2. FMGE ಅರ್ಜಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ನೋಂದಾಯಿಸಿದ ಇಮೇಲ್ ಬಳಸಿ, ಪೋರ್ಟಲ್ ಕೇಳುವ ಅಭ್ಯರ್ಥಿಯ ವಿವರಗಳನ್ನು ನೀಡಿ.

  3. ತಾಂತ್ರಿಕ ಆಕ್ಷೇಪಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಅದನ್ನು ಬೆಂಬಲಿಸುವ ವೈದ್ಯಕೀಯ ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯವನ್ನು ನಿಗದಿತ ಅವಧಿಯೊಳಗೆ ಸಲ್ಲಿಸಿ.

  4. ಸ್ವೀಕೃತಿ ಅಥವಾ ಉಲ್ಲೇಖ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯನ್ನು ಮತ್ತು ಸಲ್ಲಿಸಿದ ದಾಖಲೆಗಳ ಪ್ರತಿಯನ್ನು ಉಳಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳಿ.

ಈ ನಿಯಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೊನೆಯ ದಿನಾಂಕ ನೀಡಲಾಗಿದೆ; ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕವಾಗಿ ಮುಕ್ತಾಯದ ಸಮಯ ತಿಳಿಸಿಲ್ಲ. ಮಧ್ಯರಾತ್ರಿಯವರೆಗೆ ಅವಕಾಶ ಇದೆ ಎಂದು ಊಹಿಸಬೇಡಿ. ಲಾಗಿನ್ ಅಥವಾ ದಾಖಲೆ ಅಪ್‌ಲೋಡ್ ಸಮಸ್ಯೆಗಳನ್ನು ಸರಿಪಡಿಸಲು ಸಮಯ ಉಳಿಯುವಂತೆ ಮುಂಚಿತವಾಗಿ ಸಲ್ಲಿಸಿ.

ಉತ್ತರ ಕೀ ಬಿಡುಗಡೆಯನ್ನು ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕವಾಗಿ ನೋಡಿ

ವಿಭಾಗ 10.3ರ ಪ್ರಕಾರ ಅಕ್ಟೋಬರ್ 2026ರ ಅರ್ಜಿದಾರರ ಲಾಗಿನ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ IDಗಳು, ಸರಿಯಾದ ಉತ್ತರದ IDಗಳು, ಗುರುತಿಸಿದ ಉತ್ತರಗಳ IDಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರತಿ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗೆ ನೀಡಿದ ಅಂಕಗಳನ್ನು ಒದಗಿಸಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಈ ನಿಯಮ ಇರುವುದರಿಂದಲೇ ಉತ್ತರ ಕೀ ಈಗಾಗಲೇ ಬಿಡುಗಡೆಯಾಗಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಅರ್ಥವಲ್ಲ. ಬಿಡುಗಡೆ ಪ್ರಕಟಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಸೂಚನೆಗಳನ್ನು ಅಧಿಕೃತ FMGE ಪುಟಯಲ್ಲಿ ನೋಡಿ.

ಫಲಿತಾಂಶದ ನಂತರ ಮರುಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ ಇದೆಯೇ?

ಫಲಿತಾಂಶವನ್ನು 30 ನವೆಂಬರ್ 2026ರೊಳಗೆ ಪ್ರಕಟಿಸುವ ಸಾಧ್ಯತೆಯಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಕೈಪಿಡಿ ಹೇಳುತ್ತದೆ. ಇದು ನಿರೀಕ್ಷಿತ ಅವಧಿ; ಫಲಿತಾಂಶ ಬಿಡುಗಡೆಯಾಗಿದೆ ಎಂಬ ದೃಢೀಕರಣವಲ್ಲ. FMGEಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮರುಮೌಲ್ಯಮಾಪನ, ಮರುಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ, ಅಂಕಗಳ ಮರುಎಣಿಕೆ ಅಥವಾ ಕೃಪಾಂಕಗಳಿಗೆ ಅವಕಾಶವಿಲ್ಲ. ಫಲಿತಾಂಶದ ಮುಂಚಿನ ತಾಂತ್ರಿಕ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ ಆಕ್ಷೇಪಣೆಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಇವುಗಳನ್ನು ಗೊಂದಲಪಡಿಸಬೇಡಿ.

ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕವಾಗಿ ಅನ್ವಯಿಸುವ ಉತ್ತೀರ್ಣ ಅಂಕಗಳ ನಿಯಮಕ್ಕಾಗಿ FMGE ಉತ್ತೀರ್ಣ ಅಂಕಗಳ ಮಾರ್ಗದರ್ಶಿ ಓದಿ. ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಯ ಕಠಿಣತೆಯ ಕುರಿತ ಪ್ರತಿಕ್ರಿಯೆಗಳು ಅಥವಾ ನೆನಪಿನ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳು ಅಧಿಕೃತ ಫಲಿತಾಂಶವನ್ನು ನಿರ್ಧರಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

title: BVP CET 2027: BTech, BBA ਅਤੇ ਕਾਨੂੰਨ ਦੀਆਂ ਆਖ਼ਰੀ ਮਿਤੀਆਂ ਵੱਖਰੀਆਂ
description: ਭਾਰਤੀ ਵਿਦਿਆਪੀਠ ਦੇ BTech, BBA/BCA ਅਤੇ ਪੰਜ ਸਾਲਾ ਕਾਨੂੰਨ ਕੋਰਸ ਦੀ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ, ਪ੍ਰੀਖਿਆ ਤੇ ਕਾਊਂਸਲਿੰਗ ਦੀਆਂ ਮਿਤੀਆਂ ਵੇਖੋ। ਫਾਰਮ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹਣ ਦੀ ਹਾਲਤ ਵੱਖਰੇ ਤੌਰ ’ਤੇ ਜਾਂਚੋ।
content:
2027 ਵਿੱਚ ਭਾਰਤੀ ਵਿਦਿਆਪੀਠ ਲਈ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਦੇਣੀ ਹੈ? ਇੱਕੋ “BVP CET ਆਖ਼ਰੀ ਮਿਤੀ” ਦੀ ਥਾਂ ਆਪਣੇ ਕੋਰਸ ਦੀ ਮਿਤੀ ਨੋਟ ਕਰੋ। ਯੂਨੀਵਰਸਿਟੀ ਦੀ ਅੰਡਰਗ੍ਰੈਜੂਏਟ ਸਮਾਂ-ਸਾਰਣੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਪੰਜ ਸਾਲਾ ਕਾਨੂੰਨ ਲਈ 7 ਮਈ 2027 ਅਤੇ BTech ਲਈ 24 ਮਈ ਤੱਕ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਦਾ ਸਮਾਂ ਹੈ।

ਤਿੰਨ ਕੋਰਸਾਂ ਦੇ ਕੈਲੰਡਰ ਵੱਖਰੇ ਰੱਖੋ

ਕੋਰਸ

ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਦੀ ਆਖ਼ਰੀ ਮਿਤੀ

ਦਾਖ਼ਲਾ ਪ੍ਰੀਖਿਆ

ਨਤੀਜਾ

ਦਾਖ਼ਲਾ ਅਤੇ ਕਾਊਂਸਲਿੰਗ

ਭਾਰਤੀ ਵਿਦਿਆਪੀਠ ਅੰਡਰਗ੍ਰੈਜੂਏਟ CET ਸਮਾਂ-ਸਾਰਣੀ, 27 ਅਕਤੂਬਰ 2026। ਤਿੰਨ ਕੋਰਸਾਂ ਦੇ ਕੈਲੰਡਰ ਵੱਖਰੇ ਰੱਖੋ.

ਸਮਾਂ-ਸਾਰਣੀ ਵਿੱਚ BBA/BCA ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰੀਖਿਆ ਦਾ ਨਾਂ BUMAT ਹੈ। ਪੰਜ ਸਾਲਾ ਕਾਨੂੰਨ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰੀਖਿਆ BV-LAWUG-2027 ਹੈ। ਤਿੰਨ ਸਾਲਾ LLB ਦੀ ਵੱਖਰੀ ਐਂਟਰੀ ਹੈ। ਉਸ ਕੋਰਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਦਾਖ਼ਲਾ ਚਾਹੁੰਦੇ ਗ੍ਰੈਜੂਏਟ ਪੰਜ ਸਾਲਾ ਕਾਨੂੰਨ ਦੀ ਮਿਤੀ ਨਾ ਵਰਤਣ।

ਸਮਾਂ-ਸਾਰਣੀ ਨਾਲ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦੀ

ਯੂਨੀਵਰਸਿਟੀ ਦੀ ਅਧਿਕਾਰਤ ਵੈੱਬਸਾਈਟ ਤੋਂ ਆਪਣੇ ਕੋਰਸ ਦੀ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਤੱਕ ਜਾਓ। ਸਮਾਂ-ਸਾਰਣੀ ਉਪਰਲੀਆਂ ਮਿਤੀਆਂ ਦੱਸਦੀ ਹੈ; ਇਸ ਨਾਲ ਹੀ ਹਰ ਕੋਰਸ ਦਾ ਰਜਿਸਟ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਨ ਫਾਰਮ ਇਸ ਵੇਲੇ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹਾ ਹੋਣ ਦੀ ਪੁਸ਼ਟੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦੀ। ਭੁਗਤਾਨ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਯੋਗਤਾ, ਫੀਸ, ਦਸਤਾਵੇਜ਼ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰੀਖਿਆ ਪ੍ਰਬੰਧਾਂ ਬਾਰੇ ਸੰਬੰਧਿਤ ਦਾਖ਼ਲਾ ਹਦਾਇਤਾਂ ਪੜ੍ਹੋ।

ਇੱਕ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਧ ਕੋਰਸਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਦੇ ਰਹੇ ਹੋ ਤਾਂ ਹਰ ਫਾਰਮ, ਆਖ਼ਰੀ ਮਿਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਭੁਗਤਾਨ ਰਸੀਦ ਦਾ ਵੱਖਰਾ ਰਿਕਾਰਡ ਰੱਖੋ। ਇੱਕ ਦਾਖ਼ਲਾ ਪ੍ਰੀਖਿਆ ਦੀ ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਕਰਨ ਨਾਲ ਦੂਜੇ ਕੋਰਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੀ ਰਜਿਸਟ੍ਰੇਸ਼ਨ ਹੋ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ, ਇਹ ਨਾ ਮੰਨੋ।

ਜੂਨ ਦੇ ਅਗਲੇ ਪੜਾਅ ਲਈ ਸਮਾਂ ਰੱਖੋ

ਪ੍ਰੀਖਿਆ ਦੀ ਮਿਤੀ ਕੈਲੰਡਰ ਦਾ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਇੱਕ ਹਿੱਸਾ ਹੈ। ਨਤੀਜੇ ਅਤੇ ਕਾਊਂਸਲਿੰਗ ਦਾ ਸਮਾਂ ਵੀ ਨਾਲ ਲਿਖੋ ਅਤੇ ਉਹ ਪੜਾਅ ਨੇੜੇ ਆਉਣ ’ਤੇ ਯੂਨੀਵਰਸਿਟੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਹਦਾਇਤਾਂ ਵੇਖੋ। ਸਮਾਂ-ਸਾਰਣੀ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਕਿਸੇ ਵਿਅਕਤੀ ਨੂੰ ਸੀਟ ਦੀ ਪੇਸ਼ਕਸ਼ ਜਾਂ ਕਾਊਂਸਲਿੰਗ ਦਾ ਸੱਦਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ।

ਅੰਡਰਗ੍ਰੈਜੂਏਟ ਅਤੇ ਪੋਸਟਗ੍ਰੈਜੂਏਟ ਕੋਰਸਾਂ ਦੀ ਵਧੇਰੇ ਜਾਣਕਾਰੀ ਲਈ BVP ਕੋਰਸ ਸਮਾਂ-ਸਾਰਣੀ ਮਾਰਗਦਰਸ਼ਨ ਵੇਖੋ। ਚੁਣੇ ਕੋਰਸ ਲਈ ਬਾਅਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਉਣ ਵਾਲੀ ਅਧਿਕਾਰਤ ਸੋਧ ਮੰਨੋ।

title: NEET PG 2026 Shift Schedule and Test Centre Security Protocol: Biometric Screening and Document Rules Breakdown
description: Comprehensive guide to NEET PG 2026 shift timings, gate closure rules, biometric verification, allowed photo ID cards, and security protocols at exam centres.
content:
NEET PG 2026 Examination Shifts and Reporting Timings

Navigating the NEET PG test day requires strict adherence to scheduled reporting windows and entry timelines. The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences conducts the computer-based test across designated centres nationwide. Candidates must plan their arrival well before the official gate closure time to complete mandatory verification procedures without disruption.

Multiple verification layers operate simultaneously at examination venues. Standard morning and afternoon session frameworks demand that medical graduates reach their assigned test centres as printed on their admit cards. Late entry is strictly prohibited once security gates close, regardless of the reason.

Key Shift Schedules and Timings

  • Morning Shift Reporting Window: 07:00 AM to 08:30 AM
  • Morning Shift Gate Closure: 08:30 AM sharp
  • Morning Examination Hours: 09:00 AM to 12:30 PM
  • Afternoon Shift Reporting Window: 01:00 PM to 02:30 PM
  • Afternoon Shift Gate Closure: 02:30 PM sharp
  • Afternoon Examination Hours: 03:00 PM to 06:30 PM

Mandatory Photo Identity Documents and Admit Card Guidelines

Entry into the examination centre is contingent upon presenting valid identity verification documents. Security officers and venue invigilators cross-check primary identification details against the official candidate roster before granting admission to the registration hall.

Candidates must carry a clear printout of their official admit card issued by the authority, featuring a recent passport-sized photograph pasted in the designated space. Additionally, candidates must present an original, valid, non-expired government-issued photo identity proof.

Acceptable Original Identity Cards

  • PAN Card
  • Voter Identification Card
  • Passport
  • Driving License
  • Aadhaar Card with clear photograph

Candidates holding permanent or provisional medical council registration certificates should carry those details if specified on the admit card. Candidates are advised to verify that the name printed on their photo ID matches the name on the NEET PG admit card exactly. In case of legal name changes, supporting official documentation must be produced.

Biometric Screening and Verification Protocol

To eliminate impersonation and preserve examination integrity, robust digital biometric procedures are enforced at all examination venues. Biometric capture begins right after initial gate security clearance and document validation.

The biometric process captures digital fingerprints and high-resolution facial photographs of every candidate. These biometric records are matched against official database entries and verified again during post-exam admission counseling sessions.

Biometric Check Compliance Steps

  • Ensure fingers are free from ink, henna, chemicals, or superficial injuries that might obscure ridge patterns.
  • Maintain a neutral facial expression during digital photo capture without wearing caps, tinted spectacles, or heavy facial coverings.
  • Cooperate with invigilators during facial recognition scans at the assigned workstation inside the examination laboratory.

Prohibited Items and Dress Code Mandatory Rules

Test centres maintain strict security checks using metal detectors and physical frisking separated by gender. Bringing banned items into the facility leads to immediate disqualification and potential legal action under examination malpractice frameworks.

All personal belongings must be left outside the venue premises as test authorities do not guarantee safe storage for personal property.

Strictly Prohibited Items

  • Mobile phones, smartwatches, Bluetooth devices, earphones, or electronic gadgets.
  • Bags, wallets, purses, belts, stationary items, calculators, or paper scraps.
  • Jewelry, metallic ornaments, hair bands, or metallic hairpins.
  • Eatables, soft drinks, or personal water bottles unless specifically authorized under verified medical exceptions.

Recommended Test Centre Dress Code

Candidates should wear simple, light clothing without large buttons, intricate embroidery, or heavy metallic zips. Standard slippers or sandals with thin soles are recommended footwear. Closed shoes with thick soles may require additional security screening and removal at entry points.

Essential Preparation Checklist for Test Day

Preparation on the morning of the exam ensures a smooth experience at the test site. Candidates and accompanying parents should review all logistical details the evening before the exam.

  • Print the admit card in high resolution on clean white paper.
  • Affix a passport-sized photograph adhering to specified dimension guidelines.
  • Locate the assigned examination venue via map applications to estimate travel time and traffic delays.
  • Arrange accepted original photo identity documents in a clear document pouch.
  • Reach the test venue at least 90 minutes prior to gate closure to avoid rush hours.

Always verify final exam center instructions, schedule adjustments, and safety advisories on the official NBEMS authority portal prior to exam day.

Frequently Asked Questions

What time do examination gates close for NEET PG shifts?

Examination gates close thirty minutes prior to the commencement of the exam. For morning shifts, gates close at 08:30 AM, while afternoon shift gates close at 02:30 PM. No candidate is permitted entry after gate closure.

Which identity cards are accepted at the exam venue?

Candidates must present an original, non-expired government photo ID such as an Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Voter ID, Passport, or Driving License alongside their printed admit card.

Is biometric verification mandatory for all candidates?

Yes, biometric screening including digital fingerprint recording and facial photo capture is mandatory for every candidate prior to entering the computer laboratory.

Are digital copies of ID proof allowed on mobile devices?

No, digital copies, photocopies, or soft images stored on mobile phones or cloud storage are strictly prohibited. Candidates must carry original physical documents.

What items are completely banned inside the exam hall?

Electronic devices, smartwatches, wallets, bags, jewelry, paper notes, pens, and personal edible items are strictly prohibited inside the venue.

title: REET Exam: Complete Guide, Eligibility, Pattern & Preparation Tips
description: REET exam details explained. Check eligibility criteria, exam pattern, key highlights, certificate validity, and preparation tips for teaching jobs in Rajasthan.
content:
A state-level eligibility test called the Rajasthan Eligibility Examination for Teachers (REET) is used to evaluate applicants for teaching posts in Rajasthani government schools for grades 1 through 8. The Board of Secondary Education, Rajasthan (BSER) administers the test, which is required for applicants hoping to work as government school teachers in the state.

REET is an eligibility test that qualifies applicants to apply for upcoming teacher positions that the Rajasthani government announces; it is not a recruiting exam.

Key Highlights of REET Exam

Particulars Details
Exam Name Rajasthan Eligibility Examination for Teachers (REET)
Conducting Authority Board of Secondary Education, Rajasthan
Exam Level State Level
Teaching Levels Level 1 (Classes 1–5), Level 2 (Classes 6–8)
Exam Mode Offline (Pen and Paper)
Question Type Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs)
Total Questions 150 per level
Negative Marking No
Certificate Validity Lifetime

What Is the REET Exam?

There are two levels to the REET test. Candidates who want to teach Classes 1 through 5 should apply for Level 1, and those who want to teach Classes 6 through 8 should apply for Level 2. Depending on their eligibility, candidates may apply for one level or both.

REET Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must have completed Class 12 and earned an elementary education diploma or an equivalent degree in order to be eligible for Level 1. Candidates for Level 2 must have a B.Ed. or comparable teacher training credential in addition to a graduation degree. Prior to applying, qualifying requirements must be met.

REET Exam Pattern

There are 150 questions on each REET paper, each worth one mark, for a total of 150 marks. Candidates can confidently tackle every question because there is no negative marking. Depending on the level, the exam includes portions on language, math, environmental studies, child development and pedagogy, and subject-specific topics.

Why REET Is Important

In Rajasthan, obtaining a government teaching position requires passing the REET. Candidates can apply for teacher recruitment examinations more than once without having to retake the REET exam thanks to the certificate's lifetime validity.

Candidates can pass the REET exam and establish a solid teaching career with diligent study and consistent practice.

title: Assam NEET UG 2026 Stray Allotment: Check Selection List and Reporting
description: Assam has published its NEET UG 2026 stray round provisional selection list. Selected MBBS and BDS candidates must report to their allotted college on 25 or 26 October with original documents. Check the official list before travelling.
content:
Assam's Directorate of Medical Education has published the provisional selection list for the 2026 NEET UG stray round. If you are selected, the immediate task is to identify your allotted college and report there on 25 or 26 October 2026. Missing the reporting window cancels the allotment, according to the official admission notice and selection list.

Find your result in the official list

Open the PDF on the Directorate of Medical Education's admission notices page. The notice is followed by a 39-page provisional selection list. Search with your NEET roll number or application number, then read across the row to the selection details and college name. Do not stop at a matching name. Similar names can appear, and a row marked “NA” for college does not itself tell you that a seat has been allotted. Check the complete row and any later official correction before making travel arrangements.

Reporting on 25 or 26 October

The notice directs provisionally selected candidates to report to the principal's office at their respective allotted college on either date. It says that failure to report will cancel the allotment. The reporting requirement is physical, so downloading the PDF or checking a portal is not a substitute for reaching the college.

Carry the original admit cards, mark sheets and pass certificates for HSLC and HSSLC or equivalent examinations. Bring the relevant caste certificate and other documents required under Assam's MBBS/BDS admission rules. The college will scrutinise the records and assess medical fitness. Ask the college for an acknowledgement when handing over original documents and keep a copy for yourself. The notice says the prescribed agreement must be submitted to the principal's office within 15 days of admission.

What the provisional result does and does not mean

Selection is conditional. DME says admission depends on eligibility, document verification and medical fitness. It also directs candidates to check its website for further notices. Do not treat the list as proof that admission is final, and do not rely on an unofficial fee figure. The admission notice refers to a separate government fee notification dated 24 September 2026 without restating the amounts.

title: NEET 2027: final eligibility criteria and application deadlines India
description: Key final eligibility criteria and important application deadlines for NEET 2027 in India, with a practical timeline and checklists for students and parents.
content:
Fast facts you can act on now

For Indian students and parents planning NEET 2027, the exam's final eligibility criteria and application deadlines determine whether a candidate can sit for the test and how to complete the form without errors. This article focuses on the concrete requirements, important dates, and a practical stepwise timeline to help families navigate the process with confidence.

Who can appear for NEET 2027

NEET is a national entrance test for undergraduate medical courses. The final eligibility criteria for 2027 emphasize two main aspects: nationality/residency and academic qualifications.

  • Nationality: Indian citizens are eligible. Candidates from overseas categories or foreign nationals must verify the specific provisions published by the exam authority for their category, as applicable.
  • Educational qualification: Candidates must have completed class 12 or equivalent with required subjects and percentages. The core requirement is completion of qualifying examination with physics, chemistry, biology/Biotechnology, and a minimum aggregate score in those subjects according to the official policy for the year of admission.
  • Age criteria: There is a minimum age limit for general category candidates and a higher or lower threshold for reserved categories, as defined in the official notification for NEET 2027. Students should ensure they meet the age criteria on the cut-off date specified by the examining authority.
  • Other criteria: Candidates must meet fitness and other eligibility conditions laid out in the official notification and any subsequent corrigenda. These can include requirements about leaving academic programs or other exceptional conditions; verify the latest guidance when filling the form.

What the application process requires

The NEET 2027 application involves several standard steps, and completing them accurately reduces the risk of disqualification or the need for corrections later.

  • Registration: Create a candidate profile with essential personal details, contact information, and identity proofs. Use a reliable email and mobile number since communications will occur through these channels.
  • Academic and category information: Enter board, year of passing, roll number if applicable, and subject details. Have class 12 mark sheet, passing certificate, and category certificates handy for quick entry if required.
  • Document uploads: Scanned copies of photograph, signature, and any mandatory documents must meet specified size and format requirements. Ensure the photo matches current appearance and reflects the guidelines exactly to avoid rejection.
  • Choice of examination center: Select center preferences with attention to travel feasibility and exam-day conditions. Some centers may have limited seating, so prioritize practical options.
  • Payment: Complete the fee payment through the designated gateway. Save the transaction receipt and note the reference number for future tracking.

Important deadlines for NEET 2027

Timelines can shift, but the process typically unfolds as follows. Start early to avoid last-minute issues, especially for document preparation and fee payment.

  • Registration window: Open registration usually a few months before the exam date. Enter all required details accurately and double-check entries before submission.
  • Document verification and corrections: If the portal allows, there is often a short window for corrections. Do not miss these, as changes after the deadline are not permitted.
  • Admit card release: Admit cards are issued after the registration window closes and verification is complete. Download and print the card for exam day readiness.
  • Exam date: The national exam date is announced in the official notification. Plan travel, lodging, and contingency options well in advance.

A practical timeline for families

Use this plan to stay on track. Adjust based on the official notification once released.

  1. Month 1: Gather documents (class 12 marksheet, passing certificate, category certificate if applicable, Aadhaar or other ID as specified). Prepare a recent, compliant photograph and signature.
  2. Month 2: Create the candidate profile and begin application. Have digital copies ready for quick uploads. Confirm spelling and details across all fields.
  3. Month 3: Complete application submission before the deadline. Save the confirmation number and a screenshot of the submitted form. Begin center preference planning with realistic travel options.
  4. Month 4: Monitor for any corrections window if offered. Make timely amendments and re-submit if required. Download the admit card when announced and review exam-day instructions.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Entering incorrect personal information or mismatched names across documents.
  • Missing required documents or uploading non-compliant file formats/sizes.
  • Choosing a center that is impractical for travel or changing centers after submission if not allowed.
  • Delaying fee payment or failing to secure a payment receipt.

What to do if your eligibility is unclear

If any eligibility element is unclear or if you fall into a special category, do not assume. Check the official notification and follow the steps outlined there. In cases where eligibility details are ambiguous, families should seek guidance from the exam authority’s helpline or official channels and verify information before submitting the form.

Checklist for students and parents

  • Confirm you meet all final eligibility criteria for your category and board qualifications.
  • Prepare and verify all required documents well in advance.
  • Keep digital copies organized and accessible for quick uploads.
  • Plan travel and accommodation near the exam center if needed.
  • Monitor the official notification for exact registration windows and deadlines.

Notes on official guidance

When official details on eligibility and deadlines are released, read them precisely and follow the steps as described. If any part of the guidance seems unclear, verify with the authoritative source directly and refrain from relying on secondary summaries. Do not rely on third-party articles for critical dates or eligibility requirements.

Frequently asked questions

1) Who is eligible to appear for NEET 2027 in India?

Indian citizens meeting the prescribed educational qualifications and age criteria, along with any applicable category-specific provisions, are eligible. Check the official notification for exact requirements for your circumstances.

2) What documents do I need to complete the NEET 2027 application?

Standard documents include a recent photograph, signature, class 12 marksheet and passing certificate, identity proof, and category certificates if applicable. Ensure documents meet the specified formats and sizes.

3) How can I avoid common NEET application mistakes?

Double-check spelling, ensure consistency across all fields, upload correctly formatted documents, choose feasible exam centers, and keep payment receipts and submission confirmations safely.

4) When will the NEET admit card be issued?

Admit cards are released after registration and document verification are complete. Download the card promptly and review exam-day instructions printed on it.

5) What should I do if I miss a deadline or need corrections?

Deadlines typically do not allow late submissions or corrections beyond the specified window. If a corrections window is offered, use it promptly to rectify any errors.

6) Can I change my exam center after submission?

Center change policies vary by year. If allowed, it is usually within a defined window. Read the official guidelines carefully and act within the permitted period.

Conclusion

Knowing the final eligibility criteria and the exact application deadlines for NEET 2027 helps families plan with confidence. Start early, gather documents, and monitor the official channels for the precise dates and rules. If in doubt, verify details on the official authority website and proceed only after confirming the exact requirements for your situation.

title: Commerce After Class 12: Is Supply Chain a Better Fit Than Management?
description: Compare undergraduate supply chain and general management routes after Class 12 by subjects, maths, work style, admissions checks and early jobs.
content:
Supply chain courses after Class 12 may suit you better than general management if you like numbers, stock movement, vendors and problem-solving under time pressure. A management degree can fit better if you want wider exposure to marketing, sales, HR, finance and business communication. Neither choice is automatically better.

Here’s the catch: the comparison must be between similar course types. This article compares undergraduate supply chain or logistics degrees with broad undergraduate management degrees, not a short diploma against a three-year or four-year university programme. Course names, duration, eligibility and Mathematics rules vary by institution.

What will you study in each route?

Supply chain curricula commonly cover procurement, inventory, logistics, transport, forecasting, costing, spreadsheets, statistics and business analytics. General management programmes commonly introduce accounting, economics, marketing, human resources, finance and communication, with specialisation or electives in some colleges.

These are broad patterns, not fixed rules. The programme’s university or college is the responsible entity for the syllabus and admission conditions. Treat the following conclusion as a fit-based interpretation: supply chain can point more clearly towards operations work, while management keeps more business areas open. Your first role still depends on the institution, internship, skills and employer.

Which work style is less likely to surprise you?

Decision pointSupply chain routeGeneral management route
Course emphasisStock, purchasing, transport, planning and dataBusiness functions, communication and commercial decisions
Quantitative demandOften regular use of quantities, costs and forecastsUsually varies by papers and chosen role
Possible first rolesOperations trainee, procurement assistant or inventory analystManagement trainee, sales coordinator or HR executive

Actual entry-level duties differ. A supply chain job may involve warehouse visits, shift work, vendor calls or field operations, but not every employer expects all four. A management graduate may support sales, recruitment, administration or campaigns. Read the job description, not just the role title.

What should you check before applying?

  1. Open two course pages for each route and record the exact eligibility rule, Mathematics requirement, duration and degree-awarding university.
  2. Download the syllabus and mark statistics, operations, accounting, forecasting and data-analysis papers.
  3. Check named placement roles and internship settings, such as retailers, manufacturers, procurement teams or warehouses.
  4. Use the courses directory to compare pages, then confirm admission conditions with the responsible institution before submitting an application.

If you choose supply chain, practise reading a stock table and explain how a delayed shipment changes cost and delivery. If you choose management, compare a sales report and prepare a short customer or recruitment plan. That small test will tell you more than popularity claims.

title: Counselling readiness for Indian admissions 2027 across central and state portals with regional backup plans
description: A practical guide for Indian students and parents on preparing for counselling processes for admissions in 2027, covering central and state portals, timelines, required documents, regional backup planning, and how to align counselling with regional education goals.
content:
Key takeaway for families

Successful admission counselling in 2027 hinges on early preparation, cross-portal coordination, and a regional backup plan that buffers against portal downtimes or delays in seat allocation. Start with a verified checklist, track deadlines, and know where to turn for regional alternatives if central portals face heavy load or outages.

Understanding the portal landscape for 2027 admissions

India runs multiple portals for central and state-level admissions. Central portals cater to national-level programmes and certain centralized admissions, while state portals handle state-level courses and quotas. In many states, counselling sessions follow a two-tier flow: initial seat allotment rounds, followed by upgrading rounds and final acceptance. Students should plan to monitor both types of portals and set alerts for important dates.

Central portals: what to expect

  • Unified application windows for common admissions and some national institutes.
  • Common documentation requirements, including identity, qualifying examination results, and category certificates where applicable.
  • Several rounds of seat allotment with the possibility of upgradation based on vacancy and merit lists.

State portals: regional variation matters

  • State boards and state-level counselling bodies set quotas for home-state and other categories. Some states may reserve seats for special programs or for local students in certain districts.
  • Document formats and submission methods can vary. Some states offer both online and offline verification paths; others move entirely online for efficiency.

Timelines and preparation steps for 2027 admissions

Begin preparation well before counselling opens. A proactive plan reduces last-minute stress and helps secure preferred programmes. Use the following phased approach:

  1. Phase 1: Information gathering (6-9 months before counselling) - List potential courses, institutes, and states. Create a document with eligibility criteria, required certificates, and potential reservation benefits. Note any special rounds for reserve categories if applicable.
  2. Phase 2: Documentation readiness (4-6 months before counselling) - Ensure you have standard documents in multiple digital formats, including identity proofs, qualifying exam marksheets, migration certificates if needed, and category certificates. Preserve scanned copies with clear filenames for quick retrieval.
  3. Phase 3: Online profile and password hygiene (2-4 months before counselling) - Create or update profiles on all relevant portals. Use strong passwords and enable two-factor authentication where offered. Prepare secure backups of login information to prevent access issues during peak times.
  4. Phase 4: Mock checks and backup plans (1-2 months before counselling) - Run through the expected steps on trial basis, noting where to upload documents and how to verify entries. Establish a regional backup plan in case central portals are slow or temporarily unavailable.

Counselling readiness checklist

  • Verified identity and eligibility: ensure your name, date of birth, and academic records match on all portals.
  • Category and reservation documents: keep current certificates ready if applicable to your state or category.
  • Academic transcripts: have marksheets for 10th/12th and qualifying exams, along with any required entrance scores.
  • Admission preferences: shortlist institutes and programmes with their feeder streams and eligibility criteria.
  • Payment readiness: if fees or processing charges are part of the portal, have a payment plan ready and accessible.
  • Backup contact points: keep regional helpdesk numbers and email IDs handy for faster resolution during portal issues.

Regional backup plans for Indian students

Regional backup plans help families navigate potential disruptions in central or state portals. Consider the following practical options:

  • - Many institutes maintain regional representatives who can guide applicants through counselling processes, verify documents offline, and help with seat confirmation once online rounds conclude.
  • - Some states provide in-person support centers or district-level help desks during key counselling phases. Visit these centers if online access becomes a bottleneck in your area.
  • - If home internet is intermittent, identify nearby libraries, community centers, or colleges that offer reliable internet access during critical windows.
  • - Maintain both digital and ready-to-print copies of all certificates. In case of portal outages, you can submit hard copies as per institute guidelines when allowed.
  • - Monitor official state education department announcements via SMS or official mobile apps, where available, to receive real-time guidance on changes to schedules or procedures.

What to verify on the day of counselling

On the day you participate in counselling, confirm these essentials to avoid last-minute hiccups:

  • Your registered mobile number is active and accessible for OTP verifications.
  • There is sufficient wallet balance or payment method ready if a fee is due during allotment rounds.
  • Document uploads are complete and timestamped, with backups stored securely.
  • You understand the rules for seat allotment, upgradation, and final acceptance to prevent accidental loss of a seat.

Common questions about counselling readiness

FAQ 1: How early should I start preparing for counselling?

Begin at least six to nine months before the counselling window opens. This allows time to gather documents, verify eligibility, and create backups for regional plans.

FAQ 2: What if central portals are slow or down during rounds?

Rely on regional backup plans first. Use state-level help desks, offline document verification, and alternate channels for updates. Do not wait to act on deadlines; communicate any issues promptly through official channels.

FAQ 3: Do I need different documents for central and state counselling?

The core documents are similar, but some states may require additional certificates or forms of residence proof. Prepare a master folder with all potential certificates and keep originals handy for verification.

FAQ 4: How can I ensure my documents are correctly matched across portals?

Use consistent spellings of names, parent/guardian details, and dates of birth. Maintain digital copies with clear labeling and ensure scanned documents are legible before uploading.

FAQ 5: What happens if I miss a counselling deadline?

Missed deadlines can limit options. Your regional backup plan may still offer a chance to secure a seat. Always check alternative rounds or institute-level admissions guidelines on official channels promptly.

Final guidance

Planning for 2027 admissions requires coordination across central and state portals and a practical regional backup plan. Establish a written schedule with key dates, prepare all essential documents in digital and physical forms, and keep multiple, secure backups. Encourage families to stay informed through official alerts and to lean on local admissions offices for support when online systems are strained. With proactive preparation, students can navigate the counselling process more smoothly and focus on securing a seat in the programme that best fits their goals.

title: CLAT 2027 College Choice: Check These Rules Before Paying Fees
description: Compare a CLAT 2027 law seat by eligibility, total fee liability, reporting terms and withdrawal risk before accepting an allotment.
content:
A CLAT 2027 allotment is not a final decision until you check the course rules, payable amount, reporting deadline and withdrawal terms. Before paying through counselling, download the allotment notice, read the university instructions and calculate what the seat will cost your family if you later move or withdraw.

A high rank can open a door. It doesn’t tell you whether the fee, location or course conditions fit.

Start with the CLAT exam guide for the counselling context, then compare each allotted seat using the same four checks below.

What should you verify in a CLAT 2027 allotment?

Check the exact programme name, eligibility condition, payment deadline and reporting requirement in the allotment communication. Don’t assume that a seat in a participating National Law University means every document or category claim has already been accepted; the admitting university can still require certificates and physical or online reporting.

  • Course: Confirm whether it is the five-year integrated law programme you selected, and read any subject or passing-condition requirement.
  • Documents: Match your application details with marksheets, category certificates, domicile proof, identity documents and other items named in the notice.
  • Reporting: Note the exact time, reporting mode, payment gateway and consequence of missing the deadline.
  • Money: Separate the counselling payment, university fee, hostel charge, mess bill, deposits and one-time charges.

How do fees and withdrawal rules change the decision?

Fees should be compared as money at risk, not just as a brochure figure. A parent may see a manageable first payment, while the written rules may impose later instalments, non-refundable components or a deadline for withdrawal. The CLAT 2027 counselling notice and the university’s admission rules should control your decision, not a coaching-centre estimate.

CheckQuestion to askWhy it matters
PaymentWhat must be paid now?Missing the amount or deadline can affect seat retention.
RefundWhich parts return after withdrawal?You may lose more than the counselling charge.
ReportingIs online payment enough?Some admission steps may still require document submission.
Course fitDoes the programme match your eligibility?A fee payment cannot fix a later document or eligibility problem.

Should you freeze, float or withdraw?

Choose freeze only when the college, course and cost work for your family. Float can make sense when you would genuinely accept an upward allotment and can meet another payment deadline. Withdraw only after recording the refund rule and saving the acknowledgement.

Make a one-page comparison for every seat: total first-year outgo, hostel need, reporting date, refund exposure and preferred order. That simple sheet can stop a rushed payment from deciding your five-year law plan.

title: NAAC grade versus NIRF rank what matters when choosing a college
description: NAAC grade and NIRF rank measure different things. Learn which signal matters more for quality, risk, placement context and college fit before admission.
content:
Answer first

If you are choosing a college in India, do not treat NAAC grade and NIRF rank as the same thing. NAAC mainly tells you about institutional accreditation and quality assurance, while NIRF compares institutions on a performance ranking model. For a safer admission decision, use NAAC to check reliability and compliance, then use NIRF to compare relative standing, and finally judge whether the course, faculty, location, fees and placement fit your goal.

In simple terms: NAAC answers “is this college accredited and how strong is its internal quality system?” NIRF answers “how does it perform against other colleges on a national benchmark?” A college can have a decent accreditation grade and still not rank high, or rank well while not giving the exact course experience you need. That is why students and parents should use both, not either one alone.

Key facts

  • NAAC is an accreditation framework connected to quality assurance. It is especially useful for judging whether a college has been formally reviewed on institutional processes, teaching support, student systems and overall academic environment.
  • NIRF is a ranking framework used to compare institutions on a score-based model that looks at multiple parameters such as teaching, learning, research, graduation outcomes and perception.
  • NAAC grade is not a placement guarantee. A higher grade suggests stronger institutional processes, but it does not automatically mean better jobs, a better campus life or the best course for your stream.
  • NIRF rank is not a substitute for fit. A college may rank well overall but still be weak in your exact subject, city preference, fee range or hostel needs.
  • For risk reduction, accreditation matters more. If a college has weak or missing accreditation signals, that is a warning sign for students and parents, especially for a major fee commitment.

What NAAC and NIRF actually measure

NAAC focuses on whether a college or university has been assessed for quality in a broad institutional sense. It is about accreditation status and grade, which can help you understand whether the institution has passed a structured review of academic and support systems.

NIRF is a comparative ranking system. It places institutions in order based on a formula that includes several performance dimensions. A higher rank means the institution scored better in that national comparison year, but it still does not tell the full story of your branch, classroom experience or placement probability.

That difference matters because many families use the two signals for the wrong question. They ask which one is “better”, when the better question is what decision does each signal help me make?

Use NAAC when you want to know

  • Whether the college has formal quality accreditation
  • Whether the institution has a basic system of academic review
  • Whether the college looks institutionally stable enough for a long course
  • Whether you should be cautious about a college that offers attractive promises but weak documentation

Use NIRF when you want to know

  • How the college compares with others nationally
  • Whether it has stronger overall outcomes than similar institutions
  • Whether the institution is improving or slipping in competitive standing
  • Whether it is worth shortlisting alongside peer colleges

Why students should not choose on rank alone

A rank can create a false sense of certainty. Two colleges may sit close to each other in NIRF, but one may be better for engineering, another for arts, and a third may have better local industry access. For example, a student from a middle-income family may see a high-ranked college and assume it is automatically the right choice. But if the fees are too high, the course is over-subscribed, the commute is unrealistic, or the hostel is unavailable, that “better” college may become a poor practical decision.

Parents often worry about safety, continuity and return on investment. For them, NAAC helps confirm whether the college has been through a recognized quality check, while NIRF helps place it in a broader competitive group. Used together, they reduce the chance of selecting a college that looks attractive in advertisements but weak in actual systems.

Why students should not choose on NAAC grade alone

NAAC is valuable, but it does not answer every admission question. A college can have an acceptable or even strong accreditation grade and still not be the best option for your subject, city, budget or career plans. A student seeking computer science placement in a metro city should not ignore NIRF, branch reputation, recruiter presence and internship ecosystem just because the college has a good NAAC grade.

NAAC is best understood as a quality floor signal. It tells you whether the institution has crossed a serious review threshold. It does not tell you whether it is the best option among nearby alternatives for your exact goal.

How to decide: a practical comparison framework

Use this simple order before finalizing admission:

Decision questionBetter signalWhat you should check
Is the college institutionally credible?NAACAccreditation status, grade and validity
How strong is it against peer institutions?NIRFRank band, category and year-to-year trend
Will my course and branch perform well?Both, plus course dataDepartment strength, labs, faculty, internships, placement records
Can my family afford it comfortably?Neither aloneTotal fees, hostel, travel and scholarship options
Will this college fit my career plan?Neither aloneLocation, alumni network, recruiter access, higher studies record

If you are comparing two colleges, use this rule of thumb:

  • Choose the one with stronger accreditation if one college has weak or unclear quality signals.
  • Choose the one with better ranking and better course fit if both are similarly credible.
  • Do not pick the highest-ranked college automatically if the branch, fees or location do not suit you.

A simple college decision checklist for students and parents

  1. Check whether the college is properly accredited and whether the accreditation is current.
  2. Compare the NIRF position in the relevant category, not just the overall headline rank.
  3. Look at the exact program, not only the institution name.
  4. Review fee structure, scholarships and refund rules.
  5. Check placement data carefully and ask what the numbers actually represent.
  6. Confirm hostel, safety, transport and distance from home.
  7. Ask whether the college suits your target: job, higher studies, government exams or entrepreneurship.

This checklist is especially useful when families are under pressure to finalize quickly during admission season. A structured comparison helps prevent the common mistake of chasing prestige while ignoring practical fit.

What to verify on the official college and regulator pages

Before paying a fee or confirming admission, verify three things directly from the responsible official pages: the college’s accreditation status, the latest ranking category and the current program details. If the college says it is “top rated” but the ranking category is unclear, or the accreditation appears outdated, ask for proof. Keep screenshots or printed copies of the current status for your records.

If the college is not transparent about accreditation, placement definitions, or category-specific ranking claims, treat that as a warning sign. Transparency is part of college quality, not a bonus.

Bottom line

NAAC and NIRF answer different questions. NAAC is more useful for judging institutional credibility and accreditation, while NIRF is more useful for comparing colleges on national performance. For the best decision, use NAAC to screen for quality risk, use NIRF to compare standing, and then choose based on course fit, fees, location and career outcome. The safest college is not always the highest-ranked one. It is the one that is credible, suitable and affordable for the student’s actual goal.

FAQs

Which is more important, NAAC grade or NIRF rank?

Neither is universally more important. NAAC is better for checking accreditation and quality credibility, while NIRF is better for comparing institutions nationally. For final admission decisions, use both along with course fit, fees and placement context.

Can a college have a good NAAC grade but a low NIRF rank?

Yes. A college can be well accredited but not score as highly in a ranking comparison. That does not automatically make it weak. It may simply be stronger in internal quality systems than in the specific ranking parameters or relative competition set.

Can a college have a high NIRF rank but a weak NAAC grade?

It can happen in some cases, so students should not assume a rank alone proves overall suitability. If you see a strong rank but unclear accreditation, verify the current accreditation status before paying fees or accepting admission.

Does NAAC grade guarantee placements?

No. NAAC does not guarantee placements. It indicates quality review of the institution, not job outcomes. For placements, also check the branch-wise recruiter pattern, internship support, alumni outcomes and how the college reports placement numbers.

Should parents trust ranking more than accreditation?

Parents should not rely on ranking alone. Accreditation helps reduce risk, while ranking helps compare reputation and performance. A balanced decision uses both signals and then checks fees, safety, commute and career fit.

What should I check first when comparing two colleges?

Check accreditation first if you are worried about credibility or long-term quality. Then compare NIRF in the correct category, followed by the specific course, total cost, location and placement information. This order helps prevent costly admission mistakes.

title: JEE Main 2026: IIIT Hyderabad UGEE Admission Without 75%
description: IIIT Hyderabad allows JEE Main 2026 aspirants to secure B.Tech admission through UGEE without the 75% board marks requirement. Check eligibility and selection process.
content:
A flexible admissions approach for JEE Main 2026 candidates has recently been offered by IIIT Hyderabad.  Traditionally, candidates needed at least 75% marks in class 12 or be in the top 20 percentile of their board to be eligible.  However, by applying through the Undergraduate Engineering Entrance Examination (UGEE), candidates can now obtain admission without meeting the 75% requirement.

About UGEE

IIIT Hyderabad's entrance exam, UGEE, is intended to assess students' analytical, logical, and problem-solving skills.  Candidates who might not meet the traditional board percentage criteria nevertheless have an equal opportunity to compete for spots in the B.Tech program thanks to this exam.  Talented students won't be turned away because of stringent board mark standards thanks to the UGEE route.

Eligibility and Selection

To apply through UGEE, students must have finished their 12th grade or equivalent from a recognized board.  Counseling and document verification come after passing the UGEE as part of the selection process.  This method is especially advantageous for students from boards where marking patterns are rigorous or for those who thrive in ability and problem-solving rather than rote memory.

Benefits of the UGEE Pathway

This program guarantees that competent students are not disqualified based on percentage criteria, promotes merit-based selection, and improves accessibility.  It expands chances for a wide range of candidates while reflecting IIIT Hyderabad's dedication to academic achievement.
