title: JEE Main 2027 Registration: What Aadhaar and City Errors Can Cost
description: Audit identity, category and exam-city entries before submitting JEE Main 2027 registration, while keeping unconfirmed NTA rules separate from practical checks.
content:
JEE Main 2027 applicants should treat Aadhaar, category and examination-city entries as a pre-submission audit, not as routine form filling. A spelling error can leave you checking documents later, while an impractical city choice can create avoidable travel pressure. The National Testing Agency has not yet been shown, in the available evidence, to have confirmed the 2027 field rules or correction facility.

So separate two things: what the live NTA form and notice actually require, and what is simply sensible preparation. The official JEE Main website is the right place to check the current instructions before you submit.

Which identity details should you compare?

Read the preview against the identity document you plan to use. Check the exact spelling of your name, date of birth, gender, initials, spacing and surname order. Don’t rely on a coaching form or an old saved application.

  • Use the name and date format shown by the live NTA form.
  • Follow only the identity-document choices displayed in that form and its notice.
  • Keep your registered mobile number and email account accessible after submission.
  • If records differ, don’t guess which version NTA will accept. Check the stated instructions before paying.

This is a practical precaution, not a claim that every mismatch triggers a special NTA identity procedure. No such 2027 process is established by the supplied evidence.

What makes a category entry risky?

Compare the category selected in the preview with the certificate and documents you actually have. Check the name, category wording, certificate date or validity details, issuing information and any condition shown in the current NTA instructions. These are applicant checks, not confirmed 2027 certificate rules.

If a certificate is pending, outdated or unavailable, pause before submission and read the applicable notice on the official JEE Main website. A forwarded message cannot decide what NTA will accept.

How should you choose examination cities?

Choose preferences your family can reach reliably, with a workable train or road route, manageable overnight travel and a backup plan. A city preference isn’t the same as a confirmed examination centre. Treat that distinction as practical planning until NTA publishes the 2027 allotment rules.

Don’t assume a later correction window will cover city fields. NTA must specify the editable fields, dates and conditions. Save the submitted application PDF, application number and payment record in two locations.

Five-minute submission audit

  1. Read every preview field aloud.
  2. Compare identity details character by character.
  3. Check category and certificate status.
  4. Review city preferences against the actual travel route.
  5. Save the final record after submission.

Before you lock the next step, compare entrance exams against the options you have shortlisted.

title: NEET UG 2026 Stray Vacancy: When Waiting Can Cost You a Medical Seat
description: Should you wait for NEET UG 2026 stray vacancy seats? Compare eligibility, reporting risk, fee exposure and the safer choice before leaving an available seat.
content:
Waiting for the NEET UG 2026 Stray Vacancy Round makes sense only when your current seat is unacceptable and the responsible counselling authority confirms that you’re eligible. If you already hold an MBBS or BDS seat, giving it up for a hoped-for vacancy can leave you with no confirmed admission.

NEET is conducted by the National Testing Agency, but NTA doesn’t allot medical seats. For central counselling, the Medical Counselling Committee handles the counselling route. State quota and state-controlled seats are handled by the designated state counselling authority. Registration, eligibility, reporting, resignation and refund conditions can differ between these routes.

Should you wait for a stray vacancy seat?

Wait only after checking four facts: you can enter that round, a realistic vacancy could improve your current option, your family can absorb the possible loss, and you know the last date for reporting to the seat you already have.

The 2026 rules may depend on whether you were allotted a seat, reported to it, resigned, joined an earlier round or stayed out of counselling. Those are not universal assumptions. Match your exact situation with the 2026 stray vacancy notice issued by MCC or the relevant state authority when it is published. The available official NEET website confirms where current exam notices appear, but it does not establish counselling dates, fees or stray-round eligibility.

When accepting the available seat is safer

A missed joining deadline can cancel your allotment. Leaving after admission may affect tuition, security deposit or other payments, and the authority may place conditions on later participation. The college’s refund terms can also matter. Get the rule in writing before surrendering anything.

Be especially careful with a private MBBS seat. Don’t pay a large amount merely to keep hoping for a government vacancy. Withdrawal, refund and later participation rules can differ sharply by authority and college. Ask both for written confirmation and keep the reply.

A four-check decision before you give up the seat

  1. Confirm eligibility in the applicable MCC or state 2026 notice, including your earlier allotment and reporting status.
  2. Compare your present college, course and category with vacancies you could realistically receive, not with an ideal seat list.
  3. Calculate the money at risk: paid fees, possible deductions, fresh fees, travel, accommodation and document costs.
  4. Verify the final reporting date, save the allotment letter and receipts, and surrender only after you understand the written consequences.

For exam-related notices, use the official NEET UG website. For counselling action, follow the notice issued by the authority handling your seat. You can also review the NEET UG exam guide, but counselling rules must come from MCC or your state authority.

title: The Success Story of Groww: Transforming Investments for Millennials & Gen Z
description: Explore the inspiring success story of Groww, an Indian investment platform that has reshaped how millennials and Gen Z invest in stocks, mutual funds, and ETFs. Learn how it democratized investing with its user-friendly approach and innovative tools.
content:
Groww Success Story: Transforming the Investment Landscape in India

Introduction: Groww, a leading investment platform in India, has made a significant impact on the Indian fintech ecosystem. Founded in 2016 by three ex-Flipkart employees – Lalit Keshre, Ishan Bansal, and Arjun Kothari – Groww’s mission was simple: to make investing in mutual funds and stocks easy, accessible, and transparent for everyone. With a focus on millennials and Gen Z, Groww has disrupted traditional investing models, making it easier for users to navigate the often-complex world of investments.

Early Struggles & Challenges:

Starting as a mutual fund platform, Groww faced early challenges in gaining trust from investors, especially in a market where traditional investment practices dominated. However, the founders, driven by a vision to democratize wealth-building for young Indians, persisted in their mission to simplify the investment process.

Initially, the company struggled with educating the masses about the importance of investing. However, Groww’s team took the approach of being fully transparent about fees, risks, and returns, which soon began to build a loyal user base.

Key Milestones in the Journey:

  1. Launch of Stock Trading Platform: In 2018, Groww made a game-changing decision – it expanded its offering to include direct stock trading. This move allowed users to invest in a wider range of financial products, attracting a broader audience. The introduction of zero brokerage charges for trading was a major attraction, further solidifying its reputation as a customer-first platform.

  2. User-Centric Interface: Unlike traditional platforms that were difficult to navigate, Groww designed a user-friendly, mobile-first interface that appealed to tech-savvy millennials. This helped the platform gain quick traction in the Indian market, particularly among first-time investors who were previously intimidated by complicated investment products and platforms.

  3. Series A Funding and Expanding Team: In 2018, Groww raised its Series A funding of $6 million from Sequoia Capital and Tiger Global, a vital step in fueling its growth. This funding allowed Groww to expand its services, build a stronger product, and improve its technology infrastructure.

  4. Customer Growth & Recognition: By 2020, Groww had surpassed 10 million users, making it one of India’s fastest-growing fintech platforms. It also received recognition in the industry for its ability to simplify complex investment processes. Groww’s commitment to offering transparent and low-cost financial services resonated with millions of Indians who had previously been underserved by traditional banks and brokers.

  5. Diversification and Offerings: As the company grew, so did its product offerings. In 2021, Groww started offering stock trading in a seamless manner, integrated with various educational content, and analytical tools. The platform enabled users to track their portfolios, access expert insights, and invest with a greater understanding of the market.

  6. Massive Valuation: In 2021, Groww reached a significant milestone by becoming a unicorn, crossing a valuation of $1 billion. This was a testament to the increasing demand for its services and its impact on the Indian investment ecosystem.

  7. Partnering with Top Financial Institutions: Groww collaborated with some of the leading financial institutions in India to ensure access to the best mutual fund products, making investing simple, fast, and reliable. By partnering with these institutions, Groww improved its credibility in the market and helped users make informed choices.

The Growth Story: From a Simple Idea to Industry Leader

Today, Groww stands as one of the most trusted and popular online investment platforms in India. With its extensive user base and comprehensive service offerings, it is shaping the future of investing for the next generation. The company has not only focused on providing financial products but also educates users on the best investment practices, risk management, and portfolio strategies.

What sets Groww apart is its vision to democratize wealth creation. It aims to break the barriers that traditionally separated everyday people from wealth-building tools and opportunities. Through continuous innovation and user-first policies, Groww has empowered millions of Indians to take control of their financial futures, making investing accessible to all.

The Future of Groww:

As the Indian fintech ecosystem continues to grow, Groww is well-positioned to remain at the forefront of the industry. With new features like fractional shares, SIP (Systematic Investment Plan) options for stocks, and global investment options, the company is poised to further revolutionize the investment landscape.

Conclusion:

Groww’s journey from a startup to a unicorn is an inspiring testament to the power of innovation and the ability to simplify complex concepts for the masses. By focusing on user experience and making investing easy, transparent, and low-cost, Groww has redefined how Indians approach wealth creation and financial independence. Today, it stands as a shining example of how technology can transform an entire industry for the better.

title: Decoding Indian Scholarship Ecosystems: How to Identify, Apply For, and Secure Funding Across Central, State, and Private Programs
description: A practical guide for Indian students and parents to locate, apply for, and secure funding from central, state, and private scholarship programs with actionable steps and real-world tips.
content:
Understanding the scholarship landscape in India

Scholarships in India come from three broad sources: central government schemes, state government programs, and private or nonprofit initiatives. Each category has distinct eligibility criteria, application timelines, and funding scopes. Mapping these options early helps families align academic goals with available support and reduces the burden of financing higher education.

Central government scholarships and fellowships

Central schemes often target specific groups, such as dependents of armed forces personnel, students pursuing technical or scientific education, or those from economically disadvantaged backgrounds. Key characteristics include:

  • National-level coverage, often with standardized eligibility norms.
  • Common application portals or single sign-on processes for multiple schemes.
  • Funding can cover tuition, maintenance allowances, and travel grants, depending on the program.

Action steps:

  • Identify schemes relevant to your field of study and family background.
  • Note important deadlines and required documents, such as income certificates, academic records, and identity proofs.
  • Prepare a basic shortlist of up to five central schemes to monitor throughout the admission cycle.

State government scholarships

States run a mix of merit-based and need-based scholarships, often with focus on domicile students, rural candidates, or students pursuing courses within the state. Typical features include:

  • State-specific eligibility rules and reservation considerations.
  • Separate application windows that may open after admissions.
  • Funding may cover tuition, stipends, and book allowances, sometimes with renewal criteria tied to academic performance.

Action steps:

  • Consult the state education department portal or designated scholarship portals for your district and school type.
  • Track renewal requirements year by year to avoid lapses in funding.
  • Engage with school counselors or district education officers who can help with documentation and processes.

Private and nonprofit scholarships

Private scholarships span corporate CSR programs, private trusts, foundations, and alumni networks. They often emphasize merit, leadership, specific disciplines, or geographic origins. Highlights include:

  • Broad variance in award amounts and renewal conditions.
  • Faster decision timelines in some cases, but with highly competitive selection processes.
  • Clear communication about required essays, recommendations, and project work.

Action steps:

  • Build a focused list of scholarships aligned with academic interests and career goals.
  • Prepare a robust portfolio: academic records, letters of recommendation, a concise personal statement, and any required essays.
  • Stay alert for notification cycles and keep copies of all submitted documents for reference.

How to identify opportunities efficiently

Develop a practical research routine rather than chasing every available grant. Useful approaches include:

  • Set up a monthly scholarship tracking sheet with scheme names, deadlines, required documents, and status updates.
  • Register for official alerts if available and subscribe to trusted education portals that curate scholarship news without relying on unofficial postings.
  • Leverage school and college admission offices, which often maintain updated lists of eligible schemes and renewal criteria.

Crafting competitive applications

Strong applications share a few core elements across schemes:

  • Clear demonstration of financial need or merit aligned with the program’s aims.
  • Consistency between academic records and stated goals in essays or statements of purpose.
  • Thoughtful letters of recommendation from teachers or mentors who can attest to character and achievement.

Practical tips:

  • Keep digital copies of all forms and documents in a single organized folder.
  • Draft essays early, then revise for clarity, impact, and alignment with the scholarship’s objectives.
  • Double-check spellings, numbers, and contact details to prevent processing delays.

Common pitfalls and how to avoid them

  • Missing deadlines due to poor calendar management. Solution: maintain a reminders system and check portals weekly during peak cycles.
  • Incomplete applications. Solution: use a checklist before submission and verify each document meets format and size requirements.
  • Ignoring renewal criteria. Solution: note academic performance thresholds and required reports for each scheme at the outset.

Verifying details and where to look for official guidance

Scholarship specifics can change from year to year. Always verify eligibility, deadlines, and renewal terms on the official portal of the respective scheme. If you cannot locate this information easily, contact the relevant state education department or the central portal’s help desk for guidance. Rely on trusted educational authorities and direct government or foundation communications for final confirmation.

Putting it into a plan: a six-step approach

  1. Map your field of study and potential financial needs.
  2. Build a curated list of central, state, and private scholarships with basic eligibility notes.
  3. Prepare a generic application packet: academic records, identity documents, a personal statement, and recommendation letters.
  4. tailor additional materials (essays, project abstracts) to individual schemes as required.
  5. Submit applications well before deadlines and track confirmation receipts.
  6. Monitor renewal criteria and maintain academic performance to secure ongoing funding.

FAQ

What is the first step to start seeking scholarships?

Begin with central and state schemes that match your field of study and family background, then add relevant private scholarships. Create a simple tracker to manage deadlines and required documents.

How do I know if I am eligible for a central government scholarship?

Eligibility is typically defined by factors such as course type, stream, category, and family income. Check the official scheme page for precise criteria and required proofs.

Can I apply to multiple scholarships at the same time?

Yes. Apply to several programs that fit your profile, but tailor each application to its aims. Keep track of overlapping deadlines to avoid conflicts.

What documents are usually required?

Common documents include identity proof, academic transcripts, income certificates, caste or category certificates if applicable, passport-sized photos, and recommendation letters. Some schemes may require essays or project proposals.

How can I improve my chances in private scholarships?

Highlight leadership or community involvement, provide a clear statement of purpose, and obtain strong recommendations. Ensure essays address the scholarship’s stated objectives and demonstrate impact.

description: Understand CUET 2027 central and state counselling timelines, eligibility, and portal steps. A practical, student-focused guide for Indian families planning admission.
content:
Why this matters now

CUET 2027 introduces integrated counselling across central bodies and state authorities. Knowing the exact timelines, portal access, and document requirements helps families plan early, avoid last-minute stress, and align options with preferred institutions.

What changes this year

Besides the exam itself, admission authorities may publish parallel schedules for centralized counselling and state-level processes. Users must distinguish between the common application window and state-specific allotment rounds, as both influence final seat allocation and fee structure.

Key terms to know

  • CUET Counseling Portal: The unified online interface or state variants where applicants register, fill choices, and view allotments.
  • Merit-based rounds: Seat distribution based on CUET scores and eligibility criteria set by authorities.
  • Document verification: A mandatory step post-allotment to confirm identity and academic records.
  • Cut-off marks: Minimum scores for program eligibility, varying by course, campus, and category.

Timeline overview: central vs state pathways

The process typically unfolds in parallel tracks. Central counselling may be coordinated by a national body for participating universities and participating programs, while state counselling operates through state portals for public and private institutions under state jurisdiction. Both tracks require registration, choice filling, and payment of processing fees.

Central counselling timeline (illustrative)

  • Registration window opens: Prepare CUET application number, personal details, and requisite documents.
  • Eligible programs published: Review shortlist of degree courses and campuses.
  • Choice filling and lock-in: Prioritize programs; consider backup options.
  • Allotment results published: Check status on the central portal.
  • Document verification: Submit originals/attested copies as required.
  • Seat confirmation and reporting: Complete seat acceptance and report to designated institute.

State counselling timeline (typical flow)

  • State portal opens for registration: Individual state authorities may require separate login credentials.
  • College and course lists released: Focus on region-specific opportunities.
  • Choice filling and round details: Some states run multiple rounds with varying deadlines.
  • State allotment results: Publicized on the state portal; cross-check with central results where applicable.
  • Provisional admission and verification: Submit state-required documents and migrate to the institution.

Practical steps to navigate both tracks

  1. Prepare documents early:10th and 12th mark sheets, identity proofs, category certificates, passport-size photos, and CUET scorecard.
  2. Create a master list of programs: Include a mix of preferred, safe, and aspirational options from central and state lists.
  3. Note critical deadlines: Mark opening dates, last dates for registration, and last dates for fee payment and choice locking.
  4. Cross-check eligibility rules: Some programs or colleges may have additional criteria beyond CUET scores.
  5. Monitor official portals: Set reminders for status updates, document verification windows, and reporting instructions.
  6. Plan for contingencies: Have alternative programs in case preferred options are not allotted in time.

Document checklist and verification tips

  • CUET admit card and score report
  • 12th grade mark sheet and passing certificate
  • Identity proof (Aadhaar or equivalent)
  • Category certificates if applicable
  • Migration or equivalency certificates if required
  • Photographs and scanned copies as per portal specifications

Always verify document requirements on the official portals for each track. If the portal asks for specific formats or additional certificates, prepare them in advance to avoid delays.

Strategic tips for choosing programs

  • Balance merit and interest: Do not rely solely on rank; consider campus location, faculty strength, and placement records.
  • Rank in the context of program demand: Some popular courses may have higher cut-offs in both central and state rounds.
  • Consider back-up options: Include programs from both central and state lists to broaden chances of admission.
  • Track fee structures: Central and state institutes may have different fee regimes; factor scholarships and financial aid into the decision.

What if timelines differ or change?

Counselling timelines may be revised by authorities in response to orders or practical considerations. Students should rely on the official counselling portals for the most current dates and procedures. If dates appear unclear, verify on the relevant authority’s site and set alerts to catch any updates promptly.

Frequently asked questions

Q1: When will central CUET counselling begin for 2027 admissions?

A: The exact start date will be published on the central counselling portal. Prepare by having your CUET score, eligible documents, and a prioritized list of programs ready.

Q2: Do I need separate registrations for central and state counselling?

A: Yes. Some states run their own portals with unique login processes. It is important to complete registrations on both tracks if you are aiming for programs across different jurisdictions.

Q3: How many rounds are typical in counselling?

A: Central and state authorities may publish multiple rounds, including mop-up rounds. Each round has its own deadlines for choice filling and seat confirmation.

Q4: What documents are commonly required for verification?

A: Identity proof, prior academic certificates, category certificates if eligible, CUET score card, and recent photographs. Always confirm on the official portal for any additional requirements.

Q5: Can I change my program after seat allotment?

A: Some processes allow changes within the allotted framework during specified windows. Review the instructions on the portal and proceed before the deadline.

Q6: How should I prioritize programs across central and state lists?

A: Build a mix of preferred, safe, and backup options. Consider campus location, course demand, and future opportunities to optimize your choices.

Bottom line

CUET 2027 introduces parallel central and state counselling pathways. By preparing early, maintaining organized documents, and aligning program choices with realistic expectations, students can navigate the process with clarity and reduce last-minute stress. Always rely on official portals for the latest dates, requirements, and steps specific to central or state authorities.

title: NEET PG 2026 Memory Recall MCQs: Analyzing Question Patterns for Post-Exam Rank Estimation
description: Learn how NEET PG 2026 memory recall MCQs help medical aspirants analyze difficulty levels, evaluate high-yield topics, and estimate post-exam rank percentile accurately.
content:
Immediately after the NEET PG exam, candidate discussions shift heavily toward memory recall MCQs. Because the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences conducts the exam as a computer-based test without releasing immediate official question papers, recalled questions compiled by test-takers offer the earliest glimpse into exam difficulty, subject distribution, and candidate performance trends. Understanding how to properly analyze these recalled questions helps candidates and parents form realistic expectations regarding marks, cutoffs, and tentative rank estimations before official results are declared.

Understanding the Role of Memory Recall MCQs in NEET PG 2026

Memory recall MCQs are question statements, options, and clinical scenarios reconstructed by test-takers immediately after stepping out of the examination hall. While they are not official copies, high volumes of matching inputs across various candidate groups allow educators to reconstruct a large percentage of the exam paper with reasonable accuracy.

Analyzing recalled questions serves three primary purposes for candidates:

  • Evaluating individual accuracy across high-yield subjects like Medicine, Surgery, Obstetrics and Gynecology, and Pathology.
  • Identifying clinical case-based questions that carried higher difficulty or ambiguous options.
  • Understanding the overall balance between image-based questions, factual recall, and multi-step reasoning problems.

Key Question Patterns Highlighted in Recalled MCQs

Recent trends in post-graduate medical entrance tests show a distinct shift toward clinical decision-making rather than simple rote memorization. Post-exam recall analyses consistently highlight specific structural patterns across subjects.

1. Integrated Clinical Scenarios

A substantial portion of questions presents patient history, lab values, and physical findings requiring multi-system diagnosis. Candidates must link basic science concepts with clinical treatment guidelines to arrive at the correct choice.

2. Image-Based Diagnostics

Visual questions featuring histology slides, radiological scans, gross pathology specimens, and clinical signs continue to feature prominently. Recalled questions reveal whether image items were straightforward or required complex differential diagnoses.

3. High-Yield Topic Weightage

Memory recall statistics help pinpoint whether high-yield topics such as Pharmacology drug interactions, Preventive and Social Medicine statistics, or Pediatrics developmental milestones aligned with historical paper weights.

How to Calculate Estimated Scores Using Recalled Papers

To calculate a preliminary score from recall keys, candidates should follow a standardized scoring template based on the official marking scheme.

  • Award 4 marks for every recalled question answered with high confidence.
  • Deduct 1 mark for every incorrect attempt to account for negative marking.
  • Unattempted questions receive zero marks.

Because memory recall keys may contain altered options or slight omissions, candidates should categorize their answers into three confidence levels: Certain, Probable, and Uncertain. Calculating a best-case score and a worst-case score gives a realistic range rather than a single fixed number.

Estimating Rank Percentile and Seat Matrix Options

Translating a raw score into an estimated rank requires understanding mark-versus-rank trends from previous examination cycles. Factors that influence the rank distribution include:

  • Overall Paper Difficulty: A tougher paper shifts the score required for a top 5,000 rank downward.
  • Total Candidate Volume: Higher participation increases competition at key score clusters, especially between 500 and 600 marks.
  • Negative Marking Impact: High negative marking counts significantly lower percentile ranks for aggressive guessers.

Parents and students should use rank predictors as broad guidance rather than definitive outcomes. Official percentile normalizations and merit lists published on the authority website remain the final criteria for counseling eligibility and seat allocation.

Best Practices for Post-Exam Analysis for Students and Parents

While post-exam discussions are valuable, maintaining a balanced approach prevents unnecessary stress during the waiting period.

  • Cross-check recall keys with standard reference textbooks rather than relying solely on social media opinions.
  • Avoid over-analyzing disputed or ambiguous questions, as these are often reviewed by subject experts before final answer key freezing.
  • Gather required documentation, internship completion certificates, and category details in preparation for upcoming state and central counseling processes.
  • Verify all official announcements, scorecards, and counseling schedules on the official examination authority portal.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are NEET PG memory recall MCQs?

They are test questions reconstructed from the memory of candidates who took the exam. They help recreate the paper structure shortly after the test concludes.

Are recall answer keys 100 percent accurate?

No, recall keys are unofficial compilations and can contain minor errors in question phrasing or options. Candidates should treat them as broad estimates.

How does negative marking affect post-exam rank estimation?

Incorrect answers deduct 1 mark each. Overestimating accuracy on uncertain questions can artificially inflate predicted scores and distort rank expectations.

When are official NEET PG results and scorecards released?

Official results and individual scorecards are usually declared on the authority website within a few weeks after the completion of the examination.

title: Odisha NEET PG 2026: Choice Locking from 1 to 3 November
description: DMET Odisha has scheduled Round 1 choices for 1-3 November. Review the revised merit list and seat matrix before arranging preferences, and note the central reporting venue.
content:
Odisha NEET PG 2026 Round 1 choice filling and locking is scheduled for 1 to 3 November, with the window closing at 11:55 pm on the final day according to the server time. Candidates should first review the revised provisional merit list and seat matrix scheduled for 30 October at 4 pm.

The official Round 1 schedule is provisional and may change through a further notice. Keep the DMET Odisha PG notifications page beside your application record when preparing for the next step.

A provisional list is already available

The notification page lists a provisional Round 1 merit list dated 28 October. The schedule separately provides for a revised provisional list and seat matrix on 30 October. Read the latest applicable version before making choices; an earlier list does not confirm your final seat.

Check your own details and the programme category relevant to your application. The portal carries separate seat matrices for MD/MS, post-MBBS DNB and post-MBBS NBEMS diploma courses. Do not assume that a seat shown in one matrix is available through every route.

The first allotment and reporting dates

Round 1 choice filling and locking

Allotment-cum-admission letter

Provisional admission reporting

Plan for reporting at MKCG, Berhampur

The schedule directs candidates to report before the Convener at the 650 Lecture Theater, M.K.C.G. Medical College, Berhampur. It asks for the original College Leaving Certificate, other original documents and the online-generated admission-fee receipt through SB Collect.

Read your allotment letter before travelling and use the payment instructions on the official portal. Check the payment category carefully and retain the receipt. This reporting step should not be replaced with an assumption that admission is completed by downloading the letter.

Build a choice list you can act on

Use the PG counselling home page for the bulletin, seat information and choice-filling instructions. Compare eligible courses, college fees and the practical cost of joining before ordering your preferences. Save the final choice record after completing the portal’s locking process.

The same schedule includes a later upgraded-allotment stage against Round 1 vacancies. Follow its instructions if it applies to you rather than treating the first reporting window as the end of every Round 1 step.

Applicants using multiple state processes can also check the separate Uttarakhand Round 1 choice schedule. Its deadlines do not apply to Odisha.

title: JEE Main 2027 Form: Fix Identity Details Before You Decide to Start Again
description: NTA advises candidates to use their own identity login, update DigiLocker KYC and match Class 10 records. If you made a form mistake, know when a fresh paid form counts and when to use correction.
content:
Before you submit JEE Main 2027 Session 1, check the identity details that NTA says must match. If you have already made a mistake, a fresh application is allowed under NTA's later clarification, but a second fee will not be refunded or carried over. For a smaller editable error, the scheduled correction facility may be the better choice.

Match the identity record before filling the form

In its 28 October advisory, the National Testing Agency asks candidates to use their own DigiLocker, JanParichay or e-Pramaan credentials. It also advises DigiLocker Re-KYC before filling the form so the latest details are fetched. Your name and date of birth in the application must match the Class 10 certificate or marksheet. Check those records first, particularly if your identity account has an old spelling or birth date.

Already generated an application number?

NTA's 30 October clarification allows a fresh Session 1 form even after an application number was generated or a fee paid. Its rule for which form counts is precise:

NTA clarification dated 30 October 2026 on fresh forms and fee payment. Read the original notice.

  • New form paid and confirmation page generated: the last such form is valid.

  • New form started but payment or confirmation incomplete: the earlier form remains valid if its fee and confirmation were completed.

  • Only certain details need amending: NTA advises using the correction facility rather than paying for a fresh form.

Every fresh form gets a new application number, and the photograph, signature and documents must be entered again. The fee paid on an earlier form is neither refunded nor adjusted. More than one application number does not allow more than one exam attempt in the same session.

Which date matters for your next step?

The clarification says a fresh form and fee payment must be finished by 22 November 2026, 11:50 pm. NTA lists a late-fee window from 23 to 26 November, ending at 11:50 pm on 26 November, and the correction facility from 27 to 29 November. Check the current JEE Main portal before paying or editing, since the live form and later notices govern your case.

If a photograph or live camera step is your problem, our photo mismatch checklist covers that specific route. If the issue is whether a partly paid form counts, keep your confirmation page and use NTA's 30 October rule above.
author: Geethika Reddy

title: CBSE ക്ലാസ് 10, 12 കന്നഡ പരീക്ഷ 2027: തീയതി, വിഷയ കോഡ്, സമയം
content:
ക്ലാസ് 10 കന്നഡ (കോഡ് 015) പരീക്ഷ 27 ഫെബ്രുവരി 2027ന് 10:30 മുതൽ 13:30 വരെ നടക്കും. ക്ലാസ് 12 കന്നഡ (കോഡ് 115) പരീക്ഷ 3 മാർച്ച് 2027ന് 10:30 മുതൽ 13:30 വരെ നടക്കും.

2026 നവംബർ 6ന് പ്രസിദ്ധീകരിച്ച CBSE പ്രധാന പരീക്ഷാ ടൈംടേബിളിലാണ് ഈ വിവരം. ഇത് പരീക്ഷയുടെ തീയതിയും സമയവും അറിയാനുള്ള രേഖയാണ്; മാർക്ക് ലിസ്റ്റല്ല. ഔദ്യോഗിക CBSE ടൈംടേബിൾ

കന്നഡ പരീക്ഷയ്ക്ക് എത്ര സമയം ലഭിക്കും?

ക്ലാസും വിഷയവുംകോഡ്പരീക്ഷാ തീയതിസമയം (IST)ദൈർഘ്യം
ക്ലാസ് 10: Kannada01527 ഫെബ്രുവരി 202710:30 - 13:303 മണിക്കൂർ
ക്ലാസ് 12: Kannada1153 മാർച്ച് 202710:30 - 13:303 മണിക്കൂർ

സെൻട്രൽ ബോർഡ് ഓഫ് സെക്കൻഡറി എജ്യുക്കേഷൻ, 6 നവംബർ 2026, പേജ് 5: വിഷയ കോഡ്, തീയതി, സമയം. ഔദ്യോഗിക PDFൽ ഈ പേജ് തുറക്കുക

സെൻട്രൽ ബോർഡ് ഓഫ് സെക്കൻഡറി എജ്യുക്കേഷൻ, 6 നവംബർ 2026, പേജ് 9: വിഷയ കോഡ്, തീയതി, സമയം. ഔദ്യോഗിക PDFൽ ഈ പേജ് തുറക്കുക

ഔദ്യോഗിക PDFൽ ശരിയായ വരി കണ്ടെത്താം

പേജ് 5, 9ൽ ക്ലാസ് ഏതാണെന്നു നോക്കിയ ശേഷം 015, 115 എന്ന കോഡ് കണ്ടെത്തുക. ഒരേ തീയതിയും സമയവും പല വരികൾക്കും ബാധകമാകാം. ഫോണിൽ മുഴുവൻ പേജും വലുതാക്കി നോക്കുക.

സ്കൂളിലെ രജിസ്ട്രേഷനിലുള്ള കോഡും വിഷയത്തിന്റെ മുഴുവൻ പേരും ഒത്തുനോക്കുക. മറ്റൊരു ക്ലാസിലും ഇതേ പേരുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ നിങ്ങളുടെ ക്ലാസിന്റെ വരി മാത്രം തിരഞ്ഞെടുക്കുക.

ഇംഗ്ലിഷ് പരീക്ഷയുമായി തീയതികൾ താരതമ്യം ചെയ്യാം

ക്ലാസ് 10 കന്നഡ (015) പരീക്ഷ 27 ഫെബ്രുവരി 2027നും ഇംഗ്ലീഷ് ഭാഷയും സാഹിത്യവും (184) പരീക്ഷ 26 ഫെബ്രുവരി 2027നും ആണ്. തീയതികൾ തമ്മിൽ 1 ദിവസത്തെ വ്യത്യാസമുണ്ട്. ക്ലാസ് 12 കന്നഡ (115) പരീക്ഷ 3 മാർച്ച് 2027നും English Core (301) പരീക്ഷ 5 മാർച്ച് 2027നും ആണ്. തീയതികൾ തമ്മിൽ 2 ദിവസത്തെ വ്യത്യാസമുണ്ട്.

ഈ ദിവസങ്ങളെല്ലാം പഠിക്കാൻ കിട്ടുന്ന അവധിയല്ല. മറ്റു പരീക്ഷകളും കലണ്ടറിൽ ചേർത്ത് ഇടയിൽ പരീക്ഷയില്ലാത്ത ദിവസങ്ങൾ മാത്രം എണ്ണുക. പരിശീലനത്തിന് യഥാർഥ പേപ്പറിന്റെ ദൈർഘ്യം തന്നെ എടുക്കുക.

പരീക്ഷാകേന്ദ്രത്തിലേക്കു പോകും മുൻപ്

പരീക്ഷ തുടങ്ങുന്ന സമയം കേന്ദ്രത്തിൽ എത്തേണ്ട അവസാന സമയമല്ല. റിപ്പോർട്ടിങ്, പ്രവേശനം, രേഖകൾ എന്നിവയ്ക്ക് അഡ്മിറ്റ് കാർഡ് നോക്കുക. തീയതി മാറിയെന്നു കേട്ടാൽ ബോർഡിന്റെ പുതുക്കിയ അറിയിപ്പിൽ ക്ലാസ്, കോഡ്, തീയതി എന്നിവ ഒത്തുനോക്കുക.

ആശയവിനിമയ ഉപകരണങ്ങൾ പരീക്ഷാകേന്ദ്രത്തിനുള്ളിൽ അനുവദിക്കില്ല. കൊണ്ടുപോകാവുന്ന സാധനങ്ങളെക്കുറിച്ച് CBSE നൽകുന്ന പ്രത്യേക നിർദേശങ്ങളും അഡ്മിറ്റ് കാർഡും പിന്തുടരുക.

content:
MET 2027 registration is now available online through Manipal Academy of Higher Education. Students who want to study B.Tech and other programs that are eligible can start their application process by going to the MAHE admissions website. The deadline to submit the MET 2027 application for Phase 1 is March 15, 2027. Everyone applying should check the information on the official website before they apply.

Follow these steps to complete the registration process:

  9. Review the form, submit it, and keep the confirmation page for your records.

Eligibility differs for each program. For B.Tech Eligibility generally asks that candidates meet the Class 12 subjects and marks. Before you submit your application, eligibility requires you to review the MET 2027 eligibility criteria.

title: CBSE Classes 10 and 12 Gujarati Exam 2027: Dates, Codes and Timings
description: CBSE Classes 10 and 12 Gujarati: check the 2027 exam date, exact subject code, paper duration and official PDF entry before making your timetable.
content:
Class 10 Gujarati (010) is on 4 March 2027; Class 12 Gujarati (110) is on 3 March 2027. The table below keeps each registered course and its exam slot separate, so you can select the entry that applies to you.

These entries appear in the CBSE main examination date sheet issued on 6 November 2026. It contains the examination schedule for Classes 10 and 12. It is not a result or marksheet download.

Gujarati dates and paper durations

Class and paperCodeExam dateTime (IST)Duration
Class 10: Gujarati0104 March 202710:30 am to 1:30 pm IST3 hours
Class 12: Gujarati1103 March 202710:30 am to 1:30 pm IST3 hours

Find your Gujarati entry in the PDF

Open PDF pages 6, 9 and look for codes 010, 110. First check the class heading, then read across the subject row to the date and time. Some date labels and time cells cover several rows. On a phone, enlarge the page rather than reading an isolated screenshot without its heading.

The entries above do not all fall on the same date. A subject name alone is therefore not enough to choose a day. Copy the code and course label from your school record and retain only the matching row in your personal timetable.

Place this paper in your revision calendar

Class 10 Gujarati (010) falls 6 calendar days after English Language and Literature (184), which is on 26 February 2027. Class 12 Gujarati (110) falls 2 calendar days before English Core (301), which is on 5 March 2027.

That is a calendar comparison, not a guaranteed preparation break. Count only the clear days between your own registered papers. Put other examinations into the calendar first, then choose realistic revision sessions and a timed practice slot matching the duration of this paper.

Before travelling to the examination centre

The start time is not an arrival deadline. Read the admit-card instructions for reporting, entry and the documents you need. If the school shares a revised CBSE notice, compare its class, code and date before changing your calendar. Do not infer a new date from a social-media headline.

CBSE says important instructions will be issued separately and students must follow the admit card. Communication devices are not allowed inside the examination centre. Check the instructions for permitted materials before packing your bag.

For the wider schedule, use the Class 10 and 12 date-sheet overview and the paper-duration guide.

title: West Bengal NEET UG 2026 Round 1 Seat Allotment: WBMCC Reporting Timelines, Fee Verification, and Seat Surrender Rules
description: Comprehensive guide on West Bengal NEET UG 2026 Round 1 seat allotment by WBMCC, including physical reporting schedules, fee verification, document requirements, and seat surrender policies.
content:
The West Bengal Medical Counselling Committee (WBMCC) publishes the Round 1 seat allotment results for West Bengal NEET UG counselling. For candidates seeking admission into MBBS and BDS courses across state quota and private seats in West Bengal, completing the post-allotment process accurately within the designated timeline is mandatory to secure their admission.

Overview of WB NEET UG Round 1 Seat Allotment

Once the West Bengal NEET UG Round 1 seat allotment is announced, candidates must log in to the official WBMCC portal using their registration credentials to download their allotment letters. The seat allotment list is generated based on NEET UG Merit Ranks, candidate categories, state quota eligibility, and choices filled during the option entry phase.

Candidates who receive a seat allocation have two primary paths: accept the seat and complete physical verification, or opt for willingness choices (such as participating in Round 2 for an upgrade) as permitted under WBMCC guidelines.

WBMCC Physical Reporting Timelines and Document Verification

Allocated candidates must report physically to their designated medical or dental colleges within the specific dates outlined by WBMCC. Failure to report within the prescribed timeline leads to automatic cancellation of the allotted seat.

Key Documents Required During Reporting

  • Printed WBMCC Round 1 Seat Allotment Letter
  • NEET UG 2026 Scorecard and Admit Card
  • Class 10 Pass Certificate / Birth Certificate (Proof of Age)
  • Class 12 Marksheet and Passing Certificate
  • West Bengal Domicile Certificate (Proforma A1, A2, or B as applicable)
  • Category Certificate (SC/ST/OBC-A/OBC-B/EWS/PWD) issued by competent state authority
  • Medical Fitness Certificate in the prescribed format
  • Identity Proof (Aadhaar Card, Passport, or Voter ID)
  • Passport-size photographs matching those used in the NEET application
  • Payment transaction receipts for admission and token fees

Fee Payment and Verification Procedure

The fee structure varies between government medical institutions, state quota seats in private colleges, and management quota seats. During the physical reporting phase, candidates must undergo thorough fee verification.

Fee Verification Steps

  • Online Token Fee: Candidates must pay the prescribed seat acceptance or token fee online through the WBMCC portal to generate the allotment slip.
  • College Admission Fees: Remaining tuition fees, admission charges, and security deposits must be paid directly at the allotted institution via demand draft, online transfer, or specified bank pay orders.
  • Verification Confirmation: College authorities verify payment receipts alongside physical original documents before issuing the final admission letter.

Seat Surrender and Resignation Rules

WBMCC maintains strict rules regarding seat surrender and exit options to ensure fair distribution of medical seats across subsequent counselling rounds.

Key Surrender Policies

  • Free Exit in Round 1: Candidates allotted a seat in Round 1 who choose not to join or who wish to surrender their seat within the stipulated Round 1 reporting window can do so without forfeiting their security deposit, subject to WBMCC guidelines.
  • Formal Surrender Process: If a candidate joins the institution but later decides to resign within the permitted timeframe, they must submit a formal resignation request to the college principal and obtain an official acknowledgment.
  • Impact on Round 2 Participation: Candidates who surrender their seats within the allowed deadline remain eligible to participate in Round 2 fresh option filling, whereas non-reporting without fulfilling exit norms may carry specific restrictions.

Important Guidelines for Candidates and Parents

Candidates and parents should carefully review all details printed on the allotment letter. It is recommended to keep multiple attested photocopies of original documents and payment receipts before submitting originals to the allotted college. Always check the official WBMCC website for sudden administrative notices or timeline modifications.

Frequently Asked Questions

What happens if I fail to report to the allotted college during Round 1 reporting dates?

If you fail to report physically to the designated institute within the official WBMCC timeline, your Round 1 seat allocation is automatically cancelled.

Can I upgrade my seat in Round 2 after accepting the Round 1 allotment?

Yes, candidates who report to their allotted college, complete document verification, and express willingness for upgrade can participate in Round 2.

Is the security deposit refunded if I surrender my Round 1 seat?

Under WBMCC rules for Round 1, candidates who surrender their seat within the permitted free exit deadline retain their security deposit and eligibility for subsequent rounds.

Where can I verify official updates regarding WB NEET UG counselling schedule changes?

All official notices, schedules, seat matrices, and results must be verified directly on the official WBMCC portal.

title: Navigating the New Age Job Market: Career Tips for Students after 12th Commerce
description: Discover how to navigate the new age job market with essential career tips for students after 12th Commerce. Explore skills, opportunities, and smart pathways to build a successful future.
content:
The world of work is no longer limited by rigid career paths or traditional professions. Technology, automation, and globalization have reshaped industries and created new opportunities that didn’t exist even a decade ago. For students completing 12th Commerce, this new-age job market may seem both exciting and overwhelming. The good news is that with the right approach, you can turn this dynamic environment into a space full of growth and possibilities.

Here are some essential tips to help commerce students confidently navigate today’s evolving career landscape.

1. Stay Future-Oriented and Market Aware

Jobs of the future will revolve around technology, sustainability, and innovation. For instance, fields like financial technology (FinTech), blockchain, e-commerce, and artificial intelligence in business are growing rapidly. Students should research industry trends, follow news about emerging sectors, and choose career options that are future-proof.

  • Developing transferable skills such as communication, problem-solving, and adaptability.

  • Embracing technology since AI, automation, and digital platforms are reshaping industries.

  • Lifelong learning through certifications, online courses, and professional training


👉 Example: Instead of only focusing on traditional B.Com, consider integrating it with certifications in data analytics or financial modeling.

2. Prioritize Skill Development Over Just Degrees

A degree provides the foundation, but skills provide the ladder to climb higher. Employers now expect candidates to bring practical knowledge to the table. Along with your commerce studies, focus on developing:

  • Digital skills: Excel, Tally, QuickBooks, and financial software.
  • Analytical skills: Data interpretation, statistics, and problem-solving.
  • Creative skills: Social media marketing, content writing, and brand communication.
  • Tech adaptability: Comfort with AI tools, online collaboration, and remote work platforms.
    👉 Tip: Platforms like Coursera, Udemy, or LinkedIn Learning offer affordable certifications that can boost your employability.

3. Explore Beyond Traditional Careers

Commerce no longer means only CA, CS, or MBA. The job market welcomes those with passion and specialized skills. Options include:

  • Entrepreneurship and start-ups: Launching your own business idea.
  • Digital marketing & content creation: Growing in the influencer economy.
  • E-commerce and supply chain management: Joining booming platforms like Flipkart, Amazon, or Zomato.
  • Finance and investment: Careers in stockbroking, wealth management, and equity research.
  • Creative fields: Event management, fashion business, or advertising.
    👉 Real-life example: Ritesh Agarwal, founder of OYO Rooms, started his entrepreneurial journey at 19 without a conventional degree path.

4. Gain Practical Experience Early

Internships, part-time jobs, and volunteering help bridge the gap between classroom learning and industry needs. They also build confidence and improve networking skills. Many companies today hire interns directly from school or first-year college.

  • Internships – Short-term roles provide exposure to professional settings and hands-on learning.

  • Part-Time Jobs – Even small roles can build responsibility, time management, and customer interaction skills.

  • Volunteering – Contributing to NGOs, events, or community services adds experience while making a social impact.

  • Live Projects & Case Studies – Working on real industry problems sharpens analytical and decision-making abilities.


👉 Tip: Use platforms like Internshala or LinkedIn to find internship opportunities, even if they are unpaid in the beginning. The experience will be invaluable.

5. Embrace Continuous and Lifelong Learning

The half-life of skills is shrinking—meaning what you learn today may become outdated in a few years. Continuous learning ensures you remain relevant. Attend workshops, pursue online courses, and keep updating your knowledge base.

  • Keeps You Relevant: Industries evolve quickly, and skills that are in demand today may become outdated tomorrow. Lifelong learning ensures you stay updated.

  • Boosts Employability: Employers value candidates who show curiosity, adaptability, and a willingness to upgrade their skills.

  • Enhances Personal Growth: Beyond career benefits, lifelong learning expands knowledge, improves confidence, and nurtures creativity.

  • Prepares for Future Careers: With emerging fields like artificial intelligence, data science, and green technology, learning continuously prepares you for opportunities that don’t even exist yet.


👉 Example: A commerce student interested in marketing can continuously upskill by learning SEO, digital advertising, and influencer management.

6. Focus on Soft Skills and Personality Development

Employers today want candidates who can adapt, collaborate, and lead. Developing strong communication, teamwork, critical thinking, leadership, and emotional intelligence is just as important as technical skills.

  • Communication Skills – Expressing ideas clearly and confidently.

  • Teamwork & Collaboration – Working harmoniously with colleagues and peers.

  • Leadership – Inspiring, guiding, and managing groups effectively.

  • Adaptability – Handling change and uncertainty with ease.

  • Emotional Intelligence (EQ) – Understanding and managing emotions in oneself and others.


👉 Tip: Participate in group discussions, debates, or cultural clubs in college to build confidence and improve public speaking.

7. Build Your Digital Presence and Personal Brand

Recruiters often search for candidates online before interviews. A strong LinkedIn profile or digital portfolio can give you an edge. Share your projects, certifications, and even your entrepreneurial ideas online. This creates credibility and shows you are career-focused.

  • Visibility: Being active online increases your chances of being noticed by recruiters, mentors, and industry experts.

  • Credibility: A professional and consistent online image builds trust and authenticity.

  • Opportunities: A strong digital presence can attract internships, projects, collaborations, and job offers.

  • Networking: Social media and professional platforms help connect with like-minded professionals and industry leaders.


👉 Example: If you are learning stock market basics, post insights or market updates on LinkedIn—it can attract mentors and recruiters.

8. Develop an Entrepreneurial Mindset

Even if you don’t want to start a business immediately, thinking like an entrepreneur helps. It means being innovative, resourceful, and resilient. Students can begin with small side hustles such as freelance writing, graphic design, or online reselling to learn real-world business dynamics.

  • Innovation – Seeking creative solutions to problems.

  • Proactivity – Taking initiative rather than waiting for instructions.

  • Resilience – Learning from failures and persisting despite setbacks.

  • Opportunity Recognition – Identifying gaps in the market or ways to improve processes.

  • Risk Management – Making calculated decisions rather than avoiding risks entirely.

Conclusion

The new-age job market is fast-changing, but it is also full of opportunities for those who are adaptable and forward-looking. For commerce students after 12th, success lies in going beyond conventional choices, focusing on practical skills, and embracing continuous learning. Whether you dream of becoming a financial expert, a digital marketer, or an entrepreneur, the key is to stay curious, open to new ideas, and unafraid of challenges.

The future belongs to those who are ready to innovate, adapt, and grow with the times.

title: INI CET ಜನವರಿ 2027 ಫಲಿತಾಂಶ: ನವೆಂಬರ್ 7 ನಿರೀಕ್ಷೆ, ಸೀಟು ಹಂಚಿಕೆ ಬೇರೆ
description: INI CET ಜನವರಿ 2027 ಫಲಿತಾಂಶಕ್ಕೆ ನವೆಂಬರ್ 7 ನಿರೀಕ್ಷಿತ ದಿನಾಂಕ ಎಂದು AIIMS ಹೇಳಿದೆ. ಅರ್ಹತಾ ಪರ್ಸೆಂಟೈಲ್ ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕ ಸೀಟು ಹಂಚಿಕೆ ಮಾಹಿತಿ ತಿಳಿಯಿರಿ.
content:
INI CET ಜನವರಿ 2027ಗೆ 7 ನವೆಂಬರ್ 2026 ಫಲಿತಾಂಶದ ನಿರೀಕ್ಷಿತ ದಿನಾಂಕ ಎಂದು AIIMS ತಿಳಿಸಿದೆ. ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಯನ್ನು ನವೆಂಬರ್ 1ಕ್ಕೆ ಪ್ರಾಸ್ಪೆಕ್ಟಸ್ ನಿಗದಿಪಡಿಸಿದೆ. ಫಲಿತಾಂಶಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ಕಾಯುತ್ತಿರುವವರು ನವೆಂಬರ್ 7ನ್ನು ಯೋಜನೆಗೆ ನೆರವಾಗುವ ದಿನಾಂಕವಾಗಿ ಪರಿಗಣಿಸಬೇಕು; ಫಲಿತಾಂಶ ಪ್ರಕಟವಾಗಿದೆ ಎಂಬ ದೃಢೀಕರಣವಾಗಿ ಅಲ್ಲ. ಓಪನ್ ರೌಂಡ್ ಸೇರಿದಂತೆ ಆನ್‌ಲೈನ್ ಸೀಟು ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯ ವೇಳಾಪಟ್ಟಿಯನ್ನು ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕವಾಗಿ ಪ್ರಕಟಿಸಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

ದಿನಾಂಕದ ಜೊತೆಗೆ “ನಿರೀಕ್ಷಿತ” ಎಂಬುದನ್ನೂ ಗಮನಿಸಿ

ಜನವರಿ 2027 ಭಾಗ A ಪ್ರಾಸ್ಪೆಕ್ಟಸ್ ಪ್ರಮುಖ ದಿನಾಂಕಗಳ ವಿಭಾಗದಲ್ಲಿ “expected” ಎಂಬ ಪದ ಬಳಸಿದೆ. ಪ್ರಯಾಣ ಅಥವಾ ಇತರ ಜವಾಬ್ದಾರಿಗಳ ಯೋಜನೆ ಮಾಡುವಾಗ ಈ ಷರತ್ತು ನೆನಪಿರಲಿ. AIIMS ಪರೀಕ್ಷಾ ವೆಬ್‌ಸೈಟ್‌ನ ಫಲಿತಾಂಶ ಸೂಚನೆ ಅಥವಾ ಪರಿಷ್ಕೃತ ಅಧಿಕೃತ ವೇಳಾಪಟ್ಟಿ ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಮುಂದಿನ ಕ್ರಮ ಕೈಗೊಳ್ಳಿ.

AIIMS ನವದೆಹಲಿ, INI CET ಜನವರಿ 2027 ಭಾಗ A ಪ್ರಾಸ್ಪೆಕ್ಟಸ್, 16 ಸೆಪ್ಟೆಂಬರ್ 2026ರಂದು ಅಪ್‌ಲೋಡ್ ಮಾಡಲು ನಿಗದಿಪಡಿಸಿದ ದಾಖಲೆ, ಪುಟ 31. ದಿನಾಂಕದ ಜೊತೆಗೆ “ನಿರೀಕ್ಷಿತ” ಎಂಬುದನ್ನೂ ಗಮನಿಸಿ

ಅರ್ಹತಾ ಪರ್ಸೆಂಟೈಲ್ ಎಂದರೆ ಸೀಟು ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲ

ಪ್ರತಿ ಗುಂಪಿಗೂ ಕನಿಷ್ಠ ಅರ್ಹತಾ ಪರ್ಸೆಂಟೈಲ್ ಅನ್ನು ಪ್ರಾಸ್ಪೆಕ್ಟಸ್ ನಿಗದಿಪಡಿಸಿದೆ. ಪರ್ಸೆಂಟೈಲ್ ಎಂದರೆ ಅಂಕಗಳ ಶೇಕಡಾವಾರು ಅಲ್ಲ. ಈ ಮಿತಿ ದಾಟುವುದರಿಂದ ಕಾಲೇಜು ಅಥವಾ ವಿಶೇಷ ವಿಭಾಗದ ಸೀಟು ನಿಮಗೆ ಕಾಯ್ದಿರಿಸಿದಂತಾಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

ಸೀಟು ವರ್ಗ ಅಥವಾ ಅರ್ಜಿದಾರರ ಗುಂಪು

ಕನಿಷ್ಠ ಪರ್ಸೆಂಟೈಲ್

ಮೀಸಲಾತಿ ರಹಿತ, OCI ಸೇರಿದಂತೆ; EWS; ಪ್ರಾಯೋಜಿತ; ವಿದೇಶಿ ಪ್ರಜೆಗಳು

50ನೇ ಪರ್ಸೆಂಟೈಲ್

OBC, SC, ST ಮತ್ತು PwBD

45ನೇ ಪರ್ಸೆಂಟೈಲ್

ಭೂತಾನ್ ಪ್ರಜೆಗಳು, PGIMER ಚಂಡೀಗಢಕ್ಕೆ ಮಾತ್ರ

45ನೇ ಪರ್ಸೆಂಟೈಲ್

ಮೆರಿಟ್, ಸಲ್ಲಿಸಿದ ಆದ್ಯತೆಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಭಾಗವಹಿಸುವ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಗಳ ಮೀಸಲಾತಿ ನಿಯಮಗಳ ಮೇಲೆ ಹಂಚಿಕೆ ಅವಲಂಬಿತವಾಗಿದೆ. ಕೋರ್ಸ್ ಅನ್ನು ಲಭ್ಯ ಆಯ್ಕೆ ಎಂದು ಪರಿಗಣಿಸುವ ಮೊದಲು ಸಂಬಂಧಿತ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಯ ಭಾಗ B ಪ್ರಾಸ್ಪೆಕ್ಟಸ್‌ನ ಅರ್ಹತೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಷರತ್ತುಗಳನ್ನು ಓದಿ.

ಕಾಯುವಾಗ ಸಿದ್ಧವಾಗಿಟ್ಟುಕೊಳ್ಳಬೇಕಾದವು

  • ನೋಂದಣಿ ID ಹಾಗೂ ಅರ್ಜಿ ದಾಖಲೆಗಳನ್ನು ಕೈಗೆಟುಕುವಂತೆ ಇಡಿ. ಅಭ್ಯರ್ಥಿ ಸಂಬಂಧಿತ ಮಾಹಿತಿಗೆ AIIMS ಪರೀಕ್ಷಾ ವೆಬ್‌ಸೈಟ್ ಬಳಸಿ.

  • ತೆರೆಯುವ ಸೂಚನೆ INI CET ಮತ್ತು ಜನವರಿ 2027 ಅವಧಿಗೆ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸಿದೆಯೇ ನೋಡಿ. INI-SS ಮತ್ತು ಹಿಂದಿನ ಅವಧಿಯ ಸೂಚನೆಗಳು ಬೇರೆ ಪ್ರಕ್ರಿಯೆಗಳಾಗಿವೆ.

  • ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ವಿಶೇಷ ವಿಭಾಗಗಳ ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ ಪಟ್ಟಿ ಮಾಡಿ, ಭಾಗ Bಯಲ್ಲಿ ಅರ್ಹತೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಷರತ್ತು ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ. ಸಿದ್ಧತಾ ಪಟ್ಟಿ ಸಲ್ಲಿಸಿದ ಆಯ್ಕೆಪಟ್ಟಿಯಲ್ಲ.

  • ಆಯ್ಕೆ ನಮೂದಿಸುವ ಅಥವಾ ವರದಿ ಮಾಡುವ ದಿನಾಂಕಗಳ ಕುರಿತು ಕ್ರಮ ಕೈಗೊಳ್ಳುವ ಮುನ್ನ ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕ ಸೀಟು ಹಂಚಿಕೆ ಸೂಚನೆಗಳಿಗೆ ಕಾಯಿರಿ.

ಪ್ರವೇಶಪತ್ರವನ್ನು ಅರ್ಜಿ ದಾಖಲೆಗಳೊಂದಿಗೆ ಇಡಿ. ಜನವರಿ 2027 ಪ್ರವೇಶಪತ್ರ ಮಾರ್ಗದರ್ಶಿ ಅಧಿಕೃತ ಡೌನ್‌ಲೋಡ್ ಮಾರ್ಗ ತಿಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ನೆನಪಿರುವ ಸರಿಯಾದ ಉತ್ತರಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯನ್ನು ಖಚಿತ ರ‍್ಯಾಂಕ್ ಅಥವಾ ಪ್ರವೇಶ ಕಟ್‌ಆಫ್ ಎಂದು ಭಾವಿಸಬೇಡಿ.
author: Geethika Reddy

content:
CBSE Class 12 Accountancy Sample Paper 2026 – Important Questions & Exam Guide

Introduction

Accountancy is a core subject for CBSE Class 12 Commerce students and one of the most scoring subjects if concepts and questions are practiced regularly. Sample papers help students understand the exam pattern, improve calculation speed, and reduce mistakes.

This article covers CBSE Class 12 Accountancy sample paper pattern, important questions, high-weightage units, and revision tips for the 2026 board exams.

High-Weightage & Easy-to-Score Units (Fast Recap)

Category Units (Class 12 Accountancy)
High Weightage Units Partnership Accounts, Company Accounts, Financial Statements Analysis
Very Easy to Score Cash Flow Statement, Ratio Analysis
Moderate Difficulty Admission, Retirement, and Dissolution of Partner
 

Partnership and Company Accounts carry the highest marks, so they must be prepared first.

CBSE Class 12 Accountancy Sample Paper Pattern 2026

Section Question Type Marks
Section A MCQs 20 Marks
Section B Short Answer 20 Marks
Section C Long Answer (Numericals) 30 Marks
Section D Case-Based Questions 10 Marks
Total   80 Marks
 

Important Accountancy Sample Paper Questions (2026)

Section A – MCQs (Very Important)

  • Define partnership deed.

  • What is goodwill?

  • Meaning of debenture.

  • What is a cash flow statement?

Section B – Short Answer Questions

  • Explain types of reserves.

  • What is revaluation account?

  • Define share capital and share premium.

  • Explain financial ratios.

Section C – Long Answer / Numerical Questions (High Weightage)

Topic Expected Question
Partnership Admission and retirement of partner problems
Dissolution Realisation account and cash account
Company Accounts Issue of shares and debentures
Cash Flow Statement Preparation of cash flow statement
Financial Analysis Ratio calculation and interpretation
 

Section D – Case Study Questions

  • Company financial performance analysis

  • Partnership business scenario-based numericals

  • Cash flow management in business

One-Day Accountancy Sample Paper Revision Plan

Time Topic
Morning Partnership numericals
Afternoon Company accounts
Evening Cash flow & ratios
Night MCQs and theory revision
 

How to Score High Marks in CBSE Accountancy

  • Practice numerical questions daily

  • Learn formats of accounts and statements

  • Show proper working notes

  • Revise theory terms and definitions

  • Solve previous year sample papers

Common Mistakes Students Make

  • Skipping partnership numericals

  • Forgetting formats in exam

  • Calculation errors

  • Not writing working notes

Avoid these mistakes to improve your score easily.

Conclusion

CBSE Class 12 Accountancy sample papers are essential for scoring high marks in board exams. Focus on partnership and company accounts, practice numericals, and revise formats to pass easily in 2026.

title: ICSE, ISC 2027 Timetable Awaited: Plan Revision with Official Papers
description: The ICSE and ISC 2027 subject-wise timetable is awaited. Use CISCE’s specimen-paper resources to prepare while keeping unconfirmed dates out of your calendar.
content:
The ICSE and ISC 2027 subject-wise timetable is still awaited on CISCE's official notification pages. Until the council publishes it, keep individual paper dates and start times unconfirmed in your planner.

You can still make useful progress. CISCE has announced specimen papers for selected 2027 subjects and papers from the 2026 main and improvement examinations. Use the resources for your class and subjects to identify what needs more practice.

A practical plan while the paper order is pending

Start with a short diagnostic session: attempt a section without looking at the answers, then mark the places where you lost time or could not explain a step. Separate gaps in understanding from avoidable errors such as units, spelling, diagrams or incomplete working.

Give the next revision session a specific aim. For example, revise one weak concept, answer a small set of related questions and then retry the problem you missed. Record the result so you can see whether the revision helped.

Keep the resource year visible

A 2026 examination paper is useful practice, but it is not a 2027 timetable or a guarantee of the next paper's questions. Check the class, subject and examination year on each file. For a change in format or prescribed content, ask your teacher to help you apply the relevant current CISCE circular.

When a timetable link appears

Open the document from the CISCE notifications page. Match ICSE with your Class 10 programme or ISC with Class 12, then check the year and the subject names or codes before entering dates.

Keep the full PDF, including instructions. Read the timing for each paper rather than assuming every examination starts at the same hour. If a revised timetable is issued, replace the saved version and check all your subjects again.

A school test schedule or a forwarded image can look convincing without being the council's board timetable. Use the official document and your school's guidance to resolve any mismatch.

For planning after school, explore the DekhoCampus course directory without letting timetable speculation interrupt your revision.

title: GATE 2027 Previous Papers: Build a Practice Log Without Guessing Topic Weightage
description: Use IIT Madras’s year-wise paper and answer-key archive to review mistakes, check current syllabus coverage and practise with the correct marking rules.
content:
Start your GATE 2027 previous-paper practice with the official paper and answer-key archive. IIT Madras provides year-wise downloads for 2021-2026. Choose the correct paper code and session before checking an answer; some subjects have more than one paper in a year.

Make an error log from one complete attempt

Attempt a paper before opening its key. For every missed question, record the topic, marks, question type and reason for the error. Separate a missing concept from a calculation mistake, misread instruction or time shortage.

This is a practical way to decide what to revise next. It is more useful than treating a list of repeated topics as a guarantee of future marks.

Apply the actual scoring rules

Under the 2027 paper pattern, an incorrect one-mark MCQ loses one-third mark; an incorrect two-mark MCQ loses two-thirds. MSQ and NAT answers have no negative marking, and MSQs have no partial credit.

IIT Madras, GATE 2027 official question-paper pattern; marks distribution varies by paper. Read the marking rules.

Use these rules when reviewing an attempt. A score calculated without MCQ deductions can hide an avoidable guessing problem.

Match old questions to your current syllabus

Keep the 2027 syllabus for your paper beside your practice log. Map questions to its headings instead of assuming every old question or topic list remains applicable.

The official pattern also distinguishes marks distribution across papers. Do not apply a blanket 13-mark Engineering Mathematics allocation to every subject.

Use the next paper to test the repair

Revise the concepts behind your mistakes, solve a few related problems and then attempt a different paper. Compare the kinds of errors that remain, not only the total score. If a topic appeared often in your sample, note the years and marks you actually counted; describe that as a past trend, never a forecast or a guaranteed score.

title: Resume & Cover Letter Writing Tips | How to Craft the Perfect Job Application
description: Learn expert tips for writing resumes and cover letters that stand out. Improve your job application with practical advice, formatting tips, and key strategies to impress employers
content:
In today’s competitive job market, a well-crafted resume and cover letter can make all the difference. Employers often spend only a few seconds scanning each application, so making a strong first impression is essential. This guide will provide practical tips to help you create standout documents that highlight your skills, experience, and potential.

1. Resume Writing Tips

a. Keep It Concise

Your resume should ideally be one page for entry-level positions and up to two pages for experienced professionals. Focus on relevant experience, achievements, and skills that align with the job you are applying for. Avoid unnecessary details that do not add value.

b. Use a Clear Format

A clean, easy-to-read format is crucial. Use clear headings, bullet points, and consistent font styles. Recruiters should be able to scan your resume quickly and identify key information.

c. Highlight Achievements, Not Just Duties

Rather than just listing responsibilities, focus on your accomplishments. Quantify achievements where possible. For example:
“Increased social media engagement by 35% in six months.”

d. Tailor Your Resume for Each Job

Customize your resume for each position. Highlight skills and experiences that match the job description. This increases the chances of passing through Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) and catching the recruiter’s attention.

e. Include Keywords

Many companies use ATS software to filter resumes. Incorporate relevant keywords from the job description to ensure your resume gets noticed.

2. Cover Letter Writing Tips

a. Personalize Your Greeting

Whenever possible, address the cover letter to a specific person rather than using generic greetings like “To Whom It May Concern.” This shows that you’ve done your research and are genuinely interested in the position.

b. Start Strong

The opening paragraph should grab attention. Mention the role you are applying for and briefly highlight why you are a strong fit.

c. Show Your Value

Explain how your skills and experience can benefit the company. Provide specific examples that demonstrate your achievements and problem-solving abilities.

d. Keep It Concise

A cover letter should be no longer than one page. Keep paragraphs short, focused, and easy to read.

e. End with a Call to Action

Conclude your cover letter by expressing interest in an interview and thanking the reader for their time. This leaves a positive, proactive impression.

3. Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Spelling or grammatical errors

  • Using a generic cover letter for all applications

  • Including irrelevant work experience

  • Overloading the resume with too much information

  • Using unprofessional email addresses

4. Final Thoughts

Your resume and cover letter are your first opportunity to impress potential employers. Investing time and effort into crafting tailored, polished documents can significantly improve your chances of landing an interview. Remember to keep them concise, highlight achievements, and ensure they reflect your unique value.

title: BITSAT 2027 Second Attempt: When Retaking the Exam Makes Sense
description: Planning a second BITSAT 2027 attempt? Use mock scores, branch preference and available study time to decide whether retaking is worth the cost.
content:
A second BITSAT 2027 attempt can help if your first score is close to the branch and campus you want. It can also eat into board preparation, JEE work and other 2027 Exams if you retake without a clear score target. Before paying, compare your latest full-length mocks with the score you need and the preparation time you genuinely have.

The BITS Pilani admission authority has not established the 2027 attempt schedule, fee or eligibility details in the supplied official material. The official BITS admission brochure page should be checked when the 2027 notice is released.

When does a second BITSAT attempt make sense?

Retaking is sensible when your first performance was dragged down by a fixable problem, not by a large syllabus gap. A second attempt deserves serious thought if your recent mocks show steady improvement and your preferred BITS programme is within reach.

  • Your mock score is close: If your last three full-length scores sit near the range you need for your preferred branch, targeted revision may produce a useful gain.
  • You can name the weak areas: For example, slow Physics calculations, missed Chemistry facts or poor time control in English and Logical Reasoning.
  • You have protected study time: The retake should fit around board exams and other entrance tests, not replace them.

One bad mock is not evidence. Look for a pattern across at least three timed papers, then review every wrong answer and every question left unfinished.

When should you skip the retake?

Skip it when your score is far below your target and the second attempt would need a complete syllabus rebuild. It is also a poor choice if you are already behind in board chapters or preparing for JEE Main, because splitting attention can damage both applications.

Parents should ask a practical question: what will the student do differently after paying? If the answer is only “study harder”, the fee is probably buying anxiety, not a better result.

A simple BITSAT 2027 decision test

  1. Write your preferred campus and branch, then identify a realistic score range from recent counselling information when available.
  2. Take one computer-based mock in exam conditions.
  3. Sort errors into knowledge gaps, calculation mistakes, guessing and time loss.
  4. Reserve a short revision block for those exact areas and take two more mocks.
  5. Retake only if the score trend improves and the second attempt does not damage boards or another entrance exam.

Use the BITSAT exam guide to organise the paper pattern and preparation plan. Keep your application decision separate from counselling hopes: a higher score may improve choices, but it cannot guarantee a particular branch or campus.

title: SSC CGL 2026 Final Selection: What Tier-Wise Changes Mean for Merit
description: Understand SSC CGL 2026 merit, qualifying papers, preferences, vacancies, post conditions and document checks before allocation.
content:
SSC CGL 2026 final selection won’t depend on clearing one paper alone. Your result must lead to a merit position, a valid preference submission, vacancy-based allocation, successful checks and appointment by the concerned department. The 2026 notification will decide the exact marks formula, so separate confirmed SSC practice from details that are still pending.

For the wider exam route, see our SSC CGL exam guide. This page focuses on the decisions that can change your final post.

Which SSC CGL stages count for merit?

In the established SSC CGL framework, some papers or sections are used to screen candidates, while others contribute to the merit list. A qualifying paper can decide whether you continue without adding its marks to your final ranking. A merit-counting paper can change your position among candidates competing for vacancies.

Recent SSC CGL patterns have also used post-specific papers or tests for certain roles, while some sections remain qualifying. That is the concrete point many candidates miss: “qualified” and “high enough for allocation” are not the same result. The SSC CGL 2026 notice must confirm the papers whose marks count, any qualifying paper excluded from merit, normalisation rules and post-wise requirements.

What happens after the result?

Final selection is a chain of separate decisions, not one announcement.

  1. Result and merit position: SSC publishes the relevant result or merit outcome under the notified formula.
  2. Preference submission: you rank posts and departments through the process and deadline stated in the notice.
  3. Allocation: the notified merit-cum-preference method is applied against vacancies, category rules, eligibility and available choices.
  4. Post checks: some roles may require a computer proficiency or data-entry test, while posts with notified physical standards may require those standards. Not every SSC CGL post has an extra test.
  5. Verification and appointment: SSC conducts the examination, but document checks and appointment formalities may be handled by the concerned user department or office.

A lower preference may be considered when a higher choice cannot be allocated, but this isn’t an automatic rule for every candidate. The outcome depends on the notified method, vacancies, category position, eligibility and the options you submitted.

What should finalists check now?

Match your application with original records: name, date of birth, qualification, category and disability details. Check certificate format, issuing authority and validity requirements. Keep your preference record and watch SSC notices for the 2026 formula and department instructions. A strong score cannot repair an unsupported claim or an unmet post condition.

content:
NPAT 2027നായി തയ്യാറെടുക്കുകയാണെങ്കിൽ ആദ്യം നിങ്ങൾക്ക് അനുയോജ്യമായ കോഴ്സും NMIMS ക്യാമ്പസും തിരഞ്ഞെടുക്കുക. ഔദ്യോഗിക പേജിന്റെ തലക്കെട്ടിൽ 2027 ഉണ്ട്. എന്നാൽ അവിടെയുള്ള പ്രവേശന കൈപ്പുസ്തകത്തിന്റെ ലിങ്ക് 2026-27 അധ്യയന വർഷത്തിലെ രേഖയിലേക്കാണ് പോകുന്നത്. അതിലെ വിവരങ്ങൾ 2027ലെ അപേക്ഷാ കാലയളവോ ഫീസോ പരീക്ഷാ തീയതികളോ സ്ഥിരീകരിക്കുന്നതായി കരുതരുത്.

ഏതു കോഴ്സുകൾ താരതമ്യം ചെയ്യാം?

ഔദ്യോഗിക പട്ടികയിൽ BBA, B.Com., B.Sc. Finance, BBA FinTech, സംയോജിത BBA-MBA, B.Sc. Economics, BA Liberal Arts എന്നിവയുണ്ട്. Branding and Advertising, International Business, Management and Marketing, Finance തുടങ്ങിയ പ്രത്യേക മേഖലകളിലുള്ള BBA കോഴ്സുകളും കാണാം. പേര് മാത്രം കണ്ട് തിരഞ്ഞെടുക്കാതെ പഠനവിഷയങ്ങൾ വായിച്ചുനോക്കുന്നതാണ് നല്ല തുടക്കം.

മുംബൈ, ബെംഗളൂരു, നവി മുംബൈ, ഹൈദരാബാദ്, ഇൻഡോർ, ചണ്ഡീഗഢ്, അഹമ്മദാബാദ് ക്യാമ്പസുകളെ പേജ് പരാമർശിക്കുന്നു. എല്ലാ കോഴ്സുകളും എല്ലാ ക്യാമ്പസുകളിലും ഉണ്ടെന്ന് ഇതിന് അർഥമില്ല. നിങ്ങൾക്ക് വേണ്ട കോഴ്സ് ഏതു ക്യാമ്പസിലാണുള്ളതെന്ന് അതിന്റെ ഔദ്യോഗിക വിവരങ്ങളിൽ ഉറപ്പാക്കുക.

ഔദ്യോഗിക NPAT കോഴ്സുകളുടെ പേജ്

കൈപ്പുസ്തകത്തിലെ വർഷം ശ്രദ്ധിക്കുക

Admissions Handout, Important Dates ലിങ്കുകൾ 2026-27 രേഖയിലേക്കാണ് പോകുന്നത്. വെബ് പേജിലെ 2027 തലക്കെട്ടും PDFലെ അധ്യയന വർഷവും വേർതിരിച്ചു വായിക്കണം. പഴയ ഫീസോ അവസാന തീയതിയോ പുതിയ പ്രവേശനത്തിന് ബാധകമാക്കരുത്. 2027 പ്രവേശന ചക്രം വ്യക്തമായി സൂചിപ്പിക്കുന്ന കൈപ്പുസ്തകവും സമയക്രമവും വരുന്നതുവരെ ആ വിവരങ്ങൾക്ക് സ്ഥിരീകരണമില്ല.

SVKM’s NMIMS 2026-27 പ്രവേശന കൈപ്പുസ്തകത്തിന്റെ ഒന്നാം പേജിലെ തലക്കെട്ട്. ഈ ഭാഗത്ത് പ്രത്യേക പ്രസിദ്ധീകരണ തീയതിയില്ല. ഇത് 2027ലെ സമയക്രമമല്ല. അസൽ 2026-27 പ്രവേശന കൈപ്പുസ്തകം

മുൻഗണനാ പട്ടിക ഇപ്പോൾ തയ്യാറാക്കാം

പരമാവധി അഞ്ച് പ്രോഗ്രാമുകൾ തിരഞ്ഞെടുക്കാമെന്ന് ഔദ്യോഗിക FAQ പറയുന്നു. ആ പരിധിയിൽ നിങ്ങളുടെ മുൻഗണനകൾ ക്രമപ്പെടുത്തുക; 2027 അപേക്ഷയിലെ നിബന്ധനകൾ വീണ്ടും ഉറപ്പാക്കണം. ഓരോ തിരഞ്ഞെടുപ്പിനും കോഴ്സ്, ക്യാമ്പസ്, യോഗ്യത, പ്ലസ് ടു വിഷയങ്ങൾ, ഗണിതമോ സ്റ്റാറ്റിസ്റ്റിക്സോ നിർബന്ധമാണോ, പാഠ്യപദ്ധതി, സ്ഥലം, ചെലവ് എന്നിവ കുറിച്ചുവയ്ക്കുക.

Finance കോഴ്സിലാണ് താൽപര്യമെങ്കിൽ അതിലെ കണക്കുകളും അളവാധിഷ്ഠിത വിഷയങ്ങളും പരിശോധിക്കുക. Management അല്ലെങ്കിൽ Liberal Arts തിരഞ്ഞെടുപ്പുകളിൽ വിഷയങ്ങളും പ്രത്യേക പഠനമേഖലകളും താരതമ്യം ചെയ്യുക. പേരുകൾ സമാനമായാലും യോഗ്യത ഒരുപോലെയാകണമെന്നില്ല. നിങ്ങളുടെ വിഷയങ്ങൾ മതിയാകുമോ, ഏതു പ്രവേശന പരീക്ഷാ മാർഗമാണ് ബാധകം, ക്യാമ്പസ് മുൻഗണന എങ്ങനെ നൽകണം എന്നീ സംശയങ്ങൾ NMIMS പ്രവേശന വിഭാഗത്തോട് ചോദിക്കുക.

അന്വേഷണ ഫോമും അപേക്ഷയും ഒന്നല്ല

വിവരങ്ങൾക്കോ തിരികെ വിളിക്കാനോ ഉള്ള ഫോം പൂരിപ്പിക്കുന്നത് NPAT പരീക്ഷാ രജിസ്ട്രേഷൻ പൂർത്തിയാക്കുന്നില്ല. ആ പ്രവേശന ചക്രത്തിലെ അപേക്ഷ, പണമടയ്ക്കൽ, ആവശ്യമായ പരീക്ഷാ ബുക്കിങ് എന്നിവയുടെ ഔദ്യോഗിക നിർദേശങ്ങൾ പാലിക്കണം. അവ തുറന്നതായി വ്യക്തമായ സ്ഥിരീകരണം ലഭിച്ച ശേഷം നടപടിയെടുക്കുക. സമർപ്പണത്തിന്റെ അംഗീകാരവും പണമടച്ച രസീതും സൂക്ഷിക്കുക.

പുതിയ കൈപ്പുസ്തകം വരുമ്പോൾ കോഴ്സ് പേരുകൾ, വിഷയ യോഗ്യത, ഫീസ്, പരീക്ഷയുടെയും തിരഞ്ഞെടുപ്പിന്റെയും തീയതികൾ വീണ്ടും പരിശോധിക്കുക. അതുവരെ ചെയ്യാവുന്ന പ്രായോഗിക ജോലി, നിങ്ങൾക്ക് അനുയോജ്യമായ കോഴ്സ്-ക്യാമ്പസ് പട്ടിക തയ്യാറാക്കുകയാണ്.
